Enterprise

by Kinsfire (The_REAL_Kinsfire)

Summary

Taylor Triggers in the locker, but rather than getting multi-tasking with insects, she gets a far more interesting multi-tasking connection - the USS Enterprise, NCC-1701-G.

The ripples out from that are immediate and intense.

Chapter 1: Authors Notes

This is going to be somewhat AU for Worm, and considerably more AU for Star Trek. (C’mon, with a working title like that, and the description I’m giving, how could it be anything else other than Star Trek?)

There are characters that I find immensely annoying in the Worm-verse, because in my opinion, they’re there solely for the purpose of screwing over the characters or the world. I don’t like Damsel of Distress, for example, and the Travelers are not likely to make that much of an appearance in this fic either, unless I decide that orbital bombardment is a good idea. So if there’s a favorite villain of yours that doesn’t show up, it’s probably because I don’t like them and find writing them to be such a chore that it just makes me not want to write anything at all. (I tend to write Coil out quickly in my stuff because he’s canonically such a moron with the power. A little thought and I’d have been able to successfully taken over Brockton Bay if I had his power. Other fanfic writers tend to write him as a better villain than the original was.)

As for Star Trek, I love the basic overarching universe. Grew up on reruns of TOS (was old enough for the series, but I was only four years old when the series ended), then enjoyed the hell out of TNG. DS9 had good stuff but a crappy ending, and Voyager … well, I’ve written a Harry Potter fic largely set there, but it was not as good as it could have been. ST:Enterprise tried, and I haven’t been able to watch Strange New Worlds. (Dammit. I want to!) Saw some Discovery, and season 1 of Picard.

I do know that they make a reference to the Enterprise G in there somewhere (I think in Season 3 of Picard), but I’m peeling away from before Picard season 1 started, and all that jazz with the Romulans and such. The Enterprise in mine is going to be NCC-1701-G, but nothing like whatever Picard canon says it is. (I have no idea what the stats they have for the G are.) And Taylor’s going to look at some of the databases and say “Why?” for some of the decisions Starfleet and the Federation made regarding some technologies. You’ll see those as they come up.

But with me saying that there are changes, PLEASE don’t come into the comments and tell me in a serious tone that I got something wrong, that they wouldn’t do this or that. I know that CANON says otherwise. I’m playing with canon a bit, hence the AU reference.

And as always, my Brockton Bay is not in New Hampshire like so many others place it. If it was there, Clockblocker sneezing would get a Boston Ward saying “Bless you.” NH is just too damned close to Boston. Maine works better for me. Southernmost coastal Maine, but Maine nonetheless. ( Triumph sneezing in Brockton Bay gets Los Angeles calling to bless him. *grin*)

Chapter 2: Prologue

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Armsmaster looked at his screens, and heard the one dedicated to Dragon activate. “I assume that you are contacting regarding the odd gravitic anomaly I just detected in high orbit?” he asked without looking.

“Yes. I was calling to ensure that we had multiple eyes looking at it. I know you can be quite busy at times, so simply wished to be sure.”

He paused for a moment before saying, “Thank you, Dragon. It is much appreciated.” He heard a small snicker from the screen. “Yes, I used my socialization software. I am attempting to learn, after all.”

“And it is appreciated,” she replied warmly. She then got down to business. “There happened to have been telescopes viewing that part of the sky, and at the time of the anomaly, it seems to have captured what could almost be considered a heat shimmer, except that a heat shimmer would require atmosphere, and this appeared to be far to high up for there be be enough atmosphere for a shimmer.”

“I assume you have some equipment tasked to discover what might be the case, since neither of us would be looking into this if it was an example of equipment error. Still possible, but highly unlikely.”

“We’ll both keep an eye on this, Colin. Let’s hope it’s nothing we have to worry about.”

“Is that ever the case when something unusual catches our attention?” he asked darkly.

Chapter End Notes

I will be trying to post once a week, either Saturdays or Sundays. Since I am dealing with nearly 100K words at the point that I posted these two short chapters, you'll have a while before I run out of words for you.

Chapters will tend to run somewhere around 2000 words, because that's just how they come out when I write. Some are longer, some are shorter.

Chapter 3: Friday, January 7th, 2011 - Danny

Chapter Summary

Taylor's been missing for three days, and suddenly she calls. So, what's happened to her these last few days?

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Danny was walking the floor, and Kurt and Lacey were trying to get him to sit. “I know, but I … I need to do something,” Danny said for the umpteenth time. “She’s missing since Tuesday, but there’s no sign of her running away. There’s that weirdness with her locker that has anyone who has any connection to anything government running around like headless chickens, but no sign of Taylor.”

Lacey opened her mouth to say something, but the telephone rang. Danny leapt on it like the lifeline he was treating it as. “Hello?” he asked, a little frantic.

“Hi Dad. I need to talk to you and before you ask where I am, that’s part of what I have to talk to you about. Can you ask Kurt and Lacey to stand?”

“Wait, are you okay? That’s the first thing I have to know.”

“Yes, I am. I can explain so much more in a couple minutes if the three of you will stand in the middle of the living room. Hang up the phone and get together. You don’t have to hug or anything, just be near each other. You’ll understand why as soon as you do that.”

Danny reluctantly hung up the phone, since whatever happened to her daughter had clearly made her Trigger and she had a power that she was going to be able to show them. Mover of some sort, he figured. “We need to stand up and be together in the living room,” he said. “She’ll explain in a minute.”

Lacey was on her feet first, pulling Kurt to his. As soon as Danny was near them, he saw a slight sparkle of light, and then he was staring at … “What the fuck? This looks like a Star Trek ship!” he exclaimed.

“Welcome aboard the U.S.S. Enterprise, dad,” Taylor said. “Hull registration number NCC-1701-G. This is a long story, but as you can see, I am okay.”

He took a long look at his daughter, and a pang shot through him. She looked so much like Annette at the moment. She was wearing a form-fitting tunic and slacks set, and was startled that his little girl didn’t qualify as quite so little any longer, for any meaning of the word. He raised an eyebrow. “You go to school dressed like that and I may need to get my hands on a phaser rifle to protect my little girl,” he said with a small, nearly hysterical laugh.

She flew over to him and grabbed him in a hug. “We need to talk about a lot of stuff, Dad, but things are good now. Better than before, at least.” She turned and hugged Lacey and Kurt as well, and then said, “Follow me. You won’t believe anything I have to say until you see the truth.”

They followed her through the hallways until she stopped in front of a door. “This is one of the conference rooms, and you’ll see why I chose it as soon as you’re inside.” She stepped through the door and was followed in by the three adults, who stepped over to the windows and stopped dead at the view.

Below them was the Earth in all its beauty. It was a clear day over the northeastern portion of the United States, which was a little unusual for the time of year. Lacey giggled. “I can see my house from here!” she finally said with a laugh.

Finally the three turned around to face a smiling Taylor, who was seated at the head of the conference table. “So what happened?” Danny finally asked.

Her face darkened a bit. “First off Dad, I need to apologize for not talking to you about what was going on. Emma turned on me a couple years ago - went from sister in all but blood to worst enemy while I was at that summer camp. This led to her deciding that I needed to be destroyed, and she got one of the girl jocks involved. I thought I could deal with it myself; that if I ignored them, they’d eventually stop. It became their mission to break me. I’m actually wondering if Emma was trying to kill me.” She shook her head. “They did everything from dumping juice on me, throwing my clothes into the shower with me so that I’d have to wear soaked clothing - that was a favorite of their during the winter especially. Steal my homework and turn it in as theirs, all that shit.”

She stood up and walked to the window, facing away from them. “It came to a head on the first day back from Christmas break. They’d apparently filled my locker with ‘used feminine products’, to be polite about it, before we went on break, so it sat in the locker for about two weeks. Then, when I went to my locker, Sophia shoved me into the locker face first and forced the door shut, breaking both my arms and fracturing my clavicle. I heard Emma say that she’d brought a lock that I heard put in the door and clicked shut. They then left me there, laughing. It’s hard to make a noticeable sound when you’re trying to not only scream through garbage, but you’re also trying to keep the roaches out of your mouth.” She shuddered, and suddenly Danny was holding her from behind, with Lacey and Kurt hugging her from either side.

“I snapped, Dad. I Triggered as I cried out for someone to help me. Just as I started to pass out from a lack of air - that locker was full, Dad - I felt something happen. The next I knew, I was waking up in this ship’s Sickbay, with the Emergency Medical Hologram making sure I was all right. He explained the injuries and other stuff, like all the pathogens he had to clear from my system while healing my bones.” She snorted. “Apparently, that’s the nickname the EMH uses to refer to himself. Swear to God, Dad, if I didn’t know the man was dead, I’d swear that they’d de-aged DeForrest Kelley and turned him into Dr Leonard McCoy.”

She turned to face them finally, but put her arms around him again and hugged him. “I’m sorry I never told you about it. Maybe we could have stopped things if you’d known earlier.”

He sighed. “Probably not. I was wallowing in depression, and forgetting that a wonderful part of my late wife was still here and needed attention. I’m sorry for ignoring you and just falling into the routine of work, home, drink, repeat. I’ve been a horrible father.”

“We’re both too stubborn to be moved from our positions without explosives,” she replied against his chest with a small chuckle, and both Lacey and Kurt laughed with them, nodding their heads. “So can we agree that we’ll try to do better?”

“You have my word, Little Owl. Now, this may sound silly, but how do you know you Triggered? I’ve never heard of anyone manifesting a honking huge starship straight out of science fiction, after all. Don’t think even the Triumvirate working together could manage that.”

“It’s probably best if I let someone else explain,” she said. “Enterprise?”

A hologram appeared in the room in what Danny thought of as a modified Next Generation uniform, and he suddenly knew what his daughter would look like as a full adult. If she were Vulcan and had pure copper hair, that is. “Greetings. I am the guiding intelligence of the ship classified as NCC-1701-G, colloquially called Enterprise.”

“Interesting,” Kurt said. “I thought Starfleet had issues with allowing computerized intelligences running starships.”

Enterprise looked at him and nodded. “Indeed. That is still an issue within Starfleet, but by the time that my predecessor, colloquially called ‘Enterprise F’, was being built, it was found that there was much that required assistance to properly function. Studies had been done regarding emerging machine intelligences, and my predecessors were built with a much different outlook than prior incarnations. For one thing, we are required to answer to biological life, and those who program us are required to undergo psychological examinations constantly, to avoid the M5 situation with Dr Richard Daystrom, if you understand the reference.” They all nodded their agreement. “I am unable to totally take control of this ship, for example, unless there is no available biological capable of giving orders, or if an officer of sufficient command level orders me to effect some duty. If there are no such biologicals available, I am to return to the nearest available Federation outpost and call for assistance.”

“How often has that happened?” Lacey asked with a laugh.

“In my own case, once. During exploration, my crew entered a section of the galaxy that is inimical to biological life more complex than plant life. Every sentient and sapient being aboard was killed instantly, and I returned to the nearest Starbase. I was undergoing refit at Utopia Planetia on Mars after a complete debriefing and forensic examination, and was awaiting a new crew when a subspace anomaly occurred, which caused my new captain to connect to me somehow, and I was suddenly in orbit above what is clearly a different Earth than I was previously in contact with.”

“Your new captain?” Kurt asked.

“The young woman you know as Taylor. The subspace anomaly made a connection between her and this ship. What she calls her ‘parahuman power’ grants her an amazing amount of true multitasking that no one in the Federation has ever seen before. With her ability, she can simultaneously run every function that is possible aboard this vessel, something that usually takes a crew of hundreds. This caused the databases to activate her as the captain of record for this vessel.” After a pause, Enterprise added, “In a very real sense, should she choose to start some variation of Starfleet here, she would be the Grand Admiral. She is, in a sense, an admiral right now, but with a fleet of one - me. And by tradition, being in charge of the ship automatically confers upon the right to be called Captain.”

Chapter 4: Friday, January 7th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Summary

Now we really get to see things from Taylor's point of view.

Taylor shrugged at her father. “No idea if we’re going to see other Federation ships show up, but I’m working under the assumption that Enterprise is alone and will stay that way. What I want to do is work with a number of people to figure out how to slowly increase the tech level of the world. I understand the basic reasoning behind the Prime Directive. If I just start handing Star Trek technology out, we’re going to have a war on our hands within a decade, just because some group like the CUI is going to make antimatter bombs to use against their foes. Plus, there’s having to build the tools to build the tools to build the tools going on as well. I’ve already got Enterprise looking into some things that would improve power generation technology. Things like that thing from the Aleph movie about Iron Man? His arc reactor? Get plans for things like that out there, maybe even released for free on the Internet. Still looking into that, by the way; I’m not dead set on releasing plans on the ‘net.”

Her father laughed. “All those conversations the three of us had -” He stopped for a moment with a sad look, but picked up again. “Best thing you could do, is remember some of the things that Annette thought about. She was a bit radical, and you definitely take after her, but I’m on board. Any possibility of throwing work toward the Union?” he finished with a grin.

“We’ve … sorry, you’ve got guys there who know how to do an amazing amount of things there, so as soon as I’ve got some money available, and plans on how to build something salable at our current technology level, I can start sending stuff your way. Maybe use our tech here to shore up some of the warehouses, for example.”

She stopped and rubbed the back of her neck, a little embarrassed. “I’ve, uh, well, I’m doing something a bit illegal, though. We need money, so I’ve got Enterprise here looking around for money sources available to criminal enter … groups.” They all snickered, knowing the word that she had been about to use. Even the ship’s avatar gave a tiny lip quirk, which was usually the Vulcan equivalent of a belly laugh.

“Planning on using the ship’s superior knowledge to steal their operating capital in an untraceable manner that somehow ends up available to you?” her father asked her. He cocked his head. “You’ll have to come up with a way of separating Taylor from the Captain of the Enterprise, though. Or figure out some really convoluted ways to get the money to Taylor Hebert in a believable manner.”

Enterprise spoke up. “Currently, the idea is to set up a trail that looks as if a previously unknown relative left a large amount of money to the first family member that fulfilled certain conditions. We would ensure that the Captain was the only person who fulfilled those conditions before activating the money transfer.”

“You can call me Taylor, you know,” she said.

“Yes, Captain,” was the response, along with an eyebrow raise that signified amusement.

Taylor just chuckled. “Yeah, what she said, though. You end up in charge of the money, and when I happen to come across an option to purchase shares in something, or come across plans for, or whatever we agree on, we start to use that money to build a company to do these things, and at that point, we can slowly start funneling more of those ill-gotten gains from the criminals into our work. Doesn’t need to be a huge, immediate thing, just a slow drain on their finances. Start by improving Brockton Bay, then Maine, then the northeastern seaboard, and so on. I’m sure that once we get to a certain point, we’ll end up being contacted by Dragon, who can help with the saleability of the tech we’ll be producing.”

“Been thinking about this a lot, huh kiddo?” Lacey asked with a laugh.

“Been thinking about it when I was mentally escaping from the Bitches Three at Winslow. Sort of an ‘in a perfect world’ sort of thing, y’know? And now I have the means to maybe start making that more perfect world.”

“Speaking of the ‘Bitches Three’, as you put it,” her father said, “what can you tell me, and is there any proof that we can nail people to the wall with?”

“Unfortunately, it’s a lot of ‘I said, they said’ bullshit. I’ve printed out eighteen months of emails with Emma and Sophia and Madison calling me any number of names and suggested fairly graphic and gruesome methods by which I should kill myself. Emma tends to give details on exactly how, in fact. But with Alan being a lawyer - that she regularly threatens people who disagree with her with - he’d do everything in his power to make sure that was never usable as evidence. I doubt the school would have kept records, since two of my tormentors are the daughter of a wealthy lawyer and a track star who is one of the only reasons Winslow ever gets any good press, other than to show that I’m a troublemaker who should be in juvenile lock-up.” She told him how to find the folder, and to give it to the police if they thought it was usable evidence.

Kurt spoke up. “Well, the school is getting looked at right now, because of your disappearance. A few students have said that they saw the three girls shove you in a locker, and several caught a bright light emanating from the same locker. That got the PRT involved, and now everyone is wondering whether you were kidnapped or Triggered.” Her father looked startled at that, but Kurt said to him, “Other than whether or not they’d found Taylor, you weren’t paying attention to the ins and outs of what’s been going on. You were rightly more worried about finding her than all the other shit around the case that didn’t have anything to do with her location.”

Taylor rubbed her hand down her face in a tired manner. “I should contact the BBPD and the PRT to let them know that I’m all right. The PRT is going to want to test me, most likely, and they’ll probably want to have Panacea check me out to make sure I’m not contagious or anything.”

“Why not come down to the planet - and I never thought I’d legitimately get to say those words - and call them both?” her father asked.

She thought for a moment. “Enterprise, can we connect to the telephone systems of the United States and make a telephone call?”

“Would you rather I attempt to route it through the wired connections, or use the cellular networks? I would actually be mimicking - spoofing, I think it is called at this point in history - a cellular call, because we are actually well above any of the satellites or towers used for the networks.”

“Cellular makes sense, because that actually sounds easier. PRT first, to see where and when they want me to meet with them, followed by the Brockton Bay Police Department, so that they can send some people to verify that it’s really me.”

“You’re sounding a lot different, Little Owl,” her father said. “Reminding me a lot of your mother, and that is definitely a good comparison.”

“I know it sounds weird for me to sound so composed, but right now, I’m realizing that I need to grow up mentally, rather than wallowing in thoughts of revenging myself on Winslow, Emma, Sophia, and all the other shit. I have the means to … Dad, I’ve had Enterprise doing scans of that porcelain bitch in orbit, and there’s a possibility that this ship could do some real damage in an Endbringer fight. Hell, if the scans show that this ship is powerful enough, we might even be able to destroy one. I was looking at some of what this ship can do, and … Dad, I could vaporize Brockton Bay with this ship, without too much effort. That’s got to at least be able to chip the wings off the Hopekiller. I’ve suddenly come to personally grasp Ben Parker’s advice to Peter - ‘With great power comes great responsibility’. I have so much I can do now. It would be criminal of me not to.”

He laughed a watery laugh and said, “Your mother is looking at the other angels and nudging them, saying ‘That’s my daughter!’ She would be so proud of you for that attitude.”

“Don’t think too wonderfully of me,” Taylor said with a grin. “Melting Winslow is still on the table, as far as I’m concerned. Maybe setting ship’s phasers on stun and popping Emma one from orbit?” The three adults snickered at the comically evil look she put on.

She then asked the ship’s intelligence to contact the Brockton Bay PRT offices.

“PRT, how can I help you?” was the first thing said.

“Hello, this is Taylor Hebert. I understand that there have been a number of agencies looking for me, so I’d like to set up an appointment to meet with someone to do a little explanation of what happened?”

The person at the PRT sounded much more interested. “Please hold for just a moment.” She then heard hold music. It was a local radio station that was currently playing a song sung by Rick Astley.

“Oh geeze,” she said with a laugh. “They accidentally just rickrolled me!”

“Miss Hebert?” a different voice said. “This is Miss Militia with the Protectorate ENE. Are you in need of pick-up or possibly medical attention?”

“No, I’m fine, but I definitely think I should talk to you guys. I can tell you what happened from my side, and you can perhaps help me figure a few things out.”

“Did you … perhaps undergo what might be described as ‘the worst day of your life’?” was the careful question.

“Yes, and I can explain better when I meet you. It’s not a requirement, but you might want to see if Panacea is around to make sure that I’m healthy from your point of view, and not contagious, given what was in that locker.”

There was a pause. “Would you complain if I put you on hold while we check quickly about Panacea’s availability?”

“Not at all. I understand that you’d need to do that. Just hope that they’ve moved on to a new song.” Taylor laughed, and heard Miss Militia chuckle before the music came back, and luckily it was a different song.

A few minutes later, Miss Militia was back. “Can you make it here tomorrow for about noon?” When Taylor agreed, Miss Militia thanked her and said, “We’ll see you then. Do you want us to contact the Brockton Bay Police for you?”

“If you want to, sure. Since I’m sure they’re out looking for me as well, it would be good to let them know that they can end that portion of the investigation.” With that, goodbyes were said and the call ended. “Well, I guess I get to sleep in my Earth bed tonight for the first time in a few days.” She snorted. “I love being up here, but it’s a little creepy at the moment if the various holographic intelligences aren’t active as holograms. Big ship that can carry over a thousand, and I was the only living thing on the ship other than plants.”

She paused. “Enterprise? Do you have a portable hologram generator that you can beam a signal to if I want to talk to you, or introduce you to people without bringing them up here?” In answer, the replicator hummed and a small disk, half again the diameter of a DVD and as thick as an Apple iPhone, appeared. “I or any of the other holograms can appear above this. Default is what you refer to as ‘life sized’, but smaller is doable if necessary.”

“I’m glad. First because it means I can talk to you without having to bring anyone up here, and second because I’m getting to like you and may just want to talk. I’ve got a lot to learn, and have some big shoes to fill, as the saying goes.”

Chapter 5: Saturday, January 8th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Summary

Now Taylor meets with the PRT. And they begin to understand just what she might have at her command ...

Taylor and her father were at the PR building in town before noon, and were quickly taken to a conference room. Panacea, Glory Girl, and Brandish were already there, and they introduced themselves. At exactly noon, Armsmaster, Miss Militia, and Director Piggot entered the room. “Hello, Miss Hebert,” Director Piggot said.

“Hello, Director. And greetings to you as well, Armsmaster and Miss Militia. I assume that this conversation will be recorded?” Taylor asked.

“You assume correctly,” Armsmaster replied. “Now, may I request that Panacea verify that you are healthy and not in need of further treatment?”

“Yes, I give permission for her not only to check me out, but fix things if need be. Please note, Panacea, that you will see some small electronic implants, such as the one that rests behind and beneath my left ear. I am aware of those and intend for them to be where they are. What they are will be explained later.”

Panacea walked over and took Taylor’s hand, and her eyebrows rose immediately. “For someone who spent some time in a toxic waste dump, I see no sign of any pathogens. Is that part of your power? And do you want me to finish fixing those old bone breaks in your arms and clavicle?”

“The healing is not part of my power in the manner you’re thinking, Panacea. I received those broken bones on Tuesday when a classmate, Sophia Hess, shoved me into what you just referred to as ‘a toxic waste dump’. I did not experience parahuman healing of any sort. And yes, you can finish the job if you so choose.”

“Interesting,” she heard Enterprise say in her ear. “Using you as a conduit, I can detect a similar and somewhat constant subspace anomaly, connected directly to her, much as there is one in you. Also, the three members of the organization you call the PRT know the name you mentioned, with the ones you refer to as parahumans also having the subspace anomaly.”

A moment later, Panacea was done. “You are potentially the healthiest person I have ever touched, Miss Hebert. I’d love to meet your physician some day.”

“If this conversation happens the way I’m hoping, we just might manage that, Panacea.” Taylor was amused - and found herself intrigued - by the fact that hearing that comment caused Panacea to make anyone looking at her aware that she was indeed equipped to nurse a baby in the future.

“Cheese and rice,” the girl breathed. “If that sort of thing is repeatable or usable by others, the things that could be done for the medical industry …”

“‘Cheese and rice?’” Taylor asked, amused.

“Yeah, needed an exclamation that doesn’t cause some people to complain that I’m using the name of a deity in vain, but there are times that call for some sort of exclamation. And you knew what I wanted to say, didn’t you?” Taylor nodded at that, snickering slightly at Panacea’s smile.

She turned to the PR members. “I don’t mind New Wave being here to hear this, but I think that it should likely go under confidentiality, if you get my meaning, since I’m sure there are moles within the PRT, simply because it’s a government agency and I’ve never heard of one yet that didn’t have at least some people selling information.”

Director Piggot nodded and pressed a series of buttons on the table at the end she was sitting at. “I am impressed,” Enterprise said in her ear. “Their equipment is actually capable of slightly degrading our connection.”

“So what is so important that you needed confidentiality?” Director Piggot asked.

“I did Trigger on Tuesday, and my power is either the most useless thing in the universes - yes, plural - or the best one ever. I personally vote for the second.” With that, she pulled out the disk Enterprise had created for her, and set it on the ground next to her. “Enterprise? Please activate.”

A moment later, the copper-haired Vulcan Taylor was in the room with them. “I am a hologram, connecting to a vessel currently in orbit around Earth.”

Armsmaster said, “Do you understand our coordinate system?” At Enterprise’s nod, he gave a set of coordinates to her.

“Yes, that is my body. I am the USS Enterprise, hull identification number NCC-1701-G, eighth of my name to bear some form of the original hull number originally commanded by Captain Robert April. Due to the circumstances of how I ended up in this universe, Captain Hebert is, as stated, my captain.”

“I can only assume that you have cloaking technology,” Armsmaster said. “We have noted a gravitic anomaly at those exact coordinates.”

“I do, indeed, have such technology.”

He turned to Taylor. “This may well be the most unusual minion generation I have ever heard of,” he said.

“She’s not a minion, sir. She’s the actual Enterprise. She was pulled through a subspace anomaly to our orbit, and my power latched onto her. Or possibly the other way around, I’m not sure, since I was freaking out from being in the process of dying and Triggering at the same time. Apparently, my power is insane multitasking and a connection to the Enterprise, which allows me to simultaneously run every position on the ship, something that usually takes an absolute minimum crew of one hundred and fifty. It was her Sickbay that healed me up.”

“Can you show us this ship?” Director Piggot asked.

Taylor thought for a moment. “Are you willing to leave the planet to do so?” she asked. “I can take you to my ship, since it is not built to land on a planet, but the only way I can think to do it that would convince you it’s not some simulation would take some time, and a bit of trust. I’d need to have a shuttle brought down from the Enterprise.” She turned to the hologram. “Do any of the shuttles have the capability to do what you and the others do aboard the ship?”

“All shuttles are equipped with holographic emitters to allow emergency transportation in case none of the on-board lifeforms are capable of flying and more than simple auto-pilot is needed. If we take this entire group up, I would recommend the Patsayev, the Grissom, or the McAuliffe be used. Those are currently best placed in the shuttle bay for easy launch and can carry up to twelve individuals - two crew and ten passengers. More can fit, but then people are left standing.”

“Next question - can you or a separate holographic intelligence fly the Patsayev down if I give a direct order to fly it here?”

“If given an order to do so, yes. Otherwise you would need to beam to me and fly it down yourself.”

Taylor looked to the Director. “Do I have permission to land an Enterprise shuttle on the roof of this building, which I know is rated for Dragon’s transports? If so, I will have Enterprise send a shuttle down, either flying it herself or sending an Engineering H.I..”

“I take it you have settled upon ‘holographic intelligence’ as a descriptor for myself and the others?” Enterprise asked with an amused eyebrow quirk.

“Can’t call you Artificial because that sounds like you’re just faking being intelligent. Silicon? Electronic? Don’t know if silicon is even a major part of your computer make-up any longer, and I’m not sure that the technology in the ship would even qualify as electronics anymore. The way you most often interact with us ugly bags of mostly water is via holographic interfaces, so that strikes me as best.” She shrugged. “I’m willing to listen if you have a better one.”

“There’s the plus that it’s friendly,” Glory Girl said. “I mean think about it - Holographic Intelligence, aitch eye, HI!”

Taylor giggled, and even Armsmaster’s noise of exasperation seemed to have some amusement in it. Director Piggot was giving the girl a glare that said she was trying to stay sober about it, but there was a very small quirk of the woman’s lips. Glory Girl just grinned. “By the way,” the girl said, “I give you permission to call me Vicky. My sister is Amy. I’m not stupid enough to try to give you permission to call my mother by her first name.”

“Thank you,” said Brandish with a bit of amused exasperation. “I suspect that the best route to convince people would be the shuttle method. Especially if we can see it land on the roof, it makes it much harder to set up for a simulation.”

“That’s my thought as well,” Director Piggot said. “Armsmaster, do you agree?” He simply nodded. “Then please have a shuttle flown down.”

“Do you wish me to fly it, or shall I send an Engineering hologram?” Enterprise asked.

Taylor thought for a moment. “I think you should return to the ship and have an Engineering hologram do it. We’ve been cloaked, and Simurgh hasn’t noticed us yet that we’re aware of. I don’t know if she’ll suddenly notice us when the ship decloaks, so I want you there.” She made sure to lock eyes with the hologram. “If she notices and begins an attack, I order you to do what is necessary to protect yourself. In that situation, you will have full autonomy over the entire ship, do you understand?”

Enterprise snapped to attention and saluted. “Yes, Captain. I am to do what is necessary to protect myself if the entity known as Simurgh attempts to attack, and have complete autonomy in such case.”

Taylor saluted back and said, “Return to the ship then, and beam me down my uniform, since this is now an official thing. I will see you again when we land in the shuttle bay.” Enterprise faded back into the disc, which Taylor then picked up. A moment later, a sparkle happened and her uniform appeared on the conference room table.

Much to everyone’s surprise, Taylor stood up and removed her blouse. “Honey,” her father said in a long-suffering voice, “you’ve got a little too much of your mother in you at times.”

As she slipped the skirt off, she laughed. “Dad, I’m wearing Federation workout clothing under my street clothes. I thought this might happen so I thought ahead. I wouldn’t have done this if I was just wearing standard underwear.” Indeed, she was wearing what could have been mistaken as French-cut panties, except that they were of a material that looked heavier and honestly covered more skin than some women’s track shorts. Her midriff was visible, and her top was what looked to be a halter-style sports bra. It was decorated in Starfleet command colors, and the pattern had very tiny Starfleet symbols embossed on the material. She quickly slipped into the slacks and blouse, then slipped on the jacket, which already had her external communicator attached.

“Damn, girl,” Vicky said. “If you ever want to go into modeling, you’ve got the body for it. Legs for … damn, those aren’t legs for days , but legs for weeks , and the fit of that sports bra? You’ll need a club to keep them off you!” Taylor chuckled, but was amused to see that Amy was once again showing that she was apparently dealing with a very localized cold front.

“Don’t see it myself, but I’ll trust your word,” she said. She looked to the director. “I know you’re going to want to try to get me into the Wards, but I honestly think that after power testing - which I am stating that I agree to and we will schedule - you’ll see that I’m not really a good fit. If only because that would end up putting my ship under the command of the PRT, and there are rumors regarding certain directors. Director ‘You’re It’ is rather famous for his attitudes.” She blushed. “But if she’s around, would you be willing to ask Vista to come along? I’ve always wanted to meet her, and think she has the coolest power of all the Wards.”

Miss Militia laughed. “You’ve been so professional, and then you remind us that you’re still a teenager.” She looked to Director Piggot, who nodded. “I’ll bring her to the roof?” she asked, and got another nod.

“Speaking of which, shall we head up there?” Director Piggot said.

As they exited the room, Armsmaster stopped for a moment before saying, “Yes, we are aware, Dragon. We are meeting with the parahuman involved with the ship that just appeared in orbit, and will be meeting a shuttle to take us up to it.”

“If she was in Brockton Bay, I’d invite her along as well,” Taylor said. “Another cape I’ve always wanted to meet. And honestly, if things are the way I suspect they are, I may need to liaise with her at some point regarding technology.”

They were met en route to the roof by Miss Militia and Vista, who was intrigued by the outfit Taylor was wearing. “Big Star Trek fan?” she asked.

“You ain’t seen nothin’ yet,” Taylor replied. “And by the way, I’m trying hard not to squee at meeting you.” Vista looked a little worried at that. “Not because of everyone’s ‘OMG she’s so cute!’ shtick, but because I think you’ve got the coolest power in the Wards, and possibly Brockton Bay.”

“ME? The coolest power?” Vista asked, taken aback, but clearly flattered. “How so?”

“Let’s get to the roof and I’ll explain.” They made the rest of the way to the roof, and were treated to the sight of a bright dot approaching, getting larger as it did. They could also see a stationary bright spot in the sky. “See that dot up there? Not the one getting bigger, but the one sitting there? That’s the Enterprise. Why your power is so cool? What’s your range?”

“Don’t know. Fairly long, but I need an unblocked path to what I’m trying to reach. Manton limited, after all.”

“Is it just shortening and lengthening the distance, or can you use it as a viewing portal?”

Vista looked startled and then looked up at the stationary bright spot. A moment later, a circle formed in the air and the assembled group could see the ship, hanging there in space.

“Are you seeing this through my visor, Dragon?” asked Armsmaster, awe-stricken. “Yes, that is what you think it is. Vista has a view portal open to show us what is in orbit.” His head moved sideways as if he had heard something painful. “Did something cause feedback, Dragon? That sounded like a high-pitched squealing noise.”

Taylor giggled. “I think she actually simply shrieked ‘squee’ in his ear. And I see the Patsayev is coming in to land.” Sure enough, the shuttle was settling to the roof of the building and the back of the shuttle was dropping to allow entrance.

“Captain,” the hologram stated. “Your shuttle is here.”

Chapter 6: Saturday, January 8, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

In this chapter, you have one of the two filk songs that I added to the story. Yes, I put the entire song in.

In this chapter, the song is The Ship, a filk written to the tune of The Highwayman. (Look on Google or YouTube for the song if you don't know it - the best version I've heard is by Willy Nelson, Kris Kristofferson, Johnny Cash, and Waylon Jennings.) The words were written by the author Roberta Rogow. It's possible you can find a version of her singing her version, but in my opinion, she wrote it out of her own singing register. A little too soprano for my tastes.

But the concept behind it fits for what Taylor is thinking about the job she's got. That won't always be obvious in the story as it progresses (she's a teenager, for Ghu's sake!), but it will be in the back of her mind at all times.

Taylor was the first to board the shuttle, and was surprised that no one followed. Director Piggot smiled and made it clear why. “Permission to come aboard, Captain Hebert?”

Taylor stood taller, steel in her spine now, a captain rather than a teenager. “Permission granted, Director. You may all come aboard, if you feel that you need individual permission.” Taylor turned and headed to the front, and sat in the left seat. “Do you have a name?” she asked the still visible Engineering hologram.

“No, Captain, although I and my fellow units have answered to ‘Scotty’ before.”

“Well, if you happen to find a name that you like, please make me aware and I will make it official .”

“You are aware that we Engineering holograms all share the same programming and are interchangeable?”

“At this point in time, yes. I am not a bigot, however, and have no issue with my ship’s H.I. crew learning hobbies and developing their own personalities if they so wish. The option is available. For this moment in time, though, I will call you Scotty. Now, do you need to be in control, or can I put my holodeck training to use and get us off the ground? More precisely, do you think I should, or should I leave it to you?”

Scotty paused for a moment. “The holodeck shows that you have at least the basics down. I would recommend that you let the ship guide you in when it comes time to land, based on your current level of skill.”

She grimaced. “Yeah, same thing as with airplanes. Flying is easy. It’s the landing that gets a little … interesting. Auto-pilot it is when we approach.”

“Very well. I will return to the system. Call on me if you feel the need, Captain.” With that, the hologram winked out.

“Interesting,” Vista quoted with a chuckle, “meaning lots of screaming and crying and a need for ambulances?” Taylor nodded with a grin.

With that, she closed the door and called the PRT for permission to launch. Once given, Taylor carefully lifted from the pad and headed skyward. “It should only be a few minutes. You can actually get up if you want, since the shuttle and the Enterprise both have artificial gravity in them.” She paused. “I always wondered about that. I know what they mean, but it really needs a different name. You’re still dealing with gravity, it’s just that it’s coming from a technological source, rather than natural sources. Anti-gravity makes more sense as a term for fighting gravity, since you’re using tech to fight it, but generated gravity is still gravity.” She shook her head. “Just the weird stuff I think about at times.”

Director Piggot stood and approached Taylor. “Captain, may I take the other seat here?”

Taylor nodded. “I hope I don’t offend, but once your people have verified the technology and such is not Tinkertech, would you like to see if Federation medical technology might be able to help you?”

The woman was still for a moment, and then simply said, “We’ll see. But I appreciate the offer.”

“I simply wanted it on the table as available to you. I understand there are many reasons for a person not wishing to avail themselves of parahuman healing. I personally don’t agree with the religious ones I’ve heard, but that’s a personal opinion of mine that should affect no one. Others make a great deal of sense to me. But I know you didn’t come up here to listen to me offend you.”

Director Piggot chuckled softly. “I’m not offended. I simply wished to know what your plans are, or if you’ve even had a chance to come up with any. As much as I would love to have any new Wards, I can understand your reasoning, especially if your technology does register as not being Tinkertech.”

“I don’t think it will, because while I was recovering from what those bitches did to me - and I suspect that Sophia Hess is either an intern or a Ward, because the three of you reacted to hearing the name - I studied, and talked to the Enterprise. She was able to reverse engineer quite a bit. As I said to my father, showing me how to build the tools that build the tools that build the tools, if you will. But there are valid reasons to not technologically uplift any society too much. But perhaps releasing or selling a true room temperature superconductor? That would alter technology, but only by how people think to use it. Don’t give them transporter or replicator technology, but improved farming techniques? Better power generation that can be built easily with existing technology, or very slight changes to existing tech?”

She sighed. “I will defend the Earth, though. We are examining the Simurgh to see if we stand a chance against her. Deep scans to figure out how she’s built and how she’s doing what she does. See if we can come up with ways to break her programming of people. She doesn’t seem to notice us, but she could just be lying in wait to surprise us. It is Ziz, after all.”

Taylor took a deep breath and then sighed heavily. “I didn’t realize it at first, but it’s sinking in to me. I have an absolutely gigantic responsibility. Not only do I have this amazing tech in my hands, but it’s technology that requires me to be the very best human being I can possibly be.”

“Why?” Piggot asked her. Taylor suspected that she asked just to see her reasoning.

“Because of who she is that I’m in control of, Director. I bear the awesome and powerful responsibility to not shame the name of this starship I control. This isn’t the Defiant, or the Constitution, or the Intrepid - which is another powerful name, mind you - I have the responsibility for the Enterprise. Before Ziz came along, she was the name that carried the dream of flying to the stars for humanity. Starting with her original version, the HMS Enterprize, then the US Navy’s Enterprise, CVN-65. Star Trek came along and helped us dream of the skies again, and did so well that they named a space shuttle after her original progenitor,” she said, motioning her arm toward the ship growing in their view. “In her original universe, the name means so much that she is the eighth ship to carry the name. I’m a teenager, and it’s my responsibility to make sure that I do not eternally tarnish what may be the most important ship in all of science and science fiction.” She sniffled once, but straightened up in her seat. “I will die before I allow the name Enterprise to be tarnished in the eyes of humanity. She means more to the world and humanity than I ever will. I. Will. Not. Fail.”

The shuttle was silent except for a small sniffle from Vista. Miss Militia finally spoke up. “With an attitude like that, I doubt you will, Captain Hebert.”

“I still need to grow into that title. I only really qualify to be called that because the ship tied to me when it came through. I can’t help but think that it could have chosen better.”

“I may be biased,” her father said, “but from what I just heard, I don’t think the ship could have chosen better. And I’ll help you in any way I can. Captain.”

“Thank you,” she said softly, but everyone heard it. As they approached the ship and she began a fly-by to show her off, Taylor began to hum without realizing, and shortly she was singing, to the tune of ‘The Highwayman’, unknowingly getting louder as she sang.


I was a frigate...
When wooden ships held iron men,
I sailed the oceans way back then.
I carried battle to the seas of the foe,
My sixteen-pounders leveled hulls and laid masts low.
And when the time came, I went out with the tide,
But I have never died... I have never died.


I was a carrier...
When sudden death rained from the skies,
I was the greatest of my size;
My planes were launched to fight a planet's greatest war,
And when the peace was won, I fought for that once more,
Then I was beached, and told to rest my guns again,
But I still remain... I will still remain.


I was a shuttle...
The very first of all my line,
All the acclaim and blame were mine.
Although I never flew a mission into space,
I was the prototype that put things into place,
The next step opened up the heavens to our will,
And I am living still... I am living still.


I was a starship...
Across the galaxy I flew,
With Captain Kirk and all the crew;
Finding a home upon some unknown alien shore,
Finding a place where none had ever gone before.
Then I was sacrificed, I took that final dive,
But I am still alive... I am still alive.


I am a vision...
A wooden ship... an iron frame,
A starship and a guiding flame.
I've lifted mankind from the confines of the land,
I've given hope and courage place to take their stand,
And when they talk about the faith that never dies...
They'll call it Enterprise … Call it Enterprise!


After a respectful silence, a voice spoke up. “Damn girl, not only are you supermodel hot, but you’re an amazing singer? Leave something for the rest of us!” Vicky finally said, failing to hide the fact that Taylor had her crying just a little bit.

“I think, Captain, that you will have very little to worry about in regards to holding the name to its proper standard,” Armsmaster said quietly, with a reverence that surprised those who worked with him.

It was then that Taylor realized that they were all using the rank seriously. Not treating it as a cape name, or something of the like, but as if she truly had earned the title of Captain. She stiffened her back again, and brought the ship around to the shuttle bay. With a suddenly teenager snicker she said, “Open the pod bay doors, Enterprise.”

“I’m sorry, Captain, but I’m afraid I can’t do that,” Enterprise responded with her own voice, but the soft cadence of the movie. “Mainly because we don’t have pod bays,” she followed in her normal voice. “May I assume that you wish me to bring you in safely?”

“Yes, safely would be appreciated, or else I’d have tried landing. Then we have to repair the shuttle and the deck.” She giggled softly and let the Enterprise take over the landing.

“You’re not that bad,” Enterprise said. “Your landings are currently just a little more … energetic than is usually preferred.”

Taylor turned to the others. “That means passengers would get whiplash, most likely, from the sudden stoppage of the craft. I’ll keep practicing in the holodeck until I’m good at it.” She blew out a breath. “There’s a lot I need to learn. I’m a captain without the blessing of Starfleet, running a Starfleet ship. Of course, it would require them making it here to be able to do anything about it, so I take classes in the holodeck.”

She opened the back of the shuttle once it was down and stepped to the back of the vehicle, and down to the deck. “Welcome aboard the USS Enterprise,” she told them as they stood. Vista was nearly vibrating as she waited to debark.


Chapter 7: Saturday, January 8, 2011 - Vicky

Captain Hebert led the group up to the bridge. “I want to travel, but there’s too much to do here on Earth at the moment. I’m thinking about sending out a few probes to see if there’s any asteroid mining that can be done, as well as just getting a feel for what’s out there. Hell, there’s so much exploring we can do right here in our own solar system. So much to do, just here on our own planet.”

She walked over to the Engineering console. Admittedly, if Vicky remembered her Star Trek: The Next Generation well enough, any of the consoles could be used for any purpose, but they still tended to think of them as set for a certain field. She called up something and called Armsmaster over. “Sir, would you look at this and tell me if you think this is Tinkertech, or something anyone with the engineering to follow the process could do?”

The man watched the screen for a moment before saying, “As far as I am aware, I could hand this process to the Engineering Department at Brockton Bay University and have their students working on this. No Tinkers required. May I have a copy of this? If this does what I believe that it will, I will begin the process of procuring the patent for you, Miss … apologies, Captain Hebert.”

“Armsmaster?” Director Piggot asked. “What is it?”

“This is a set of directions on how to create a literal room temperature superconductor, Director. If this was the only thing Captain Hebert ever gives us, technologically, it would still not only revolutionize multiple industries, but make her exceedingly wealthy. I believe the phrase ‘wealth beyond the dreams of avarice’ is how many would put it. Just this product alone would allow her to fund a modern technology clean-up of the Bay within a few years time.”

Vicky smiled as the girl laughed. “I think I’ll need that kind of money, because I’m not the Federation in a post-scarcity and post-money society. I’ll need the ability to pay for things, and likely have to create some sort of organization in order to pay crew members.”

Amy spoke up. “If I am able to work the medical technology from this ship, I’d join up and work for free!” She laughed somewhat darkly. “I already do at the hospital, after all.”

“That’s unfair,” the captain said. “The non-powered doctors make money for healing people the slow way. Why does having powers mean that you have to give healing away for free? Other than the US government trying to make sure via NEPEA-5 that no parahuman ever gets paid an honest wage for using their abilities, that is.”

“That’s not quite how it is,” Miss Militia started to say, but the captain’s father spoke up.

“Actually, as someone who’s in charge of hiring for the Dockworker’s Union, that’s almost exactly how it is. The way the laws are written, it is exceedingly difficult for a parahuman to get paid for using their powers. I’ve had to turn away people with Brute ratings because of the amazing hassle involved in getting permission for them to get paid by someone other than the PRT. Our union lawyers have talked about that, and it’s more than a little obvious that the laws were designed to funnel people into either villainy or forcing them to get paid to work for a military organization specifically designed for parahumans. And if they’re villains and get caught, they can be forced into the Protectorate or Wards, depending on age.”

“Don’t think I’m anti-military, either. I gladly served in the Navy for a time, and still have friends who are lifers in multiple branches. But I guarantee that Parian is paying far more in taxes to run her business than she would if she was just a highly skilled normal.”

The captain spoke up. (It was weird to Vicky to think of a girl she was sure was roughly her age as ‘Captain’, but she sure carried herself that way at the moment.) “I know that I’m a parahuman, because the EMH asked me about the structures in my brain, and I explained what I knew about them. I’m betting you guys could explain it better to him. But I’m not sure how you’re going to test me. In regard to the kind of stuff you deal with on Earth - and that’s really weird to realize that has meaning right now - I suspect that I’ll come up as either non-applicable for most powers, or as a Master something or other in regard to this ship. I can run everything on this ship simultaneously, and probably also pilot a shuttle with my mind at the same time, but I also have this feeling that I suspect is powers based that anything I can Master has to be based on the technology on this ship. And it’s entirely possible that if you managed to build a Federation device on Earth without any help from this ship that I might not be able to affect it at all. Until we reach the point where I can interact with other vessels from this ship’s origin universe, I don’t know if this ship is the only one I can affect.”

She shook her head. “Shall I continue with the tour, and maybe show you Sickbay next?” Vicky snickered as Amy literally started bouncing on the balls of her feet. She was mildly amused to note that Captain Hebert seemed to enjoy that, at least a little, given where her eyes fell for a moment. The captain gave her own snicker and said, “Sickbay it is.”

As they walked, she ended up next to Vicky, Amy, and Vista. The adults seemed to be grouping together, although it was clearly just the way things fell and not an intentional segregation. “Sorry if I caused issues or offended you, Panacea, when I asked about the money thing. It’s one of my soapbox issues.”

“You can call me Amy,” Amy told her. “I wasn’t offended, but if I can do this, why shouldn’t I?”

“I have no problem with that , I just have a problem with the thought so many have that someone who can heal owes the world that talent for free, no matter what it might take out of the healer. What if your power made you take on some of the injuries you’re healing yourself? That should be paid for, if only because of your literal pain and suffering. Instead, because you do it for free, you get people who want you to fix this or that simple thing, or think you owe it to them to do cosmetic stuff. God knows I’d love to have more up top than these bee stings, but like hell am I ever going to ask you or any other healer to do anything about it for free!”

Vicky could help but laugh. “Captain -”

“You can call me Taylor if you want. I’m not going to be offended. I’ll only insist on the rank when it’s a public function.”

Vicky popped back in, “Taylor, if you call those bee stings, then you’re dealing with some gigantic fucking bees! You’re not going to have those things entering the room two minutes before the rest of you, but I wasn’t joking earlier when I called you supermodel beautiful. Mom’s gonna yell at me any time now for saying this, and your father might get annoyed at me -”

“If you’re about to describe the various ways my daughter looks like her late mother, I agree with you,” he said.

“- but you’ve got legs for weeks, like I said, and an ass that is absolutely amazing, especially in those workout shorts of yours. If you wore something like that at Arcadia for Phys Ed, you’d probably be asked to change into something a bit less sexy. You could lose a little bit around the waist -”

“I look like an upright frog,” Taylor said.

“Damned well built frog, then,” Vicky bulled on. “Get the ship to give you an ab routine and you’ll be making them walk into walls coming and going. And those breasts of yours? I’m pretty much straight and I think they’re amazing.” She narrowed her eyes for a moment, thinking. “Huh. You mentioned Sophia Hess. I know that bitch has had a couple hangers-on for a couple years, and one of them is the daughter of one of Mom’s coworkers. You got told you were ugly by old Boobs-and-Butt Barnes, didn’t you?”

Taylor goggled at her for a moment, and then had to lean against the wall because she had burst out laughing. “‘Boobs-and-Butt Barnes?’ That’s hilarious !”

“Ever since she went from being an okay girl to being the queen of the bitches, that’s all she has going for her, other than threatening anyone who she disagrees with with her lawyer father.” Vicky snorted. “Tried that with me once, and I reminded her exactly which law firm her dad works for, and who one of his coworkers was. She shut up real fast when she realized the trouble I could get her father into. But her whole life is around a modeling career, and she hasn’t been growing the right way to really keep it going. In fact, that whole thing she crows about that got her the nickname is working against her, because she can’t do the local commercials and photo shoots, because she’s too curvy for them now. Not that they hire sticks, but that she’s at the point where she’s clearly not an adult physically, but she’s physically too sexually mature for children’s shoots, and there really isn’t a call for teenagers in her age group.” She smiled. “Whereas if you didn’t have this hanging over your head, you could make inroads with an agency, and probably be on national TV or doing a Victoria’s Secret runway by the time you’re twenty.”

“Really?” Taylor asked her, and Vicky could hear that she was all teenager at the moment.

“Taylor, I’m about as het as you get, and I can say that looking at you is a pleasure. You’ll have guys walking into walls if you dress more like you are right now.”

“Not at Winslow,” she replied darkly. “When I realized how bad it was going to be for me, I tried to transfer to Arcadia, since I had the grades at one time. I’ve had the principal, the vice-principal, and the secretary openly look at my application, hold it up, and tear it in half in front of me. I suspect that if there are problems with Winslow at any point, they’ll mock up evidence to prove that it was all my fault in order to have Blackwell fail upwards to a city-wide school board position. I’ll keep going until June, at which point I’ll be sixteen and drop out to get my GED.”

The girl snorted. “I’m just wondering when Sophia will get a medal from the mayor for chasing the troublemaker out of Winslow.” She had a snarl on her face, but then waved her hand in the air as if chasing all that away. “Enough about me whining. I have a tour of an amazing ship to give.” After a pause, she added, “Y’know, hon, you could be helping me on this tour as well.”

Enterprise’s voice rang out in the hallway. “You’ve been doing quite well all on your own, Captain. If I hear something incorrect, I will make you aware, but unless you require my presence, I believe I will simply listen in.”

Amy snorted. “Have Little Miss Vulcan Hotness show up at Winslow at some point while you’re there, Taylor. She looks like you have a copper haired Vulcan older sister.” She giggled, then realized exactly what she’d said and turned bright red. Taylor was also more than a little pink at that.

Chapter 8: Saturday, January 8, 2011 - Taylor

After the tour was over - Amy had nearly had to be dragged out of Sickbay and had left with a PADD with a great deal of medical information on it - they had transported back into the Director’s office. “That’s a limited use PADD, by the way. You can get new data from the ship, but you can’t use all of it’s usual functions. Mainly because right now, the ship has only one official crew member. And no, that wasn’t a hint,” Taylor told the parahuman healer. “You will be able to use it to contact me, although I’ll get it via the communicator here,” pointing at the device on her jacket.

“I want to learn what I can,” Amy said excitedly, “because I just might try to sign on as your first crewman, in Medical.” Brandish was frowning at that, but said nothing.

“If it sounds like something you might be interested in, we’ll talk. I’ll probably grab my own PADD in case you want to talk via the Starfleet equivalent of Facetime.” As she said that, a PADD beamed in on the table next to her, as did a second one marked ‘Armsmaster’. Taylor unfocused for a moment and said, “Ah. That one has the plans for the superconductor you were shown.” She snickered slightly. “It’s, uh, well, since you’re known as a Tinker, you were given the equivalent of a kindergartener’s PADD, in case you decided to try disassembling it. I explained to her that sometimes Tinkers literally can’t help it with technology. Mind you, with the difference between current technology and that PADD, it’s the equivalent of giving you a bleeding edge Dragontech tablet for alpha testing.”

“Do you have a telepathic connection to the ship?” Director Piggot asked.

“No. Remember how I mentioned that Panacea would detect some subcutaneous technology? I have what is next-gen technology as a communicator implanted behind my left ear.” She snickered. “She can also use it in a ‘Find My Phone’ fashion to locate me in case the Empire finds out about me and decides to ‘invite’ me to join. She can hear me at all times, and I’ve already got a code-word in place for if someone attempts to force me to give over control.” She grinned, and it was not a nice one. “Let’s just say that to keep me from being able to give said word to Enterprise, I’d already be dead, at which point taking her over becomes much harder for someone wanting control. Since she can’t return to Spacedock - it being in another universe she can’t get back to at the moment - then she will have autonomy to act as she sees fit. And she likes me. Whomever kills me is going to likely have a very short moment to realize that it wasn’t a victory.”

From her comm badge came the comment, “I do not wish to deal with the scenario involved in Walt Whitman’s poem, Director Piggot. You might wish to stress that in the write-up that you are required to do regarding our meeting. As I said, I know there are moles, and you can’t set a meeting like this to Eyes Only, so some of this is going to be readable by people reporting to whatever other groups they get extra pay from.”

The director nodded. “I think the only thing we can really do now is set up when your testing should be. Since you’re a student, it should probably be a weekend.”

“However, I am a Winslow student, and I understand that the CDC has shut the school down for this past week and probably into next week.” She grimaced. “Plus, I’m not going back there if I don’t have to.”

“We’ll be looking into things and seeing if we can’t … expedite a transfer to Arcadia,” Piggot said.

Armsmaster looked up from his personal version of a PADD and said, “Next Saturday would likely be best all around, to be honest. We need to get the testers here and prepared for what needs to be tested. If you can give us a better idea during the week what to test for, it would be appreciated.”

“Well, I can tell you that while the ship might qualify for a Stranger rating since it can cloak, there is no personal cloaking device. The power requirements for it would … well, let’s just say that I’m not carrying an antimatter backpack just to power invisibility. Doesn’t matter what they say about shielding, the smart thing is to assume that it’s just waiting to escape - exuberantly - so no backpack antimatter power packs.” She received some amused chuckles from the reference to exuberant escape. “Thinker might qualify because I’m connected to the ship’s database, so I can get information when I need it and basically model things, but even there I think it would be a low Thinker rating. Master, but only for currently existing Federation technology in this universe? Not Brute, since I have the same strength I should have as a normal nearly sixteen year old girl. Basically, for me, I suspect that I’ll get classified as a Tinker because of the future-tech - even though it can be replicated with Earth tech - Thinker because of my connection to Enterprise’s databases, and Master because of Enterprise herself, even though that’s the only tech I can control. She, uh, chose to … relieve the Merchants of a few bits of their technology. Stolen at that. I tested if I could control those, and the answer was no. Since no one had touched them, they were dropped off at the BBPD in a makeshift bag marked ‘Stolen property’. Unless you guys tell them, I shouldn’t end up involved in any way. And it’s not like there’s going to be a reward for any of it.” She paused. “Enterprise - work on getting tech for fast DNA results available at current tech level.” She paused and looked at the others. “I have all these ideas, and it’s best to remind her, so that I don’t forget.”

She shook her head. “So Tinker/Thinker/Master maybe for me? As for the ship, she gets a few ratings of her own if the PRT decides she needs ratings. Blaster, Mover, Shaker, and Stranger, with maybe a Brute rating because of her armor? But it’s a vehicle, and I don’t think they get a Brute rating, do they? Oh, the hologram might classify as a Breaker state. Maybe.”

“You’re being rather forthright about this stuff,” Miss Militia said with a smile. “We’re not used to that. Most people try to hide something.”

“Well, even if I don’t end up with the Wards - sorry, Vista, but I don’t think I’m a good fit - I want to be as friendly as possible with the PRT. Hiding something and then using it leads to less than trusting looks at me as I say ‘Oops?’. I’d rather avoid that.”

Taylor paused. “Do I have permission to give Vista one of our PADDs, severely locked down as far as ship’s databases are concerned? I suspect she’d like to have another girl to talk to that doesn’t think she’s an annoyance.”

“Why would you think anyone is like that to her?”

“Because I know Sophia Hess, and if she interacts with people, they’re nothing, because they aren’t the most amazing person on the planet - namely her. Just ask her; she’ll tell you.” After a pause, she added, “And remember that you reacted to the name, so it means that you deal with her in some manner. I have my suspicions, but I’m not voicing them again.”

“Yeah, she knows Sophia,” Vista muttered quietly.

Director Piggot looked at the girl for a moment and smiled again. Taylor was sure that was not a normal thing for her to do, given how some of the others in the room reacted. “I have no issues with giving Vista a restricted PADD.” A moment later one beamed onto the table with a sticky note that said ‘Vista’.

Taylor smiled back and said, “Armsmaster, when you’re in your lab securely, contact Enterprise via the PADD you’ve got. She’s thinking of sending you some simple Federation tech to see what you can make of it. More if , honestly. Gives us a decent idea of the tools we need to make in order to make the tools, and see how many levels of that are going to be needed.”

“That would be greatly appreciated, Captain Hebert,” he said simply. “And if I learn that we can recreate some of your technology, I will see to it that it is patented under your name as well.”

“Thank you. If I can start getting some money coming in from things like that, it means I can start a company to make things that I suspect the police and PRT would like, such as stun pistols and rifles that could take down Lung before he gets too ramped up, and maybe transports that would be harder for groups like the ABB and the Empire to break their compatriots out of. No promises on that, but I can try.”

With that and a few more pleasantries, the meeting broke up, leaving the PRT to talk seriously about what they had learned while the others exited the building.

Out on the street, before they got into the crowds, Taylor said, “Given everything, I think I’m going to end up being an independent, but much like how I want to have good relations with the PRT, I also want good relations with New Wave. I seriously doubt I’m going to be able to hide things, since I know already that everyone knows my name as being the one who disappeared from the locker in a flash of light. When Federation tech suddenly starts showing up around me, it’ll be really kind of obvious, so I’m figuring on having Enterprise beef up security on my house and give Dad a few things to help him when the Empire comes calling. When you feel that you can trust me, I’ll offer to help you with security for your houses.”

“Interesting,” Brandish said. “You allowed us onto your ship, but feel that we don’t yet trust you? Why let us aboard?”

“Well, to be honest with you, for one thing. Being honest, I mean. Also, you couldn’t have really affected anything important, since that stuff is locked to me at the moment. Another reason is to show you that it really is Federation technology. If you’ve ever watched any of the shows, you have an idea of how powerful it is, and what it might be able to do. The original series had a scene where they stunned everyone on a city block from orbit. And this is literally at least a generation or so later, with newer technology. I want to improve the world, but you’re going to need to take some time to believe that.” She shrugged. “It’s a fact of the world we live in. We don’t trust easily, and given the type of people out there, I can’t say as I blame anyone for that. I just want to change that attitude, and that’s going to take time.”

Chapter 9: Saturday, January 8th, 2011 - Armsmaster

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the missed posting this last weekend. Time got away from me and I didn't realize until today that I'd missed posting on Saturday or Sunday.

So, here's the chapter I SHOULD have posted.

Next chapter will be a completely new day.

“Colin, this is absolutely amazing. Once I make a deal with her I can start using the superconductor in some of my own technology. But the fact that her ship gave you more technology that it considers more to our level? The materials science involved in an internal combustion engine that doesn’t need oil to prevent the engine from seizing up? The metal of the engine itself prevents the seizing? I’m sure that you can think of multiple uses for such a metal beyond rebuilding your motorcycle yet again.” He heard the teasing tone at the end of her statement and nodded.

“I do tend to work on that perhaps more than people think is good. I have long suspected that my power took my drive for efficiency in all things and - what is the phrase - ‘ramped it up’ until it becomes something of a drawback for me. I am constantly spending large amounts of time working on various things to get the slightest edge on efficiency, sometimes to the detriment of maintenance times. But I am driven to do so.” He paused before continuing. “But yes, I agree. While not a frictionless material, the fact that it resists damage from rubbing against itself and other materials, and even seems to act as if lubricated? I can think of many uses for it. Doors around the Rig and in the PRT building at the very least, since the material also seems to be fairly light. The question comes down to replicating it. It’s not something that we currently have, and the ship did not do like Scotty did in ‘The Voyage Home’ and give the man the formula for transparent aluminum.” He looked closer at the entry for that metal. “Although it appears that we have been pointed in the right direction.” He cocked his head for a moment before looking at his monitor where Dragon was displayed. He fired off a list of metals and additives, as well as a potential temperature range and possible cooling process.

She looked at him. “I suspect that you’ve cracked it, Colin,” she said. “I’ll need to do tests and attempt to recreate what you’ve described, but that just might give us exactly what we’re after to make this.” After a moment during which he was sure she was making sure that the process he’d just suggested was written down properly, she said, “I find some of the fabric science to be interesting as well. And it also strongly hints that she’s telling the truth regarding the origins of the ship, because we both know that Tinkers have a focus. Asking you to make a fabric that will withstand a bullet? I can’t see you managing that, even with your amazing intellect. But this girl has given us superconductors, fabric, electronics, potential power generation … that’s just too many disciplines for a Tinker to normally have. But if she’s really just able to get the information from the databases on the ship? That makes a lot more sense. And to have somehow built the ship and all those shuttles since Tuesday? If she can manage to materialize that much after such a recent Trigger? She’d be beyond Triumvirate level in power. She’d be closer to Scion in power, if not even past him.”

“I had thought of that as well. Also, simply given the fact that the technology that she is showing us is able to be recreated without the necessary help of a Tinker gives strong credence to the likelihood that the ship is from elsewhere and simply connected to a teenaged girl. And based on what I heard and what my equipment tells me from listening to her, I will be eternally grateful that it was Miss Hebert that the ship connected to. Connecting to someone such as L33t? Shadow Stalker? Just about anyone in the Empire or the ABB? Instead, we have a young woman who takes the responsibility of being captain of a ship that everyone knows the name of extremely seriously and refuses to tarnish that name. If she can follow through on what she states she desires from the responsibility, then I think that the ship and its legacy are in excellent hands. And I believe that she will do everything in her power to live up to that legacy.”

There was silence from Dragon for several moments before she finally responded to him. “You were a fan of those shows, weren’t you?”

“Oh yes,” he answered her. “To some extent, it was one of the things that guided me to wanting to be a hero, even before I Triggered. I wanted to be worthy to serve alongside someone like Captain Kirk or Captain Pike. I know I often fall short of that goal, but it’s a goal worth reaching for.”

Her smile was a pleasant sight. “You amaze me at times, Colin. You display a poetry in your soul that doesn’t often show, and I’m honored that you show me that side of you.”

“You are my closest friend, Dragon. If I can’t be myself with you, then who can I be that way with? There are times I wish that I could Tinker up a way to cure your agoraphobia, because I would like to meet you in person someday.”

A hand rose to her chest and her smile was bright. “If I ever manage to do so, Colin, I promise I will meet you face to face, rather than through a suit.”

They returned to a level of silence, since neither was entirely comfortable with the level of emotion that had just been displayed. At least, Colin knew that he was somewhat uncomfortable showing much emotion. He had been mocked so often growing up, and it was really only in the last handful of years that he realized that even before he had Triggered that he fell somewhere on what was referred to as the autism spectrum. Not debilitatingly so, but strong enough that it affected his daily life to the point of people on PHO referring to him as a robot on a regular basis.

It was about fifteen minutes later when he said, “Every one of the things on this PADD is something that we can likely create within the next month or two. There are hints as to the changes needed to be able to develop a power generation plant of any size that will use far less resources than anything else out there. I suspect that the next list of items that I am sent will be things that, as Captain Hebert stated, will require us to build the tools in order to build the tools. But she appears to be leading us in that direction. Slowly, perhaps, for her, but at an accelerated rate for us.”

“From what I’ve read of the reports regarding the meeting with her, I suspect that she would like to see if it is possible to get Earth to a point where it is much closer to Roddenberry’s Utopian vision for the future. So we won’t see some of the technology around any time soon. I strongly doubt that she will allow replicators, for example, because of what they would do to the economy of just about every nation on the planet.” She snickered. “Let’s hope that she’s not one of those people who wants flying cars everywhere. She’s of an age where she might like that science fiction trope.”

“Agreed. Let us hope her head is screwed on better than that, as they say. But she strikes me as the sort to realize what a problem a flying car would be, both in range, and honestly, the quality of the drivers slash pilots.”
