Chapter 10: Monday, January 10th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

Starts to get a bit adult in this chapter, but this is not going to turn into a porn story. It will, however, remember that teenagers don't suddenly develop sex drives when they hit the magical age of eighteen. There is nudity and something I've never seen for Annette before, that actually won't have a huge part of the story, but is there nonetheless.

*shrug* Some will like it, some will hate it, and some might leave - who knows?

The rest of Saturday went well, and Sunday was definitely a day of rest for everyone. The news stated that Winslow was still closed and would likely be reopening on the seventeenth of January, so all Winslow students had an extra week. The anchors recommended that they study to make sure they were caught up, because it was likely that the school would stay open at least a week later at the end of the school year.

Monday saw her father head off to work, more cheerful than she’d seen him in a long time, and was glad that she’d gotten her head out of her ass and actually talked to him. They had a ways to go, but they were healing. She got comfortable and studied, making sure that the holoprojector disc was with her in case Enterprise needed to talk to her and wanted to be visible while doing so.

Of course, for her comfortable meant that she was dressed much like her mother dressed when she was home from work - in as little as possible. Often nude. She didn’t think she was an exhibitionist, she just learned from her mother that clothes were for adornment and protection. If you weren’t doing something like going out in public or staying warm, why wear something that could feel binding on you?

So she spent most of the day staying up to date on her schoolwork, finding that the connection to the Enterprise databases was making her work a lot easier. Not that she was constantly seeking for info; it was more that she was just aware of the answers when she was working out a problem. Math was far easier for her as well. She could tell that she wasn’t actually searching the ship’s computers; it was more that she had all that computing power available to solve things. Yeah, definitely a Thinker rating.

About one pm, she got a call on her PADD. Since it could only be one of three people, she answered it, not thinking about how she was dressed. It turned out to be Amy, with Vicky looking over her shoulder. “Taylor, mind if we … oh, sorry, didn’t realize I’d caught you at a bad time.” Amy was blushing furiously.

“What? No, I was sitting around studying in my room. What’s up?”

“Wondering if you’d have a problem with us dropping by to talk,” Vicky said. “Might want to put on a robe first if you’re embarrassed by others seeing you, though.”

It was then that Taylor remembered she was nude, and looked down. “Oh. Sorry. This is me being comfortable. I’ll put on something for when you guys get here.” She gave the address, and Amy hung up, still quite pink in the face.

Taylor chuckled and grabbed a skirt and t-shirt before heading downstairs. She brought her PADD and holo-disc with her and dropped it on the couch while she threw the shirt and skirt on. Hmm, need to do a little shopping. Skirt’s shorter on me than I remember. She went into the kitchen to grab a drink, then remembered something. She popped back out and called Amy on the PADD, and the very small unhappy look on her face when she realized that Taylor was wearing clothes made Taylor smile and feel a little warm. “Watch out for the stairs outside. Second step from the bottom needs to be replaced, we just haven’t gotten around to it, what with the weather and dealing with other stuff.”

“Thanks for the warning. We’re coming in for a landing right about now.” Taylor opened the door, and sure enough, there was Glory Girl with her sister in her arms in a bridal carry. Amy’s feet touched ground and she started to bound up the steps, clearly remembering at the last second about the step warning. She got the the top and grabbed Taylor in a hug. Vicky was clearly startled by that. Taylor was as well, to be honest.

“Thank you so much for giving me all that medical data! I’m understanding so much now, and it almost feels like my power is … it’s weird to say it, but it’s almost like it’s sitting there munching popcorn, excitedly waiting for what comes next.”

“Well, we’ve already realized that powers come from somewhere else. Enterprise located subspace connections to every single one of the parahumans who were on the ship on Saturday. They’re all slightly different, but very similar in a lot of ways. So maybe whatever allows you to heal people is actually sentient or sapient in some fashion. It’s not the weirdest thing.” She smiled as she realized that Amy was still hugging her, and had sort of relaxed against her as she did so. She liked it, so she wasn’t about to say anything to make her stop.

After a minute or so, she saw Amy’s eyes go wide and she pinked again, and let go of Taylor as if she was red hot. “I am so sorry!” she started to say, but Taylor held up a finger.

“Did I show any sign of wanting you to let me go? I rather liked having a friend hug me.” As she saw Amy’s face drop very slightly, she said quietly. “Might end up more in the future, but we did just meet, after all. But I’m not against more.”

“God, that’s the first time I’ve ever been that forward,” she said, trying to put her blush on afterburner.

“And I’m not against it happening again, even if it’s just hugs. I like hugs.” Taylor got serious. “Spent two years being shit on at school - thank god it wasn’t literal - and between Dad and I both being depressed over Mom dying in a car accident a few years ago, I haven’t had a lot of friendly physical contact.”

Vicky made it into the house and threw her arms around Taylor. “Then we need to change that. You’re eminently huggable. Soft in all the right places.”

Taylor giggled a little. “Kinda wish I was a little ‘softer’ up top, I gotta admit.”

“Nah, your tits are perfect for your height,” Vicky said. "You’re probably a B-cup, and if you slid into C-cup, that’s probably the absolute biggest you should get, and I wouldn’t recommend that if you can avoid it, genetics being a bitch sometimes. Huge nipples from what I saw, but that’s not a detractor, honestly. I personally like your chest exactly the way it is.”

“Says the girl with the nearly D-cup breasts,” Amy snarked with a laugh.

“Yeah, but I’m shorter, and with my hips, smaller tits would be out of place.”

“Old cigarette commercial, back when they legally could put them on TV - ‘So round, so firm, so fully packed’,” Taylor said, laughing.

“Exactly!” Vicky said, bouncing on her heels after letting go of Taylor.

Taylor blushed. “You probably have figured it out, the way I’ve been acting, but I am bisexual. I like a really muscled guy as much as the next het girl, but gotta admit that you both are put together in a way that makes me want to get a third look. And yes, I said that correctly.” She shook her head. “Now let’s get away from talking about how sexy we all are and into other, less charged subjects.” After a second she added, “Just let me know when you’re coming over so that I can dress as to not offend you.”

“You run around naked a lot?” Vicky asked, honestly curious.

“Nude, and yeah. To be honest, up until I decided that I was healthy enough and knew enough about what happened to contact my dad, I walked around the Enterprise completely nude for two whole days. Wouldn’t think of doing that if I had a crew running around the ship, because I’m not a militant nudist. That’d be a decision for the crew to make.”

“First off, with your body, I suspect it would be a resounding ‘Please do!’ from the crew,” Vicky said with a giggle. “Second, you use nude instead of naked. What’s the diff?”

“Nude just means that you’re not wearing clothing. Naked involves embarrassment in some way. Ever have your parents yell at you deservedly for something, and wish you could be elsewhere? That’s naked. There’s shame involved with it. For most people, naked and nude are synonymous. For me, it’s a world of difference.”

“Learn something new every day,” Vicky said in amusement.

“Even if you don’t want to,” Amy snarked at her. She looked at Taylor. “That was aimed at Vicky, by the way. I was actually interested to learn the difference.”

“I was pretty sure that you were teasing your sister. So, before we sit down in the living room, want something to drink? We’ve got root beer, orange soda, Coke, Dr Pepper, and if you’re feeling adventurous, Brockton Bay tap water. Can make tea if anyone’s interested.” The three of them ended up with Dr Pepper and sat in the living room, Taylor in the recliner and the Dallons on the couch. “Anything other than just a desire to hang out bring you two here? Not complaining if you just want to hang out, mind you. It’ll be nice to try to develop friendships again.”

“Hanging out’s a big part of it,” Vicky said. “Admittedly there’s a bit of selfishness in it, because you have a big honkin’ starship, but I like you for you, not just because I can talk you into letting me look at Earth from space.”

“That is a great view, isn’t it?” She snickered. “When I beamed Dad and my honorary aunt and uncle up and showed them the view, Lacey quipped that she could see her house from up there.”

Amy bit her lower lip. “I’m actually … well, I’d like to sign up with you for the ship. I need to get out of the house, to be honest. Carol was interested in what you were talking about, but she’s very suspicious about everything. Definitely of the ‘there must be a dark secret hiding’ point of view, and she spent the last couple days checking your family out. Interestingly, part of the reason that she’s so distrusting is that you acknowledged that it was a normal thing these days”

“And found out about Mom’s previous connection to Lustrum, ignoring that it was before the crazy set in?”

“Yeah,” Vicky said sadly. “And she’s sure your dad must be a mobster or something dangerous because it’s known that he talked to Lustrum when she didn’t want to let your mother get out of the ‘movement’. She’s wondering what sort of threats he was able to hit her with.”

“That’s easy,” Taylor said with a laugh. “He told her that if she tried to keep Mom in the movement, first off she was doing to Mom what she was complaining men did all the time to women, AKA making their decisions for them, and second, that he didn’t want Mom’s hands dirtied. Mom would kill Lustrum but make it hurt for a long time. Dad would be kind and just kill her. Did your mother find out the history from my Dad’s side of the family, specifically the Sicilian connections and all that implies?” She snorted quite humorously. “Also, did she locate Mom’s lesbian porn career as well?”

“So that’s why that woman looks so much like you!” Amy blurted before starting to get up from the couch to run and hide.

Taylor was on her feet and caught Amy quickly, pulling her into a hug where Amy buried her face against Taylor chest. “So you’ve seen at least one of them. I’ve got copies of all nine of her movies.” She snorted. “Dad’s aware of her career as well. Brought extra cash into the house, and she only ever did lesbian work. She was worried that he’d consider it cheating on him, because she was doing it from about age eighteen, but he pointed out that it was a side of her that he literally wasn’t capable of satisfying, not being equipped that way. He just asked that she never did scenes with men. That was part of her contract with the studio.” A giggle escaped her. “Dad was involved with the contract negotiations, in fact. Very favorable terms for both sides. Studio tried to hire him away from the DWU just to handle contract negotiations.”

She looked down at Amy, who was still hiding her face. “Mom was fuckin’ hot, wasn’t she? No pun intended.” Amy just nodded.

“Daughter’s getting that way too,” Vicky said with a grin. “I called myself het the other day, but I’ll admit that I’ve seen the scene I know Amy’s thinking of, and well … from the way that redhead was acting, I can’t say as I’d have complained about being said redhead. I’m just mostly hetero.”

Taylor patted Amy on the back. “As much as I like holding a sexy girl in my arms, it’s kinda hard talking to you when your voice is muffled against my chest. I’ll wear a shirt with cleavage next time so you can at least motorboat my tiny tits. Sit back down and know that I don’t hate you or pity you or think you’re weird or anything, okay? We’ve probably both masturbated to the same scene.”

Amy jerked slightly and looked up at Taylor. “Really? Even though it was your mother?”

“Yeah. Probably makes me a huge pervert, but I can see why Mom’s videos were so popular. I referred to her as hot, remember? Society says it’s entirely wrong of me, but I can’t say as if I’d have complained being that redhead either. Wouldn’t have complained about being Mom, either. That redhead was sexy. But nothing ever happened with Mom and definitely never will, so where the harm in thinking it? Thinking isn’t the problem, it’s acting on it.”

She let go of Amy, who sat back down on the couch. “Now, I get the impression that your mother saying that about my folks wasn’t all?”

Amy growled. “I need to move out as soon as I can. She’s convinced herself that I don’t remember anything about how I got adopted. I remember all of it.” She turned to Vicky. “Sorry, Vicky, but I will likely never like the woman who was involved in breaking into my house, attacking my father, and then sending him to the Birdcage, only to ‘adopt’ his child, even if he was the one to insist on it.”

Vicky’s eyes were wide. “I never knew about that!”

“It wasn’t important for you. I was just there one day, and I was smart enough to realize that you weren’t any part of where I had my problems, so never took it out on you.”

Taylor sighed. “Let’s talk to Dad. I suspect that moving you to the ship would lead to problems, but you staying here in our guest room for a bit while we work this out? Loads better.” After a moment she said, “Since I heard the quotes around the word ‘adopt’, should I have Enterprise look for signs of something … perhaps a little shady?”

“Mom wouldn’t …” Vicky started to say, but stopped herself. “I was going to say that she wouldn’t do something illegal, but I’ve read about Marquis’ arrest. They sort of looked the other way on the fact that the Brigade committed the crime of breaking and entering to arrest him.” She paused, then said, “I can’t believe I’m saying this, but if Enterprise should definitely see if my law-and-order mother did something illegal.”

Enterprise appeared over the disc. “I have been checking since hearing this over the captain’s comm link to me, and there is strong evidence in just the short search I have done that Amelia’s adoption was illegal in nature. Shall I continue and search deeper?”

“If you please,” Amy said softly. “And thank you.”

“You are welcome, although no thanks are necessary.”

Chapter 11: Monday, January 10th, 2011 - Amy

Taylor had called her father, who had given a thumbs-up for Amy staying the night, and possibly for a few days, so Vicky had flown Amy home to pack up a few things, including things that meant something to her, in case Carol decided to explode and start breaking things, as she was wont to do when truly furious. They were gone again before Carol ever got home from work. “Sorry that you’re going to be the one to face her wrath when she realizes that we visited Taylor, and that I’m staying at least overnight here.”

“It needs to happen. Maybe I’ll get into a shouting match with her. It happens.”

Vicky would just be … icing on the cake, I think they say?” Enterprise leaned forward and actually pressed her lips to Taylor’s. “I would prefer to either do that on the ship, or with a proper holo emitter, so that I can properly enjoy kissing you.” With that, they turned to working on Taylor’s studying again.

When Amy and Vicky arrived at the house, Taylor and Enterprise were seated on the couch together studying some of Taylor’s history, since that was the one she was most worried about. “Jesus, it was bad enough with one nude hottie, but two?” Vicky mock-complained.

Both looked up and smiled. “Well, she’s teaching me about myself, if nothing else. I commented that it’s unfair that she’s as painfully sexy as she is, and she proceeded to point out that she looks like what I should when I’m twenty-five, so basically I’m getting horny looking at myself.”

“Makes sense,” Vicky said with a smile. “I’m rather enjoying the view right now, and stereo makes it even better.”

Taylor chuckled. “I’m thinking you might be a touch more bisexual than you think.”

“Or I finally met someone other than my adoptive sister who is hot enough to make me notice. Trust me girl, when you stripped to that workout outfit - and I so want one like the one Amy wore today! - and bent over, I was seriously enjoying the view. It took a bit to not rub my nipples, they went so hard so fast.”

Amy giggled. “You definitely fit for that comment some people make about ‘I hate to see you go, but I love to watch to leave’, Taylor.”

“You’ve got it too, Ames,” Vicky said. “Taylor’s is tight and curvy, but you have that upside-down heart shape to your ass, and there’s always a little bit of a swing to your hips because of it. Of course, with the way you were feeling today with the help of that sports bra, you actually strutted a few places. No bounce to the breasts, but I was getting questions about who your lover is.”

Taylor raised a hand. “When you’re ready, Amy, I’d like to apply for the position?” she said with a grin.

Amy opened her mouth to say something, then turned bright red. Vicky snickered. “I think I can hear the entire exchange that ran through you head just now. Something about having an opening, and one of us shooting back with an extremely sexual comment about your ‘opening?” she said, pointing below Amy’s waist. Amy giggled slightly and nodded.

“Well, as much as sitting or standing here talking about our individual openings that I think we’re all charged up to potentially explore, I’m going to turn the conversation over to needing to go to Arcadia in the morning, since they’ve scheduled my tests for the next three days."

“So maybe by next week you’ll be coming to school with us?” Amy asked happily.

“No maybe about it,” Enterprise said. “To be honest, the worst problem may be that she’s likely to test out of high school on what I have learned to be their core subjects.”

“They’ll keep her anyway,” Vicky said. “We’ve got a couple girls there who are actually taking college courses, but are attending Arcadia because of socialization issues with peers, since there end up being so many issues with someone significantly younger than their fellow college students. So Taylor will get noticed no matter what. Especially since she’ll be one of the taller girls at school.”

“So I’ll be looked at even at the new school,” Taylor said a little unhappily.

“Yeah, but this time they’ll be drooling and hiding hard-ons rather than finding ways to ridicule you,” Vicky told her.

Amy shook her head. “Blunt doesn’t begin to describe Vicky,” she said with a small laugh.

“Avoids a lot of misunderstandings, and embarrasses people who need to be embarrassed.” She shrugged, “Sometimes people who don’t need to be embarrassed, but them’s the breaks, as they say.”

Chapter 14: Wednesday, January 12th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the late posting - was driving from Thursday until mid-day Saturday, and used Sunday as a "Thank God I'm not driving anymore" day.

Taylor and Amy woke up the same way they had the day before, only with Amy’s hand taking the place of Taylor’s regarding more southerly spots, but this time Taylor decided that both were going to the Enterprise to shower, since it was a larger shower. A very happy Amy chose to forgo the same bra as yesterday - in fact, she decided that today she was going to forgo a bra entirely, if only because she was a little sensitive due to the shower antics. Enterprise convinced her to wear a silk blouse, pointing out that this silk was capable of stopping a Barret round of the .50 caliber variety at its most lethal range. She’d end up bruised, of course, but had stated that she suspected that Taylor would have no issue kissing the bruise to make it feel better, and that she’d offer her own kisses if Amy so desired.

“We’re both falling rather deeply in love with you, Amy,” Taylor admitted. “Enterprise knows me better than I know myself, and is in love with me despite that.”

“Stop that,” Amy admonished.

“But we’re both utterly smitten with you, and … well, you seem to return the feelings.”

Amy nodded. “Honestly, my subconscious has decided that you are trustworthy. I’ve been in a position to wake up with other girls where the same thing might have happened that did with you, and Vicky’s the only other one I do that with. Not even my cousin Crystal, and trust me, if it was purely physical, I’d definitely do that to her. She’s got better tits than Vicky does, and even Vicky admits that. But I’ve only ever latched onto Vicky and you. That tells me my subconscious has put together everything it needs to know about you, and your waking reactions show me that you’re what I think you are.” She turned to Enterprise’s hologram. “And your personality is so much like Taylor’s and for good reason, from what you guys said. So why wouldn’t I fall for you as well?” She leaned forward and kissed Enterprise’s lips, and Taylor was standing there bouncing on the balls of her feet in happiness.

Taylor stopped a moment later and reached up to cup her breasts. “I may need you to dial back the sensitivity, Amy. As nice as it is, between the heightened sensitivity and the fact that you gifted me with both of those silly ideas I had, well, I’m likely to orgasm my way through the tests today if I stay this sensitive.”

“Need the force dialed back on the pulsing? Or maybe put your areolae back to their original shape?”

“Nah, I kinda like them being heart shaped now that you made my pulse visible in them, and it’s not like the pulsing is so strong that it will immediately draw attention to my nipples the second I walk into a room. You’ve got to look for it, and someone I don’t want looking is likely to end up with a black eye first. I’ll enjoy that, but with me being as overall sensitive as you set me to, I’ll end up enjoying it too much.” She cocked her head. “Need to figure out if we can come up with something for you to wear that will let you bounce your power back on yourself to allow self-healing.”

“That would be nice. I’d even wear it as a thick breast piece if it let me do that.” Amy smiled at the thought.

“We’ll have to do experimentation,” Enterprise said “but I suspect we might be able to shrink it down much smaller than that. Possibly even an implant of some sort. I suspect when we start looking into the augmentation that is in the historical archives will be the best time.”

“Yeah,” Taylor said. “I was realizing that doing some sort of carbon fiber mesh for armor would be interesting, and unless I’m mistaken, there are organic things that can be done to the muscles and nerves that don’t require constant fiddling with, that will increase both speed and strength.”

“I was reading that too,” Amy said. “It felt like my power was getting excited by the possibility of doing something like that. As it is, doing the changes I made to you last night helped calm down a … well, the best description of it is a power-related itch that I was feeling.”

“I haven’t had that sort of itchy feeling, but I’ve only had my powers a week now, and I’m pretty much in constant contact with Sexy here, so I don’t know if that itch will ever happen to me, but I can’t say as the concept surprises me. Kinda explains some of the weird shit some capes do after you haven’t seem them for a while.” She paused, then snickered. “If you do carbon fiber for armor subcutaneously, would the mesh have enough give, or would you either have to settle for permanently hard nipples or no armor at all on them?”

Amy gave her a half-lidded look and said, “If I’m hanging around you, my nipples would never have a chance to go soft, so who’d know?” She then giggled. “Sorry, can’t hold the sultry look for too long. The mesh would by nature have to have some give in it, so I think that no one would ever be aware of it until they tried to do something that would affect the armor mesh. I’ll think on that and the compounds for nerves and muscles during the day today while you’re in the tests. What are you doing for lunch?”

“They told me I’d be provided lunch, so I suspect that they’ll supply it rather than have me join everyone else in the cafeteria.” She motioned toward the door. “Shall we go back down to the planet - and god do I love being able to say that seriously! - and join Dad for breakfast?”

Amy linked arms with her and was amused when Enterprise linked with her other arm as they headed to the transporter room. None of the three of them would admit to being the one who started skipping.

Down at the Hebert household, Danny was smiling at the two girls who were still laughing as they materialized in the living room. “Good night for you guys?” His smile was teasing in nature, which told Taylor that he’d heard them.

“Yeah,” Taylor said, blushing a little. “Sorry if we were a little … noisy … this morning. I know how thin the walls can be in the house.” Amy’s eyes went extremely wide and she turned a red that neither of them had seen from the girl before. “Yes, he likely heard us. Serves him right, given the number of times I heard Mom call him some … interesting things. Helped wake up my sex drive, though. If I ever take a guy as a lover, I hope he’s got half the stamina Dad seemed to have.” She looked to her father, who was blushing slightly, but tipped the spatula to her as a salute that she’d turned his teasing around.

Eggs, bacon, and toast were all delivered to plates, as were glasses of orange juice. Pleasant breakfast noises were made as they ate, and Amy insisted on helping with clean up. “Give you both a ride to the school today?” he asked them when they were done. “And thank you, Amy.”

“I’d appreciate it, Dad,” Taylor said. “Enterprise thinks she’s got it worked out to get me the first chunk of money by the end of the week or the beginning of next week, at which point we can start working on some of the other stuff. Plus, we’ve come to the realization that I’ll need a cape identity, just because it ends up giving me some protection in a legal sense. So if you can ask around for serious ideas - I know some of the smart-asses working there, remember - I’d appreciate it. Enterprise is taken by my sexy ship herself, so that’s out, and it strikes me as asking for trouble for something like Roddenberry, if only because his estate might try to jump up and down on my spleen. Might let his son come on board to look at the place, though, but that’s in the future. But to avoid Taylor Hebert getting various lawsuits for doing stuff, I need to have a name like Captain Starfleet or something.”

“Just Starfleet could work,” Amy said, “although you might want to check with Paramount.”

Enterprise spoke in her ear. “Actually, using my name would be a valid possibility. I would be flattered, rather than confused, and is somewhat less likely to lead to legal battles than ‘Starfleet’ would.”

“Another precinct heard from. My sexy ship says she would be flattered if I took her name as my cape name, so I think that I am provisionally ‘Enterprise’ now.”

“Kinda fits,” Amy said. “She admits that her body is based off your genetics and is what you will likely look like at twenty-five. She’s you and you can be her.”

“I like it,” Danny said. “By the by, can I get one of those old style original series communicators for when I feel like talking to my other daughter and don’t have a holoprojector nearby? I always loved the looks of those things.”

“How many of you want one?” asked Enterprise of Taylor. “I’m fairly certain that you’ll want one for the same reason, even though we speak this way often.” Taylor asked the question, and soon three old style flip communicators appeared on the kitchen table.

“I’ll leave mine home, because they’ll assume that it’s a cell phone otherwise. Since they’re supplying everything I’ll need, I’m just bringing me.” Her father picked one up, as did Amy, and they headed out the door.

They talked on the way there, and decided on something. When they reached the school and met up with Vicky, as they split to go to their respective destinations, Taylor leaned in and gave Amy a quick kiss on the lips, which Amy clearly returned. Vicky looked as if she was fighting an ear-splitting “Squee!”

Taylor was led off to the testing area, with a very gentle admonishment that public displays of affection stronger than what had been seen in the hallway were frowned upon. She told them “That was astonishingly out of place for me. But I understand what you’re telling me.”

She was led to a classroom that she could tell was well shielded, because Enterprise told her so, and she could actually feel a little of the field that was preventing external contact. Well, for people other than her, that was. She was led to a desk that had what she knew was a top of the line machine. “You’ll be doing all of your testing on this machine, even the occasional essay we ask of you. We have paper here for you if you want to do scratch work for math or English problems before inputting them into the computer. Some of the things we’ll test will end up being safety procedures for our shop classes, which you will likely be required to take at least one of. Practicals in those, of course, will happen in those classrooms if you are accepted here. Plus, if you are accepted, there will be vocational studies, often including some sort of internship with various organizations.” The woman gave her a significant look, which told Taylor that she was in the know regarding the PRT’s efforts to get her into Arcadia.

With that, they began the testing, starting with mathematics. As she took the test, she realized that the programming was very well done. As they asked various questions, it probed her knowledge and made the questions increasingly more difficult. She was quite aware that she was already at a college level, even with Winslow’s poor teaching. She finished that test and was able to head directly into the next subject. She was surprised with the fact that by the time lunch came around, she had completed the tests for eight different subjects.

After lunch, she picked up again and made it through only five this time, because all three had required some level of essay writing to explain various aspects of the course being tested, the most obvious of these being English. She suspected that she might get a poor grade on the English essay regarding Shakespeare, because she remembered quite a few of her mother’s conversations with people regarding the man and his works. She had been solidly in the camp that it was the height of intellectual snobbery to state that they could not have been written by the man himself simply because his profession was a low class one in their minds. Taylor’s essay was actually on the astonishing amount of sexual humor that ran through all of his plays, and the reasoning for said humor.

When she was done for the day, she was told, “You probably won’t have to come in on Friday, to be honest. You’ve already made it through more tests than we expected. I can already tell that you’re college level in at least math.” The woman snorted. “And I took a look at your English essay, then really looked at your last name. Your mother was the professor of English Literature at BBU, wasn’t she?”

“Was it that obvious?” Taylor asked with a laugh.

“I used to hang out with her when she needed to decompress sometimes. You had her turn of phrase in several spots in your essay. I have rarely seen someone so elegantly state that Shakespeare loved dick jokes and such in his works. The last time was listening to Annette expound on it. And your reasoning as to why they were there? Pure Annette, and that’s a compliment.”

“Thank you. That means a lot to me. I guess I’ll see you tomorrow?”

“Yes. And thank you, by the way, for not bringing a backpack or any technology. We would have had to have kept them from you until the end of the day anyway.”

“Which is exactly why I left them home. At most, I might bring a mindless paperback book tomorrow for lunch, but leave it with you up front so that you know I didn’t try to sneak any potential notes or anything in.” The woman laugh and chased her from the room with a smile.

When she got out front, Vicky and Amy were waiting for her, and since they were outside the building and no longer during the school day, the kiss lingered a bit longer. Taylor heard more than a few girls voicing variations on “Awww” in an admiring and happy tone.

“They’re happy Amy’s found someone,” Vicky said. “And your picture is going to be all over PHO, if it isn’t already, just because of that kiss.”

“I get to kiss an amazing girl,” Taylor said. “I’m sure not going to complain if people see that I’m lucky enough to have her willing to allow it.” She paused. “Did that sentence make sense?”

“Did to me,” Amy said, “and that’s the important part.” She frowned. “Gonna have a conversation with Carol later on, to see if I return to the house, or if I find somewhere else to stay,” she said softly.

“Well, if you can’t live there, and she makes threats about being with me, remember that you have access to a big honkin’ starship up there,” Taylor said quietly. “You saw where my cabin is. Grab the one next to it or something, just in case you decide you want a place to go to be alone sometimes. I’m not going to complain if most nights I happen to have someone with me in my cabin, though.” She smiled. “I think that’s been clear the last couple nights, y’know?”

Chapter 15: Thursday, January 13th, 2011 - Taylor

Taylor woke up, this time with her arms around Enterprise, aboard the ship. She’d found that she couldn’t sleep without someone else in the bed now, which surprised her, because everything she’d heard said that it took much longer to get used to that sort of thing. She’d been lonely, so she left a note for her father on the door, saying that she was sleeping on board Enterprise and that she’d be back on Earth in plenty of time to get to Arcadia.

“Is it normal to fall in love that fast?” she asked Enterprise.

“I can’t honestly say, never having been human before, or even biological ever. But I have come across many a reference to not only things such as ‘love as first sight’, which honestly sounds a bit more like lust to me, but also stories from people who knew the person that they were going to marry after having only been around them for a very short period of time, so such apparently can happen. Are you worried about how you feel regarding Amy?”

“And you, honestly. I mean, Everything I know tells me that I shouldn’t have gotten so used to sleeping with her so fast, but I was lonely last night because she wasn’t there.” She paused. “And can I get a bed in here that can accommodate the three of us at times, if she moves in with me? Because I’ll be damned if it ends up an either or situation, and she certainly seems to feel something for you.”

“Quite likely because I am very much you in many ways, Taylor,” Enterprise said with a gentle kiss on Taylor’s lips.

Enterprise then sat up. “I am ready to begin some things with your permission. I have things set up to direct that rather large sum of money your way via the invented relative, and I have decided that it would be an excellent idea to begin a company or two that could conceivably need an intern or two. The companies will appear to have been around for some time, but are going to be opening sites in Brockton Bay. A great deal of the rest of the literal trillions will find its way to Brockton Bay in various ways, either to you or the various companies and agencies I will be creating with your permission.”

Taylor looked at her. “Enterprise, you have my permission to use your best judgment unless it comes up against a hard-coded requirement that you ask me. You are so much like me because of the connection, you pretty much know what my decision will be. So you have my permission to make decisions for things like that. After all, you may run into situations where you have to act quickly, but I’m in Arcadia and hiding the fact that my communicator can punch right through their measures.” She took Enterprise’s face in her hands and kissed her. “I trust you.”

“Then I shall begin immediately.” Enterprise then got A Look in her eyes. “I believe that we have time for a shower before you need to beam down to head to Arcadia.”

“I notice that you didn’t say that it will be a quick shower,” Taylor purred at her.

It was a very satisfied Taylor who beamed into her house, and it took everything she had to not strut, her mood was so good. Her father just smirked and said, “Enterprise obviously took good care of you overnight.”

Taylor looked down at the smirk and realized that her pulse was somewhat visible from the work that Amy had done on her. “So I’ll wear a blazer, like Mom did on the days she chose to forgo a bra.” She smiled and said, “I don’t know whether it will start this Saturday, or maybe Sunday, or some time next week, but Amy, Enterprise, and I are going to work on some of the potential augmentations that are illegal in the Federation, but are dead useful here.” She smiled at him. “Might work on some of the anti-aging stuff too, I like the idea of keeping you around a long time, y’know? The real Leonard McCoy lived to at least 137 years old, and I suspect he lived a good few years past when he visited the Enterprise D before its first mission. Oh, by the way and having nothing to do with what I was just talking about, are there any lawyers you can recommend for working with Enterprise on getting things set up? She’s likely to start buying up properties around the area and rebuilding them as a way of bringing money in, and also … well, Arcadia does a vocational track for the latter half of the day, which everyone suspects is an excuse for the Wards that everyone knows go there but officially have no idea who they are to be able to ‘intern’ with the PRT. She wants to set up the possibility of me interning with one of the new companies.”

“I’ll talk to Bian Doan,” he said, pronouncing the name as ‘bee-ahn doh-ahn’. “She needs something to sink her teeth into.”

“Other than you? I’ve seen the way she looks at you, Dad. And it’s okay to look back, if you want to. I remember how she used to visit, Dad. I’m not going to complain if she maybe starts to visit again. I understand completely if Mom was the only one for you, ever. But I’m saying that if you think Mom wouldn’t complain; if you have room in your heart for someone else, I’m not going to get all pissy and childish if you start looking. Nor will I insist that you start looking if it was ‘Mom and no one else’. I just want you to know that I love you and I won’t complain if I maybe hear you talking about someone, okay?” She sat down, and the two of them had cereal that morning before heading off.

When he dropped her at the school, she said, “I get the impression that I’m doing these faster than they expected, and might be done today. If I get out too early, I’ll likely find an area to sneak off to and beam up to Enterprise and work on some things. But I’ll contact you by communicator if I do, okay?” He nodded and drove off to work.

She was greeted by a somber Vicky and slightly annoyed Amy. “Mom trouble,” Vicky said. “Especially after we brought Aunt Sarah into it. Aunt Sarah is usually the voice of reason when Mom gets this way, and that usually gets Mom pissed for a few days that her sister had a good point. But this is going to blow up again, I’m sure.”

Amy growled. “Especially if I point out something that no one in the family wants to hear, and I am not saying it out here, Vicky.” She looked to Taylor. “Sorry for the attitude.”

“I understand anger,” Taylor replied, then pulled Amy in and kissed her quickly. “Try not to let it get to you too much. Now as much as I’d love to be able to stand here and kiss you all day, I need to get to my testing.” She gave Amy another quick peck on the lips and headed off.

It was another day of her blazing through the tests, and she was done with her final test just after lunch. “Well, I expect I’ll be seeing you around the school once these results get tabulated,” The teacher said. “You did amazingly well on all of them, from what I can see. College level on some of them, and from what I could see in mathematics, you could probably go for a PhD if you had the credits.” Taylor just blushed. “Now get out of here and enjoy the rest of your day.”

Once outside the school building, she sub-vocalized to Enterprise about letting Amy and Vicky know that she was out of school and heading up to the ship. They were more than welcome to join her once they were done with their school day. That said, she found a spot with no cameras and beamed up to the ship.

After getting to her cabin and stripping to her skin, she headed to the bridge. “So how goes the various plans?”

“I expect that you will be visited by a lawyer by Friday of next week at the latest in order to deliver the ‘trust fund’ I set up for you. The companies are created and a very large sum of money has been transferred from the ill-gotten gains of others into those three companies. I have developed a technology company, an energy company, and because it seems to be something that could be useful in this world, a materials science company which also includes textiles and designs.”

“So we’ll have a place for me to intern and a place for Vicky to intern. We’ll figure out for Amy, I guess. How goes it on getting property purchased and prepared?”

“I’ve been working on buying up a large amount of vacant and effectively useless property in the area of the Docks, and have been in talks with your father about perhaps hiring some of the dockworkers to help with demolition and fencing and such. I expect the first set of sales to complete tomorrow, which means that I will be able to get your father involved with getting the dockworkers some actual, viable work, and possibly a need for hiring more people, which is never a bad thing according to the sources I have read. I expect to be able to turn the area into a corporate center within a year while ensuring that there is plenty of space for the docks to continue that sort of work. I have verified that while the city officially owns the derelict ships in the bay, they can be claimed as salvage by anyone with the means to actually effect a removal. I believe that we shall make a splash - no pun intended - in the local news once you are public by removing the container ship, which should not have been within the area in the first place, given the comparison between the size of the bay and the size of the ship. Being able to use it for raw materials would save money for other things as well.”

“Since I intend to be an independent hero, I can out myself by doing just such a thing. I know that you can’t land, but how low into the atmosphere can you come before problems arise?”

“I assume you intend to ‘go big or go home’, as they say, and show people that I exist in a manner that they will have trouble denying?” When Taylor nodded, Enterprise said, “I am not capable of landfall, but the structural integrity fields will have no issues with holding me together so that I can be low enough to be easily seen from the ground. Local fliers would be able to rise up and touch my hull, in fact.”

Taylor snickered. “I can just see Vicky flying up and doing the equivalent of giving you a hug. Hell, I could see people thinking that she was going to attack, and then seeing her make it clear that she knows you?”

Enterprise gave her own snicker. “I suspect that you will be inundated with requests to meet the crew, and when it is discovered that you currently are the only crew, have people asking how to join up. And yes, I have plans for a local Starfleet Academy, although I am working on a new name as to avoid trademark issues with Paramount.”

“I suspect that it would be in their best interests to try to get on board with it, but they’d push for control over curriculum and such, and we can’t have that. And a number of things have to be dealt with in the curriculum, because there are Federation-specific things that simply will not be the case here, such as the issue with computer intelligences and physical augmentation. For that matter, is it a technological problem, or an ethical issue that keeps Starfleet from using the transporter to … well, bring someone who died of something traumatic back from death? Because there aren’t many people I know who would complain if there was a way of bringing them back if a rock crushed their head on an away mission. I mean yeah, I’m thinking of Mom, but going back in time to beam her up long enough to leave a dead body behind or something? That way lies madness, and is far too goddamn selfish of me, even if I really want her back.” Taylor felt her eyes burning with unshed tears. “So I understand if there’s an ethical problem.”

“There is an ethical consideration in the Federation that governs it, partially led by the simple fact that it is so easy to survive things that were once fatal. Lifespans in this era are slightly less than 80 years, whereas the fact that Leonard McCoy lived to nearly 150 years old was not beyond the pale. Admittedly slightly unusual, but it was not seen as newsworthy that a human being lived to be 147 years old, much as the way that people living to be greater than 100 years old in this era is now more of a human interest story rather than an international news story.” Enterprise paused. “Ethics was what drove most of it for the biologicals, but technology is another factor. I could not store every single person aboard the ship had I a full compliment of crew members. For an away mission, I can store those individuals and their engrams at time of beam down. If they take a shuttle, they are out of luck, as the saying goes. They obviously would lose the memory of what happened to them on the planet, of course.”

“So I have a technological reason as to why to refuse to help people survive the unsurvivable,” Taylor said. “Thank you. I can see far too many people wanting to be ‘backed up’ in order to live a long time. I’ve even seen fan written fiction where someone did regular back-ups of their mental engrams and just transported themselves into a younger body when they got too old, in their opinion. That way lies megalomania, at least.”

Enterprise was actually biting her holographic lower lip. “Should I erase the engrams I have of you, C … Taylor?” she asked softly. “I have been doing a fairly constant updating of the engrams I have for you. It was painful to lose my last crew, and with how tightly tied to you I am now, I … I do not know if I would survive as an intelligence were I to lose you permanently. I have actually been thinking of the exact scenario you just described in order to keep you around, only without the megalomania involved.”

Taylor smiled at her and shook her head. “Keep them. Hopefully it’s a long time before we have to revisit the concept, y’know?” She paused for a moment before asking, “How many people can you safely do that for? Just me?”

“If you authorize usage of various materials to increase storage capabilities without loss of computing ability, I could manage a significant number of people. As it currently stands, you are the greatest ‘pull’ on resources, what with your intimate connection to me, so with no discernible degradation of capabilities, I could store the engrams of five more people of your choosing before I would need greater capabilities.”

“Interesting conversation to walk in on,” Amy said. “And I definitely prefer this uniform for you, Captain,” she added with a saucy wink.

“Damned nice one,” Vicky said. “Mind if we join you in the uniform choice?”

“I’m not Jim Kirk, but I sure as hell am not going to complain if you do,” Taylor said. “And I’m surprised that you’re willing to be nude around me.”

“Well, between my being a bit of an exhibitionist - I mean, look at my costume and one of my powers; they scream ‘Look at me!’ - and knowing that Enterprise decides who comes up here at the moment, it’s a safe place for me to run around like this. And it is freeing.”

Taylor giggled. “Plus, from my point of view, it’s a damned nice view as well.” As the girls clothes were removed, Enterprise beamed them into the quarters that they’d talked about. Taylor knew that the slight smirk on Enterprise’s face meant that Amy’s clothes were in her quarters and not the one that Amy had chosen as her private space when she needed it.

“Thank you,” Vicky said. “So what led to the interesting conversation about bringing people back from the dead?”

“It started from business opportunities, and slid into starting an academy to teach people how to work this ship, and I got asking about a handful of things from her original universe. Using the transporter to bring someone back after a traumatic death was part of it. I’m kinda glad it’s difficult, because I truly understand so many of the ramifications of it. God knows I want to jump back to the day my mother died and pull a bit straight out of Heinlein saving Lazarus Long’s mom, but where does it stop? Do I go back and save your Aunt Jess? Who next? Do I get politicians demanding that X person or Y person must be brought back? Do I go back and save the vice-president’s wife and daughter from the accident that killed them, and save the son from the tumor that’s going to end up killing him? Where does it stop? So as much as it hurts, I can’t allow myself to save my mother, because the can of worms that opens will tear the world apart. People would demand control of Enterprise just to bring people back. But we got talking about saving the people who have patterns in the buffer. She pointed out that she was willing to save me and bring me back.” She turned to Enterprise. “I think we’re going to have to talk, the group of us, because I love you, Enterprise, but I think I’m in love with Amy as well. Right now it’s a decent amount of lust and deep friendship for Vicky. Given how I grew up, Dad had no problem with Mom having relationships with other women, and … well, I know that there were times when Clarisse would visit, as would Bian, and it would get very crowded in their bed. Dad was … I guess the way to say it somewhat clinically is to say that he was penetratively monogamous with Mom, but I know damned well that neither Bian or Clarisse had issues with his finger or tongue regimens, shall we say?” She blushed. “Mom was very open about sex with me, I can tell you.”

Vicky laughed. “So that was a really long-winded way of saying that you’d like a bed all four of us could sleep in - and other things - comfortably?” Amy giggled at that.

“She said you were blunt, and yes. Amy and I have started exploring, and I admit that Enterprise … well, I’m not sure if I still qualify as a virgin in some senses, but I’m not complaining about anything a hologram can do with their body. I have fantasized about seeing you exactly as you are right now at the very minimum, and some of those fantasies went further. But that’s on you with zero obligations to do anything. Just want you to understand why you might see my pulse being a little fast when you’re undressed.”

She shook her head. “We always talk about sex when we’re together. Damn. Anyway, Enterprise was telling me about some of the stuff she’s dealing with. Got some serious money coming in through … means. Not necessarily legal, but the people it came from aren’t exactly going to be beating down the doors of the police to get it back, if you get that meaning. We’re using that for buying up properties and setting up businesses. Vicky, once it’s set up, you might get asked if you want to intern with a textile company as a potential designer using cutting edge fabrics.”

“Like those sports bras that can stop bullets?”

“It’s the silk blouse that can stop bullets,” Amy said with a laugh. “I suspect that the sports bra would stop a tank shell.”

“It’s still shove you back like crazy,” Taylor said with a laugh, “but yeah, actually. But the companies now exist, and hiring will start soon, and a lot of shit is going to happen. I’m pretty much going to out myself as Enterprise by lifting the container ship from the bay. As we pull the other ships from the bay, we’ll beam people off and work from there. If there are any out there that can be fixed with minimal work, we’ll probably save them. There’s at least one yacht that looks like it’s been stripped of stuff inside, but still has a decent enough shell to fix and update with Federation level technology.”

“Make it space capable,” Vicky said. “Have a yacht you can fly to the Moon!”

Amy laughed at that. “Can you imagine the looks on faces if a yacht lifts out of the water and starts flying toward space?”

Chapter 16: Saturday, January 15th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Summary

Time to do some testing at the PRT.

Taylor was at the PRT testing site on Saturday at 9 am and was whisked quickly into testing. The first tests were easy, proving that she had a Brute: NO rating. They quickly determined that she personally had ratings in only Thinker, Tinker, and Master, with her Mastery having to do only with the technology gained from the ‘minion’ she had - the Enterprise. This was tested by having her try to control a large number of devices, with the only one she was capable of affecting being the PADD that she had given to Armsmaster with the schematics. Thinker was the only one they could come up with a decent rating on, given that she was clearly working at post-graduate level work in a number of various fields, which gave her a rating of Thinker 6 at an absolute minimum. Given the level of technology she had available, and what she could understand how to build by herself, she was likely a minimum of Tinker 4, with an argument made for 6 as the likely setting. Master was a different thing. Her Mastery dealt only with the Federation technology, but that control was absolute, and given that she could order the ship to open fire on any point on Earth from orbit, they were pretty much forced to classify her as Master 12+, with a very tight focus for said Mastery.

As for other classifications, those came about from what it was that she had Mastery over. The Enterprise gave her Blaster, Mover, and Shaker ratings of 12+ as well, but those were specific to the ‘minion’ and not Taylor, or as she was going by currently, Grey Ghost.

“I choose to go by that name at the moment because I want to honor where the name Enterprise came from originally. And I want my ship thought of as a minion rather than as a holographic intelligence right now because people tend to think of things like HAL, or Skynet, or Colossus: the Forbin Project when they think of non-biological intelligences,” Taylor said. “They don’t think of the admitted rare example like Minerva from Heinlein’s Time Enough for Love or her later sister Athena. They don’t think of Solace from Spider Robinson’s Callahan’s books, although I think Solace was from after they rebuilt the place as Mary’s Place. Hell, they don’t even think of Data from the Next Generation series! Those are benevolent non-biologicals, who actually tried to help humanity when they could. Admittedly Minerva was an example of Heinlein’s philosophy, so if someone placed themselves outside societal norms in anti-social ways, they didn’t deserve help from Minerva, but I tend to think the same way. If it was up to me, Sophia Hess would end up with a photon torpedo suppository, which is why I’m glad it’s not up to me.”

She shook her head. “Sorry. I should check on what’s going on with Winslow, but given the past, I suspect it would just infuriate me with the tendency toward slaps on the wrist for all the people involved. ‘For punishment, Sophia, you don’t get chocolate pudding tonight for dessert. Emma, you have to go to bed at 8:59 pm instead of 9, so that’s your punishment. Madison, you have to use dollar store make-up today.’ They won’t be paying for any of what they did. Blackwell will cover for them.”

Taylor waved a hand in the air as if wiping all that away. “That’s neither here nor there, and nothing you can deal with, so no reason to bitch to you about it. Sorry.”

Armsmaster paused for a moment before saying, “It is understandable that you feel that way, given how long the … harassment … was going on. I will check into what has been happening in regard to Winslow and tell you later on what I am permitted by law.”

“Thank you,” she said. “I didn’t mean to make that sound like I was hinting at anything, sir. And I understand that legal reasonings may prevent any information being passed along.”

“I am aware, but as you pointed out, you realized that at least one of the four has a connection to the PRT, even though none of us are stating what that connection may be.” When she met his eyes - or where she suspected they were in regard to his helmet - he nodded significantly. She nodded back and motioned that her lips were sealed regarding his breach of the Unwritten Rules, although it was unprovable.

He finally told her, “You have my preliminary thoughts on what your ratings will be, and those may be altered as we further examine the results. I have a question for you regarding potential patrolling - will you be using a phaser?”

“Yes I will, and as normal for Federation phasers, the base setting is set for stunning someone. An extra precaution will be that I will have my devices that I carry with me locked to my signature. If I am disarmed, the phaser will not work for anyone else, nor will any tricorder, PADD, or similar devices. If they get so far as to relieve me of my best communicator, we have other problems, because it means that they’re performing unscheduled surgery of some sort on me, which is likely to unleash the ship’s attempts to retrieve me. Since she has a copy of my engrams,” she said, tapping her head, “she knows how I think, and I have already granted her permission to do what she believes that I would desire in order to retrieve me. She already knows that I would prefer minimal problems for people in any recovery efforts, which means no melting downtown just to get me back.” She said with a laugh.

“That said, I would like to schedule a point when I might be able to allow some people aboard to start looking at things such as our medical technology, and how to alter it to current technology levels. I would like to find a method, for example, of healing Director Piggot, and I am aware that she has issues with parahuman healing. I might disagree with her reasons, but my right to my opinion stops at the point it affects her body. But if I can find something that she can agree to, I would gladly heal her.”

“I will make her aware of that, and I will also vet those that might be chosen for such information. A different idea has come to mind, admittedly from Dragon. The television series had replicators, which could generate foodstuff and other things from apparently nothing. Will you be installing any of those in Brockton Bay?”

She laughed. “Not until human nature changes. Even if I charged money for the replicators to make things based upon a person’s wealth level - and tell me that figuring that out wouldn’t be a massive invasion of personal privacy - I won’t for one very simple reason. Tell me that Uber and L33t wouldn’t decide to see if they could take the power supply out of one of those things. Or Squealer, in order to power one of her monstrosities.”

“I can’t. That is something they would likely do.” He was frowning as he said that. The frown almost deserved to be capitalized in its description.

“Now, on what sounds like a tangent, let’s assume that a Fugly Bob’s Challenger is one kilogram, fixings and all. Probably less, might be more, but one kilogram works best for seat-of-the-pants calculations. Also going to work with three hundred million meters per second for the speed of light.” She paused. “Yeah. A replicator is doing direct energy to matter transformation, with a small amount of loss due to the fact that there is no purely perfect transformation - there’s always some loss. You can see where this is going. Doing the calculations and conversions, one Fugly Bob’s Challenger takes the equivalent of some European Union countries’ yearly output in kilowatt-hours to create from ‘nothing’. A replicator is designed to be able to make thousands upon thousands of them, if done in a portable replicator device. That kind of energy release in a city? Not doing the calculations to figure how much damage, but I can honestly say that Maine, New Hampshire, and coastal Massachusetts at the absolute least would cease to exist. It is honestly conceivable that if released, it could crack the crust and let the mantle release pressure somewhat explosively. So yeah, no replicators for public use until it becomes public knowledge and ingrained in the public subconscious that those things have too much power to trust that some Tinker isn’t going to try to steal one and break containment.”

“Forgive me if I find that level of power anywhere near Earth to be somewhat frightening,” he admitted.

“I understand it completely. It’s why the engineering of Starfleet ships have multiple backups for the backup systems that back up the backup systems. And I’m not joking. The level of failure required for a starship to become a danger to a planet requires either damage that I don’t think anyone or anything on this Earth could do, or active sabotage to a degree that would require that the entire crew be terrorists. Very dangerous stuff, but very carefully watched for and prepared for. That’s why I’m I’m setting up an Academy for those who might want to serve on board a ship like mine. It’s going to be years before I accept more than the absolute minimum of people for my ship, and the first ones are going to be people I know and trust and care for. If I could drag him away from the Docks and the fun he’s going to be having over the next few years as things come back, I’d make my father my First Officer. It will have to be someone I trust and who has no issue telling me I’m being an idiot if need be. Preferably in the Ready Room, away from other crew, but still.”

“But I will say that I want to see what might be necessary to get small shuttlecraft style air vehicles available for sale. Not sure I want to get them in public a la flying cars, because people are idiots on the roads - what happened to my mother proves that - and I can’t imagine them stopping being idiots in the air, but for purchase for groups like fire departments, police departments, the PRT? Specialized for each group? Dockworker craft with tractor beams to make moving huge things easier? We’ll be working on tech to make lives a little easier while trying to avoid too much uplift too fast. We’ve got a faster than light vehicle in orbit at the moment, but we’re not a warp-capable society. I want to get us there without having the problem of blowing ourselves up because we want to be the only ones with the hyper-tech. That road is way too damned wide and too damned easy to travel.”

“It is fraught,” he said. “But I said it last week and reiterate it now. From what you have said, I believe that you will do your utmost to travel this difficult road, and I believe you will succeed.”

“Thank you. I not only have that responsibility, but the responsibility to not tarnish the name of Enterprise for generations to come. I dare not fail.”

“I don’t believe that you will, Captain Hebert. Grey Ghost.” He cocked his head. “Which would you prefer I call you?”

“I’m not sure. It’s an awesome and terrifying responsibility to be Captain Hebert, but equally as awesome and terrifying to call myself by any name that stands for the Enterprise. Really, I’m calling myself Grey Ghost as legal protection, the way Brandish and Carol Dallon are legally separate individuals.”

“Very well. I shall endeavor to refer to you as Grey Ghost when dealing with you as a parahuman, but by your proper title when it does not involve legal requirements.”

“I didn’t exactly earn the rank, you know.”

“Perhaps, but you are accepting the responsibility and as such, should be treated with the respect due the position.”

She smiled at him even as his words made her stand straighter in pride. “Thank you. I need that reminder occasionally.”

“Understandable. You only came into your power on the 4th of this month.”

She nodded. “May I beam up from here, as in the building, or would you prefer I leave and beam up that way?”

“It depends. I would not have an issue with you leaving from within the building, but you need to decide how public you plan to be. If you have things well in hand as far as protection of yourself and your father, perhaps exiting the building and beaming up in the view of the public?”’

She thought for a moment. “I need to set up a shield generator for the house first. Then I’ll … well, just to let you know, she and I -” Taylor point up to indicate her ship, “- are working with the city to claim everything in the Ship’s Graveyard as salvage. We’re going to be very obvious about it. I suspect that we’ll try to set it up for the soonest weekend after we get all our ducks in a row, as they say. At that point, I’ll be blatant that Captain Taylor Hebert is the hero Grey Ghost. And before you ask, I’ll keep you apprised of when the event will happen. There will be no mistaking that I have a ship available to me.”

“Thank you. And thank you again for coming in for testing today, Captain.” She gave a small respectful bow to the man and tapped her comm badge. “Beam me up, Enterprise.” Her last view of Armsmaster showed something of a look of wonder on the man’s face.

Chapter 17: Saturday, January 15th, 2011 - Vicky

Vicky was floating in one of the conference rooms, dressed the way that Taylor found most comfortable. She was discovering that it was freeing as well, and didn’t have to have a sexual component to being nude. She was thinking about what she’d learned from the tests she’d taken this morning, and some of the other things that she’d learned in the process as Enterprise had scanned her.

“Vicky? Taylor has beamed up. If you desire to be alone, I will let her know,” Enterprise told her.

“Nah, I’ve just been sitting here thinking, but I’m not requiring alone time. I just kinda wish Amy wasn’t at the hospital right now, because I’d love to talk to her as well about what we learned.”

“We will be working to figure out a method of locating what grants powers to parahumans. At this point in time, all I can do is correlate information, but I believe that I will quickly learn enough to proceed further with what grants powers. And I believe that I have also learned all that I can currently regarding the device that orbits Earth, masquerading as Simurgh.”

“That’s an interesting thing to come in on,” Taylor said as she entered the conference room. She smiled at Vicky. “Freeing, isn’t it? And avoiding the sexual connotations of everything I can see in the room, it’s a great view.”

“If any of that was aimed at me, then thank you,” Vicky said, “and if you’re talking about viewing Earth, it’s why I chose this conference room. Something entirely different about seeing it through a transparent window, no matter what the ‘glass’ is made of, than it is looking at it on the bridge view screen. That’s wonderful, but there’s an ineffable something in seeing it without being filtered through some sensor suite.”

“I truly wish I could experience that,” Enterprise said. “But all my ‘sight’, ‘hearing’, and other senses are effectively carefully curated sensor readings. While I can generate holographic nerves so close to biological that it permits me to experience things such as touch and even experience orgasm, it still is filtered through some sort of technology.”

“I wonder if that’s an oddity of those non-biological intelligences that are created by humans, rather than somehow evolving into it, that they desire to become biological, if only temporarily. Personally, sexy, I love you just the way you are. If you look at it a certain way, I’m not seeing Earth properly. I’m seeing it through biological sensors that evolved a certain way. You have different sensors than I do. You do things that I wish I could.”

“Such as?” Enterprise asked, sounding interested.

“Well, the first that comes to mind is sexual in nature, but I have to admit that since meeting you and Vicky and Amy, I wouldn’t complain about being able to do what you did to me in the shower the other day?” Vicky gave her an amused questioning look. “Well, I think I might have mentioned it before, but I don’t see myself as qualifying as a virgin anymore. Holograms can generate what they need, and in this case, what I needed.”

“As in?” Vicky asked, her nipples showing that she had more than a merely informational interest.

“If you wanted to be extremely offensively insulting to a beautiful woman, I had the universe’s most impressive dildo inside me. What I see it as was that I had a beautiful and sexy woman making love to me in a way that no other woman I know of could without Amy doing some work on them.”

Vicky was biting her lower lip a little, but asked, “Offensively insulting, as opposed to merely insulting?” Her tone was definitely amused.

“I can insult you, for example, by calling you that insulting nickname of ‘Collateral Damage Barbie’,” Taylor said. “Or I could phrase it such that the kindest thing I say to you is calling you ‘Collateral Damage Barbie’. The kind of insults guaranteed to make you want to put your fist through my skull on purpose.” Vicky nodded.

“I notice that you didn’t try to come up with any examples,” she said with a laugh.

“First off, I like my skull in one piece,” Taylor said in an answering laugh. “Second, and by far more important, I like you, and even if I had any of those in mind - which I don’t - I wouldn’t say them, because you might think that I really did think of you that way. I’m not Emma Barnes, who pretended to like me all those years. I actually like you, and it would hurt me to hurt you that way.” She paused. “Y’know, I can’t think of anything nastier to say than calling you CDB? I’m glad of that.”

“Hang around me for a while and you’ll hear all sorts,” Vicky said in a wry tone.

“Can I phaser them unconscious if they offend me?” Taylor asked in bright voice, making Vicky giggle.

“Nah, might make people look sideways at you,” Vicky finally said. “I think that they’d rather just stare at you as you are, sexy.”

“No, that’s her,” Taylor said, pointing her thumb at the ship.

“That describes you as well, Captain,” the ship replied with a somewhat amused tone. “Vicky, may I explain some of what we learned?” Vicky nodded.

Enterprise appeared, dressed the same as Vicky, and Vicky couldn’t help but feel her pulse react again, especially remembering what Taylor had said that Enterprise had done. The hologram gave her a smile and a wink, then looked back to her captain. “I ran her through several early Academy tests to find where an aptitude might lie. Artistic talents are very evident, and she would be likely to be asked to join public relations and the like in Starfleet, if not the various design departments. I have no doubt that she would easily end up in the department that designs uniforms and various other clothing. She also has an aptitude for navigation, and in the process we discovered that there are signals coming from the subspace connection that I detect from all parahumans. What I find especially interesting is that there is a difference between the connection that you have and the one that I have detected in all other parahumans I have been within scanning range of. What was truly interesting was that when I began to interfere one of the signals that I detected - with Vicky’s permission first, of course - I discovered that she calmed a great deal and her ability to fly a simulated shuttle improved immensely. Given that it was her first time ever, I believe that if she were given the opportunity to learn properly, she could one day be spoken of in the same way that many speak of Admiral Hikaru Sulu’s capabilities. There seems to be a push toward aggressiveness carried in the signal that I muted.”

Vicky nodded. “I think that if there’s an aggressiveness signal, that would explain why my go-to reaction is punch first and hope they survive to ask questions later, and might even explain my flying. I love to fly, but if I come across another flier, it often feels like a competition.” She thought about it again, as she had been while floating and staring at the Earth. “I don’t like that something outside me is making me angrier than I should be. I don’t deny that even before I Triggered, I was competitive and maybe got angry faster than I should, but … if my powers are doing this to me? We … I need to find a solution.”

Taylor put her hand on Vicky shoulder. “We need to find one. I am wondering if this anger feeling is endemic to whatever grants powers. I haven’t noticed it myself, but I’ve only had them for eleven days. Twelve? If you include the day I Triggered it’s twelve.”

“You were unconscious for most of it, so I don’t think it counts,” Enterprise said. “As an aside, I believe that I have learned all that I am capable of with the one you call the Simurgh. The scans have taken so long because I have had to continually change the scanning, because the device is dimensionally folded. It may be a being, but I detect no biological aspect to any of it, and much of its reactions seem to be more preprogrammed than how a sapient or sentient would respond. It also has the subspace connection to elsewhere, and I also detect a separate signal I have not detected yet elsewhere. It most often seems to ‘point’, if you will, in a direction toward the southern central part of the United States, but that signal occasionally moves … elsewhere that I cannot yet trace. It is a dormant signal, although it seems to be increasing in power at a constant rate, as if it were a timer.”

Vicky thought for a moment. “Y’know, it’s her turn,” she finally said. “They rotate between themselves, so to speak. We never get two Behemoth sightings in a row anymore, or Leviathan, and I think the nations of the world would vote to crack the planet themselves if the Hopekiller struck twice in a row. It’s been long enough that I suspect she’s next on the list.”

“Should we remove her from the equation before she can attack?” Enterprise asked. “I believe that if I target the most dimensionally dense part of the Simurgh, I can damage, if not destroy her.”

“Sounds silly,” Taylor asked, “but if we destroy her, is there any part of her that we could use? I hate to sound like a cannibal or something, but if she’s just a big non-intelligent robot, then we could potentially use the resources to do things like speed up building things like Moon bases and such.”

Vicky laughed. “Now that’s where you should build your Starfleet Academy! Drive the point home about how things have changed if they’re studying on the Moon!”

“She has a point,” Enterprise told the Taylor. “Drive home to the students that things are definitely changing.”

Taylor’s laughter surprised Vicky. “As if what we’re going to do when we get the clearance isn’t going to make that clear?”

“What do you have planned?” Vicky asked, trying to bounce, but remembering that she was currently floating. “Can’t bounce on my feet if they aren’t touching the ground. Darn,” she said with a chuckle.

“Trust me, you’ll be made aware in advance of it happening, because there are a lot of groups that have to be told - the PRT, New Wave, the BBPD, the FAA, the military … a lot of people.”

“We should be able to do it next Saturday,” Enterprise said. “Since multi-tasking is part of who I am, I’ve carried on multiple simultaneous conversations. The military and the FAA have already verified that there are no issues with something large being in Brockton Bay airspace next Saturday, all day. The military has been told that we have no issue with observers being sent, since what we are doing will be more than a little obvious.”

Vicky couldn’t help it - she let loose with a “SQUEE!” She dropped her feet to the floor and bounced over to Enterprise. “You’re going to be lowering into the atmosphere to show off your sexy self, aren’t you?”

“We intend to clear the Boat Graveyard,” Enterprise told her. Vicky was amused that even Enterprise’s eyes followed her breasts as she bounced.

She giggled. “I can imagine that dropping a huge ship from orbit to just above the bay and lifting ship with a tractor beam would catch just a little attention.”

“Yeah,” Taylor said. “And with the PRT on board, there’s no worry about the Endbringer sirens going off.”

“What are you going to wear?” Vicky asked.

“Well, as much as I’d prefer to be as comfortable as possible, I really doubt that I could handle standing nude in front of the world, because you know that the networks are going to send people.” Taylor looked to Enterprise. “Would you have an issue if Vicky designed a new set of uniforms? Something that tells people who know the television and movies that it is from Starfleet, but that it’s also something completely new and not like any previous uniform?”

“You are making it your own, Captain,” Enterprise said. “I am rather intrigued by the concept of seeing what Head Designer Dallon might come up with.” Both of them looked to Vicky, who felt like her eyes were going to fall out of her head, they were so wide.

“Are you serious?” she finally asked, barely able to breathe from the excitement. “You’re willing to let me design the uniform that everyone who joins up will be wearing?”

“Subject to final decisions from Admiral Hebert, of course.” Vicky cocked her head at Enterprise. “While she is officially Captain in regard to my physical form, she is, in fact, the ranking member of the organization in this universe. And new ships commissioned under this banner will answer to her. Therefore, Admiral Hebert.”

Vicky turned and faced Taylor, and felt herself almost ready to cry from the sheer amount of emotion. “I will do my best not to let you down, Admiral Hebert.”

“You won’t, Vicky. I know that. And you’ll be paid well for it as well. The first thing you’ll want to design is the outfit I’ll be wearing, which should probably look somewhat military formal, if that makes sense.”

“Skirt or slacks?” she asked, already starting to get into the design mindset.

“Enterprise? First, please give her a design PADD, and second, what’s your take on the question?”

“I am biased, Captain, but if you decide on slacks, they should be form fitting, because you have legs that deserve to be admired. I can see a skirt as well, but to properly show off your legs it would need to be closer to a mini-dress, much like those from the era of James Kirk. That look would potentially give the wrong first impression. You could and certainly should wear a mini-dress in later, less formal settings. Then again, my bias toward your figure may be showing through in that appraisal. So I would recommend slacks. As for the top, the fashion grew to prevent any cleavage if wearing a tunic.
