I rather think that tasteful cleavage in your case would work quite well. A uniform jacket that should be worn open, as well.”

“If I had something to show off, cleavage-wise,” Taylor said, making Vicky frown.

Enterprise answered before Vicky could. She did so by dropping the holographic outfit, leaving her nude. She changed her hair to black, and then de-aged herself to Taylor’s age. “Taylor, how do I look? Be honest with me.”

“Like my sexy twin sister if I had one. So?” Enterprise generated a mirror next to Taylor. “Please strip to your skin and look in the mirror, then compare that image to the form I currently wear.” Vicky watched as Taylor stripped, and when the girl bent over, was once again reminded that she wasn’t as purely heterosexual as she once had thought. She looked in the mirror when she stood again, then looked to Enterprise.

“I promise you that I am not manipulating the mirror’s image, Taylor. That is you reflected there.” An astonished Taylor reached up and cupped her breasts while looking in the mirror, and got a look of wonder.

“Holy shit,” she finally breathed. “I am sexy! I actually have tits!”

“Yes, and that was from simply ensuring that your diet was proper and that the stress hormones were cleared from your system. There had been some regeneration of skin and muscle required, but at no time did any of the medical equipment make any alterations to your body that would account for larger breasts than you remember. What you see is what your genetics state you should have at this point in your life.”

“So, when I design the new uniform, I have to take your hotness into account, and ensure that you don’t display too much, or else people won’t pay attention to what you’re doing at the bay.”

Taylor looked at her. “For the first time in my life, I honestly believe that me standing nude in front of an audience would actually cause members of the audience to have sexual thoughts about me,” she said in wonder.

Vicky scowled. “I blame Boobs-and-Butt Barnes for that. She didn’t like that her supposed friend was growing into being supermodel sexy, so tore you down, the bitch.” She couldn’t help the vicious grin. “Everything I’m hearing, it’s not looking good for her or anyone else connected. Daddy Barnes is having issues at the law firm, since he threatened occasionally to use them to cow people into submission. The partners aren’t happy about that, needless to say. Emma’s out on bail, since there was more than enough to arrest her and charge her. Clements is apparently managing a deal, having rolled on the other two.”

“Doesn’t surprise me. Solid follower who looks out for number one. If her ship was sinking? She’s bailing onto the first lifeboat available.”

“Pretty much. A huge number of teachers and administration at Winslow are under investigation, and both Sophia Hess and one of the high level admins have … disappeared … with rumors that they’re being talked to by the PRT for some reason. Especially since the person that was tormented vanished in what could only be a parahuman incident.” Vicky couldn’t help but snort. “Somehow, they still aren’t stating that you’re a parahuman over on PHO, although the thought is making the rounds. You haven’t been named, and Void Cowboy has been given a three day ban from his last attempt to mention you by name. The attitude at the moment is that, unless you are somehow outed as a public parahuman, any hints that you could be one might put your family in danger. Hence his ban.”

Chapter 18: Wednesday, January 19th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the late posting - been dealing with a dental infection, and pain strong enough to keep one from sleeping also is pain strong enough to make one forget about posting. Pain's down to a manageable level (antibiotics are your friend), so here's the next offering.

Monday had led to a call from Arcadia wondering when the best day for her to start would be. Taylor asked what she’d need to start there, and they had emailed her the list, so she suggested Wednesday, in order to get her the chance to buy the things she didn’t have. She actually had Enterprise create them, since Winslow had left her twitchy. She was pretty sure she wasn’t going to have worries about being shivved in the hallway, but at least she now had a backpack that would deflect most modern Earth military weapons. She couldn’t say all, because she was pretty sure that a nuke would take out the backpack, but beyond that? She’d likely survive it if someone hit her backpack with a rocket propelled grenade.

When she’d gone in on Tuesday, to finish her paperwork, she talked to the principal and admitted that she was going to be outing herself as a parahuman on Saturday, and that she wanted to see about registering a phaser with the school. The principal’s eyes had widened at the sight of it, and was very happy when Taylor showed that it was bio-locked to her. Taylor had filled out the paperwork - with a few handwritten changes to it, of course - and submitted that. She also promised to keep it in her backpack for the time being.

On Wednesday, she stepped into the school again, happily kissing Amy quickly, and they walked hand in hand to Taylor’s homeroom, where there was once again a quick chaste kiss before they separated. Once homeroom was done, she began her college level classes, and was immediately glomped by two of the perkiest girls she had ever met, one a redhead and the other a platinum blonde. Quite possibly in other meanings of perky as well, unless they were wearing steel bras. “Hi! I’m Deena, and this is Charlie!” said the blonde.

“Parents named me Charlessa, but I prefer Charlie.” With a mock growl she said, “I will cut you if you call me ‘Lessa’.”

Taylor snickered. “Understood. Any puns about being the ‘Lessa of two evils’ are a quick ride to Painsville.”

Charlie grinned at her. “They said she was smart!” and hugged Taylor’s arm. Which, to Taylor’s surprise sank between the girl’s breasts. Girl didn’t even react and the two dragged her toward the desks and got ready for math class.

Taylor ended up making her name in that class about halfway through as the teacher was writing a formula on the board. As they finished and turned back to the class, Taylor put her hand up. “Yes, Miss Hebert?”

She bit her lip before saying, “Did you mean to use a delta instead of a lambda at the tail end of the equation? Because I think it’s unsolvable if it’s a delta.” The teacher looked at the formula and nodded, before changing the symbol in question.

“Excellent catch, Miss Hebert. I suspect you’re a prodigy in mathematics if you could follow the formula and realize that it would be unsolvable otherwise. As much as I should be thinking solely on this problem, a little part of my mind is working on something else, hence the accidental symbol.” As Taylor shrunk a little in her chair, Miss Harkness said, “Don’t be ashamed. You have a gift, possibly. To some extent, that’s what these classes are for. These are college level classes, after all. You just might need to do external study if I am not capable of challenging you on mathematics. It has happened before to me as a teacher, and I’m certain it will happen again.” She smiled at Taylor.

When class was done, Charlie engulfed Taylor arm with her breasts again and started to lead her out of the classroom, Deena laughing as she did. “Uh, Charlie, you’re aware that the way you’re gripping me makes it look -”

“You’re hot, I’m lesbian, and maybe Amy shares. If not, I will certainly enjoy the eye candy!”

Taylor stopped for a moment as she parsed that rapid-fire bit, trying to ignore Deena almost hurting herself trying not to laugh out loud. “Honest,” she finally said. “I appreciate that. And not only do you have to find out if Amy shares, but even if she does, are we all compatible?”

Charlie grinned and let go of Taylor’s arm, quickly becoming far less manic. “Thank you,” she said in a far less chipper voice. “I think we’ll get along just fine. I’m sorry, but you came from Gangland Central. I am lesbian and I do think that you’re hotter than any two girls have a right to be, but I’m not about to try to force myself into your relationship with Amy.”

Taylor laughed. “Testing to see if the white girl might goose-step a little after school?”

“We’ll definitely get along,” Deena said. “You get her, and therefore me, and you sure as hell don’t seem offended.”

“Pretty much everyone but Vicky and Amy are people I need to learn who they are before I can really make any friends here. One of my tormentors at my previous school had been all but my sister when we were growing up. Then she turned on me and became my literal worst nightmare. So … not sure why I really trust Amy and Vicky so quickly, but it’s gonna be ‘trust but verify’ for pretty much everyone else for a bit.”

“Makes sense to me,” Charlie said. “Forgive me for the over the top hyper-sexual bit?”

“I understand why you did it, Charlie. Just, be careful and make sure it’s only arms you shove between your breasts? If you’d grabbed me and shoved my face in there, I’d have smothered.” She smirked. “Died happy, admittedly, but still dead.” Both Deena and Charlie threw their heads back and laughed as they headed off for their next classes.

When lunch came around, Amy was amused at the reactions from people regarding Vicky’s deep concentration over the last few days. She was working with the PADD and actually had her tongue sticking out the left side of her mouth as she worked. She looked up and saw Taylor, who had been joined by Charlie and Deena again, and thrust the PADD at her. “Got a couple interesting design ideas. Willing to take a look and let me know what you think?”

Vicky had come up with an interesting idea. The slacks were black, and the top was a single shoulder unit. “I chose red just because,” she said as Taylor looked. The top in the design left the right arm bare, but there was a note that it could be built the other way as well. Half of the top was black, and met the slacks to appear as a single field of black, traversing diagonally across the body and between the breasts, while the red started in a wedge as soon as the design left the shoulder and widened as it went down the body. Taylor knew that a standard comm badge would look best straddling the line where black and color met.

She looked at it for a bit while Vicky bit worriedly at her lower lip. Her worst problem wasn’t all that big of one - where to put the rank pips. That would likely be on the jacket, to be honest, which was a dark charcoal color that meshed quite well with the rest of the outfit.

Finally she looked at Vicky. “To be honest, I’d wear something like this to a formal occasion if it called for it. It looks really nice and professional, and I mean that both in the drawing style and in the clothing style. Interesting choice with the bare shoulder, but I think it works.” She figured out how to flip the drawing without the jacket so that it now looked like the left shoulder was bare, and thought that it still worked well.

Charlie and Deena looked over Taylor’s shoulders, then Deena said, “Yeah. Make that out of the right materials and it does a nice job of looking extremely professional with the jacket on, but with it off, it stays professional but gives it a slightly casual feel at that point. Design of the jacket gives a little bit of a Star Trek feel, though, so if you’re doing this for pay, you might want to take that into account.”

Taylor nodded. “If this isn’t just you deciding to follow a concept, then talk to the buyer. Personally, if it was me? I like the Star Trek look so I’d keep the jacket as is, but your buyer needs to make the final decision. Got any other stuff along these lines?”

“Swipe along in that file. Got some male designs - could make the off-the-shoulder look work for guys, dammit - and when I realized how Star Trek some of it looked, I made some modernized mini-dresses in that general style.”

When she reached the mini-dress design, she heard Charlie inhale. “Amy, I know you’re dating her, but have you seen the mini-dress design?”

“You’d like to see Taylor out of it as much as I would, right?” she asked with a grin.

“Out of?” Dennis asked, not having seen the drawings yet.

“Trust me, the way Taylor would look in that dress, I think we can guarantee that everyone who saw her in it would be wanting to get her out of it. It’s just a mini-dress, but Taylor wearing it would make it accidentally X-rated from her figure, because the thing would stop just shy of showing all of her legs, and showing all of her legs would mean she was also be showing … other things as well.”

Taylor was attempting to set the table on fire from her blush. “I’m not that attractive!” she protested.

Deena laughed. “Forgive those of us who appreciate the female form if we choose to disagree with you, Miss Hebert.”

Taylor slowly handed the PADD back to Vicky, still blushing. “My opinion on all of them is that they’re excellent designs. If you’re getting paid for the designs, then I hope they’re paying you well for quality like that.” She gave the girl a very quick wink.

“Please tell me you didn’t agree to do them ‘for the exposure’, Charlie said to Vicky.

Deena laughed. “Whoever wears that mini-dress is the one exposing themselves.”

“Okay, so I made it unintentionally sexier than I meant to,” Vicky said, blushing. “Let me get rid of it.”

“No,” Taylor interjected before she could. “If they wanted you to submit designs, then leave it. The worst that your employer can do is tell you that they don’t like the design. Submit it as it is.”

“You really think so?” Vicky asked. “I’m still working on designs. I focused mainly on females, but I’ve still got a few male ones to work on.” She blushed. “I made a Speedo-like design for men, and I admit that I was thinking about Dean wearing it while designing it.”

“If it’s anything like the mini-dress design, do you really want every girl who sees him in it throwing themselves at him?” Charlie asked.

Vicky’s blush deepened. “There’d be no mistaking that he’s male,” she said quietly.

Taylor giggled. “Make a bikini in the same style and wear it for him. I guarantee that he’ll advertise just how male he is.” Dean was stoically sitting at the end of the table, trying valiantly to set fire to everything near him, based on his own deep blush. She couldn’t resist it; she had to make the situation worse. “And given a couple of the outfits that I’ve actually seen him wear, I suspect that he is impressively male, if you get my meaning.”

Vicky smirked. “I can neither confirm nor deny your allegation,” she said with a purr. Dean’s head went to the table, and he gently started banging the table with his forehead, much to the laughter of everyone. When he stopped, he looked up, and the look of consternation on his face was ruined by the fact that he was trying hard not to laugh.

Chapter 19: Friday, January 21st, 2011 - Taylor

“Okay, so everything changes tomorrow,” Taylor said. “We’ve got the companies set up and building started, which we can speed up when I officially admit that the ship everyone has been seeing in orbit is mine.” She looked at everyone in the conference room on the Enterprise. “Well, she belongs to herself -”

“The truth, Captain Hebert, is that I am, in a real sense what this age would call a shackled AI. You give me as much freedom as you possibly can, but if you give me an order, I must follow it, unless it conflicts with a previous of your orders, in which case I must request a clarification of your orders. This is hard-wired into my systems and cannot be removed. So it is best if those of your world are not aware of just how self-reliant I am, since there is so much fear as in the examples that came from within the very franchise that your people will think of when they see me. If they think of me as much closer to your program Voyager’s Emergency Medical Hologram, things will go much easier for you.”

Taylor frowned, but agreed. “That said, I out myself to the public tomorrow. I’ve set up protections at the Docks and at my home, to the point that I think even the Triumvirate would have serious issues getting through.” She snorted. “It would certainly take long enough that Enterprise here could stun them, from orbit.”

She sighed. “I had to bring the PRT into what I want to do, because my lady here showing up over the bay - quite literally, by the way - would probably cause the Endbringer sirens to go off. The military will be there as well, since I needed to warn them as well.” She laughed. “I’ll probably be in meetings until I’m old enough to vote after tomorrow, especially with the changes that will be coming as I slowly start releasing technology. I understand fully the reasons for the Prime Directive, and right now, this is the only planet we’ve got, so any new technology is coming slowly, like the super-conductor I gave the plans for to Armsmaster.” She paused. “Mom would have rinsed my mouth out with soap for the construction of that last sentence,” she said with a small laugh.

Danny snorted from his seat. “Or crossed her eyes trying to follow it.”

“So what exactly is happening?” asked Emily Piggot.

“The current plan is to get the thing started by introducing myself, which, without the Enterprise immediately there, is likely to cause the world to have a cry of ‘Who cares?’ Until the ship drops from orbit and starts to hover above the bay, that is. I suspect that they’ll care then. I’ll tell people that I will be cleaning up the bay, starting with the Northern Girl. It will then be carefully tractor-beamed out of the mouth of the bay and allowed to drain of water, then carefully tractored over to where it will be cut apart and prepared for reclamation of the metals and plastics, which will be used - where possible - in the rebuilding of infrastructure around the Docks area, and in the building of the new industrial park near the Docks.”

“Which T.A. Enterprises, D.C. Textiles, and D.C. Industries happen to already own the land needed,” Emily said with a snort. “If you don’t mind - basically, if it’s not a big secret - what do those initials stand for?”

Danny started snickering while Taylor blushed. “T.A. is my initials, standing for Taylor Anne, but I … when I was still single digits, I used to run around wishing I was a superhero, although in our games of make-believe, I was always the mad scientist Doctor Curlyhair. I thought about it for a split second or two when trying to come up with a cape name, and decided that calling myself Doctor Curlyhair was too silly, even for me.”

“That’s Captain Curlyhair!” Vicky admonished with a giggle.

“Plus, it’s not as curly anymore, since I let it grow to a length I really like,” Taylor replied with an amused shake of her head.

“Getting back to the situation at hand. Once I start releasing some of my stuff, I’m going to offer certain things like body armor and non-lethal methods of take-down - no complete phasers, sorry - to the PRT and police at near cost. Stronger vehicles and the like the same. Better fire-fighting equipment, but not the sort of stuff that is decades past. It’ll be more along the lines of someone looking at it and saying ‘Huh, so that’s how that works!’ with the equipment. I am going to be stingy with hyper-technology. I might be able to trust some people here in Brockton Bay, but let some of my more dangerous technology get into the hands of someone like James Tagg? He’s famous outside the PRT for his attitudes. There are those on PHO who say that if you want a war started somewhere, just put him in charge of the PRT in that area. And these are people who have worked with him. Even if it’s not that bad, the fact that the stories exist means that stuff like that has to be carefully dealt with.”

She sighed. “So many of these meetings are going to be with organizations who are going to try to figure out how to take control of Enterprise here. They won’t phrase it like that, but it’s going to be the case. Can you really see the military not fighting over which branch she should be made part of? Navy and Air Force would probably be fighting really hard. And the highest levels of the Protectorate? Anyone want to take bets on whether or not someone at the top tries to argue that since I’m a parahuman, I have to be a member of the Wards, followed by the Protectorate? Which ‘just so happens’ to allow them as complete control over my ship as they can manage?”

She met the eyes of the PRT and Protectorate members there. “Please stress to the Chief Director that they are far more likely to get things from me if I’m affiliated than if I’m legally forced into joining. If I’m forced, I am stating now that I will follow the exact letter of the contract with them, and before I sign any contract that forces me to join, it will be looked over by my own lawyers. Bian alone would have a field day.”

She rubbed her face. “I hate that it sounds like I’m threatening you guys. I really don’t mean to.”

Emily Piggot spoke up. “You’re stressed over tomorrow and what barrel of monkeys that will end up releasing, and you’re smart enough to be aware that it won’t be sweetness and light and fluffy pink unicorns dancing on rainbows. You’re also a teenager still, which is driving the stress that much higher.” In a softer voice, the Brockton Bay director said, “You’ve been careful in what you said. You’re basically telling me to try to get the point across to my bosses to use a honey-soaked carrot rather than a vinegar-soaked stick, to intentionally mangle sayings.” Taylor snickered, and saw the small smile that Piggot gave her in return. “I’m known as a hard-ass around here, and it’s for good reason. But I also appreciate the hell out of the fact that you’re doing everything you can to keep us in the loop on this potential … Charlie Foxtrot. I’ll pass that up the line, and stress as strongly as I can that you want to work with us, so affiliation is the best route, rather than trying to force things.”

“I really would appreciate that, Director. I really would rather avoid as many issues as I can. I know I’ll have problems, but if I can start from a position of friendliness - or at least neutrality - I’m much better off.” She shrugged. “And honestly, so’s the one causing me problems. Sort of the equivalent of deciding to tell me you want to talk to me by buying me a cup of tea as opposed to telling me you want to talk to me by pointing a gun in my face. I’m probably not going to want to talk to the one with the gun.”

“As an aside, can I borrow Vista for tomorrow? I suspect that I could really do some interesting things for her reputation if she helps me bring Enterprise down.”

“What are you thinking?” Armsmaster asked.

“Rather than have people watching for several minutes while a ship that is easily two miles long comes down safely from orbit, Vista shortens the distance. We know that there’s an aspect of her power that prevents pressure differences from causing wind - and may I say that having her practice with allowing it could be an excellent battle control mechanism - so she opens a large ‘window’, if you will, and Enterprise comes through that. Roughly a mile or so up in the air, so she’ll be huge to everyone on the ground.”

“Can she make a portal-slash-tunnel that big?” Emily asked.

“We’ve used her once or twice when we absolutely needed to get troop transports to a site immediately,” Armsmaster said. “Our transports aren’t small, and there was zero strain upon her doing it for some period of time, so I have no issue believing that she can do so for a short period with a larger portal.” He smiled lightly. “I had words with her regarding a practice that she did, but it shows her range perfectly. One of her prized possessions now is a small lunar rock. She literally opened a tunnel between her and the Moon and reached through for a second and grabbed one. She even wore gloves to avoid being cut by the sharp edges.”

“We’ll ask her then, and have her get in contact with you if she says yes,” Emily said. “Is there anything else?”

“Not that I can think of right now,” Taylor said. “So much of what needs to be talked about comes after I’m officially announced. I asked that it be held up here because …” She blushed as she stopped speaking. “It’s such a beautiful view and everyone seems to enjoy it, so …”

Emily gave a soft laugh. “I can’t say as any of us seem to have an issue with having something nicer to look at than four beige walls.”

“That was my thought,” Taylor replied. She walked to the replicator and punched in some information, and an original series communicator appeared. “Give this to Vista. Since she was up here and agreed to be scanned by medical, I was able to bio-lock it to her, so if anyone tries to steal it from her, it’s just a paperweight for them.” She grinned. “Plus, I can always recall it if it does get stolen.”

Once the PRT were beamed back to Piggot’s office, Taylor looked at the others. “If it turns out that Vista can’t, I’ll lower her through the atmosphere, but I think her floating through a fuck-huge portal to come to rest over the bay should make more of an impact.”

“Can’t argue with you there,” her father said with a chuckle. “So what are you doing with the rest of your day?”

“I’ve got some work to do to plan for tomorrow. I’ll probably stay up here tonight, just because I’m thinking of starting things off by beaming onto the platform that’s already in progress of being built and protected.”

“Makes sense,” he replied. “It lets you sleep just a tiny bit later, rather than waking up, getting ready, beaming up, and then beaming right back down. Will you be planet-side for dinner?” He paused. “I am fighting the urge to jump up and down like an excited child at the fact that I can actually ask a question like that and have it have real meaning.”

“We could eat up here, if everyone wanted,” she offered. “Don’t think we’ve done anything like that before, and it would be nice if I had the people who really mean something to me do it first before I start holding official diplomatic dinners up here.”

Chapter 20: Saturday, January 22nd, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Summary

And now we get to see Taylor announce herself to the world.

Amy had stayed the night with her, but beamed down before the show would begin, since New Wave was officially on board to offer security. Brandish might have had issues with Taylor and her father, but there was no obvious wrongdoing, and they were getting paid good money for each person in New Wave involved. Taylor dressed in the tight slacks and left shoulder bare version of the top, with command red as the color, then put on the pips for Captain. She would only ever claim any right to Admiralty if they had more ships available, and even then, she would undergo what training was necessary. “Have to see, once we’ve got me announced and such, if I can maybe get some training from Colin Powell. Whether or not I agreed with his politics, from what I’ve seen, he knew how to properly deal with multi-branch forces. I’ll likely need that.” She snorted. “And I doubt that he’d turn down a chance to look at Earth from Space.” She thought for a moment. “Have to see if any of the crew of Apollo 13 are still alive. I’d gladly take them to the Moon and let them step where they were meant to go.”

Enterprise spoke up. “At this point in time, both James Lovell and Fred Haise are still alive. John Swigert unfortunately died in 1985. Shall I prepare for making such an offer to them?”

“I think so. Perhaps ask all of the currently living astronauts who can travel if they’d like to return to space again. Maybe show them where we’re going to build our own Starfleet Academy?”

“I suspect that by the time we could work things out, we will have begun at least the foundations of our academy.” After a pause, she added, “I am receiving a call from Vista. She wants to know if she should ask to beam up, or wait on the ground.”

“Patch her through.” After a short pause she said, “Vista? I’m thinking that you wait on the ground and show up when I ask for you.”

“Makes sense. This is your show, after all,” the youngest Ward said. “And should show quite well that you’re working with the PRT, backing up the statements that you’re affiliated.”

“That was my thought. After we’re done, I’m thinking I’ll ask a few people up and maybe throw a party on one of the holodecks. You’re invited.”

“Cool! See you when you get down here, then. Heading out to the area right now. Probably be on a local roof.”

Taylor smiled as they disconnected. She looked at herself again in the mirror Enterprise was providing, and tugged the jacket slightly to ensure that the fit was just right. She was trying to decide whether or not to remove the jacket during her talk, because, well, she was currently saluting the inside of her uniform top, and they were large enough to be noticeable. Damn. Arousal, cold, stage fright … any one of those and SPUNG! they’re trying to tear through my shirts.

She did a last few things before her alarm told her that she had five minutes to make it to the transporter room. She headed down there, and as the clock ticked over to 9 am Brockton Bay time, she beamed down onto the platform.

As she materialized, she could hear that the general murmur of voices that always happens when people get together went immediately to silence. “Hello Brockton Bay, and visitors from elsewhere. I will be going by the name Grey Ghost as my cape name, but as you can see, I wear no mask. I am Taylor Hebert, and I Triggered at the beginning of the month under harrowing circumstances. Somewhat redundant, if you think about it, given what is known about Triggers.”

“The reason I’m here today is because I intend to make a change in Brockton Bay, and the most obvious way to do that is to open the bay back up so that we can become a shipping hub again.”

“How you gonna do that?” someone yelled from the audience in a mocking tone. “Snap your fingers and vanish all the ships?”

She smiled out at the audience. “Actually, they won’t be vanishing into nothingness, but they will be moved.” She looked up at the building where Enterprise had told her Vista was. “Vista? Some help here?” An eye-watering moment later, Vista was on the stage with her. “About a mile or so up, out over the water.”

Vista grinned and looked out at the audience first. Taylor had an idea that mocking her plans had been a setup with someone in the local PRT, because she looked up at the sky, raised her hand, then snapped her fingers. Suddenly, the audience could see the Enterprise, which moved slowly through the warp that Vista had set up. Taylor was watching the girl carefully to ensure that she wasn’t stressing herself, even though she doubted it would, since the worst part of it was the size of the warp. In amazingly short order, a two mile long ship hovered over the bay, and Vista snapped her fingers again and closed the rift. She looked almost bored with what had just happened, but Taylor could see the excitement in her eyes.

Taylor looked blandly out over the audience, who were silent in awe of the vehicle above them. The saucer section of this Enterprise was shaped much like the comm badges of the Next Generation series, with the Starfleet Delta point laid atop an oval. “I believe that you all can see why I’ve chosen the name Grey Ghost as my cape name, since it fits as well for her as it does for the CVN-65 and the CVN-80, and did for the CVN-6.” She snickered. “It’s certainly better than the one I made up as a six year old, when I decided to be Doctor Curlyhair.” That got the laughter that she was hoping to hear, even if it was still mixed with more than a little awe and shock.

“As if the way I arrived on the stage didn’t prove the point, what you now see above the bay is, in fact, the latest in the line of ships named Enterprise. This one is the NCC-1701-G, but still is a ship worthy of the name. It currently has a crew of one - me. That is why, while I am Grey Ghost as a cape, I am also Captain Taylor Anne Hebert, who intends to uphold the tradition that this ship’s name carries with it. It is an awesome and frankly terrifying burden to carry, because there is so much history behind her, and I have no intention in faltering in my duty as her captain.”

“The first thing that so many will likely ask is regarding technology. I will follow the Prime Directive in this. I have no issue with giving people a nudge, but I will not be rapidly uplifting the whole planet with what is frankly terrifying technology for these days. People will want replicators in their homes or on street corners. I will not be doing this.” She heard complaints from the audience, and explained. “I said it to someone else recently, when I was talking to them about my debut today. I won’t go into all of the science and mathematics behind it, but to generate one kilogram of mass - which is roughly the size of a full-on Fugly Bob’s Challenger with all the fixings - you will use energy that is just under twenty-five billion kilowatt-hours. That is the yearly energy output of some European nations. A portable replicator has a generator in it capable of creating thousands of those one kilo items. Do you want to trust that there’s no Tinkers anywhere in the world who might not try to take one apart to get at a power supply like that? Do you want to trust that those Tinkers will manage to do it safely?” She could almost hear the wince from the audience. “Until I’m sure that it will be safe to do so and that I will not be crashing any economy by doing so, I will not supply replicators.”

“That’s another thing. I can promise the world that I will not be generating anything precious for sale on Earth. I have no intention of crashing any market, be it the diamond market, the precious metals or gems markets, clothing, or any other type of market. Anything that my companies will end up selling will be created here on Earth, using existing Earth materials, be they cloth, metal, plastic, or gems. My purpose is to begin the uplift of mankind into the stars, not take over the world with superior technology.”

“It would be so easy for you with a ship like the Enterprise, though!” someone yelled.

“Yes, it would. Luckily, I realize what an amazing pain it would be. All those would-be dictators who want to rule everything - do you really think about what it means? If you’re that kind of conqueror, then you don’t want any competition, so you end up culling all the people who would be best suited for helping you run the world. And those of you who work in governments, or have to deal with them on a regular basis in any form, such as lawyers and law firms. Think how much paperwork a law firm has to generate. Now imagine how much paperwork is required - and I mean required - to keep a town or city government going. I don’t envy Mayor Christner his carpal tunnel problems from all that signing he needs to do, and all the meetings over all the things required to keep the city going. He’s been doing an amazing job trying to keep this city afloat over his terms, but I think he’d be one of the first to tell you just how much of his job is bureaucracy shenanigans.” She paused. “I was going to use a different term, honestly, but I’m trying to keep this at least PG rated.” She got another laugh.

“So imagine all that paperwork. Remember that the conqueror in question isn’t just going to let the sub-bureaucracies just do their thing. The person who wants to rule the world has his fingers in all the pies. So now take that paperwork for Brockton Bay, and multiply it until you’re dealing with the planet. You’ll be working eight hundred hours a week just to keep up with the paperwork. Problem is, a week only has one hundred and sixty eight hours. I have better things to do with my time than worry about the price of peaches in Patagonia and the cost of kumquats in Kalamazoo. I want to think about the best way to help us get those of us who want to explore the stars out there. We’ve got the Enterprise, but I want to be able to begin our own fleet of ship to take us out there. And if I’m doing something stupid like trying to run the world, then I’ve got no time to explore.”

She paused and looked out at the audience. “I may never make everyone understand, but those who have been fans of the shows may. I said that being captain of this ship is a responsibility. For some reason I was given the power to multitask to a degree that I can simultaneously do everything aboard that ship that doesn’t require a hand to physically disconnect something and plug it into someplace else. If it can be done on the ship’s panels, then I can do it. And most everything aboard that ship can be done from those amazing LCARS consoles. But the fact that I now have this ship gives me a responsibility to live up to the ideals of those before me. James Kirk may have been a little too fond of the ladies, but he was also an inspiration in how to be a captain, facing danger and new situations. Jean Luc Picard the same. A different style, but he showed that he was well chosen for the role. Captain Rachel Garrett of the Enterprise C, followed by Richard Castillo who took over at Captain Garrett’s death, showed the true meaning of captaincy, by leading their people to certain death, knowing that the universe would be better off in the end. They wanted to live; I guarantee you that they wanted to live. But they saw that the universe would change for the better if they returned, even though it meant their deaths. I hope to live a long and healthy life, retiring someday, maybe to an off-world colony if we can get them set up. But I want to also live up to the responsibility to my fellow sapients - to give my life if I believe that the universe will prosper.”

The audience was silent. “But as much as you’re all hear to listen to me speechify, as some might say, you’re really here to see if I can do as I say.” With that, she looked up at the ship and subvocalized, making sure that her words were not going to be heard by anyone other than the ship. She pointed out at the container ship that blocked the harbor, and a tractor beam shot from the ship’s saucer section. The Northern Girl slowly lifted from the water, draining as it rose. When it was completely out of the water, Enterprise began to slowly move it toward the dry-dock area that had been set up for it. The process took a few minutes, but she knew that every camera in the area was focused on the movement of the container ship. It was set down so lightly that people were surprised that it hadn’t been significantly louder.

The crowd numbly looked back to her. “I will be removing more of the ships from the bay as space clears from the reclamation efforts, but our worst offender is now removed. Once I have a better idea of how long it will take to deal with these ships properly, I will let people know.” She laughed. “If there are people living on those hulks out there, they’re going to want to find new shelter, because the bay will be cleaned. The metals, plastics, and oils will be reclaimed and recycled in various ways. Before this year is out, I intend to have people employed at various companies, and hopefully we can get to shipping again. With luck, revitalizing shipping here will help revitalize shipping in other cities as well. We may not deal as much with trans-oceanic shipping anymore, but coastal is still a valid option. And I suspect that Brockton Bay will have things to ship within the next few years.”

“Do you have any idea why the Simurgh hasn’t tried anything yet, since you’re up in orbit and she is too?” someone called out.

“None whatsoever. Maybe she can’t see us. Maybe we’re too powerful. Maybe there’s a specific thing she has to watch for that we don’t have. Maybe her precognition is more of a random number generator and our number hasn’t come up. Maybe we’re too inconsequential for her to even care about us, although I doubt that last one. If she’s capable of fending off the full power of a Federation starship in war mode - which is what I will put her in if need be,” she said, pointing at her starship, “then we as a world stand no chance. And I refuse to believe that we can’t at least hurt her. I’d love to be able to actually destroy her, but I won’t promise that, because I just don’t know yet. But trust me, we will see that the full might of a Federation starship falls against an Endbringer. I’m betting that between everyone, we can drive an Endbringer away before too much damage happens.”

“Do you think you’d be able to destroy an Endbringer?” someone else asked.

“Don’t know until I try, but I’m betting that the ship can at least give them pause, if nothing else. I promise you that I will be involved with the next Endbringer attack, if only because I have something that I believe can hurt an Endbringer.”

Chapter 21: Saturday, January 22nd, 2011 - Taylor

She looked up at the huge ship looming over the bay. “I need to get it back into orbit, so I’ll do that now, but I’d prefer to do it from aboard the ship. So …” she said, and something detached itself from the bottom of the saucer and quickly flew to her. “Captain’s yacht,” she told the people watching. “The captains never used them in the series, but I think that’s because they would have had to build an entirely new set for it and that’s expensive for a television show. In the real world, however, it means that it’s perfect for the captain of the ship to use when necessary. Vista, want to join me as I fly back to the ship and then back to orbit? I’ll beam you back down here when we’re done if the answer is yes.”

Vista paused for a moment before saying, “I have permission, so I’d be crazy to say no!”

The yacht came down and nearly touched down on the platform. “I’ll be back in just a few minutes, folks. Having my lady here is definitely making some people nervous, so let’s get her back where she belongs.” Taylor and Vista climbed aboard the yacht after the door opened, and were quickly heading up to Enterprise.

Making sure that she was no longer broadcasting, she said, “I want to work on you with you costume and see if we can get the PRT to age you up a bit. When you were scanned the first time you came up, I could tell that you’re binding both breasts and butt, in order to keep being able to wear the current design. Part of the issue is that while you won’t end up my height - you’ll probably top out no taller than five-foot-four - you are still getting taller, and it’s probably no more than a month or two before you start needing that skirt to hide camel toe.”

“Already beginning to fight it,” Vista grumbled. “But they can’t admit that, because Youth Guard refuses to let me lose that ‘cute’ thing because it makes so much money.”

“I wonder if you can get a copy of all contracts regarding you?” Taylor asked. “I find myself wondering if part of the problem is that the Youth Guard is getting either a kickback or a percentage of your merchandise. Because to be dead honest with you, the way you’re growing, someday you’re gonna make a lot of teenagers real happy when your costume gives up the ghost and splits wide open. I think public nudity should be your choice, not the fabric’s.” She laughed as she said that.

“I’d love a new design for my costume. I’d love it if they let me have breasts, at least,” Vista grumbled.

“The problem is, given the figure you’ve already got, the minute they allow Vista to have breasts in her costume, they have to start thinking about marketing you for innocent sex appeal. Maybe we should get Vicky - Glory Girl - involved. She’s the one who designed my uniform.” She blushed. “I’m going to have to ask her to de-sexy-fy the minidress design, though. Form fitting enough that I got turned on looking at myself in a mirror, and that’s unusual.”

Vista giggled. “Let me wear one the next time I have to go in for my next patrol. None of the guys would see me as a little girl anymore.”

“Especially with those tits.” Taylor said. “Big enough that it much hurt like a sonuvabitch to bind them.”

“Yeah.” Vista paused. “You say that … like … well, how do I say or ask this?”

“I am bisexual, Vista. I am not sexually aroused by the official Vista look, which is designed to make you look prepubescent. But based on the scans, if I didn’t know you were thirteen -”

“Twelve, actually. Thirteen in May.”

“Even more so. If I didn’t know your basic age, your figure would make me think that you were fourteen at the youngest, and more likely my own age. I turn sixteen in June.” She snickered. “You wear one of the minidress designs as they currently are and I guarantee that you’re going to hear a ‘clang’ from the groin area on at least one set of Ward armor.”

“Why would I hear …” she started to ask, and the sudden dark red blush told Taylor the second that Vista got it. “Oh,” the girl squeaked. Taylor just snickered again. She took a moment to reorient the yacht to properly connect to the ship again, and Vista smiled. “Weird. Gravity in here stayed the same, but if I went by look, I’d think I should be on the ceiling right now.”

“I could shut off the gravity altogether and let you learn how to move in zero gee. Takes a bit, but it’s fun,” she said. “I do that sometimes when it’s just me up here. Using everything I can to train myself to do things properly in order to become a worthwhile captain for my lady.”

“You are doing an excellent job as it is, if only just in your attitudes, Captain,” Enterprise said. “May I assume that you want me to climb back to orbit?”

“You may in fact assume that,” Taylor said. “And you’d be right, even! We’ll be coming aboard proper now.”

“If you weren’t returning to the planet, I’d ask if you were going to don your normal ship’s outfit.”

“I don’t think that Vista’s quite ready for a nude starship captain.” Vista squeaked quietly, and Taylor noted with amusement that the girl did a quick wipe across her bound breasts. “Don’t mean to be too embarrassing, but despite doing it myself God knows how many times, brushing your hands across your breasts as if to make your nipples be less prominent usually has the exact opposite effect. And if that was the reaction you had, thank you.”

“I mostly like boys, but there are a few girls I’ve given a second look to,” she admitted. “If she hadn’t been such a bitch, I’d’ve enjoyed watching Shadow Stalker.”

Taylor calculated for a split second before saying, “Yeah, Sophia had a great ass and halfway decent tits, but her driving personality as an egregious thundercunt overpowered all that.”

Vista looked at her for a moment. “How long have you known?”

“Well, when I woke up on the ship and checked out what was going on as far as Earth was concerned - after the freak-out over effectively having the greatest starship in the universes as my ‘minion’ in parahuman terms - I realized that the PRT was paying more attention to things than if they thought I’d been captured by a parahuman or Triggered myself. Which I did, of course. So I thought for a second or two -”

“And she is capable of using my processors to speed up her thought processes,” Enterprise said as they heard a gentle hum.

“Oh, is that why I think so much faster now?” Upon receiving an affirmative answer, Taylor continued with her previous thought. “Well, that meant someone at the school was noticed by the PRT. It’s one of the worst kept secrets in Brockton Bay that the Wards except for Shadow Stalker and you go to Arcadia. So, if the PRT was paying attention to Winslow and not necessarily because of me, that meant that there was a parahuman likely involved in my Trigger. Emma Barnes is too short and busty for Shadow Stalker, and Madison Clements is to willowy for Stalker. That leaves Sophia Fucking Hess.”

“Makes sense to me, and you hinted to the director that you knew.”

“Officially I don’t,” Taylor replied.

Vista smirked. “Be a pity if you accidentally discovered my civilian identity of Missy Biron,” she said innocently.

“Missy a nickname for something?”

“You’d think so, like maybe Melissa, but my birth certificate says Missy. Like a friend of mine at school whose name is Velvet. Most people think it’s a nickname because of her hair, but she swears it’s her birth name.”

They made it to the bridge where they could see the ship settling back into orbit above Earth. “Shall we head down to the transporter room, Vista-who-in-no-way-could-be-a-girl-named-Missy?” She snorted. “Interestingly, their insistence on Vista being eternally nine helps keep your identity secret. You wouldn’t expect Vista to cause guys to walk into walls when she walks by unless they’re fan-thinging over Wards, whereas Missy Biron would make people impact walls by wearing form fitting clothes.”

“I’m not that sexy,” she replied with a blush.

“I think you are, and kinda wish you were closer to my age so that some of the thoughts I’ve had knowing what you really look like weren’t quite so jailbait-y. Problem with having my libido come back after a couple years of not wanting to deal with anything, and discovering that I’m hanging around sexy girls.”

“We should probably stop this line of thought,” Vista said with a giggle. “As it is, your jacket’s open enough that I can tell that you have a pulse by looking at your chest.”

“Yeah. Always been that way, really, just been amped up a little bit since Triggering. The harder my heart’s beating, the more noticeable, and I did just do public speaking,” she said to Missy, knowing she was stretching the truth regarding her visible pulse.

“Weird side effect.”

“Tell me about it. Other similar side effect means that I can’t wear something skin-tight below the waist. I jokingly trimmed into a heart shape, so now …”

“As long as it’s not harmful,” Missy said as they entered the transporter room.

“Amy’s looked at me and assures me it isn’t.” She motioned to the pads. “Shall we?” A moment later, they were back on Earth, on the platform.

Bagrat (Original Poster) (Veteran Member) (The Guy in the Know)
Posted On Jan 22nd 2011:

You've probably all seen this on the news, since I noticed that CNN, Fox, and all the locals were out in force.

We have the Enterprise in orbit around Earth now. Not the ones from the shows or movies, but a later iteration.

For one of the few times in my life I am nearly at a loss for words.

A local girl, Taylor Hebert (she named herself on stage, so I feel safe in naming her) literally BEAMED onto the stage, where she began to explain some things, such as the fact that she IS a parahuman who will be using the cape name Grey Ghost. She then called on Vista to help her prove that her comments regarding the ship some have showed photos of was, in fact, real.

BY HAVING VISTA OPEN A WARP TO ALLOW IT TO HOVER A MILE ABOVE THE BAY. Video (Sorry for the shouting, but that’s a fuck-huge ship, let me tell you.)

I love the fact that our local Shaker 9 looks happy to do it, but shows absolutely no strain in opening a 'doorway', if you will, to allow a two mile long ship to silently enter Brockton Bay airspace. Once again Vista reminds us that she's as dangerous as she is adorable, and she’s damn near weaponized being adorable.. The warp closed behind the ship. And it says so much about Vista’s power that she could allow the ship through without there being a wind problem from pressure normalization between sea level and outer space.

Grey Ghost then showed that she was in charge of the ship by having it lift that huge container ship that has blocked the bay for years. The bay is blocked no more, and the ship did it with ease. Considering that the original Star Trek Enterprise could likely have done the same without issue (were she atmosphere capable, which at least one episode made clear in TOS that she wasn’t), I can't say that a later generation of ship lifting it easily surprises me. (And rereading that phrase, let me be precise. A later generation of ship lifting it easily does not surprise me.)

From her own description of her power, she has multi-tasking to an insane degree, and is basically a Master: YES in regard to the ship. She says that she can run all consoles on the ship simultaneously. Considering she pointed at the ship and then at the Northern Girl, which led to the tractor beam, I can believe her.

I would normally be scared of someone who has a minion that could wipe Maine from the map with a handful of photon torpedoes, but the emotion in her voice when she talked about the awesome and terrible responsibility of being the latest captain to be in charge of a ship with That Name, and how she was actually scared that she might end up tarnishing that name, I'm not worried. The references to prior captains, such as Captain Garrett, who returned to hell (if you've seen the Next Generation episode Yesterday's Enterprise, you know what I'm talking about) in order to make the universe a better place, knowing it meant her death, and the deaths of her crew. The fact that the crew returned as well, knowing this would happen. That IS a responsibility to live up to, and you could tell by the steel in her spine as she spoke that this young woman will never become a tyrant.

I especially like her reasoning for not making replicators available. Have some higher level math myself, although nothing like the math she’s clearly dealing with, and she's right. Just E=mc2 shows a god-awful amount of energy that needs to be stored in a battery/generator, and can you honestly think that Uber and Leet wouldn't try to get their hands on one of those to power something? I like Brockton Bay where it is, thank you very much, not orbiting the planet in microscopic pieces.

I'd make a Simpsons joke here, but people might take it seriously.

What I will say is this - thank you for helping to restore some of my faith in humanity, Grey Ghost. (And the ship, to be honest.)
