Chapter 23: Monday, February 7th, 2011 - Amy

Chapter Notes

Sorry about not posting last week - it was one of THOSE weeks, and by the time I got my brain wrapped around when it was and that I'd forgotten to post, I decided to just give two this weekend. This one, and the other one will be up by Sunday.

February rolled around with it’s usual cold fanfare, and both D.C. Textiles and D.C. Industries began working in earnest. Taylor was able to have a number of devices built fairly quickly by supplying plans to the dockworkers and letting them build them, purchasing what needed to be purchased, and re-purposing things already in storage at the docks’ warehouses. Her reaction at finding a 1940 Indian Chief was a “Squee!” that was probably heard in Boston. It needed a lot of work, but she claimed it and had it beamed up to her ship to work on. Danny told her that she was not riding it until she had a license. She promised, but told him that she’d be practicing in the holodecks with holographic models, so that she could get used to the feel, and also be in a place where injury was far less likely. Amy had been with her when it was discovered, and had discovered in a couple ways that Taylor was a slight motorcycle enthusiast - first by nearly tearing through the blouse she’d been wearing, and second, by having Taylor kiss her with an appendix-probing kiss that left Amy trying to tear through her blouse. And she’d been wearing a bra, as opposed to Taylor.

Amy looked out over some of the construction. “How is it that they’re getting the building and factories built so fast?” she asked. “I’ve heard of getting the shells up quickly, but the entire facility?”

“A lot of it comes down to the planning. We decided where everything was going to be before anything started, and went from there. You have to remember that the Empire State Building in New York City went from start to business ready in thirteen months. A huge part of that was prior planning and making sure everything was ready before beginning. With having technology available to render the materials gotten from the ships usable for building the office buildings and factories, it makes things much easier. We’re building devices to pretty much clear out the bay and surrounding areas, because to be honest, this area was a major shipping hub since the 1700s. Ships have been sunk and scuttled here for a very long time. We can see what of the wood from those ships might be salvageable, and even if we can’t use it, selling it to people who want old usable timber? There’s money in that as well. There was a naval yard in the Lordsport area, and damn me if that’s not giving us access to stuff. We’re mining - for lack of a better term for it - the crap in the sand and soil that have seeped in over the years. Pull out all that old oil and either purify it for use or use it for plastics and such. Enterprise is helping me figure out how to use as much of the by-products of our construction as possible, so that’s helping out. Between Armsmaster, Dragon, and Enterprise, I think I’m waiting on something like ninety different patents right now, which I think is pissing off some people at the top in the PRT, because none of it is Tinkertech, and they’d really like to lay claim to a lot of it, given how much money the tech is already bringing in. Bian is already starting to deal with the beginnings of the PRT trying to claim it since the person putting in the patents is a parahuman.” She blinked. “That was a lot more alliterative than I expected.” She shook her head, hard enough that Amy enjoyed the very slight sway under the girl’s blouse. She looked up to see Taylor’s smirk. “Why do you think I tend not to wear bra? Anyway, we should be able to put the first production line into use before the end of the month or the beginning of March.”

“What will you be making first?”

“Easiest thing to get going is some of our fabrics, which we’ll be doing over in that building. Still working on a decent name for them, because all the obvious ones are taken.” Taylor laughed at that. “We literally have the paperwork ready to go, we just can’t think of a name. But I’ve been told by Dad and Bian that I have until Sunday the 13th to come up with something or they’ll call it Doctor Curlyhair’s Fabrics. I’ve been wracking my brains over it since then. I’m leaning strongly toward involving the name Brigid somehow, because she was a goddess of not only weaving and things like embroidery, but also smithing of metals, so Brigid Ironmongery, Brigid Weaving, that sort of thing. I’ll throw that past Dad and see what he says. If I make a line of toys or something educational, I might pull out the Doctor Curlyhair line, and use a stylized picture of me as a child. Maybe.”

“If you were as adorable then as you are gorgeous now, then they might have to put warning labels on the packaging,” Vicky said as she came in for a landing next to them. “By the way - thank you for the payment for the designs for uniforms. That was far more than I was expecting, to be honest.”

“I looked up what a fair payment for that sort of work was, as opposed to what some companies try to pay for that kind of work. I mean, not only did you design some decent stuff, you suggested possible materials amongst the ones that you know of. Uniforms will likely be generated by the ship’s replicators at the moment, so some of the material will be different, but largely those work quite well. We may have to make the minidresses a bit less form fitting, though,” Taylor finished with a blush. “When I saw what I looked like in my reflection, well, if someone had told me to go fuck myself at that moment, I’d have said that I would if I could.”

“We told you so!” Amy said with a laugh. “Both that you’re hot as hell, and that people would want to see that on their floors if you wore one!”

Taylor shook her head with an amused smile before looking back to her sister. “Vicky, I like your designs so much that if you decide that you want to go to school for fashion design, I’m willing to sponsor your education, on the agreement that you work for me a certain number of years after you’ve graduated. How’s that sound?”

Amy chuckled as she saw a wide-eyed Vicky vibrating. “I think the answer is going to come out to something like ‘It sounds like we’ll be working with Mom to get a good contract nailed down.’ Right Vicky?” Vicky nodded furiously, looking something like a bobble-head doll before letting out a squee that was almost into canine range.

Amy noticed Taylor cock her head and knew that Enterprise was talking to her about something. Her face went from amused to serious before saying, “Understood. I’ll be up in a few for a briefing. Let me talk to Dad first to let him know what’s going on, then I’ll be up at a minimum. Might bring him and the Dallon sisters as well.” With that, she headed toward her father’s office as she pulled out her old style communicator. “Yeah, I know I could use the uniform one or the implanted one, but there are times I just like the feel of the old style one.” She flipped it open. “Taylor to Dad.” When he answered, she asked, “You in your office? Got a couple things to talk about.” On his affirmative, she politely closed the call then the communicator and continued her process to his office.

“What’s up, Taylor?” he asked her, obviously a little worried.

“Least of all is that I’ve come up with an umbrella name for some of the fabric and metals manufacturing subsidiaries of D.C. Industries, and Textiles, and I’ll leave it to you and the lawyers to see if you can come up with something better. Brigid. She’s the Irish goddess of weaving, embroidery, and metal-smithing, so you can see why that might be good. I joked with Amy about a line of educational toys - the Doctor Curlyhair line, once I’m better known.”

Danny put his head back and laughed. “I love it! Have to do some sort of stylized extra-cute version of you as a child as the mascot.”

Amy couldn’t help but laugh as she said, “She said something very similar out there.”

“Smart girl. I’ll have to look at the various ways we can work with Brigid, because Brigid Fabrics doesn’t quite sing at the moment. But it gives us a starting point, and we’ve actually got some time before we have to finalize. I just set the 13th as a way to keep you from dithering, the way you do sometimes. So what’s the next thing?”

“Last, really. I need to head up to the ship, because she’s figured out a few things regarding the interesting subspace connections we parahumans have in our heads, and I want to find out what they mean. I’m probably going to ask for Amy and Vicky to come along in order to get a second or third opinion. Are you available to come up as well, because it might be a good idea to get a non-parahuman’s take on whatever we learn.”

“How long do you think it might take?”

His communicator chirped, so he answered it. Enterprise’s voice came out of it and said, “I expect no more than an hour, Danny. That would allow you to officially take your lunch hour that you actually worked through today. I can feed you while you’re here as well.”

“How long have you been watching me?”

“Once there was technology near you that I can control. You mean more to Taylor than anything else in the world, so I am doing my duty in keeping you as safe as I can without interfering with you. You work a dangerous job, so I will not affect too much there, but if keeping an eye on you and ensuring that some group of idiots such as your local Nazis don’t stand a chance of bothering you or your workers helps Taylor sleep better, then I will do it.”

“I’m not in bubble wrap, I’m just being monitored for my safety. I can live with that.”

“And I effectively wipe it as it happens unless I recognize that it is an unusual situation, at which I keep the data until I learn whether or not the situation is potential problematic. Which would allow you to approach Miss Doan if you choose to.”

Amy saw Taylor’s eyebrows rise in an almost Vulcan manner. “Is the chasing one-sided, Dad?” she asked in amusement. “Because if you’re interested back at her, I can’t see Mom complaining if you took things a bit further. Given a couple of those nights I can remember when I couldn’t go to the Barnes house for one reason or another. You guys did your best to keep it down, but for multiple reasons, I know what the sound of female orgasms sound like.” She blushed furiously. “If only because of what I was doing while you guys were being a little loud. I know that Mom was the only one you … well, I know that Clarisse and Bian never had problems with your fingers or tongue. Overheard them a couple times when they thought I was further away from them.”

Amy was trying very hard not to laugh at the fact that Danny was now the same color as Taylor. “We’ll talk about that later. Let me tell Ruth that I’m taking lunch and we can go to the ship.”

Within five minutes, the four of them were in a conference room on the Enterprise. “What do you have for me?” Taylor asked.

Enterprise appeared in the same outfit that Taylor had worn on the day of her debut, without the jacket. Amy snickered when Vicky murmured, “Damn, I do good work.”

“Zounds, I forgot modest!” Amy snarked back.

Enterprise chuckled before saying, “Yes, Miss Dallon, you do excellent work, and I wish that I could convince the captain to wear the minidress more often. But that is not why I asked her here.” A transparent hologram of the Simurgh appeared about the table, rotating slowly. “I have finished the examination of the data regarding the object known as the Simurgh. It is not alive in any sense that I have in my databanks, and I ask you to remember that the Federation has dealt with multiple crystalline species before, as well as other non-carbon based lifeforms. This appears to be a simulacrum of life. Not even worthy of being called an android.”

She pointed at one of the wings, which seemed to be the one that Simurgh always kept closest to her body. “The item is at its densest here,” she said, pointing at one specific spot. “What with being able to scan multiple parahumans, I have begun to trace the various feeds from the entities that grant the abilities. In the case of you three, who around me the most, I have made excellent inroads into learning what is happening, and this helped my exploration of the Simurgh. She - although not alive, it is how your world refers to her - is effectively an automaton, and I have not only been able to locate her subspace origin, I have traced communications between her and two others that I believe to be the others that you refer to as ‘Endbringers’. I have also detected another connection to an individual in Houston, Texas. At least when he is on this Earth and not being in an extra-dimensional area I have not yet been able to trace. The communication between this individual and the Simurgh has allowed me to decode a significant amount of the programming behind the Endbringers. He has connections to the other two, but at the moment, the connection is strongest between him and the Simurgh.”

“Did he build them or something?” Danny asked, horrified.

“Not that I can tell. If he did, then they are for him to test his powers against them, because the message, which seems to be increasing in intensity, translates out to variations on ‘Give me a challenging fight.’ It has not reached the threshold necessary to spur Simurgh into motion, but I do not see her not responding to it any later than the end of this month.”

“Okay, two things,” Taylor said while everyone else at the table looked horrified. “One, do you know precisely who the person sending the ‘fight me’ message is, and two, do you have enough information to deal with the Simurgh? Would we be able to use any of her form to help our own stores, for example.” Taylor looked at the others. “If she’s not actually living in any sense of the term, then I see no reason not to use the bitch’s body for something good. If she’s actually as intelligent as my lady here and wants free of her programming, then I help her. If she’s intelligent and evil? She dies and we use her as much as we can.”

“Simurgh is, from my point of view, a dumb program. She is, in her own way, even less than the one you know as Dragon, whom I would dearly like to speak to once I can sever the connection between her and a specific computer system. If Dragon would be destroyed, it would be a death of some sort in my eyes. If Simurgh is destroyed, it would be as if I had destroyed the world’s most expensive university computer system. We will not be killing the Simurgh, we will be ending her program. And I believe that I have enough knowledge to end her. As for the one asking for a fight, releasing that information will likely lead to issues with your Parahuman Response Team and Protectorate, because the signals trace back to an individual you call Eidolon.”

Chapter 24: Monday, February 7th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

Okay, so I didn't get to it until oh-stupid-hundred in the morning on Monday, but to me mentally, it's still Sunday. So have your second chapter this weekend.

Taylor stared at Enterprise. “Come again?” she finally said. “I’ll get back to Dragon being a non-biological intelligence later. But Eidolon is the driving force behind the deadliest things to hit the planet since Chicxulub?”

“It appears so. Once I detected the connection, I began to pay attention to his actions, and he is becoming shorter tempered and more likely to engage in fights. Research shows that people believe this to be due to the knowledge that an Endbringer is likely to appear soon, but it may well be that he has a three month period where his desire to fight increases until it sets off an attack, because the message from him seems to be a command of some sort.”

“Can you block the message from him?” Amy asked.

“Not without getting him into my Sickbay and potentially implanting something in him. I doubt he would be terribly sanguine about that. Also, predicting a question to come, I believe that the time to deal with the Simurgh would best be when she has begun what is called ‘an attack run’. At the moment, Simurgh is capable of running a very large number of processes, and could put up quite a fight. If what I have been able to learn of her programming is correct, however, once she is forced into a course of action, AKA ‘an attack run’, most programming becomes narrowly focused on the attack, and all of those processes are used to make the attack as successful as possible. That will be the best time for us to go after her. I believe that we would be even more successful than might be expected, because Simurgh is apparently not even aware that I exist, despite references in media. I seem to be a literal hole in what she perceives, and as my captain, you are largely the same to her.”

Her father spoke up. “What are the general odds on defeating her now as opposed to when she begins an attack?”

Enterprise said, “I believe that were we to make an attempt before she begins a run, we would have about a seventy-five to eighty percent chance of completely finishing her and being able to render the construct down for useful materials. If we wait until such point that her focus is on a city attack, the likelihood of complete success is at a minimum of ninety percent.”

“I like the sound of ‘minimum of ninety percent’,” he replied with a smile.

“I will be honest with you, Danny, and will say that there is an element of risk no matter the situation, but I believe that allowing her to be ‘distracted’, if you will, gives a much greater possibility of success.”

“As much as I’d love to wrap Taylor in cotton wool and bubble wrap -”

“Which I’d figure out how to pop,” Taylor giggled.

He shook his head with a smile but continued as if she hadn’t interrupted, “I’ve already failed miserably at protecting her once and I’m not stupid enough to go too far in the opposite direction and helicopter parent her now for fear of getting her feelings hurt or something. She may have grown up faster than I like because of her experiences, but she’s … she’s growing into a fine woman, and I trust her. But I may want to be aboard the ship when you attack, just to … just to be there, you know?”

“Now that I’m out as Grey Ghost,” Taylor said, “I’m going to tell the school that there’s a standing order with my ship that if there is an Endbringer attack, I am to be beamed aboard even if I’m in the middle of a class.”

“Can we get that as well?” Amy asked. “If nothing else, I’m pretty sure you could get me anywhere in the world faster than waiting for Strider.” She paused. “Unless whichever Endbringer aimed for Brockton Bay, but we’re so small, and they prefer bigger targets like New York or Boston. Hitting us would be like hitting Alice Springs in Australia. It may be on everyone’s maps, but it’s really just a tiny place, barely big enough to be called a city. It just shows up on maps because of the fact that it’s smack in the middle of the continent.”

“Give us a few years and maybe we’ll be something, but I’m hoping the Endbringers will be dealt with by then,” her dad said.

“One of the things I am hoping for is to be able to use some of the mass stored in the Simurgh to build probes. I believe that I will be able to insert probes into the subspace area that the Simurgh signal is coming from, and possibly those of other parahumans. I have detected that the signals are very similar amongst parahumans, but not precisely the same. I feels almost as if they are going to slight alterations of the same place. But since I have found the other two Endbringers, I can tell that all three have a signal that emanates from the same place, if it is, in fact, a place. And since we don’t have as many probes as I would like, being able to build more would only be common sense.”

“Agreed. I think we’ve done all we can in regard to the Simurgh right now,” Taylor said. “And dealing with her might give us an idea of how to deal with the other two.”

“I wish to trace the Endbringer connection,” Enterprise stated. “A single small probe should do quite well for that, and I suspect would not be noticed at the other end. Have I your permission to do something that might spur Simurgh into activity if what I do is detected, Captain?”

“We’re about as ready as we can be for her attacking wherever, correct? You said we have a three in four chance if we attack her now, so we’re looking good there, although I much prefer the minimum of ninety percent. You want to try to insert a probe to wherever she connects back to in order to learn more, don’t you?”

“Precisely. I strongly suspect that Simurgh will not notice the intrusion, since ‘she’ has not reacted to my appearance in any way. Perhaps I can find the computer that speaks to her and sends her updates, or whatever may be behind her.”

“How soon could you do this?”

“Immediately. This was something I would not do without letting you know in advance, even if I suspected you would permit it. I may have your permission to use as much free will as possible, and doing this thing would fall within that remit from you, but in the end, you are my Captain. If it is not an emergency, then you will be consulted.”

Taylor chuckled. “Let’s go to the bridge for this. Maybe it’s from watching the shows, but I think I’d like to be in the place of power when this starts. Make sense?” Everyone nodded, and they filed from the room, Taylor in the lead.

She heard her father chuckle as they approached a turbo-lift. “I liked walking behind Anne for the same reason,” he said.

“Busted!” Vicky snickered.

“Can you deny that it’s a nice view, Vicky?” Amy asked.

“No. I’ve been enjoying it too, to be honest.”

The doors opened, and as Taylor entered and turned, she pinched the bridge of her nose, trying very hard to hide her blush, leaving her father snickering. “Bridge” was all she said however, and the lift started moving.

When the doors opened, she strode onto the bridge and headed straight for the main chair, sitting without even thinking about it. “Enterprise? Main screen on. Fire the probe when you are ready.” A moment later, there was the sight of a small lozenge rocketing forward before disappearing in a manner that made Taylor think of Vista’s power. “Hmm, need to see if there’s a closer connection other than just getting her powers from elsewhere. Maybe she could use her power to go to other Earths?”

“It is worth checking into,” Enterprise said. “Bringing probe’s signal up on main view screen.”

The screen changed from the view of near-Earth to … something else. The stars visible looked as if it was within the Earth solar system, but the planet beneath was certainly no Earth that they were used to. Below them was a massive crystalline thing that looked as if something had broken the crystal in three different places. All three holes were of a similar size. “The signal from Simurgh leads back to this crystalline device. It appears that there are another seventeen sub-devices in a state of … perhaps hibernation might be the best descriptor?”

Vicky was goggling at the screen. Amy spoke up first. “Wait. There are three broken spots of similar size, and it looks like room for seventeen more, which fits with what you just said. I know that Simurgh isn’t alive, but are you hinting that this is maybe a crèche? Or incubator?”

“If they were alive, I would agree. It would perhaps be better to think of it as a storage facility. As one robot is needed, it is released to its duties. Every time one is needed, it is released. There is no life down there, Amy. I think that once we have dealt with the Simurgh - who, as an aside, does not seem to have noticed our probe incursion - sending in a spread of Quantum torpedoes to deal with that monstrosity below should save us the worry of more Endbringers.”

Taylor noticed her father looking at her with a smile mixed with a mischievous grin. “You know that if you eradicate one Endbringer and show proof that there won’t be any more, you’ll likely be granted a sainthood, whether or not the churches in question have saints?”

“And I’ll also have the Fallen focusing on you and me. And they’re known for things like Mastering a town and telling everyone to kill themselves unless their target arrives.”

“Once we know where they are, I can likely deal with each of their parahumans. While I, like most of the Federation, prefer to avoid killing, I am fully aware that there are those who simply will not listen to reason, and will continue to cause issues. And I believe that I would be incapable of being Mastered.”

Taylor snorted. “Says the being currently Mastered by her captain.”

Enterprise paused, and with a small smile said, “Thank you, Taylor. Not for pointing out that I currently am being Mastered, but for simply treating me as any other being. You’ve said it before, but the simplicity in which you stated it … I know your mind. You didn’t have to think about it.”

“You have emotions and you exist. That makes you sentient. You have intelligence of your own, and that makes you sapient. So what if your physical body is two miles of sexy starship? You exist, and are alive as far as I’m concerned.” She shrugged.

“As for the Fallen, well, if we can figure out where they are, orbital phasers always work.” She paused. “Holy shit, they do. After we FAFO regarding Simurgh, you want to offer to take out places like Ellisburg and Eagleton? I’m betting that your computers are literally generations beyond anything that Eagleton can come up with. Might be able to just shut it all down, or just vaporize down to the bedrock as necessary. I suspect that will be the need for Ellisburg.”

“I believe that my original point stands, however. I am, in the terms of your PRT, a minion on a Master, and my reading tells me that it is very hard to Master a minion that belongs to someone else. Mama Mathers would be the one most needing to be dealt with. I am currently working on methods of at least temporarily severing the subspace connection I detect with all parahumans, but am afraid that it might be fatal when we don’t wish it to be so. I have developed something that should block the signal that seems to ramp aggression, and would like permission to implant the device subcutaneously on both Amy and Vicky, since I was able to activate it via programming on Taylor’s implanted communicator. Although - interestingly enough - I have not noted the aggression signal aimed at my captain.”

“You have one implanted?” her father asked. “Why do you use the hand held one, then?”

“I talk to Enterprise all the time with the implant, but I like the look and feel of the old style communicator.” She shrugged. “Plus, it leads people away from realizing that I can talk to the ship at any time, which means that if someone is stupid enough to kidnap me to try to force me to work for them *cough* Nazis *cough* ABB *cough* I can subvocalize my code phrase, which is highly unlikely to ever come up in natural conversation.” She paused. “Unless it’s a situation like right now, where Enterprise will ignore the usage of the word,” she looked significantly at Enterprise, who nodded, “if you hear me say ‘Abaddon’, then all hell is about to break loose.”

Enterprise added, “And we have tested her subvocalization capabilities. She can subvocalize to me without people around her knowing that she’s speaking. The captain has done it around all three of you without your knowledge.”

“What if some of us say it?” Vicky asked. “Like if she’s been knocked unconscious and can’t say it?”

“Since I keep a constant eye on her vital signs, I will know when she is unconscious. There are few situations that I will be unable to remove her from, largely, and currently, I do not believe that your world has access to the types of force fields required to keep me out. None of the current ones that I have detected, such as your Rig, are capable of keeping me out for very long.”

Taylor snorted. “Which is why that word is a call for ‘Take cover!’, because it means that I really need whatever it is dealt with right now. So, on to the concept of implanting a tiny doohickey - technical term, mind you - to cut down on the aggression?”

“Given how much better I flew when Enterprise dampened it that time? Hell yeah!” Vicky said, flying out of her seat. Literally.

“I’m agreeable as well,” Amy said. “I don’t know how it’s affected me since I Triggered. Might be the reason I’m so damned snarky to most people.”

“You’ve been snarky for as long as I’ve known you, Ames, so I doubt that.”

“As I said,” was Amy’s only response.

Vicky looked at her for a long moment before saying, “I thought you Triggered when I was injured by all that falling debris back when you were thirteen.”

“Nope. Triggered the day some people broke into my Dad’s house and threatened to destroy the closet I was hiding in.” She locked eyes with Vicky. “Worst day of my life.” Vicky’s response was to put both hands to her mouth for a second, then swoop forward and engulf Amy in a hug, which Taylor could see Amy relax into.

“And Mom worries about you taking in his footsteps because she’s a bigot, not realizing that you’ve had how many years on not turning her inside out? Never think you’re not a hero, Ames. No matter what Mom thinks.”

“She does make it kind of obvious.” Amy turned to Taylor after Vicky reluctantly let go of her. “Captain? I know that I’m not up to snuff on everything, but I think it’s in my best interests to join up with your fleet, which is currently a fleet of one. May I begin the process of on-boarding as a crewman?”

“I am not telling you no, Amy, but I want you to think for a few more days, just to be sure, okay? Talk to me again Friday, and if you still feel that way, I’ll welcome you aboard as crewman.”

“I’m going to think about this as well, Captain Hebert,” Vicky said. “Mom’s been okay, but … I don’t like some of her attitudes recently. I may ask on Friday as well, if that’s okay.”

“Same deal as Amy. If you feel that way on Friday, I welcome two new crew to the Enterprise.”

Chapter 25: Monday, February 7th, 2011 - Taylor

Once in the Sickbay, it was literally a hypospray to get the device injected behind both girls right ears. Taylor then looked at Amy and asked, “Willing to some of the work we’ve talked about regarding augmentation and carbon fiber armoring?”

“Once we’ve got some material to work with, yeah,” she said, brightening up. It almost seemed to Taylor as if her power was the one that had perked up and passed that along to Amy.

“What would work best, Amy?” asked Enterprise.

“Well, if I was affecting bone structure and repairing, I’d say uncooked meat with the bone in, but we’re altering a lot of stuff to organic compounds that the body is capable of continuing production of with very minor tweaking. So, if you’ve got them available, maybe some onions? Any kind, mind you. Their cell structure is dense enough and easy enough to work with.”

“Chopped and uncooked?” Enterprise asked. When Amy gave the affirmative, a crate containing what was likely a few hundred pounds of chopped onions appeared in the room right next to one of the Sickbay beds.

It was then that her father spoke up. “If anything is being done, it’s being done to me first to make sure that it’s safe. Taylor is the captain, so she should only be worked on after the procedure is proven to be good.” He looked to Amy. “Everything looks and sounds good, but remember that we’re working off technology that the Federation disavows, and in fact made illegal, if I remember that Deep Space Nine episode correctly. So they may not have done enough documentation.”

She nodded at him, smiling. “Thank you. I knew that you weren’t making a comment about my healing abilities. That’s just not you.” She took a deep breath, and Taylor tried to break the mood by clapping, which just made Amy shake her head in a ‘Why me?’ gesture, although she was smiling. “What I was looking at doing was changing the nerves to a faster medium and the bones and muscles to something that reacts faster and is more robust. I suspect that when I’m done you’ll end up with a Brute 3 or 4 rating, if not higher, and possibly a Mover rating that would likely not go any higher than 2. In the beginning I’ll leave you awake, but if this takes a while and seems to be going well, then I’ll simply make you doze off while I finish. I also suspect that I’ll only be able to do one of these a day to start, until I get used to what I’m doing. You are, unfortunately, my test subject.”

“I trust you. Shall we get started?”

Vicky piped up, “You were supposed to add a ‘Muahaha!’ at the end when you called him your test subject, Ames!” Taylor and her father couldn’t help but snicker, and they saw Amy hiding the smile as she did the ‘Why me?’ head shake again.

“Embarrassingly for you, Mr -”

“Danny. And I need to be as unclothed as possible, don’t I?” Amy nodded. “Well, needs must,” and he started to take off his shirt right there. Vicky’s eyes went wide and she fled the room with a bright red face.

“She doesn’t want to see the proof of just why you made Mom walk bow-legged sometimes,” Taylor said with a laugh. “I’ll join her, since I’d imagine it’s going to be embarrassing enough for the two of you as it is.” She walked toward the door, offering a jaunty salute into the air as she left.

“You guys really don’t worry much about clothes, do you?” Vicky asked.

“Well, he started wearing more when he noticed that his daughter was starting to notice the difference between boys and girls, but with my Mom around, for the longest time growing up, clothing was just a thing we wore sometimes. But yeah, I kinda hope he’s out cold when she gets working waistline and below, because she’s going to be dealing with all musculature.” At Vicky’s confused look, Taylor said, “Remember that they call that part of a guy’s body a muscle. I think it actually is. And Dad is … well, lets just say that if he wears a Speedo, no one will ever make comments about him being small. He’s … noticeable. And if things go the way I think they’re going to with the lawyer we’ve known for years, he’s going to finally make Bian very happy. I know I overheard her talking with Mom about how lucky she was to get to ‘deal’ with that particular muscle. I suspect that Amy’s going to get a ‘big’ surprise in multiple meanings of the word.”

“Now, what say that we go to the holodeck and check out your flying? I need to get some practice in, and I really don’t think that Amy’s going to be doing a *POOF* and he’s done sort of thing. That should take a while, and Enterprise will let me know when she’s nearing completion.”

“Let’s,” Vicky agreed. “I can already feel at least a little difference in my attitudes. I wonder if this will help me lose the Collateral Damage Barbie nickname.”

“That’ll probably stick with you for a while, I’m sorry to say. Now, here we are at the nearest holodeck … and I need to move a motorcycle first. Found it when we were going through crap at the docks, and I’m going to see about fixing it up and maybe giving it anti-gravity capabilities or something.” The door opened to show the 1940 Indian there in all it’s … glory? It really did need work, and she hadn’t really had the time to put in on it recently. She rolled it out into the hallway and looked carefully at it. “Cataloged all the issues, love?” she asked the ship.

“Yes, Taylor. Luckily I will be capable of producing the necessary components to allow for flight capabilities. Do you wish me to place orders for the parts that will need to be replaced?”

“We’ll talk about that after Vicky and I take a flight or two around the solar system in a shuttle. We’ll be switching off flight and landing duties, to make sure we’re both good on them.”

“Do you wish the Earth system I originated in, or this universe’s? I have some fairly complete scans of this system now.”’

“As much as I would love to explore Spacedock, I think this universe is better, because we wouldn’t do any flying, we’d be running around looking at what Spacedock looked like, and what that Earth looks like from orbit. This way, before we actually take this ship out of orbit, we can get a look at places like Jupiter and Pluto.” Taylor actually bounced on her heels a little bit. “I really want to visit Pluto for real someday. Gods, need to see if Neil DeGrasse Tyson wants a ride on … what am I saying, of course he’d want a trip in a bonafide Start Trek ship! Saw a video of him extolling the design at a science fiction convention. And if that doesn’t tell you damned near everything you need to know about how cool the dude is, nothing will.” She shook her head. “Enterprise, I know that you’ve been dealing a little bit with the military and such, but can you add to the list to try to get in touch with both Mr Tyson and the surviving Apollo 13 astronauts? I would love to give all three of them the chance to walk on the Moon, especially the two who were supposed to but never got the chance.”

“Notes made - you had already mentioned the Apollo astronauts - and I shall begin initial contact for Mr Tyson. We are working on scheduling for Mr Lovell and Mr Haise. May I also suggest that rather than the original power source you were thinking of, that we give the necessary people the information that they need to make fusion power plants a reality? Current non-Tinker science is extremely close to the necessary breakthroughs, so giving that slight nudge would be less of giving them the technology and more giving them the next step that they are currently dancing around without actually seeing.”

“The answer’s right there, but they keep looking to either side, so to speak?” Vicky asked.

“Effectively correct,” Enterprise said. “Now, shall I activate the training program for shuttle flight?”

“Indeed,” Taylor said in a pretend posh tone, spoiled by immediately giggling.

The door opened to show what looked to be the Enterprise shuttle bay, with the shuttle Cochrane sitting open, waiting for both girls to enter it. As they did, Vicky insisting that Taylor enter first - being captain, after all - the shuttle door closed behind them.

As they sat, Taylor taking the right seat and leaving Vicky the left, she looked out at the simulated view of outer space. The holodeck was amazing - you had to actively release the protections in order to do something truly dangerous. If you did disable the interlocks and such, then it was quite possible to die in outer space while inside the ship. They were not releasing said interlocks - if they made a mistake they were just going to end up on their butts in a blank holodeck.

“Care to take us out, future Ensign Dallon?” She watched Vicky straighten in her seat, the same way she knew she did when it fully struck her that she was actually captain of this amazing vessel.

“Aye, Captain,” was the response. Vicky followed words with action, and expertly took them out of the shuttle bay. Once outside and away from the ship, she asked, “Where to, Captain?”

“Got a planet you’ve always wanted to see close up?”

“Everyone always says Mars, but I’d like to look at Saturn, to be honest. God liked it so he put a ring on it.”

“He must’ve really liked it. Saturn’s got multiple rings. Well, lay in a course and take us there.” Watching Vicky work the console, Taylor knew that design was going to be a secondary for Vicky. The girl was a natural at everything about flying Starfleet vessels. Her fingers flew over the console, and a moment later, they were warping toward Saturn, which really only took seconds to get there.

The view was amazing, and Vicky breathed, “I can’t wait until I can do this in a real shuttle. This looks so real, Captain.” Taylor smiled when she realized that Vicky had taken the ‘future ensign’ bit to heart, and was acting as if she was a crew member already.

“I know. I want to get some of the important stuff dealt with, like the Endbringers, and getting the tech climbing slowly, but we’re going to take short trips to nearby systems, like Sirius and the Centauri systems, which are both less than ten light-years away. Trips to places like Betelgeuse will be a bit longer, since that’s approaching 700 light-years. Might even visit Epsilon Eridani, since its system is so like ours and it’s a smidge over 10 light-years away.” She snorted. “Also, for the longest time, fanon said that Vulcan was in that system - or was it 40 Eridani? - so it might be interesting to see if the system actually has life there.” She shook her head. “But yeah, once we’ve got some stuff under control, day trips to Saturn and Neptune and the planet that makes everyone giggle when they say the name? Easily doable.”

They floated there for a while before Taylor asked if Vicky minded if she flew them back, since she needed to practice her landings. She’d discovered that was learning everything - even physical skills - at an accelerated rate, and her landings were much better now. She’d even tried it a few times with real shuttles - just going out and coming right back in with Enterprise ready with tractors and repulsors in case it looked to be a bit … bumpy. “Switch seats?” Vicky asked.

“Nah, I’ll just drive British style on the way back,” she replied with a grin. Her programming was not nearly as fluid and dancelike as Vicky’s had been, but it got the job done. A few seconds later they were looking at the ship, and Taylor maneuvered them around and slipped into the shuttle bay. There was a noticeable bump as they landed, but it was not a heavy one. It was actually a fairly standard landing for a pilot. Taylor suspected that Vicky would manage it so that couldn’t tell they’d touched down until they powered things off.

The two did some more practice, intentionally mimicking issues with the shuttle, and Vicky continued to prove that she was a natural. Taylor could connect to the equipment, but there was just something about flying that made Vicky better at handling of the shuttle, as odd as that seemed. She thought it might be in interesting area of study at some point. Eventually they received a call from Enterprise, stating that Amy was nearing the end of her work on Taylor’s father., so they closed things down, put the Indian back in the shuttle bay, and headed back toward Sickbay.

“Just curious,” Vicky asked. “Why are you storing it in there?”

“Because when it comes time to do the work to restore and upgrade it, I can just have the holodeck become a work area for it, or just generate the necessary tools. Never have to worry about losing a socket wrench or socket that way, either!” Vicky nodded at the logic.

Amy was blushing slightly as they entered Sickbay, and Danny was seated on the bed, looking fit and trim. Amy had probably used a little bit of what extra he’d been building around his middle. His shirt was still open, and he smiled at Taylor. “She did a bit of a tune-up on me, and I think I’m going to have to ask Enterprise to make me a new set of clothes. The pants are a little tight now, and so’s the shirt.”

“I also … well, externally he’s the same age, but with all the work, he’s about nineteen or twenty again,” Amy said.

Taylor laughed. “And between your work on him and what I’ve heard is the case about guys that age, Dad gave visual proof that he can satisfy any woman with his … accoutrement?”

“I’m not that big,” he said.

“Bian, Clarisse, and Mom all stated within my hearing that you are at least above the national average. I think I heard some reference to the numbers seven or eight at one point? Not to mention that there was one time I never mentioned to you, but I saw you push Mom up against the wall. She knew I was there, and none of the three of us were clothed.” She cocked an eyebrow at the man and laughed as he blushed.

She turned to Amy. “So how’s it working?”

“Depends on the ‘it’ you’re talking about, because the one you were just referring to is beyond my remit to test.” She blushed slightly, and Taylor wondered if perhaps she was a little tiny bit less lesbian than she thought. “I’ve got him turned down to human norms, with a slow lessening of the - blockage? Resistance? Impedance? - over the next month. He’ll basically day by day be a little stronger and faster. His thought processes are already sped up, and his reactions will be improved. And even nude he can withstand small arms fire, and probably most rifle and shotgun rounds. Not the really heavy stuff, but most of what the gangs around Brockton use. He won’t be happy, because it’ll still hurt and bruise, but it won’t go through him.” She smiled. “And I can tell that the body can deal with it, because I could already detect his body working on making some of the new cells. I’m too tired to do it again today, but I think I could give you the same process tomorrow or later. Vicky after that a day later. It’ll be faster the next time, because I know what to do now, but it’s still a lot. In a very real sense, I’m rebuilding the entire body.” She thought for a moment. “Sorry, but we went a little past your one hour lunch time.”

“Speaking of which,” Enterprise said, “I may have an idea for allowing you to use your power on yourself. May I create a device to wear on your skin as a test? If it works, it would be easy to make it implantable if you wished. It should not prevent you from affecting others with your power; it should just allow you to affect yourself as well.”

“It would be nice to be able to heal myself,” Amy said. “I’m game.” About a minute later, a sparkle deposited a device that looked a lot like a wristwatch on the bed next to Danny. Amy reached out and put it on, and Taylor raised an eyebrow at the immediate reaction. First off, Amy’s pupil dilated widely, followed almost immediately by her saluting the inside of her bra. She held out her hand and it was suddenly darkening, followed by returning to its normal shade.

“I’ll have to test more, but it certainly seems like I can affect myself now.” She pulled out her shirt a little and mumbled, “Make a few changes around here.”

“Not too much,” Taylor said without shame. “I’m rather a fan of the size they are now. Doing something like Vicky’s would look wrong on your frame, because you’re not really built for double-D cups. Vicky looks amazing with them, but you’d look like you were in danger of toppling over all the time. Maybe go with a solid C, but no bigger.” When Amy gave her an amused look, she replied, “I know what I like, and I do have an eye for art. And a C-cup would look a bit big on you. B-cup for the win.” She waggled her eyebrows at Amy at that, which set the girl to what sounded like soul-cleansing laughter.

Chapter 26: Tuesday, February 8th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Taylor snickered as she came into school. Amy had apparently decided to do a couple things overnight, and had possibly listened to Vicky as far as clothes were concerned, because the girl was wearing a white suit jacket with the International Red Cross symbol that she wore on her costume over a noticeably thin white blouse, and a knee-length skirt that matched the jacket. Taylor could tell that it was a thin blouse, because she could detect a hint of skin color through it, and - more importantly - no hint of a bra under it.

She walked over and kissed her quickly before they entered the school. “Your decision, or Vicky’s, to go bra-less today?” Taylor asked her quietly. “And may I say ‘Yum!’?”

“Well, I stood in front of a mirror and play - let me rephrase it to avoid all the same jokes Vicky made - I stood nude in from of a mirror and used my ability to see what looked best for me. You were right about C-cups, so I’m bigger now, but still just barely qualify for B-cup on the large side.” She blushed. “I really like the work I did on your nipples, shape and all, so I have the same, although I think I made my actually nipples a bit longer and thicker.” Amy blushed suddenly, and Taylor realized it was because her pupils had dilated and she’d unconsciously licked her lips. “And while I didn’t do the added erotic ‘silliness’, as you call it, I do like the looks of the trim, so mine is also heart-shaped now. It just doesn’t pulse softly.”

Amy sighed. “Carol’s going to freak, I know. She was out of the house early this morning, because it looks like they’re finally about to get Emma Barnes before a judge by next week. She was bitching about Alan trying to figure out how to legally stop things to keep his daughter out of court.”

Taylor sighed. “That means we’re going to see him for the first time in a couple years, now that it’s something that affects him.” She shook her head. “By the way, let me know if anything hurts during the day,” she said with a half-lidded look. “I promise to kiss it and make it feel better.”

“Ow,” Amy whimpered. “You said that right at a point when you can’t kiss them, dammit!”

“I really am sorry,” Taylor said. “You’re just … well, I’m not the only one gonna cause hard-ons today.” They headed into the school and to homeroom.

At lunch, Charlie looked at Amy and said with a little bit of a purr, “You should open the jacket more, Amy. It’s kinda warm in here, isn’t it?” To everyone’s surprise, Amy thought for a second and slipped the jacket off her shoulders and carefully placed it in her bag. Charlie’s eyes widened, and she was not the only lesbian in view who was suddenly stress testing their bras and blouses. Charlie whispered, “Are your nipples actually heart shaped?” Amy just corrected her with the one word “Areolae” and set about eating her lunch as if she hadn’t just become the talk of the entire school with that jacket maneuver.

One of the female teachers came over to her. “Miss Dallon? Your blouse is … perhaps a little thin?”

“Well, I’ve done some growing, and almost none of my bras fit anymore. Wasn’t going to spend the day in pain by wearing one of them. The one that did fit well, I managed to stain while getting dressed - got it soaking in a dish detergent and vinegar thing that should get the stain out - and I really didn’t think that using ‘don’t have a bra’ was a valid excuse for not coming into school. Maybe I’m distracting, but I’ll have different clothes tomorrow, and I’m doing some shopping after school for better fitting bras. Jacket was just warm enough that I wanted to cool off a little.”

The teacher listened and nodded, then walked away. After she was out of view, Charlie nearly whispered, “What a load of bullshit!” with a giggle. “Our proper, perfect Amy just lied to the teachers!” She waggled her eyebrows. “And enjoyed it, because those baby feeders are a bit more noticeable now.”

Amy bit her lower lip and said, “I guess that since I’m not feeling as angst-y and angry today, I’m getting a little bit of Vicky’s exhibitionism. And I wasn’t lying about shopping for new bras. If they also happen to be sexy bras, well, that’s something different, right?”

“If blaming it on me means that you starting showing that you’re one hot mama, then blame away,” Vicky said with a laugh. “Just maybe don’t wear the blatantly diaphanous blouse tomorrow.”

“True, but part of it was for once intentionally showing off. You’ve commented about some other times when I got attention, but today I wanted the attention. And yes, I’m finding the attention exciting in more than a single meaning of the word.”

Taylor smiled at her. “Now, a complete change of subject. I’m heading to the docks after I’m done here today, because I need to look up the best place for the power plant I want to get running. Get a small one going to power Brockton Bay and environs.”

“Where are you getting the oil?” Deena asked.

“Cracking the sea water until I can get a good Helium-3 mining operation going in the solar system. What I get out of the sea water can be used elsewhere as well.”

Most of the people listening looked confused until Charlie gasped deeply. Taylor had to admit that it certainly was a pleasant sight, given the girl’s measurements. Plus, she was apparently wearing a bra, but it was a half-cup, given that Taylor could not only detect lace, but a very clear outline of nipple under that blouse, given that she obviously liked what she’d just realized. “Holy shit!” she breathed. “You’re going to set up a fusion plant to power the city!” It was all said quietly to avoid the entire school hearing it.

Taylor tapped her nose. “Yup. Realized that the people studying it are sort of looking around the piece they’re missing, so we’re pointing them in the right direction, and will use this small plant as a proof of concept. Also have to check out the business buildings, because those should be ready very soon. I’m expecting to be able to begin work in them by the end of the month, the beginning of March at the absolute latest. I want us in decent operation by the time tax day arrives.”

The tone sounded to let the students know that they had fifteen minutes before they needed to be in their next class. Taylor, who was doing the various shops until her ‘internship’ could be brought on-line, was scheduled for wood shop next period, before she was finished for the day. She was really tempted to join Amy for shopping, if only to see some of the underwear she was going to buy, but smiled as she remembered that she’d end up seeing it at some point anyway.

“Thinking about joining Amy for her shopping?” Charlie asked.

“Have to admit that it sounds like a great idea.” She looked at Amy and waggled her eyebrows at her, getting a cute blush from the girl. “But, pernicious honesty forces me to just wait until she’s willing to give me a fashion show later, while I go off and slave over changes at the work sites.” She threw the back of her hand to her head melodramatically at the end.

The other two simply giggled and everyone headed off to class. After Taylor’s wood shop class, wherein she began to get a good grasp on how to use a lathe - from the school’s point of view, this meant that she could hold the tools without danger to herself or others, and that she could affect the wood without accidentally carving through and splitting it into two pieces. If she worked it more she might be able to turn it into a miniature bowling pin. The teacher nodded. “I like that you pick up on things quickly.”

“I think my power allows me a little cheat, because it needs to learn stuff fast in order to be able to deal with my ship. So I pick up skills faster.” She grinned. “Just gives me reason to learn new things!”

He laughed. “Now that’s proof that you deserve to be captain of that ship! Your immediate thought is that you can learn new stuff all the time.” After a pause he said, “I’ve heard some of what you’re doing, and I don’t know if me saying it means squat to you, but I’m proud of you for deciding to revitalize the Bay. My family’s been here for generations, and before, I was worried we’d have to leave to let my daughters have a chance. I know it’s only been a couple weeks at most, but just knowing that you’re trying to do something for us has put a lot back into the community. Someone that most would see as a ‘snot-nosed kid’ deciding that her city’s worth fixing? Helps kick us old fogeys in the butt.”

“It really does mean something, Mr Conners. My dad says it and it means something, but there’s always that thought that family’s supposed to be proud of what you do, even if it’s planting a tree that ends up at a forty-five degree angle the way you planted it. Not that anything like that ever happened to me,” she said with mock innocence, making him laugh. “But someone who has no reason to make you feel good saying it? It means I’m doing the right thing. Thank you. It means more than I can really put into words, despite how much I seem to like to talk.” She grinned at the end, getting another laugh out of him. She waved as she left the class, and headed out of the school for the Lordsport docks area.

She gave Amy a quick kiss as they exited the school, and Charlie gave a quick, happy “Aww!” at it, and Taylor made a quick decision. “If you feel like coming up to the ship after your shopping is done, and Charlie happens to be with you, bring her along. I bet she’d love to see Earth from space.”

Amy snickered. “Trying to make her need to buy a new blouse because she ripped through that one?”

“Gotta admit that it’s a nice view,” was Taylor’s innocent reply.

“Charlie or Earth?” Vicky asked.

“Honestly?” Taylor said, looking at Charlie. “I’d give the same answer either way.” She smiled, then beamed to the ship before beaming back down to the docks.

“Captain,” Zephron said to her with absolutely zero mockery. She smiled at him and nodded. She’d always liked the big guy, and she had always admitted to herself that he was probably the reason she got a little weak-kneed for muscular guys. A nearly seven foot tall man who looked like he should have a Brute rating enough to bend steel? She’d had a crush on him since before hormones hit, and had hidden it as well as any prepubescent kid could. He had always treated her with respect though, so between her father and Zephron’s attitudes, any male who ended up in her romantic orbit was going to have a fairly intense board to get the okay from, and was damned well going to need to treat her the way her dad and Zephron did. Right now, it seemed that only the girls seemed to be able to manage that. Still, she had to admit to herself that if Zephron ever asked her to bend over to ‘inspect something on the floor’, she’d have no issue doing it. She’d certainly fantasized it enough over the years.

She shook her head and headed to the offices to talk to her father. Bian was sitting on his desk talking as she entered the room. “Hey Taylor! Was just explaining the various things going on legally. Hess has disappeared into the PRT system somewhere, so either we have the exceedingly low likelihood that they’re disciplining an unruly intern their own way, or we’re looking at them getting Shadow Stalker out of the way. Our lawyers have made it clear that we know what the answer is there, and that we expect them to play ball. We understand that the local office is probably getting push back from on high, so we’re not going too badly after them, but we are insisting that they offer a significant compensation in order to keep us from demanding the information in open court where anyone could get their hands on it. We’re also hinting that Washington’s budget take the hit, since Brockton Bay has enough troubles, and that the PRT ENE has been doing everything as by the book as possible.” She chuckled. “Unofficially, I’ve been made aware that Shadow Stalker was forced on them and they’d have just sent her to jail for her previous shit, but were told that she could be an asset at the local level.”

“The Board of Education is bouncing back and forth with us, but I’m expecting a final offer from them before March. They started with something insultingly low, and I responded with insultingly high, but not so high that they’d immediately dismiss any talks with us. We’ve been bouncing back and forth on it, and we’ll like end up with enough money to send any kids you and Amy have to college even after the both of you get a couple PhDs each. They wanted an agreement to absolve the entire educational group in Brockton Bay from wrongdoing, but we pointed out that their request would end up saying that the various people at Winslow did nothing wrong from a teaching point of view, and there’s a lot of evidence otherwise. We’re likely going to come to the agreement that we don’t blame the entire Board for the assholes at Winslow hiding what they were doing from them.”

Taylor shrugged. “I can deal with that. I personally like the idea of making sure that Blackwell has an issue getting a job flipping burgers at a White Castle, but I’m not sure we can deal with that in the courts.”

“No, but considering the criminal evidence I’ve been made aware of, she’s going to have a number of years before she has to worry about getting a job. Embezzlement and bribery are things that often get you serious jail time if you’re not a multi-millionaire. The fact that her records show that she knew how bad the school was bullying-wise also will give her issues and a likely increase in time behind bars. I’m talking to my friends in the criminal side and trying to convince them to push for consecutive rather than concurrent sentences.”

“Clements and her family are pretty much going to skate. She’ll get a slap on the wrist and some community service if she testifies against the school and Barnes. She kept a record that she pretty much approached the cops with before they could talk to her, so she’s gonna save her own ass.”

Taylor shrugged. “She’s a complete and utter bitch, but she’s doing like any of the wannabe school queen bees - cover thine own ass first. Her worst shit against me was just tacks and glue and stuff. It was Emma and Sophia who did the nasty and breaking shit, and pouring crap on me. Madison was words more than anything else.” She grinned a nasty grin. “But she’ll never make it on board my ship, and that more than anything else, is going to drive her crazy. She’ll tell people she knows or knew me, but the slightest research will show the truth. She’ll have to pay in order to see space, if I open up any sort of tours.”

Charlie squealed happily and showed that she was a gearhead, because her now noticeably larger nipples made themselves very obvious. “You’ve got a 1940 Indian motorcycle you’re rebuilding? Can I … may I help?”

Taylor giggled and said, “I was going to say yes either way. Any of you who want to help me rebuild it can be involved. I’m completely replacing the engine with a more modern one. Enterprise G modern, I mean.”

Amy opened her eyes wide. “Aren’t you going to have an issue keeping it on planet if you open it full throttle?” she asked with a laugh.

“Well, since if I’m going full throttle I intend to be off planet … turns out that the engine area can be filled with a custom designed unit that will give gravity, full life support, and motive power up to point oh one C. Get you to Mars in six minutes, or twenty maybe if it’s on the other side of the Sun.”

Amy laughed as Charlie said, “I shouldn’t have asked for the pulsing Amy, because after hearing that, not only can I feel my heart against my ribs, but it feels like it’s trying to pound out through my nipples. Traveling the solar system on a motorcycle? Holy shit do I want to do that!”

“Well, I’m going to change the seat out for a two-seater, so I could always add a two-person sidecar to it. Take all four of us out to Mars?” She waggled her eyebrows. “And given how comfortable we all are together and the fact of full life support, we could even due nude solar system tourism.”

“Except for spacesuits,” Amy said, mildly unhappy at not being able to walk another planet completely starkers. The fact that it made her unhappy surprised her a little.

“Ever watch the animated Star Trek show? The one where James Doohan and Nichelle Nichols did almost all the extra voices? The movies had those clunky suits because the viewers expected it, but the animated series had forcefield belts. Guess what? We don’t have to worry about movie budgets and what the viewer expects!” Taylor replied happily, bouncing in her seat. Amy had to admit, that was very nice to watch.

“Also, for those interested, I may just replicator up space capable bikes for just us, if you want.” She got a slightly shy look as she said, “Can’t say as I’m going to complain if any of you insist on riding behind me with your arms around my waist instead.”

“We can do both!” Vicky said. “Obviously not at the same time, but I wouldn’t mind learning to ride. Need a license, though, if I rode it on Earth.”

“Well, I’ve been practicing up here in the holodecks, which is nice, because if you do something that should be fatal, it just means that the scenario stops and you end up bouncing lightly on your butt on the floor. I’m actually to a point where, if I was sixteen, I could go and get my driver’s permit and motorcycle license. But having to wait until June means I get to have even more practice.”

“More practice is always good,” Charlie said. “I remember that you said you weren’t going to be doing replicator stuff up here to sell down on Earth, right?” She blinked, and Amy giggled, because she knew what Charlie was thinking before she even said it, because they all had that reaction at least once. “I can’t believe that I get to make a comment like that and have it be a serious one. ‘Down on Earth’.” The girl jumped up and ran to the window to look down at Earth. “I’m in fucking space!” she shouted joyfully.

Enterprise snickered. “Given what was going on in here a little while ago, I think ‘fucking’ was the only thing not happening, and only because no one is equipped that way yet.”

Vicky’s face fell slightly. “Not for me yet. Not because I think it’s wrong or anything, but I have to remember the relationship with Dean. I have to let him know that I’m with you guys as well. He may insist on monogamy, but I don’t want to give you guys up.”

“I am not saying you should,” Charlie said, “in fact, I’m saying the opposite, really, but you need to think about your relationship with him. You guys are always on-again, off-again. You need to figure out why.”

Amy nodded, then added with a comical leer she hoped Vicky would understand, “Besides, we can always console you if things go badly.” Her voice was low and as sleazy as she could make it, which just made it even more comical. She got the hoped-for giggle from Vicky.

Taylor jumped in. “Never did get to the fashion show, and it’s a bit late for that now.” She frowned. “Charlie. Do you have clothes for overnight?”

“As in nightclothes? I sleep nude.”

“Sister!” Taylor interjected with a laugh. “I do too! Have since I was a little girl.”

Charlie chuckled. “If you’re talking about something I could wear to school, well, I’ve got all new bras and panties, and the school might look a little sideways at me ‘cause the skirt I’m likely to wear is gonna be a little on the short side, but at least it’s not one of those anime panty shot skirts. Basically shows a little more leg than I usually do, but should fall within school guidelines.” She looked down at her new nipples and said, “No fuckin’ way I can hide these new ones, so I’m not going to try. Not going to accentuate them the way I know I can -”

“- and have,” Vicky said. “Much to the enjoyment of many.”

“- and have, as she says. Wear a bra that’ll cover as best as possible, and one of my thicker blouses. They can’t complain too much, because my nipples are pretty much always hard. Had it out with one of the teachers once, because she was offended by my always being pointy.”

“Yeah,” Vicky said. “Wickins doesn’t work there anymore, and I’m not sure she ever got another job.”

Taylor raised an eyebrow. “Evelyn Wickins? Would probably have been fired when you were thirteen or fourteen?”

“She worked at Winslow,” Amy said flatly in realization before brightening up. “Not anymore!”

“Well, we’ll find you a cabin of your own, and we can go from there,” Taylor said. “Girls, want to leave your purchases up here, so that your mother doesn’t have a shit fit over sexy clothes?”

“Sounds good to me,” Amy said. Before she could move, her clothes disappeared from the table, as did Vicky’s.

Enterprise looked to Charlie. “As opposed to previous versions of the Enterprise, I can do intraship transports of smaller items and groupings with ease. Don’t really want to get past a couple people at a time, though, just because … well, to be honest, it makes people lazy if they can just use the transporters from anywhere. But once you’ve got a cabin of your own, I’ll be able to do the same thing for you.”

Amy smiled and said, “Why not choose the cabin on the other side of the Captain’s? I took the one to the left when facing the door from the hallway side, and Vicky’s to my left from there. You take the one to the right.”

“I like it!” Taylor said. “Surrounded by sexy women! Yes!” She did a fist pump at the statement, drawing laughter from them all. Amy could see that Taylor had been hoping for that, because she knew that Charlie was still a little worried about everything.

Chapter 29: Wednesday, February 9th, 2011 - Taylor

Taylor was scowling. The Dallon sisters had come to school in a grumpy mood, and had said simply, in unison, “Mom/Carol.” Charlie and Taylor had beamed down together, with Charlie being chipper, but immediately went to see what she could do to help, which made the girls smile at her concern. She contacted Enterprise and told her to make sure that she had all the ducks lined up nicely, because there was an excellent chance they were going to have to use their ammo to get Amy and possibly Vicky free from Carol Dallon.

Charlie’s new look was catching some attention, because it was obvious that she’d had something of a tune-up. Somehow people were actually noticing her breasts last, which just confused Taylor, because she thought everyone - especially the guys - went for the tits and noticed that there were people attached to them later?

What had her bothered the most had nothing to do with appearances of people, but the fact that she knew that the Barnes family was almost assured to show up and try to make nice with her, followed by threats from Alan if they couldn’t manage to save Emma. And she dislike deven thinking about Emma these days. “Maybe I’ll make the point to them by calling her ‘your daughter’ instead of Emma,” she mused during lunch.

“Probably better than ‘Boobs-and-Butt Barnes’,” Vicky quipped. “They coming over to your place tonight?”

“They haven’t called ahead to my knowledge, but if they want to try to prevent her sitting in court on Monday, they need to do it by tomorrow to allow the paperwork to go in on Friday.” She rubbed her hand down her face. “This has to be a Wednesday, because after Tuesday happens, even the calendar says WTF.”

Dennis snickered before saying, “That was bad and you should feel bad.”

She stuck her tongue out at him. “You’re just mad I thought of it first.”

“Well, yeah!” he admitted with a grin. “Wasn’t that obvious?” There were snickers around the table, even from Amy and Vicky, and she nodded her thanks at him, which received an over-the-top innocent look from him.

When the day was done, Taylor and the other three headed up to the ship. “Are we going to need to deal with getting at least Amy free of Carol Dallon?” Taylor asked. “I ask first as your friend and lover -” she paused at that phrasing and her face suddenly took on a look of joy. She shook her head and continued, “- and second as your eventual captain if you do decide to join up.” She wiped her hand across her face again. “We are seriously going to have to get things set up for training people, because we’re getting a lot of requests from people who want to join up to be able to be aboard a Star Trek starship.” She waved a hand. “Enterprise and the group of us - Dad, Bian, and a few others as well - will hash that out later. But I need to know if we need to end up releasing the information we have about how illegal your adoption was, Amy. It is likely to tear New Wave apart if it comes out, because they’ll all be tarred with the same brush.”

Both girls thought about it for a moment before Vicky spoke up. “To be honest, there’s no real way that the adults aren’t aware of things, even if all they did was keep their mouths shut. Then they went public and Jess was murdered by the Empire 88, even if the little asshole wasn’t a member at the time. They paid his lawyer fees and welcomed him with open arms after he did his short stint. Uncle Mike left when she was killed, and really, all four of the adults are more into New Wave than they seem to be into family. Eric is in the background all the time - he goes to Arcadia with us, remember, but we never really see him. Crystal’s off at college, but it’s BBU, so she’s going to school from home. Flies to campus every day. She’s the one most rah-rah about the group, the way I used to be before I really started looking at things. If New Wave can’t survive this coming out, then maybe the group shouldn’t survive.”

“You know that you may need to live up here,” Taylor said. “If things go badly enough.”

She snorted. “Give me a reason to try to find Uncle Mike and tell him Amy and I have left the group. I like being a hero, but … I’m getting old enough that I don’t like the group I’m in that much anymore, because I see that it’s barely holding itself together. Dad’s depression is bad, Mom’s a control freak, Aunt Sarah is more about the hero group than the family it seems, and Uncle Neal? He’s probably the closest of the adults to having a balanced outlook on things, but he supports Aunt Sarah’s take on New Wave.” She shook her head, then sighed. “I think we might need to collect the stuff we really want from our rooms and beam it up here.”

Enterprise spoke up. “In all honesty, if it reaches the point where you need to leave, then I can simply beam everything in your room here, have you take what you wish to keep, and beam everything else back down. It really is that simple.”

Amy spoke up. “I’ll be honest. That first day, when I came back with that duffel bag full? I had everything I absolutely didn’t want to lose. I could lose everything else. But yeah, it’s be nice to grab it and take the stuff I’d like to have but could live without.”

“Feel free to stay up here tonight and tell her you’re staying with a friend. This is looking more and more like a conversation with Carol needs to happen, to get you free. Like with Charlie here, emancipation is an option, which is where the illegal adoption paperwork would come in. Might be able to manage it for you as well, Vicky, if you wanted, even using that adoption as a reason, since it has affected your life since you were six years old.”

“We’ll have the conversation,” Amy said. “If it goes badly, paperwork. But yeah, I think staying up here tonight.”

“I’ve picked up calls between Alan and Zoe Barnes. They’ll be visiting you tonight, it seems,” Enterprise told Taylor.

“Knew it was going to happen. I’ll need to head down then, girls. Depending on how Dad feels about things, I may or may not be back up tonight. He may want the company.” She chuckled. “Or I might convince him to stay up here for a night.”

“We’ll find ways to keep ourselves amused,” Charlie said. “I can take those tests and Vicky and Amy can sit and heckle, for example!” She nodded at Taylor. “Go and deal with the crap you have to deal with.”

Taylor headed home and the two had a nice dinner - take-out this time, from the local Chinese place. As they cleaned up, Enterprise spoke in her ear, and she looked to her dad. “The Barnes’ are on our street. It looks like Alan and Zoe are right on time, so to speak. Start with today so that even they aren’t successful but manage to smooth things enough, they can come again tomorrow. If Alan waited until tomorrow, he’d have to blow his … no, that’s a disgusting thought with that phrase, thinking of him. He’d have to pray that his entire talk worked and we agree to let her off the hook criminally.”

“Devils advocate question - should we? They were our friends for years. She was your sister in all but blood.”

“I understand the question, but where were they? And Emma decided that trying to kill her sister was a thing, as far as I’m concerned. So no, unless they can come up with a good reasoning.”

“I agree, to be honest. It’s that ‘where were they’ question that I keep coming back to. They didn’t even try except for the publicly expected few days after the funeral thing,” her father replied. “Ah, I hear their car in the driveway.”

“Enterprise? Start recording, please,” Taylor said simply.

It took about a minute, but there was finally a knock at the door. Taylor looked at her father, who decided to be the one to answer it. “Hello Alan. Zoe,” he said in a nearly emotionless voice. “It’s still February, so you might as well come in.”

The two stepped in the door and saw Taylor standing there in her full Starfleet uniform, and Alan winced slightly at the sight, because she was also in full Starfleet captain mien. “Mr Barnes. Mrs Barnes. I’m pretty sure that I know why you’re here, so I’m going to get that out of the way right now. No, I will not be offering to drop any charges against your daughter Emma. The prosecutors have what evidence I had, and have likely by this point paid to have someone look into the email servers that Winslow uses to verify that I did not make up my evidence from whole cloth.”

“She’s looking at some serious charges!” Zoe Barnes said, her voice shaking.

“She did some serious crimes. She was directly involved with the locker incident, where there is evidence of the broken bones that were caused by cramming me into the locker. Even if it was Sophia Hess who did the actual physical deed, there is such a thing as an accomplice. People go to prison for being a knowing accomplice to a crime, and the evidence, to my knowledge and belief, shows that Miss Barnes was a knowing and willing participant to multiple crimes against me and my property. The theft of my mother’s flute and subsequent destruction was just the worst of them.”

“She was like your sister!” Alan Barnes cried out. “How can you do this to her?”

“She was like my sister, and she turned on me and decided that I was something that needed to be -” Taylor paused for a moment before she continued, “- to quote one of her emails to me, ‘culled from the herd to make way for the strong.’ I won’t speak as to what exactly she meant, but the definition largely comes down to being removed from the breeding population, such as removing non-viable seed grain or seed that is showing the wrong characteristics. Or pulling certain animals from the breeding population. The fact that those animals culled are often then sold for their meat in order to remain useful to the original owner is outside the original definition.”

She glared at the man. “I hope that you’ve had a chance to read the material that was likely given to your lawyer during discovery? You’ll see the things that she said to me in emails. If it was once or twice, maybe it could be explained as being angry over something. But it’s eighteen months worth of abuse, where she often tells me I could make the world a better place by joining my mother or other equally hateful statements.”

“What happened, Alan?” her father asked. “We were close, right up until Annette died. Then you and your whole family disappeared like a fart in a hurricane. You did the one or two day thing post-funeral where you brought casseroles - we still have those casserole dishes if you want them back, by the way - and then poof, nothing. This is Brockton Bay, so I know you weren’t suddenly swamped with divorce work. Was it Emma finding reasons to not come over and convincing you both, or what? You’d promised at one point to be there for us, and then you ghosted.”

They stood for a moment before Zoe looked over at Alan. “Everything changed about the time you and Emma got really scared about something, and that cape saved your lives. All of a sudden Emma was friends with that Hess girl, and Taylor was ‘always busy’ or some other reasons why she didn’t come over any longer, and Sophia was there all the time.”

“Sophia Hess, the PRT ‘intern’ who has suddenly disappeared?” Taylor asked. At their ‘look’, she said, “I know the truth about her but I’m not saying it out loud because I’m pretty sure that Alan Barnes is recording this conversation just in case we say something that could be used against us, which I understand is a tactic he uses occasionally during his divorce cases. We are a single party consent state, after all.
