But yeah, from talking with the PRT, Sophia Hess went afoul of a few things she shouldn’t have, and they’ve sent her off to either deal with juvenile hall because of my provable injuries - Panacea verified them, in case you’re wondering - or she’s disappeared to Los Angeles for intense training in how to be a proper PRT agent.”

“You were her lawyer with the PRT, Alan,” Zoe said. “Character witness, as I recall. Young lady of good character who made some mistakes?”

“She saved our lives when I screwed up and Emma and I were threatened by the ABB, okay? They were going to rape Emma in front of me and then kill us both, just because they could, and Sophia swooped in and saved us!”

“Your daughter fought back before she swooped in, though, didn’t she?” Taylor asked. “I heard enough of Sophia’s rants about predator and prey during the eighteen months she and Emma decided I was prey. So if she was there when the ABB attacked you, I’ll bet she just sat there until your daughter decided there was nothing to lose and swung.” Alan Barnes thought for a moment, and then nodded. “I suspect that if you can keep your child from prison, that you will get a requirement that she get counseling, because Sophia Hess’s world view really screwed her up.” She paused. “But from what I’ve read, I don’t think an insanity plea would work, and if it did, she would likely spend a greater amount of time incarcerated in a prison psych hospital than she would if she just served her time.” Taylor closed her eyes. “Get her a therapist or an actual psychologist to work out her attitudes that Hess imprinted on her. Because if she gets convicted and goes behind bars with those attitudes? She’ll find a whole mess of people who will remind her of who is prey and who is predator. And I’ve watched her at school. She doesn’t fall into the predator category.”

Zoe asked, “Can we at least … in memory of the friendship that the two of you once had, get something? We don’t want to see our little girl go to prison.”

Taylor’s dad took a deep breath. “This is going to be harsh, and it’ll probably make you mad, but it needs to be said. I didn’t want to find out that my daughter was so attacked by someone who she thought of as a sister so badly that she ended up Triggering. But, that’s what happened. Alan, you more than Zoe, have coddled your youngest girl until she thought she could get away with anything. And now she’s finding out the hard way that it isn’t true. Taylor had to learn the hard way that life isn’t fair, and it sounds like it’s Emma’s turn. I’m sorry, but I personally won’t be pushing to have the charges lessened or dropped. It was only amazing medical care that means that Taylor isn’t still in a rig dealing with broken arms and a broken clavicle. Emma was directly part of that. She needs to learn that actions have consequences.”

“Your daughter and I will never be friends again, at least not the way we once were. If she eventually breaks free of the predator/prey mindset and starts to think for herself again, she may realize what she threw away to ‘feel strong’. I’ll never trust her the way I once did. Honestly, in a very real sense, I trusted her with my heart, and given what she did to me, it feels like she tried to surgically remove it. I may be able to forgive her someday, but it’s still too damned fresh. The last straw was barely more than a month ago.” She paused. “To be honest, I’d have your lawyer work on the fact that it’s gotten to court this fast. They want this done and gone. And that’s the final kindness I can really grant her - that she get a proper and fair trial. I’m not saying it is unfair, but I don’t usually hear of a trial like this making it to the first court appearances this fast, so it’s worth checking into.”

Alan Barnes looked like he wanted to say something, but Zoe lightly punched his arm. “I’m sorry. For so very much,” he finally said. “Maybe we can someday try to repair between us, Danny?” he asked her father.

“We can see about that.” He shrugged. “Worth trying, but sometimes people just grow apart.” Alan nodded and they turned and left. They’d never even had a chance to sit down.

As they were driving away, Enterprise said in her ear, “Shall I stop recording now?” to which Taylor agreed.

“Sad,” her father said, “but I think they needed to hear it. I note that they didn’t really have any arguments. It was almost all you and me explaining.”

“I think they thought that they’d just fall back into the old ‘Uncle Alan and Aunt Zoe’ stuff. Things have changed.”

“I wonder if Alan will truly realize that you were being kind by suggesting he check into the process of getting her to trial?” Taylor just shrugged.

Chapter 30: Friday, February 11, 2011 - Amy

Chapter Notes

Sorry about the late posting - had one of those weekends where I lost ALL sense of time and what day of the week it was.

If you're enjoying the story, you'll be happy to know that there's still a LOT of chapters yet to come, and I'm not done writing the story yet. So more Enterprise goodness!

Amy looked around her room. On the surface, it looked as if she was still there, but if you opened her closet doors, there was nothing there except for her Panacea costume. Her desk was as clean as it ever was, but the drawers were largely empty. So were her dressers. None of the trinkets and such that she wanted to keep were in evidence. She knew Vicky would see that she was effectively moved out the second she saw the room, but Carol? She would likely have to be told before she realized it.

She made it downstairs to find Vicky there, getting cereal and milk out. “Tinker Crunch?” Amy asked, and Vicky pulled that box out as well. Amy was the only one who liked the stuff, because she enjoyed the crunchiness of it, while the others in the house tended to refer to it as the kinder, gentler, and - in Vicky’s opinion - edible version of Grape Nuts, which were kind of famous for being perhaps crunchier than maybe they should be. She’d one heard someone refer to putting the milk in and putting it in the microwave for a little bit, and their friend had sniped, “Oh great - hot, wet gravel!” which had led to a good-natured not-really argument.

“Mom’s gone off to work early. She’s still got some of that PRT stuff going on, and Washington is pushing back. That’s all she would say.” She took a look at Amy and said, “Room’s empty, isn’t it?”

“To you, yeah. To Carol? She’ll have to be told I’ve moved out. And since this will largely remove me from New Wave, since I’m pretty damned sure that I’m going to have to trot out the evidence, I’ve left my Panacea costume in my closet. Thinking about a new outfit, and I just might go with a Starfleet one. Call myself something like Elixir or something.”

“Show off this time,” Vicky said. “See if you can’t come up with something sexy for your Starfleet uniform.”

“You designed it, Vicky. Unless I wear something as covering as my Panacea outfit, it’s pretty much the definition of sexy.” She snorted. “Played with a design as well, that would definitely be pushing the ‘there’s definitely a female wearing this’ buttons. Saw a long skirt once that was cut in a V straight up to the belt line, worn so that if the matching tap pants weren’t worn, you’d know if her hair color was natural or if she shaved. Literally, if the woman hadn’t worn panties with it, there was going to be no mystery. Something like that with the panties built in, and maybe knee length or a tiny bit above the knees. The main skirt could be the Starfleet black or charcoal, while the panties themselves would be the branch you’re in - sciences, command, or engineering/security. Maybe even do a matching top that was sort of a bolero style? If it was a top designed to show a lot of skin, then the main color would be your branch, with a collar and maybe shoulder band in the black or charcoal? The longer the bolero, the different the design could be.”

“You kinda like the ‘lots of skin’ version, don’t you?” Vicky said with a smile.

“Between the four of you, and the way that some of the guys look at me, I’m actually starting to feel sexy, and having the ability to affect my own body now when I want to, I may as well look sexy as well.”

“Er,” Vicky said, “Sexi-er.” Amy gave a pretty blush in response and set to eating her cereal, now that it had softened enough to merely crunch, rather than sound like she was chewing rocks, as Vicky had often said.

Vicky had finished her breakfast and quickly washed her bowl and spoon, then picked up her PADD and started to design. “Given half a chance, I should have something by lunch today. Between you and Captain Hebert, we can decide if this can be an official outfit.”

Amy nodded, and once she was finished eating and cleaning up, she said, “Y’know, one of the things I might suggest to her is a way of proving that this is … well, the way Uncle Neal might say it is ‘this is not your father’s Starfleet’. What if we suggest that allowing varying levels of nudity, up to and including complete nudity, be allowed as a uniform? We’d have to figure out how to wear the pips and the communicators, but that could work. And have it be something that’s taught at Taylor’s Starfleet Academy. You have to be able to deal with everything including the fact that some of your coworkers might not wear a stitch of clothing. You have to admit that it would allow our captain to be comfortable when she wanted to be, rather than sort of doing it when there’s minimal people on the ship.”

“I think I see what you mean. To be a proper member of this Starfleet, you might have to work next to someone of the opposite sex who wears nothing but their insignia, even if you wear full body and a hijab. I think Taylor would like that, because that shows the kind of inclusiveness that they couldn’t show on television because of the censors. Plus, there’s the possibility that if there are other aliens that look something like humans out there, they might not do the clothing thing, and we’d keep them out for that? I don’t think so.”

“It’ll be sad not having you around the house,” Vicky added, “but it’s not like I’m not going to see you at school or on the ship.” Her face darkened. “If Mom tries to block me, then I might be doing the same thing as you.”

“I hope it doesn’t come to that, because it’s harder for you. She’s your mother. For me, she’s one of the people who attacked my father and came after me.” She shook her head. “That’s probably why they were able to get the drop on him, in the end. I Triggered when they landed, and that would have knocked him out, even if just for a minute or two. So he wasn’t really able to properly prepare, and they were able to deal with him. Threatening whatever was in the closet he was protecting didn’t help me love Carol any more, mind you.”

“And it was you in the closet,” Vicky said sadly.

“I’m sorry,” came a male voice from behind them both. “I’ve never realized, and the depression certainly hasn’t helped any,” Mark said. “But I’ve never been a good father to you, have I, Amy?”

“You’ve tried, but … well, even if you don’t say it to her face, you have to admit that she’s a bit of a control freak, so if she decides something, that’s how it is in the end. It’s why I’ve gotten screwed out of a huge sum of money, because she declared that New Wave was granting my powers to the hospital for free.”

She scowled for a moment, then came over and took his hands. “You’ve tried so hard to be a good replacement father for me. I pretended that I didn’t remember, because it means so much to you to be a good father when you can be.” She paused for a moment before saying, “I won’t change your brain, but so much of mental health is a correct balance of the chemicals and hormones in the body and brain. I can see that yours are out of whack. May I see if I can fix that, and get your body releasing proper amount of things like dopamine and such?”

“Of course, Amy. I give you permission to do that at any time, in case I happen to slip into a bad depression again and don’t really respond to you.” He turned to Vicky and said, “And you heard that, so you can back her up if Carol complains.” He looked back to Amy. “I know you won’t hurt me.” He managed a smiled, and she impulsively kissed his cheek.

She concentrated for a moment, and he shook his head. “Feel a bit different, but I suspect that if what you did is a permanent change, it won’t be noticeable for a few days, like with most medications.”

“I’m hoping that it works and things even out for you. Dad.” Her eyes were wet as she added the last, and she noticed that his were suspiciously wet as well.

“I haven’t been a good one for a while, but thank you.” He hugged her.

“I don’t blame you, I blame the chemical imbalances. It’d be like complaining that a one-handed man didn’t use both hands to pick something up. If you’re incapable, you’re incapable. And your brain chemistry was all wonked out.” She giggled. “Medical term there.”

He chuckled in response, and she heard Vicky’s giggle as well. “As much as I love hugging you, I unfortunately have to chase you out of the house to get off to school. And Amy? Not matter what Carol may stupidly say, I will always love you as much as I love Vicky. To me, you are my daughter, even if the circumstances … could have been better?” She gave him a quick squeeze, tightening the hug just a little bit, before she disengaged and looked to Vicky.

“Time for school, I guess.”

“Yes, we must go off and *shudder* learn things,” Vicky said in mock horror. The two girls left a snickering Mark behind them. As they took to the air, Vicky said, “Thank you for doing that for Dad. Hell, just calling him ‘Dad’ yourself may have seriously improved his day.”

“I realized that he really has tried. He’s done what he can through the depression. He does love me. So if I can improve his life by tweaking his brain hormones, that much better. And what I’m learning from the Starfleet medical files? I am getting a solid understanding of brains now, and am pretty sure that I could … I guess ‘optimize’ one would be the best term? You wouldn’t stop being you any more than growing up and experiencing things makes you not you. You’re not the person you were when you were seven, after all - your brain is different from then. All that I would be doing is affecting your recall and retention. You’d think a little faster and you’d remember stuff better.”

“That would be nice when I’m taking some tests,” Vicky said. “I swear that there are times that I know everything I need to in a given class. Right until that test plops down in front me and it feels like, ‘Uh, what me name?’ time.”

“Don’t know if a brain tune-up would fix that, but it might. When I’m more certain, which I should be in a few days, I’ll ask M … Dad if I can do that for him.” Vicky smiled at her, and they were silent but mostly content for the remainder of the flight.

When they landed, Taylor said, “Bad morning, huh? You’re both happy-ish, but Amy’s got this tendency to show how she’s feeling by her clothing. Kinda like me. Today she’s covering up a bit more - loose slacks, a sweater, and even a blazer underneath her winter coat. So she’s feeling a bit down.”

“Yeah,” Amy said. “Cleared the air with Dad, though, so I know he loves me.” Taylor’s smile was almost blinding. “Yeah, I realized that Mark really is trying his damnedest to be my dad, so I decided that he is. Carol’s still Carol, though.”

“So you’ll have your conversation with Carol about the emancipation, and pretty much move to the ship permanently tonight?” Amy nodded in response. The eyebrow waggle got a laugh out of Amy, and Taylor looked both pleased and smug at that.

The school day was just that - a day - and went as they usually do, only this day with Amy getting cheered up by the occasional quick kiss from Taylor in the hallway, and the sneaky gentle grope from Charlie in the library. Soon they were on their way back to the Dallon household. “I am really not looking forward to this,” Amy said.

Once home, she retrieved the emancipation paperwork and placed it where Carol could not help but see it. All that was needed now was for Carol to get home and begin what Amy expected to be a lot of yelling. At that point, she and Vicky went into the living room, joining their father there, who actually just had background music on as he read a book. Amy was pleased, because he was already showing signs of improvement just from what she had done a few hours earlier.

“Good day at school?” he asked.

“It was a day,” Amy said blandly, which got an understanding chuckle from him. The girls settled in to get homework done, to leave as much of the weekend free for themselves as possible.

At about five, they heard Carol’s car enter the driveway, and Amy murmured, “It’s about to get loud, I think.”

The door opened, and the sounds of someone stepping from cold Maine February weather to comfortable indoors temperatures was heard. The coffee maker was activated, and then Amy heard a quiet, “What’s this?” Some generic noises were heard before a harsh, “Amelia? Care to explain this paperwork? Emancipation?”

“Pretty much what it says. I am sixteen years old, and desire to live on my own, away from a mother who - if she is honest with herself - does not begin to actually love me.”

“How can you say something like that?” the woman barked. “I have been involved in clothing and feeding you six we adopted you!”

“Note that neither of the things you mentioned actually require love to do. I judge it based on public statements, such as introducing Vicky and me as ‘My daughter Victoria, and Amy’. The singular version of daughter, and the audible pause, as opposed to ‘my daughters Victoria and Amy’. People on PHO have even noticed it, and I know that your sister has also commented on it, yet you do not change your ways regarding it.” She opened her mouth, but Carol spoke.

“So you want to leave for something that simple?”

“No, I want to leave for multiple reasons, that simply being one of them. The most important reason is that, now that I’m old enough to live on my own, I no longer wish to live with one of the people who caused me to Trigger.”

“I was nowhere near that store when Victoria was injured!” Carol yelled indignantly.

“True, that was Vicky and me. But I didn’t Trigger then, I just decided to make people aware I had powers then, because she was badly injured. When I actually Triggered was when this group of superheroes calling themselves the Brockton Bay Brigade decided on Sunday to attack my biological father’s home. Mind you, I note that everyone carefully ignores that a known superhero group committed a crime to capture someone who was not sentenced to the Birdcage until after he had been captured - it was not a standing warrant.”

“You showed no signs of Triggering,” was the reply, eyes narrowed.

“You weren’t close enough to be affected,” Amy said. “He was, which is probably why you had an easier time against him, because he had to wake up from being knocked out. And then threatening to blast the closet door because there was something important in there, which is why he surrendered, because he didn’t want to lose his only daughter?”

“The man was a criminal, and was clearly hiding something,” Carol growled.

“Yes, an innocent non-combatant. And I’ve seen your fighting style. I understand where Vicky gets some of her rash ‘bash it and sort it out later’ attitude.” She turned to her adoptive sister. “Sorry Vicky.”

“It’s true, although the lessened aggression is helping me a lot with that.” Vicky shrugged after responding.

“Imagine how things would have gone if you’d been faster and hit that closet door the way you wanted to, instead of letting him surrender. How would you have felt seeing a red smear against the wall, knowing you’d just murdered a child?”

“She’s right, dear,” Mark said from the doorway. “We were younger and went blazing in, thinking we were doing the right thing, But it could have gone so horribly, such as what she just mentioned. I’m betting there’s something else Amy could mention, but is trying not to, because then it sounds like a threat.” He turned to Amy. “You know about the adoption, don’t you? The fact that if the truth about it gets out, that New Wave would have issues?”

Amy just nodded. “Yes, Dad. I don’t want that. New Wave does good for Brockton Bay. I … I just … Carol will never love me, because I’m the daughter of Marquis, and comments over the years like ‘blood will tell’ and such tell me that she’s just waiting for me to slip up and go villainous. Maybe not consciously thinking it, but it’s always there in the back of her mind.” She turned back to Carol. “Can you honestly deny that you think that way? That the thought process I just mentioned isn’t a reason why you insist that I not get paid for healing people?”

“You owe it to the people to heal for free! Why would you want to be paid for it?”

“Because doctors get paid for it? And I’m doing things that doctors literally can’t do? I’m not saying that I should get paid a million dollars a patient, far from it! That way ends up with me being the ‘only doctor’ for some creep like Donald Trump or something.” She shuddered. “At least I’m not his type. Sad thing is, Vicky is. Blonde and busty.”

She shook her head. “Medicare rates. Or Medicaid. Whichever it is. Let the hospitals do the paperwork, and I get some of that money paid to me for being the one to do the actual healing. That kind of money is not going to make me a charter member of the ‘yacht of the month club’, but maybe an apartment and clothing and some nice amenities? I’m doing things that the doctors at the various hospitals literally can’t. Which reminds me. I should make a pass by Medhall’s hospital and try to work something out with them to deal with their cancer and incurable diseases ward. I know that Max Anders who couldn’t possibly be Kaiser of the E88 is probably soaking the patients for all their insurance and families can pay. Maybe hurt him by giving that healing for free?” She grinned a nasty grin. “But yeah. Work out something with the hospitals in town, since Brockton General isn’t the only one - it’s just the only trauma center in the area, and trauma cases are the ones I most often work on.”

“But we’re getting away from the point. You don’t want me getting paid for something I can do that no one else can. Why is it wrong of me to ask a living wage for the ability to do that? And why can’t you just let me be, and go my own way? You don’t want me here and you never have. I’m quiet enough that you never realized that there were times you and Aunt Sarah talked that I heard the reasoning why I didn’t grow up with Vicky as my adoptive cousin instead of as my sister. She had to work to convince you to adopt me - and when I started looking into things, I realized that no one has put the pieces together. My adoption was flat out illegal. You openly stated that the Brockton Bay Brigade was changing to New Wave, and unmasking for accountability. The papers from then make it clear that there was a known rivalry between the Brigade and Marquis. Then suddenly one of the Brigade’s members adopts their known enemy’s child? There’s no court in the state that would stand for that without some legal shenanigans going on. Not then, and especially not now. I know, I checked, because I couldn’t actually believe what I found.”

She wiped her hand across her face. “So please, let this happen. I’m putting in the paperwork, and it has to be seen by a judge. I wanted you to be aware that it was going to happen. Just … please don’t fight it. Please?” She looked at Carol, the plea she was making evident on her face.

“That Hebert girl put you up to this, didn’t she?” Carol snarled suddenly.

“Jesus Christ!” Amy yelled back. “Y’know what? To hell with hiding it when it goes before the judge. If you’re going to be like this, then you deserve what follows! Enterprise?” With that, Amy disappeared in a shower of sparkling light.

Chapter 31: Saturday, February 12th, 2011 - Taylor

She woke up with Amy in her arms, reminding her that Amy’s trust of her was fairly erotic in how she showed it. Unfortunately, she had things she had to do today, so she reluctantly woke Amy up and disengaged her from her nipple. “Got things I have to do on planet today, and if I stayed here for as long as I want you to do that, I’d get none of it done.”

“What sorts of things?” Amy asked as she headed toward the shower, walking such that she knew Taylor’s eyes were solidly locked onto her ass.

Taylor, who had followed her in, said as she joined her in the stall, “Well, I need to meet with Bian regarding the multiple lawsuits that have made it past the first layer of being clearly frivolous. There are a lot of companies that want me and my businesses shut down before they start because it’s going to cut into their profits. So kill the companies before they get off the ground, and hey presto, no competition!” Taylor took great care in helping to wash Amy’s back as well as her front, and the girl was a little weak-kneed by the end. “You’re welcome to come along, to be honest. We also have to set up meetings with various groups to first set up a curriculum for our Starfleet, and then get it approved. Accredited? Whatever the word is.”

They both stepped out of the shower after the drying sequence - and didn’t she just love that aspect of Federation technology - and set about getting clothing. Taylor decided to wear the looser fitting ship’s uniform, but decided to wear underwear of that material that had led to the accidental orgy, and Amy clearly approved of her choice, and decided on underwear of the same material.

“I should probably make a run by the hospital, to be honest,” Amy said. “Haven’t actually been in about a week.”

“Should talk with Bian first. Get that payment thing worked out, especially now that you’re going to be dealing with being emancipated.” Taylor shook her head. “I hope that they get this worked out before all that has to be outed to the public, because that will utterly ruin the New Wave image, and could sent Carol completely over the edge.”

“Good point,” Amy said. With Taylor now dressed in a simple tunic and slacks, but with the Federation design motif, while Amy was in a thick sweater and wool skirt, they headed to the transporter room and were soon in the Hebert household, where Danny was just sitting down with a cup of coffee.

“Was about to call you to see if you were going to be by for breakfast,” he said, saluting the girls with his cup. “Bian will be down in a minute, then I’ll get breakfast started.”

Bian walked down in a skirt and bra, holding two blouses. “Which one looks better?” she asked the assembled group.

“Can’t speak for the girls,” Danny said, “But I think the lighter blue works better.” He stood up and started to collect things for breakfast.

Taylor just looked at the woman as she was getting dressed and said, “You are aware that you’re one of the people who made me realize that I like girls, right? That if you and Dad actually decide to get married at some point, you’ll have a step-daughter who is going to really enjoy the summer when you decide to wear bikinis?”

Bian didn’t finish buttoning the light blue blouse she’d slipped on at Danny’s recommendation; she just ran over and hugged Taylor. After a minute or so, she said, “You really have no problem with the relationship, do you?” she asked.

“If you’d stepped in immediately after Mom died - not that Dad would have let you, honestly, but that’s beside the point - I’d have had issues. But it’s been a while, and we’re all going to mourn her for the rest of our lives. But I remember that you and Clarisse were regulars to their bed. Mom loved you both, in both the emotional and physical senses. I can’t really think that she’d suddenly have an issue with you, and if you guys are ‘going all the way’, to be euphemistic about it, then Mom’s probably up there going “It’s about time!” She shrugged, “Probably take a while to ever call you Mom, if only because I’ve … well, I’ve masturbated to the sight of your nude body, so that would be a little weird.” She knew she was blushing at the end of that.

Bian laughed. “I can understand that. But it means a lot that you don’t have a problem with our relationship.”

“I’ve known you for a long time, and I know Dad well enough that he wouldn’t have gotten involved with you back then just because Mom asked. If anything, if he hadn’t liked you, Mom would have looked at you to see why. So you passed the test of the two most important people in the relationship.” Taylor laughed. “Listen to me, adulting all over the place! Let’s see if Dad needs help with breakfast.”

“Other than eating it, not really,” he said. “Making one of the faster French toast recipes, so all I need to do is cook them, since the egg dip is so easy.”

Food was soon on the table and then consumed, and once the dishes were taken care of, they moved to the living room. “Okay, we’ve looked at the lawsuits coming in, and a huge number of them were dismissed as frivolous, costing only the plaintiff money. That leaves us with five at the moment, which I and my colleagues working on them are pretty sure are designed to keep you in court until you run out of money or they can buy the right judge.”

“Well, we have access to a lot more money than they are aware of at the moment, given the little maneuvers that Enterprise has been doing with the finances of various criminal groups, so I think we can probably keep them in court until it starts to affect their shareholders. And if we get the right people looking into it, perhaps getting the info out to the shareholders how their money is being wasted?” She sighed. “And if they buy a judge who states that I can’t do X technology, then it doesn’t get made until patent exclusivity runs out on it, at which point we can ensure that it’s ready to be marketed immediately. Because if they buy the judge, I’m sure they’ll immediately try to buy the patent through a third party, if only to suppress it.”

She snorted. “No intention of selling flying cars, though. There are enough idiots on the roads. Do we really want them in the air as well?” The others laughed at that.

“You will have the worries about people or companies trying to take you out or gain control of you. I’ve got connections with connections, so we’re listening to see if there’s any hits out on you at the moment. I don’t think they’ll happen until your companies actually start producing stuff for sale, and given the processes, I know you’ll be releasing it at a lower price than competitors.”

“Not too low, though, given the vagaries of the human mind. Too low a price and they’ll think it cheap, and I mean that in the materials sense” her father added. He was about to say something else when the phone rang, so he got up and answered it. After listening for a minute, he said, “Which building? Okay, we’ll be there shortly. Thankfully Panacea’s hanging out with my daughter, so with luck she can at least keep her alive.” He hung up and turned to the others. “Apparently when the guys were checking out some of the building that are going to be torn down, they found Squealer. She’s under a ton of ratty old cloth, just barely enough to keep her above freezing to death. They don’t know how long she’s been there, but she’s probably not got very long. She looks in bad condition, no matter what.”

“Mind if we beam there?” Taylor asked. “Fastest way.”

“Good idea.” He gave the address and a minute later they were transported inside the building in question. Amy ran immediately to Squealer, and gasped when she touched her.

“Okay, give me a minute to stabilize her, and then … Taylor, can we beam her up? Best place for me to work, if only because it’s warmer up there.”

“Straight into Sickbay, I’d say. Let me know when it’s safe.” A moment later, Amy pointed at her, one hand still on Squealer’s body. The transport sparkles surrounded her and she was gone. Taylor looked around at the others. “Any need to stick around for Squealer related things? I think the PRT will need to be called, if only because there’s a blood trail that I can see. The cold almost killed her, but it also slowed her bleeding immensely. I’ll find out from Amy what kind of injuries she has. Well, when Amy’s done keeping her alive, had as far as the worst are concerned.”

“Should probably call the PRT now,” her dad said.

She nodded and asked Enterprise to connect her to the PRT. “Parahuman Response Team, East NorthEast. How may I direct your call?” rang out over her delta badge.

“This is the independent hero Grey Ghost. I’m calling to report that we found Squealer in one of the buildings we’re going to be either renovating or tearing down. She was in a bad way, so we got Panacea on the case and beamed her to my ship at the moment, but I suppose it is something of a parahuman crime scene, so the Protectorate should be made aware.”

“Just a moment please,” said the now concerned voice. Mere seconds later, Armsmaster’s voice came on.

“Grey Ghost. You say that you found Squealer in one of your buildings?”

“Yes. There was a blood trail, and she was barely alive. I think the February temperatures actually kept her from bleeding out. She’s barely alive, as I said, and Panacea is working on her aboard my ship, where the Emergency Medical Hologram can assist her as necessary.”

“Excellent thinking. Miss Militia and I will be on site in a few minutes. Please don’t disturb the site any more than you have to.”

“Understood. We’re currently standing away from the site by a little bit.” She gave the address, and a few minutes later, a PRT van arrived, being led by Armsmaster and Miss Militia on motorcycles. Miss Militia came over to talk to them while Armsmaster covered the scene in his usual efficient manner, taking samples, bagging the rags she had used, and slowly following the blood trail that Squealer had left.

Taylor’s father started. “We were having a breakfast meeting at our house,” he said, motioning to the three of them, which made Bian and Taylor both smile, since he had done it unconsciously. “It regarded some of the legal actions against Taylor’s corporations. While we were talking, I received a call from some of the union members who are surveying the buildings that will be used in the future to see if they just need to come down or can be renovated. They found Squealer under those rags and checked that she was still alive. I suspect that they called me because of Taylor and the fact that she has Starfleet tech at her command, which could help keep the girl alive. It was lucky that Amy … Panacea was there as well, since she and Taylor are likely to spend the day together. We didn’t even drive over, Taylor just beamed all of us over. Panacea immediately set to keeping her alive and once she was stable enough, she beamed up to the ship. We called you immediately after. ‘Bout all I can say, to be honest.”

Miss Militia nodded and closed her small notebook. “Thank you for caring. Some people would have just left her.”

“Well, some of our guys were where she has been, and were lucky enough to get clean and find a job with us. Until she’s clean and can say for herself whether or not she likes her life, we’re going to assume that she wasn’t as lucky; that she fell into drug use and then never saw a way out. If that turns out to be the case - that she wants free of the drugs and crime - we’ll probably see if something can be worked out. Drug program and a real job somewhere, or something of the like. Maybe get her paroled to the Union or something if it’s possible.”

Taylor snorted. “And maybe find out if that crappy design thing of hers is her Tinker mode, or if it’s just that she’s doing the best she can with crappy sh … stuff.” Miss Militia’s eyes crinkled in clear amusement at the near expletive.

“It would be nice if she can turn herself around,” Armsmaster said as he approached the group. “And I also wonder if her aesthetic is due to the quality or if it’s a design issue. I would hope that it is a quality issue,” he finished blandly.

“How do we do this if it turns out that she wants out of the Merchants for real?” Taylor asked. “I mean, I could probably hide her on the ship for a while, and certainly allow her to build stuff on one of the holodecks so that her power doesn’t drive her to try to disassemble part of my ship. Neither I nor my ship would appreciate that.” She sighed. “I know she’s got a record, but I’m wondering how much of that was her, and how much of it was the drugs and addictions talking? I know there’s a mental aspect to the addiction as well, so just clearing her system isn’t enough, but if we can keep her away from stuff for a while? And bringing her down here - well, whatever moles are in the PRT appear to have a tendency to let people know when someone is being transferred, so that they just end up back with their original gang. So hanging on to her until trial or whatever could work. It’s not like she’d be able to leave the ship.” Taylor grinned a little viciously. “Anyone thinking that they can just hot-wire or steal something is in for a rude surprise. If she tries to escape to get back to the Merchants, well, that’s what the brig is for, and they’re designed to keep someone from breaking in and rewiring to build new things or hot-wiring their way out, the way you see in so many bad sci-fi films.” She shook her head. “Who leaves access panels and wiring where your prisoners can get at it? If anything, I’d build it so that it looked like they were successful, but it instead sets off every alarm available to make sure that the entire security force knows what happened and whodunit.” She shook her head again as if to clear it. “Sorry, one of my issues with stories like that. I’ve read the Evil Overlord’s list, and that’s one of my personal things.”

“Evil Overlord’s list?” Armsmaster asked.

“Look it up online. It’s basically a humorous list of movie tropes, both fantasy and sci-fi, where the supposed Evil Overlord writing the list explains all the things he won’t do, like shooting his trusted lieutenant if he says something that the Overlord doesn’t want to hear. There’s a reason he’s the trusted lieutenant, after all. A lot of them are just funny, but some of them are things that people like Tinkers might be able to use to throw people off if you think about them. Like having a hidden weapon aiming at the shiny red button for whatever purpose the button is supposedly for - usually labeled as a self-destruct. And if there has to be a self-destruct button, you label it as something like ‘Tertiary sewage system override’ and put it available, but not out in easy reach for anyone to hit. Or putting a bio-lock on your motorcycle’s ignition, and anyone who tries to steal it that isn’t you or someone that you’ve given rights to gets the equivalent of a TASER jolting them.” She shrugged. “Something I’m sure that you’ve contemplated.” She ignored The Look that passed between Armsmaster and Miss Militia, and suspected that both motorcycles were soon to develop just such a system.

Armsmaster finally said, “It has been a pleasure working with you, Grey Ghost. Please keep us apprised … keep us in the loop regarding Squealer. I will make the director aware that you have her, which actually means that Squealer is quite well in hand as far as incarceration.”

“Thank you,” Taylor said with surprise. She was not expecting Armsmaster to pay her such a compliment. “Should I go up to the ship and see how Amy’s doing with her? I promise that I’ll make you aware as soon as we know the situation.”

He nodded, then reached into a small shelf that popped out of his armor on his left arm. He handed her a metal business card that simply had his symbol and a telephone number. “If you call that, you will reach me directly. Either that or Dragon will answer in some way to gather whatever information you wish to pass on.”

“Again, thank you,” she said. “I will only use this number for this situation, or if an emergency arises that I believe you should be involved with.”

He nodded. “That is why I gave it to you, Captain,” he said simply, the respect clear in his voice. After a pause, he said, “Now, unfortunately I must be rude and get these items back to the PRT for study.” With that he walked to his motorcycle and drove away.

Miss Militia smiled. Taylor could tell because of her eyes and the way her bandanna mask moved. “I need to get back as well. Thank you again for keeping us in the loop regarding this.”

Taylor chuckled. “I’m trying for good relations with you guys. Doesn’t look too good for me if you find out after the fact that I have Squealer, right?” Miss Militia let out with a small laugh of her own and nodded before going to her own motorcycle and heading back to PRT headquarters.

Taylor looked to Bian and her father and asked, “Shall we go up and see what’s happening?” At their nods, they beamed aboard Enterprise.

Chapter 32: Saturday, February 12th, 2011 - Taylor

As they materialized on the platform, Taylor nodded to the holographic tech, who saluted quickly, which she returned. It then faded back into the system. She turned to Bian. “I had a thought just as the transporter kicked in. Are any of those lawsuits from the PRT? I’m betting no.” They started walking toward the main Sickbay

“None of them are. Are you thinking of seeing if they might want to be involved, even as an amicus curiae?” When Taylor nodded, she said, “I’ll probably see if I can talk to Director Piggot to get in touch with the legal staff. There might be reasons why they can’t, but those would be within the PRT itself. And since I think you were talking about various equipment to make their troopers safer, as well as maybe improving costumes for their heroes? I suspect they’ll want to be on your side once they can test your cloth, for example, and some of the tech.”

“That’s my thought as well, which is why I suggested it.” She blew air out through suddenly puffed cheeks. “So frustrating. So much stuff to do - set up my businesses and find good people to run them, start working on setting up my version of Starfleet Academy, so that I can get people for this ship other than me, Charlie, Amy, and Vicky. Admittedly, the other three will slot amazingly into needed roles, but still, a crew of four? We need more.”

They entered Sickbay to see Amy and the EMH working on Squealer. “Captain,” the EMH said. “Got a good one here. Don’t let her get away from you, if you can avoid it.”

“Don’t plan to, for any meaning ‘let her get away’,” she said with a smile, seeing Amy’s slight blush while she stayed focused on Squealer. “Is she stable enough for either of you to give me an update on her? If not, just let me know when it’s safe.”

‘Bones’ replied in that DeForrest Kelley southern drawl. “Nice havin’ a captain who’s willing to wait for once,” he said with a small laugh. “She’s finishin’ up some of the bones as I’m teachin’ her the tech. She fixed the worst of the problems, which I made sure were set in the report you’re goin’ to need and probably show to the PRT. Bad off enough that we were basically dealin’ with blood in her drug stream. Now we’re back to a blood stream. Bunch of different pathogens cleared out of her system, any one of which could have caused your whole city issues if they got free, which means you may want to deal with her group when you can, because I’m sure she’s not the only one carryin’.”

Amy stood up. “Thanks, Bones,” she said, not thinking about the fact that she was talking to a hologram. “I tend to not heal the villains back to perfect health, because it’s hard for them to run away as they so often want to in order to avoid arrest, but with the number of broken bones and the fact that it’s really obvious that they weren’t self-inflicted? My power lets me heal them basically perfectly, but this?” she said, holding up some tool that Taylor’s connection to the ship told her was an osteogenic stimulator, “Lets me heal the bones without using up much of the patient’s resources.”

“Noticed you needed some onions to get some of what she needed fixed,” he replied. “There were times I wished I’d had an ability like that.”

“There are times it’s more trouble than it’s worth, especially when you feel like you should be doing something just because you have the ability. I’m still learning to sit back and give myself ‘me’ time, rather than heal all the time. Just do trauma, for example - the people likely to die really soon if I don’t help. Let the broken bones heal the way that nature intended.”

“It’s a balancing act,” he told her. “You can, so you want to, but do that too much and it wears you out.”

She smiled. “I know this is going to come out offensive and I don’t mean it to, but it is really easy to forget that you’re a hologram, and not the original Dr. McCoy.”

“Well, considerin’ that the man I’m based off and whose engrams I use has been dead for a good few years, just like his actor here in this universe, I’m takin’ that as a compliment.”

“It was definitely meant as one, sir,” she said.

“By the way, Doctor,” Taylor said, “I give you permission to be out and about when you want. You don’t have to sit in the memory banks just waiting for a call. I’m not going to complain if I walk into the mess hall and see you and one of my crew - total of four of us at the moment - sitting and just talking about whatever. You’re not a thing, you’re a non-biological intelligence by my reckoning.”

“Thank you, Captain,” he said. “That said, I think for the moment I’ll slip back into the system so you can talk. But I’ll likely take you up on that every now and then.” He faded out in the manner of holograms on the series.

Taylor laughed. “Won’t complain if he decides to hang around the bridge on a regular basis to snark at me. That would probably make me feel more like the captain than anything else!” She shook her head, amused, then looked up at the emitter. “Not an order, but feel free to if you’re paying attention.” She turned to Amy. “So, can you wake her so we can find out what’s going on?”

“Not a problem,” Amy said. She touched Squealer’s arm and the young woman woke up.

It took the woman a few moments to place where she was, in that manner of waking up that Taylor’s mom had always poetically referred to as ‘reseating the soul into the body’. They knew when she was firing on as many cylinders as she had available when she said, “I either died and went to heaven, am hallucinating before I die in the cold, or I’m actually on that big honkin’ ship orbitin’ the Earth!”

Taylor chuckled. “Given I’m here, I’m really hoping it’s the last, because otherwise it means I’m dead too, or you have really impressive hallucinations.”

Squealer tilted her head to look at Taylor. “Captain Hebert,” was her only comment for a moment. “Damn, I wish I wasn’t going to have to spend the next few decades in prison, because I would love to see if I could learn enough to become an engineer for a ship like this.” She paused. “You cleared out the shit from my system, didn’t you?” she asked Amy.

“Yeah. It may have kept you alive long enough for the guys to find you and get you healing, but it was going to kill you in the long run.”

“Yeah,” was the sad response. “In the beginning it was just weed, and then shit went down and I hooked up with Adam … Skidmark. And somehow voluntary went out the window when we got to a certain point. First was a contact type drug. Just get it on your skin and it’s a trip. Once you’re hooked, that’s it. Not like in some of those stories where you have to keep taking it or you die, but … well, I think you know what I mean. So we tried more and more stuff. Then it got to the point where he was injecting me, or forcing me to take a pill or some such shit …sorry. Had a mouth on me since I was ‘bout thirteen, and being with Sh … Skidmark didn’t help any.”

Amy snorted. “Although he has some of the most WTF insults I’ve ever heard of. Does he just throw a bunch into a hat and pull them out one at a time to insult people?”

Squealer laughed. “That implies a working brain. The drugs ate his, so I think it’s like one of them … what’s it called … random number generators. Leads into an insult generator or something.”

“Do you mind if I call someone like Armsmaster or Miss Militia up here to talk to you? They know about your being found and that we were healing you up here.”

“Sure,” Squealer said. She looked down and realized that she was nude under the sheet. “Maybe I could get somethin’ to wear first? Never been shy about the body, but don’t want anyone thinkin’ I’m tryin’ to seduce anyone.” She snorted. “Maybe if I get out of prison I can afford to get the tits shrunk. Reason I don’t wear bras is that H-cups are fuckin’ expensive. If I could shrink ‘em to double-Ds or somethin’, I could at least afford a tit sling. I’d love one of those uniforms, but I gotta earn it, and I don’t think that’s happenin’ any time soon, given my past.”

“Enterprise? Got her current measurements?” Taylor asked. When she received the affirmative, she said, “Could you give her underwear that fits her and an outfit that covers as much as she wants it to?”

Squealer laughed. “If I dressed the way I want to, I think I’d freak everyone out. But can it be … well, everyone calls it slutty because it shows so much skin, but I don’t like things touching my skin if I can avoid it. Too sensitive. It’s why I usually had these swinging under a thin shirt, ‘cause even bras that fit me felt too rough.”

“Mind if I give you a bra your body can do the upkeep on? Carbon fiber to hold them up, and maybe tighten the Cooper’s ligaments?” At Squealer’s questioning look she added, “Those ligaments are the reason a girl’s breasts are so perky early in life, no matter the size. The bigger the breast, the faster it stretches out.”

“Which is why I’ll be trippin’ over them when I’m fifty. Gotcha. Go ahead. No bra, I guess, Captain,” she said. Taylor could tell there was no mocking in calling her that. She was simply looking at the young woman and giving her what she felt was her due - she was captain of this vessel, therefore she gets called Captain.

Amy still had a hand on her, so Squealer blinked a little when she was clearly feeling something. Her face showed shock and amusement as her breasts firmed up and actually shrank just a little bit. “Since you said you wanted them smaller, I’m using just a little of the mass to make the bra.”

“Given that I could probably smother someone with them, or knock them unconscious if I turned too fast, not complaining if you make ‘em smaller. Love to ask you to keep goin’, but that’s cosmetic, and not only don’t you do cosmetic changes, really, but I’m a felon, so don’t get perks like that even if you did do cosmetic.”

“Well, you may not feel you get the perks due to being a felon,” Amy said, “but you have to admit that they’re a lot perkier now!” She giggled slightly.

Squealer looked at the sheet, then flipped it off, exposing her body to everyone in the room. Taylor snickered as she heard her father mock-complain as he turned around, “Is it me, or something else? Seems like every woman I come across has a love-hate relationship with clothes.”

Bian snorted. “Yeah, we all love to hate them!” Squealer had the good graces to blush at realizing what she’d just done.

“Don’t be too worried,” Taylor said. “If I didn’t need to wear this to show that I’m captain, I’d probably figure out insignia that told everyone I’m captain for wearing on my skin. When I’m alone or with people who are aware and aren’t offended by it, I run around in as little as possible. When I Triggered and ended up with this ship, I ended up spending a day or two walking the corridors completely nude.” As she finished speaking, a sparkle left a pile of clothes on the bed Squealer had just been on. The young woman slipped on the panties first, then the blouse, then the skirt.

“I’m as decent as I ever get,” she said when she was done. “Love the feel of the material, by the way. Kinda stuff that I’d actually wear more often.”

“Well, when you take into account that the Federation had a couple hundred years to figure out materials science for anything from starship design to cloth, it kind of makes sense that there’s clothing that feels good to wear,” Taylor said.

Squealer cocked her head. “This isn’t just some interesting minion that acts like a Federation ship? It’s the actual Enterprise?”

“Yep,” Taylor said, popping the P. “When I Triggered, I apparently called her here to me from the spacedock she was in.”

“Captain, Armsmaster and Miss Militia have arrived,” Enterprise announced. “Shall I lead them here?”

“Please do, Enterprise.” A few minutes later, the two entered the room. Squealer walked over to Armsmaster, turned around, and held her hands behind her back, clearly in a position for her wrists to be cuffed together.

“I’m turning myself in, Armsmaster. Now that I’m free of drugs in my system for the first time in at least five years, I’m ready to pay for the crimes I committed.”

Everyone in the room was shocked at this turn of events other than Squealer, of course. It took a moment before Armsmaster said, “We’ll wait on that for the moment. If you could -” He paused for a moment before realizing that there weren’t really all that many seats in Sickbay. “Perhaps we could take this to a conference room?”

Once they were in the conference room, they saw Squealer start to head to the window to look down on Earth, but she stopped herself and sat down, facing away from the windows. “I’ve done a lot of bad shit in the last few years,” she said. “I don’t deserve that view.”

Armsmaster looked at her for a moment before saying, “This is starting in a direction that I did not expect, so forgive me if it takes a moment to reorient myself.”

“We’re used to the more foul-mouthed and … well, frankly abusive woman we’ve run across in combat,” Miss Militia said. “So hearing and seeing you turn down something you clearly desire is not what we expected.”

Squealer responded, “If I could change the last few years, I would. Then again, I’d have to go back some distance into the past, and probably start things by killing my parents.” She shook her head. “Hard to believe, but that would probably improve my life a lot. But instead, I dealt with the crap they heaped on me, and when I’d finally had enough and left, I thought I was saved when I met Ad … Shitstain.” She laughed mockingly. “Good enough name for him, given his chosen cape name.” Taylor couldn’t completely prevent the snort of laughter that came out of her.

“My name is Sherrel Bailey, and I was born in Woodstock, Vermont. Folks are considered pillars of the community there, which is why I never reported any of the abuse I got from them. ‘Just needed some discipline’, they’d say if people saw bruises on me. So one point, after they couldn’t hide a few of the bruises, they took off to an important gathering in Montpelier, and I emptied the house of valuables, especially the bribe money my father kept in his safe. Since we lived out away from most people, I didn’t bother making it neat, I made it look like a burglary happened. Went to the back door, took some scrap burlap from outside where it was used for rag for cleaning sh … stuff, wrapped my hand in it and shattered the door pane closest to the indoor deadbolt so that the shards went inward.” She laughed. “Can tell I was meant for a life of crime - I thought about how to make it look like a robbery. Didn’t think about how to explain my absence, though, so no idea what happened there.”

Enterprise interrupted. “It appears that your robbery led to quite a bit coming out about them, and your father is apparently a resident of the Northeast Correctional Facility. If you wait another three years, it is likely that you could be declared legally dead. The information I find does lead to a presumption of your death, and they are attempting to ascertain where your body as and who your murderer was.”

Sherrel blew a raspberry at that news. “Is my father going to be released from prison if I show up?” She paused. “I’ll admit to being alive anyway, but I really don’t want to see either of those assholes again.”

“No, he was convicted of multiple counts of bribery and blackmail, and will likely not be eligible for parole until 2031. Your mother was convicted but was able to paint your father as the main instigator, so she served two years and three months before release. She has moved to Ohio, it seems.”

“Her family is from there. Probably lost the house when everything went down.”

“I do not see reference to the property, but will check. Armsmaster? Will you and Miss Militia be making the report to the authorities about her survival?”

“Yes,” Armsmaster said. He looked to Miss Militia before adding, “There will need to be conversations as to whether or not we report the fact of your thefts. What year did this happen?”

Sherrel looked up at the ceiling for a moment before chuckling darkly. “To give you an idea of how fucked up the drugs made me - what year is it now? I ransacked the house for valuables back in oh-seven, when I was fifteen, nearly sixteen. I’m thinkin’ it’s either twenty-ten or early twenty-eleven.”

“It is mid-February of 2011. The statute of limitations has run out for that crime in Vermont,” Enterprise said. “Three years is the statute. It turns out that things such as bribery have a six year statute of limitations, so your father would still be eligible to be arrested even if he weren’t discovered until today.”

Sherrel laughed. “As much as I want them both to suffer, I don’t want someone getting in their head to prosecute him for my death when I’m sittin’ right here. Never want to see either of them again, but don’t want them hit for shit they didn’t do. As for me? Well, I don’t honestly remember a lot of the … stuff I did in the Merchants, ‘cause wasted-slash-high all the time. But I know I was busy and read some of the things we did, so I know there’s some stuff there.”

“Surprisingly little of the major crimes except as an accomplice,” Armsmaster said. “Driver for Skidmark, more counts of reckless driving than I currently care to count, and likely multiple charges regarding some of the weaponry you had on your … vehicles, since quite a few of those weapons were illegal for non-military to own.”

“Yeah, Skids has connections, which is why he was always able to get me free. Which is a problem, to be honest. Panacea here got me free of all the shit in my system - not gonna be polite this time ‘cause that stuff was killin’ me - and I kinda like being clear-headed for the first time in too damned many years. Even if the reason was getting away from Skid after he had a really bad trip and decided to let me know he didn’t like how slowly his latest ride was comin’ together by workin’ me over with a crowbar. Don’t know whether he pulled the blow to the head at the last second or if I just got lucky, but when he left to scream at someone else’s fuck-ups, I grabbed what I could and left. Figured I was gonna die, but I wanted to die on my terms. Then the dock guys found me I guess - thank ‘em for me, willya sir?” she asked Taylor’s father. “They coulda just looked at me and decided it was better to let me die, but they saved my life by callin’ you guys in.”

“I will tell them, and they’ll be glad to know you’re alive and as well as can be expected at the moment.”

“Damn sight better than I was yesterday at this time,” she said.

He nodded and turned to Armsmaster. “She’s right about escapes from custody. I think we all know that there’s moles in most of the big organizations in Brockton Bay. I’m sure there’s guys at the Docks who make a little extra by passing small stuff to Kaiser or Lung. We know that there’s moles in the PRT and BBPD, even with how hard you guys are working to find them and get rid of them. Or use them for misinformation, when possible. You know this ship. What say you guys toss the idea past Director Piggot that Miss Bailey here be held aboard this ship, if the Captain agrees? I’m pretty sure that the ship could prevent her from escaping.”

“Yes,” Enterprise said, appearing as a hologram for the first time in front of Sherrel. “I have her biological signature, so I can bio-lock all systems against her.”

“Good,” Sherrel said before anyone else could. “I doubt Skids can launch himself up here safely, and he’d need me to build him a rocket to make it here. Not that he’d make it on board once he was here. But if I’m here, he can’t get me hooked on that shit again. Right now I’m fine, but I understand that part of the addiction is mental? Pyscho-somethin’ or other?”

Amy smiled, and it was then that people realized that she’d been touching Sherrel the whole time, ostensibly to keep her calm. “A psychological addiction - you get used to taking it, so you expect to take it again from habit, and also the feeling you tend to get from most of them is something you want to feel again, so you try to get it again by doing the drugs again. It’s part of why marijuana is considered a gateway drug by lawmakers and other people who have no fucking idea what they’re talking about. The type to get into the harder stuff enjoy that first high, and keep chasing it, but never get it again, so they move on to stronger stuff. If you’re using it not for a weird sensation or high, but more for a relaxant, such as for anxiety? No desire to go for stronger stuff.” She looked blankly at Armsmaster and Miss Militia. “I may or may not know some individuals at Brockton General who might have occasionally had access to the specific plant in question and have explained scientifically what the effects are. I might have verified a lack of addiction in these people, were they to exist.”

She paused. “By the way, Armsmaster, I can verify for you that everything Miss Bailey has said to you has been true to the best of her ability to know.” She looked to Sherrel. “The body has certain reactions that can’t really be measured by machines yet. People can control heart rates and blood pressure and the like, but they can’t control the various chemicals that get released when a person knowingly lies. At no time did you show any signs of lying to anyone here.”

He nodded. “We have a situation here where the criminal in question admits to doing the deeds she has been involved with, but a case can be made for diminished capacity, and from information received from others of the Merchants whom we or the BBPD have arrested, the claim of forced consumption of narcotics and other pharmaceuticals is entirely believable. I will suggest that Mr Hebert’s suggestion is accepted; that Miss Bailey be incarcerated aboard this ship if the captain is agreeable, in order to prevent her forced escape into the clutches of the Merchants once more.”

Sherrel nodded. “Thank you. I’ll try to make a list of all the stuff I do remember, not just the stuff that might make me look good to the courts.” She shook her head. “It’s just that so damned much of it is a blur. I can remember the stuff before I met Skidmark, but after I got hooked on shit, there’s blocks of time that are just blurs of me building what I could with the crap they could steal. God I wish I had access to good stuff to build with. I bet I could make some pretty kick-ass vehicles if I could just get something that didn’t start out as broken to begin with.” She paused. “Did I accidentally repeat myself there? Prob’ly.”

There were more questions asked, and when they left, Taylor officially accepted Sherrel as her prisoner. As the two Protectorate faded from view, Sherrel looked to Taylor and asked, “Where’s the brig?”

“Not anyplace you have to worry about right now. You’re here and can’t escape the ship, and with Amy vouching for your truthfulness, I think I’m willing to give you a chance. Get you learning some of our tech, and see what you can make then. If you’re the person I think you are, I just might have found my ship’s engineer.”

Chapter 33: Saturday, February 12th, 2011 - Emily Piggot

Chapter Notes

Since I didn't post last weekend for various annoying reasons, I've decided to give yo all TWO chapters this weekend. Enjoy!

Admittedly, this chapter is kinda short ...

“So you’re saying that according to Grey Ghost and Enterprise - and Panacea, Miss Bailey, known as Squealer, was more of an unwilling participant in her crimes than has originally been thought?” Director Piggot asked.

“Yes,” Miss Militia said. “Panacea pointed out that while people can control heart rate and blood pressure, there are other signs of a person lying that are released by the human body, and Miss Bailey showed none of them, according to her. And we have no reason to believe that she was lying. Especially since Miss Bailey’s first act upon seeing us was to place herself such that Armsmaster could handcuff her hands behind her back. I honestly believe that, in this moment at least, she is truly wishing to pay for the crimes she has committed.”

“And with her being effectively incarcerated aboard the Enterprise, since she has been bio-locked out of all systems until the captain releases those locks,” Armsmaster said, “there is no one in the Merchants who can free her. The only individual I am aware of at the moment who would stand a chance is Strider, and he would have to see a room aboard the vessel in order to arrive there. And we are uncertain if he could even leave the surface to do so, it is just an assumption that he might be able to.”

Director Piggot thought for a long moment before saying, “You know, I think that I’ll okay that incarceration. The captain of that ship has earned my grudging respect so far for being willing to follow the rules and contact us for things that are our remit, as opposed to so many others. Such as this incident with Squealer. So having her someplace that the Merchants can’t break her free from? I am more than happy to allow that. If Washington decides otherwise, we’ll go from there. But I can’t see a reason why they’d interfere unless they want her to escape. Plus, with her up there for a while, we not only stand a better chance against the Merchants when they try something, since they’ll realize very soon that they no longer have their Tinker to build vehicles for them, but Captain Hebert can give us a good indication of how serious Squealer is about changing, because past evidence shows that she is not good at keeping what could be a con going.”

Miss Militia spoke up. “I’ve dealt with Squealer before, and this strikes me as a completely different person, emotionally. Maybe it’s getting the drugs out of her system, or the realization that Skidmark nearly beat her to death, or a combination of the two, but I think this is serious.”

“I would concur with Miss Militia on this,” Armsmaster said. “She was still using expletives in her speech, but rather than ‘doubling down’, as the saying goes, she tended to apologize for it. That is a departure from her old ways.” After a pause, he said, “I admit that I do not understand most interactions with people. I know that there are jokes about me out there because of this. But for as much as it may mean, even without the detector built into my armor, this conversation with Miss Bailey felt honest and real. I hope that it is so, because she could be an asset to whomever she works with.” Another pause. “Especially since she seemed to hint that it was the quality of her starting materials that led to her current abominations being abominations.”

“We’ll see what the word is from Captain Hebert in a few days regarding Squealer, but I’ll have the legal team look into both full culpability, and diminished culpability slash control regarding her crimes. From what you’ve said, Panacea would likely testify on her behalf as to her truthfulness when she states that many of the drugs were forced on her. I’m also putting the PRT on high alert for a potential blow-up of the Merchants, which means that between the two of you, I have now placed the Protectorate on high alert.” Both nodded, and were dismissed from the meeting to make the rest of the Protectorate aware.

“I don’t get it, Captain,” Sherrel said. “You know I’m a criminal. Why do you seem to be standing up for me, and giving me a chance?”

Chapter 35: Saturday, February 12th, 2011 - Danny

Chapter Notes

And here's the second promised chapter...

Bian piped up. “From the way she was talking, I think she wants it to stay that way. She wants to be sent to jail for what she’s done.”

“To hit him with, or to give to him to emasculate himself with?” Larry asked with a smile.

“Either works for me,” she replied with a laugh.

“Fine with me,” Jack said. “Just don’t aim it at me, or the wife might get annoyed. Says she’s still got use for me.” They all chuckled that the two got back to checking out the buildings, while Bian and Danny headed toward the offices.

When they got there, Zephron was still around. “How’s things, Boss? Heard about Squealer.”

“She’s up on the ship right now, looking healthier than she has since anyone in Brockton Bay has known her.”

“She’s an interesting girl,” Bian said. “If we can keep her away from the drugs that Panacea cleared out of her system, we could end up with an ally. Actually wants to be punished for what she’s done so far.” Mark got a look on his face, and Bian smirked at him. “Mind out of the gutter, Mark. She’s nineteen or twenty.”

“True, but … in a certain meaning of the word - ‘healthy’.” He managed to not cup his hands in front of his chest.

“If things go the way I expect,” Danny said, “She’s going to be a lot - ‘healthier’ - when Amy and Taylor are done with her. And she’s currently aboard the ship being held, because she literally can’t escape from there.”

“We’ll get word passed around, and call a few people that we know will let others know,” Zephron said. “It was getting time for something, given that Taylor’s been doing stuff for a couple weeks now. I expect that you’ll want to keep an eye out on the E88 and ABB for now, because getting her on their teams by force, with a ship that could move the Northern Girl that easily? They’ll want that, and they’ll go big to get it, so you and Tay are in serious danger as of now, Boss man.”

“Not being flip about it, but given what Taylor and the ship have set up around our house? Lung’s going to have to ramp up pretty seriously in order to get through the protections, and by the time he’s gotten there, the ship’s going to have shot him from orbit. Fatally, if necessary. I’m getting really tempted to be lazy and beam from home to work until we’ve got things worked out.”

His communicator chirped, and he answered it without thinking, ignoring - with difficulty - that Zephron let out a SQUEE! for the first time Danny had ever heard. “What’s up?”

“This is Enterprise, Danny. For your protection, I would actually recommend being ‘lazy’, as you call it. I know that it would make both Taylor and me feel better about your safety. The same offer goes to Bian as well, since those who pay attention are now aware that you are part of her circle. The merchants are merely likely to attack the docks trying to find Squealer, but the Empire is the group most likely to cause issues with attempting to gain control of me by attempting to gain control of Taylor. The ABB is most likely going to hold off due to a grudging respect for your territory by Lung at the moment. And if a show of strength against the Empire is strong enough, it may force him to show whether he is the honorable man he attempts to show the world, or if he is simply a thug who pretends to be honorable when convenient or lucrative.”

“Given that we sometimes find the burned remains of people near the docks areas, I tend to vote on the second option,” Mark said with a snort. “But first, let’s worry about the damned Merchants showing up soon.” He nodded and headed off toward one of the buildings. Danny knew that pretty soon, half of the guys were going to be moving things around and perhaps placing … ‘party favors’ … around the site in easy reach of people who knew where to look.

He and Bian headed into his office after Enterprise ended the call, but not before giving Zephron an amused look. The man was unashamed at his reaction, and Danny couldn’t blame him for it either. He picked up the phone and called the PRT to let them know that they suspected that the Merchants might make a play in the next day or two, when Skidmark stopped being so high that he didn’t notice Squealer was gone. He was given an official thank you for the heads-up, but Director Piggot made it unofficially clear that they’d thought of that and were planning to be ready.

As the saying goes, ‘For me, it was Tuesday.’ I literally can’t grasp that specific wonder.” She smiled. “But I can derive great joy from being the one to deliver that wonder to others such as yourself and your daughter.”

He smiled and checked over the clothing. The pants felt like regular work pants, and she had even supplied him briefs and t-shirt for underwear. “I keep constant scans of you and the others close to Taylor.” She smirked. “I have designs for underwear for Bian that I suspect will not remain on her body for much longer than it takes for you to see them.”

“Even after the work that Amy did, I’m not strong enough to rip any of this stuff,” he said with a laugh as he stripped.

“Shall I leave?” she asked. “After our conversation, you might … never mind. Apparently it doesn’t bother you.” Her hologram blushed. “Although I may look a little too much like your wife, given that reaction you seem to have to my look.”

He was in briefs and shirt quickly. “No such thing as being too beautiful,” he said with a smile. And was quickly in the rest of the clothing, then slipped his vest on.

“Thank you. And in that outfit, they will have to aim specifically for your face to hurt you badly. The bullets striking you may sting, but the worst you will experience from the attack should be bruising.” She nodded at him and said, “Now, as an aside, since I did not have a chance to get one out for you, let me give you a useless tour of the armory before you beam back down to the planet.” She was grinning at him, which he had to admit was beautiful, albeit a little odd with the somewhat Vulcan appearance that the ears and blush gave her.

“How long does it have to be held on someone for it to properly stun them?” he asked her.

“With most people in the time I come from, a blast of a second or more, but that tends to be because of clothing like that you wear right now. By the way, keep those. They can be cleaned the same as any other clothing from this time period. But as for your question, I suspect that rapid fire would down many of them.”

“How about a rifle set on stun, with the trigger held for a few seconds, sweeping across a group?”

She nodded, smiling even wider. “I see half of where Taylor gets it from,” she said. “Yes, that would work quite well. And if you can find a good vantage point, you can likely turn this into a rout, rather than a fight. And given that Amy’s blocks seem to have worn off completely, I note that you are considerably faster than you used to be.”

“And testing my strength at work by bending stuff that I didn’t used to be able to. Now, I think I ought to borrow that weapon and get down there. Sound good? And don’t worry, even though I know a bunch of guys are going to want one of their own, I’ll remind them that it’s borrowed. Same for if the PRT requests it. By the way, if you haven’t yet, let them and the BBPD know what’s going down.”

“I have, and as for the rifles and phasers, I would have the same issue with giving them out as Taylor had to making replicators available to the public. The power source in one of the small phasers is enough to vaporize a somewhat large area. The representations in the television shows were off by … quite a margin. The reality is very much equivalent to a nuclear hand grenade. Only a high level Brute would be able to throw one far enough to not be caught within the blast radius, and only the highest level Brutes could avoid being within the area of secondary effects.” She led him to the transporter room after he had been given a phaser rifle and shown its operation. As he stood on the platform, she said softly, “Please stay safe, Danny.”

“Of course. I appear to have a difficult pair of conversations in my future that I oddly look forward to.” She smiled as she beamed him to the DWU compound.

He shook his head as he appeared, then looked to his guys. “They’re either still getting ready, or Skidmark is given what passes for a speech, assuming he’s sober enough to string more than nonsensical curses together. But they’ll probably be on the move soon.”

“I see you decided to bring your own party favor,” Zephron said with a grin. “Any chance -”

“Nope. As much as I’d love to, I know that someone would ‘accidentally’ ‘lose’ one of them,” he said with a laugh. “This is pretty much set on stun, and I have to return it when the fight is over.” After a short pause he added, “Damn it.” He smiled at the laughter he was hoping for from the guys. A lot of them were military and knew what Danny was doing, but also knew that it worked whether or not you knew the psychological trick.

“Let’s get you into a good position with plenty of view and range,” Mark said. “Get you a walkie-talkie so that when you start seeing them, you can let us know to look around the edges of the mass, since some of those guys still have working brain cells. Not a lot, but enough to be an issue.” He snorted. “Both brain cells and guys.”

They led Danny right where he expected to be taken - one of the buildings that was being reworked for Taylor’s companies. Top floor, with a window that pretty much gave him what he hoped would not become a killing ground. But he’d definitely be taking them down from that spot. He gave a quick radio check to make sure they could hear him and then contacted the ship. “Captain? Any sign of them moving?”

“They’re starting to mill about in that sort of ‘let’s get going’ thing groups do, so it should be any second. While you guys are doing that, we’ll be giving them our own way of hurting them - Sherrel’s tools, and all the loose money they have. Going to mark all the places we grab from so that the BBPD and PRT can swoop in and grab what weapons are still there, not to mention the drugs.” A short pause. “Ah, looks like they’re on the way. Heading in your direction. Unless they do something really weird, they’re going to head right toward you. Weird is a possibility since we’re talking Merchants, but given where you are and where they’re heading, yours is the fastest route they’ve got to try to fuck up the DWU. Stay safe, Dad. Enterprise tells me we have an interesting conversation ahead.”

“How did my life get so strange?” he asked with a laugh. “Why am I asking; I got involved with a Lustrum follower. I was destined to have a weird life. Leave this open, or call you if I need something?”

“We’ll both need to be on our best game for what’s coming, so we’ll just keep some sensors on you, and you can call when necessary.” He closed the communicator after they said polite goodbyes, and he settled in to prepare for them. He was pleased that the rifle had a scope of sorts, so he placed himself on the mattress they’d left for him and set up for some phaser sniping.

Clicking on the scope gave him a nice view that he’d use when they started to come into view. After a moment’s thought, he clicked the walkie-talkie. “Got a question - they’ll probably be able to fit the entire group coming into my field of view here.
