When I open fire, should I start from the back and sweep forward, or the reverse? I can see up and down sides to both ways of doing things.”

It was quiet for a moment before Doug Markham came on. “Nice thinking, Danny. I’d say to start ‘em from the back, because even if they can see where you’re firing from, it’s still going to panic them and tend to drive them toward us. How many shots can you do with that thing?”

He snorted, holding down the transmit button as he did. “If this works right, you guys may never have to worry about getting shot. Set on stun, and I’ve been told that I can just hold the trigger and sweep. I’ll get a few of ‘em, no doubt about that. We’ll see how long the power pack holds out while I do that.”

Doug laughed back. “I don’t think any one of us is going to complain if you manage to down them all yourself with that thing. I know I’m not gonna complain about not having any bullet wounds from some meth-head getting stupidly lucky. We’ve already got a metric fuckload of zip ties to take the ones they leave behind into custody, so if we just end up doing clean-up? I know that I’m good.” Danny could hear a lot of people behind Doug agreeing loudly.

It wasn’t very long before they started to show up in the area, and he shook his head. Way too clumped together to be useful. Which is great for me. The stragglers came into view and he estimated that Skidmark had managed to get about fifty people to try to storm the castle … DWU, he meant. If they weren’t drugged out, they might be more of a worry, because the numbers are about even for a Sunday.

When he saw that there were no more behind, he clicked the scope on again and sighted that back end of the group, the pulled the trigger. What seemed like a slow sweep back and forth for him ended up taking down most of them within forty seconds as he moved side to side, moving closer to the front of the group. They tried shooting in his direction, but no one was steady enough to do more than make him flinch. There’s a reason I was never a sniper. Not the least being that they don’t tend to have them in the Navy unless you go SEAL or the like, and I’d never have qualified.

He worked from there to ping the remaining people standing. Skidmark went down with perhaps a longer phaser blast than he should have gotten, but Danny admitted to himself that he was sexist enough to have a problem with men who beat women. Even if I was married to a Lustrum follower.

It was Mush and Trainwreck who needed noticeably longer blasts from the phaser to bring them down, but eventually everyone was down, and he gave a quick sweep across the entire group to keep them completely out. He picked up the walkie-talkie and called Mark. “I think I got them all, but be careful sending guys in, in case someone was surprisingly smart and stayed behind.” He could hear the cheer from the compound without the walkie-talkie. “Oh, leave someone behind to tell Armsmaster and whoever else shows up.” He snorted again. “’Cause you know Armsmaster’s not going to want to miss out on arresting Skidmark. Gonna return the rifle after I see you guys dealing with the Merchants.”

In short order, the dock workers were swarming the area and separating the weapons from the people. The fact that they were all wearing gloves, as opposed to the Merchants, meant that a number of these idiots were actually likely to go down for weapons charges. He laughed as he watched a few of his guys basically hogtie Skidmark such that he was not going to be leaving under his own power, even if he used his powers. When he saw that they had it enough under control, he called for Enterprise to beam him up.

Taylor greeted him in the transporter room, as did Sherrel, and he shook his head in amusement. Their temporary prisoner was mildly embarrassed by her unclothed state, but was shaking her head at Taylor’s launched hug of her father. “They didn’t come near you, right?”

“Closest any of them got was pinging bullets off the outside of the building, which probably won’t even show any sign that it was hit, given the formula for that stuff we built it with. Hope a double stun blast doesn’t badly hurt someone, because once they were all down, I swept them all again just to make sure my guys had time to get them all zip-tied. How’d your job go?”

“I think there were three safes we couldn’t get, but from what Sherrel said, even if they can get into them, that only gives the Merchants about twenty-five hundred dollars to run the whole organization on, and I can’t imagine that will cover some of the things they’ll have to pay for. Losing that many millions of dollars and precious metals and gems? Not going to do well for them even if they can somehow break out. And Sherrel’s got some nice tools. I guess she convinced Skidmark to pay for tools rather than steal them, because these are some of the same stuff the Union uses, and doesn’t have any of the marks they sneak on to tell if a stolen tool is theirs. Not pristine, but well loved.”

“They’re literally the tools of my trade,” the girl responded with a shrug.

Danny nodded in understanding. “I’d love to stay and talk, but I’m going to have to get back down there and deal with stuff, and let them know that the phaser rifle I borrowed is back in your hands. Expect the PRT and BBPD to want to see if they can come up with some way of getting something similar for their troops, because non-lethal is always a preferred method for them.” He looked to Sherrel. “Talk to Taylor about other tools if you find you need them. I’m sure we can figure something out to get some for you, even if it’s just a loan.”

“We’ll talk - the entire group of us - and see what we can come up with in near-modern tech versions,” Taylor said. “Probably throw a bone to Dragontech and get her to produce them if we come up with something, because she’s already a known provider for law enforcement. And we’ll look and see what she might think she needs as her own, rather than something the ship can ‘magic’ up in a holodeck.”

“Works for me. We’ll talk later. For now, back to the planet for me,” he said. Then met Enterprise’s eyes and pulled her into a hug. “I’ll talk with Bian as well,” he added.

Chapter 38: Monday, February 14th, 2011 - Various

Chapter Summary

People get to be brilliantly wrong ...

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Kaiser looked to his lieutenants and frowned. “Word from my people within the police department say that the Merchants have been taken out. No one is left to try to break any of their capes out. Apparently Squealer went missing, and Skidmark brought the gang to try to get her back. She’d apparently headed off toward the docks, so they went mob-handed. Some new Tinker weapon took the entire group out in record time, but it was apparently a loaner.”

Krieg spoke next. “Which leads us to the next issue. It’s horrible territory, but we all know that if we do not do something, the ABB will simply walk in and claim the territory for their own, and we can not allow this.”

“Exactly,” Kaiser said. “We need to be ready at a moment’s notice to move on whatever area we get reports they head for. We may not want the territory, but we certainly don’t want them to have it either.” After a pause, he said, “Now onto our other issue. The new Tinker slash ‘Master’ in town. She announced herself publicly, which means one of two things - she’s so powerful that she doesn’t need to worry about anyone else here in town, or she’s putting on a good show to make it seem as if she has much more power than she really does. That display she did with the supposed ‘Enterprise’ was good, but the only thing we saw was a huge device, and something strong enough to lift that container ship. Admittedly that’s an impressive thing, but, we haven’t seen anything more from her other than that she has the money to start some businesses. I can easily explain what we saw on the 22nd of January as a very well prepared holographic display, along with a very powerful telekinetic beam. Why haven’t we seen more of this girl’s power? I posit that it’s because she hasn’t got what she wants us all to believe she has. I think she’s a Tinker who has managed to convince the PRT to go along with her plan for some reason. It could be that it’s actually a PRT plan and she’s really a secret Ward.”

Hookwolf spoke up. “I’m up for a fight as much as the next guy - hell, even more than the next guy - but are you sure about this? Because I really don’t like the idea of maybe startin’ something and getting hit with a huge ‘fuck you’ beam from orbit.” He shrugged. “Like I say, I got no problem with a fight, but it’s embarrassing to think she might be able to take ya out like the original ship from the 60s show.” Everyone looked at him oddly. “What? Might not like the politics that it showed, but it was good mind candy, and they always brought on hot girls in skimpy stuff.” He shrugged.

“It has to be the case,” Kaiser said. “Do you really think that the Simurgh would just let something like that sit there without at least reacting to it? That porcelain bitch doesn’t think it’s even there. If she thinks it’s not there, then there’s nothing there in orbit. And what else has she done? Given one person a Tinker weapon that only knocks people out. If she was dealing with the actual Enterprise, they’ve got weapons that you can fit in the palm of your hand that can vaporize people. So she hands out a stun gun? Then asks for it back before the PRT or police can look at it? Really? That’s no show of power. That’s a fear of being caught out in the game she - or somebody else - is running. So I think we should also make plans to grab either her or her father. That way we can get our hands on a Tinker and find out exactly what she is really capable of doing, rather than the grandiose claims she hasn’t really backed up yet. So I want everyone to come up with some plans to grab either her or her father. Even if she’s not ‘all that’, having a Tinker who can build even stun guns can only be good for us. Being able to take down those Asian bastard quickly? Maybe even hit Lung down for the count before he can even begin to ramp up? Admittedly, that’ll take some luck to manage, but I think it’s worth it.” He looked to Victor. “Maybe she’s got some useful stuff, but I doubt it, given that she’s a teenager. If only your skill theft allowed stealing Tinker abilities as well.” Victor nodded and chuckled at that.

He ended the meeting and they all left. Funny that Hookwolf was the cautious one. Completely unlike him. Then again, he tends toward taking things at face value, and that was admittedly one hell of a show that the girl pulled off, but there’s no way she wouldn’t be flaunting it in other ways. She won’t put replicators around because she can’t make them, but has a good explanation that the sheeple will accept. It’s bullshit. If she’s got that kind of computing power at her command, she should be able to take over any business or company she wanted to. She’d vaporize the damned school she Triggered in if she had that kind of power. She has someone really good coaching her, but she’s not a threat.

                                                                                                    

“That fool Skidmark has left his territory open to us,” Lung said at the gathering. “But we need to be prepared, because the Empire will try to keep us from expanding.” He snorted, a small amount of smoke escaping his nostrils. “They call themselves an empire. They have no idea what a real empire is. We Asians can teach them, and we shall, as well as the rest of the fools here in Brockton Bay, when we rise ascendant at last. With the Merchants out of the way, it opens the way for us to gain territory which will allow us to finally crush the Nazis.”

One of his local leaders carefully drew his attention. “Great Lung, I ask what follows because it is something that my group has asked. I do not challenge you, I just wish an answer." Lung cocked an eyebrow, but motioned him to continue. “What of this girl; this ‘Grey Ghost’? The ship she has seems quite formidable. I have watched the television series, and if that ship is a later generation than what is known from television, it is a danger to the world if she chooses.”

“Yet she has not,” Lung answered. “It suddenly appears in the sky days after she Triggers. It does nothing up there. Most importantly, it does not garner the attention of the Simurgh, who floats in the sky as well. If this ship truly existed, then do you think that the Endbringer would suffer the device to share her chosen demesnes? This alone proves that it is naught but illusion, and that this Taylor Hebert is an illusionist extraordinaire. She must be working with the PRT in some fashion, because they further the lie on PHO. We have nothing to fear from the girl or her ship. She shows no imagination, other than to make the illusion ‘better, more ‘modern’ than the known versions. Fear mongering at it’s most obvious! Perhaps we can grab her at some point after we have secured ownership of the territory that used to belong to the Merchants, because Tinkers are always useful in some way, even if all they can make are trinkets.”

The leader bit his lower lip before asking, clearly fearful, “What of that … ‘tractor beam’, Lord?”

“It has been more than three weeks since her ‘show of power’. Why has she not used it again to remove more ships, or to deal with other situations around the town? Because it was a single use device, meant to strike the simple with awe and fear, to prevent them from rising against her whilst she builds more devices. And those I pay in the police tell me that she has built one new device - and all it can do is stun people. Useless. Striking fear into the few remains of the scrambled brains of the Merchants, but against a dragon? She may as well use a pea-shooter.”

“She is unimportant for the moment, however. If we move quickly tonight, we can raid their houses and remove their money and weaponry before any of them can be released from jail. They may be drugged out fools, but they are known to have significant cash reserves, so we shall relieve them of that cash before the Empire can think of it.”

                                                                                                    

Thomas Calvert sat back in his chair in his underground office and shook his head. She talked a good game, and apparently had Thinker abilities enough to hit some of the money sources before he had been able to reach them, since she had money from somewhere that, while the trail made sense, happened far too close to when her presumed Trigger point was. Once she was under his control and could use that mind of hers for his purposes, he would be unstoppable. Sarah Livsey for her nearly precognitive abilities, and this Hebert girl for her clearly superior computer abilities, as well as the rumors he had heard from one of the schools regarding the relative of the mayor’s who might have Triggered at a young age. He wasn’t certain yet, but hints were that it might be one of the more powerful precognitive senses. Further study was necessary regarding that, so ensure that he didn’t waste resources on the wrong people. No sense kidnapping the girl just to have to kill her later if she wasn’t who she was after. But under his control, he could also find ways to control the mayor’s office and through that, the rest of the city. Brockton Bay was the test bed for his plans of domination. The test bed for dealing with various annoyances, which would help him work out strategies against other players he needed out of the way, such as Accord and the Elite.

But first, he needed to acquire the Hebert girl. She’d been good so far, avoiding situations where she was overtly alone and easily taken. She’s good so far, and apparently her Thinker abilities allow her to reason the best way to avoid capture by another. But she chose poorly. That was an excellent show on the 22nd, but as much as the reports those in the PRT have in the system, there’s not enough there. She has control over technology, as long as it comes from her ‘minion’. I suspect that what is really happening is that she has some technological capabilities and has built an impressive telekinetic device and an illusion generator. The reports from the PRT and BBPD say that the stun gun used was also hers.

Her mistake was that she ‘went big’. She hasn’t done anywhere near enough to drive home the point that she’s the one with all the power, and by now she should have. More than moving a single ship. Admittedly, it was impressive since that was the largest and heaviest one out there, but only once? If she had an actual Star Trek starship, she could easily transport some of the smaller sunken boats aboard her ship and work with them there. Instead, that one show of force or capability and then nothing else.

He reached over and pulled a bottle of water from his small refrigerator and drank from it after splitting the timelines just in case the water decided to hit his computer or keyboard. They were built to withstand such things, but he was a firm believer in not tempting fate with something like that. After no issues in either line, he closed the second one. This girl is a Thinker without enough life experience. I need to either convince her to my side, or get her under my drugged control. Those computer skills alone would be invaluable to me. Have to talk to my tame doctor to see if he’s got an idea for the best drugs to control Thinkers without them losing their usefulness.

He shook his head briefly as he thought about Hebert. She’s good at convincing people that she’s got amazing technology, but she’s not actually using it, so it’s ruining her message. He chuckled to himself. If she were a bit more mature; a little more life experience, she’d have thought of a different route to take in order to fool everyone. Well, if I weren’t about to get involved, I’d say ‘live and learn’, but she’s going to be under my control soon, so she won’t have a chance to become a threat to me.

Chapter End Notes

I didn't post over the weekend because I was driving from the Finger Lakes region in New York back down to my place in Arkansas. (Grew up in NY; moved here because the grandkids are down here.)

Since internet was spotty at best at times (the hotels lie when they say they have good internet *laugh*), this is really the first chance I've had to post. So for those for whom it's already January 1st, Nappy New Year! And for those who are waiting for it still? Well, the same - Happy New Year!

Chapter 39: Tuesday, February 15th, 2011 - Taylor

Taylor woke up on the ship with a smile. Amy was with her, but rather than her usually position, she was the little spoon as Taylor’s body was curled around Amy’s. Taylor’s right hand was full of a softness with a pulse beat against her palm. She was also aware that the temporary ‘gift’ from Amy was still extant and ‘connected’, so she chuckled lustily and took advantage of that fact, since she could feel Amy’s pulse there as well.

Amy woke up extremely happy. When she was done panting, she said, “My nipples are going to be so obvious today. I may have to forgo a bra.”

Taylor snickered. “If you do that, wear a shorter skirt and forgo underwear as well. Because waking up with you like this has me randy as hell. You’re gonna need to shrink this, by the way. I really don’t want to advertise how you affect me anymore than I already do.”

With a mock pout, Amy undid her gift of the night before and the two girls separated to take showers before they beamed down to the planet for breakfast with her father. More fun was had, but they were at least clean.

Appearing in the house, Taylor snickered at Amy’s squeak of surprise. Her dad was making breakfast, and Bian was sitting at the table wearing one of his shirts. And only one of his shirts, which was obvious because it was completely unbuttoned. The woman got up and hugged Taylor, completely unashamed of the view she was giving both girls. “Have a good night?” she asked in a sly voice.

Taylor laughed. “And an amazing morning as well. Just to let you know, Bian, since you’re dressed like that, as it were, that you are one of the people who made me realize that I’m bisexual? So I’m really enjoying the view.” She snickered. “Just thought that the woman who is likely to be my future step-mom should know that her future step-daughter thinks she’s hot as hell.”

“Thank you. I’m still cooling down from last night and this morning as well.” She looked a little worried a moment later. “We … spent some time on the ship last night.”

“One of the holodecks. I know. I intentionally ignored anything going on in that one, because I was already horny enough from being with Amy and Enterprise at the moment. Watching your two and another instance of Enterprise having the same kind of fun? Amy might not have survived, but I’d be having to explain the huge grin she’d have had.”

“Doesn’t bother you that we were there?” her dad asked as he plated up some eggs.

“Nope. Does it bother you that you and I share a lover? She loves me, but she loves you as well. So as far as I’m concerned, she’s helping to keep the most important man in the world happy. And being up on the ship meant that she could generate holographic nerves to really enjoy what was going on.” She smiled slightly wickedly. “Did any of you use contraception last night or this morning?”

Bian simply said, “No. Does that bother you?”

“Not in the slightest. Might move up the date you two plan to get married, but then again, it might not.”

Bian broke out with a huge grin. “I’ve been so worried, but then you say that so easily and I finally realize that you do -” She couldn’t speak more and grapple-hugged Taylor.

“Pity I don’t have standing on Earth,” Taylor said with a smile as she returned the hug, albeit somewhat less forcefully. “Otherwise I’d offer to do the captain’s duty that so many captains say is their favorite. And besides, I wonder if you’d be a little skeeved about having your daughter be the one to pronounce you married.”

He smiled. “Would you complain if we got married without you officiating, then asked for a renewal once you’re eighteen, since that’s how old you have to be?”

“Looked it up already, huh?” she asked with a laugh.

He shrugged. “Well, having the child put the ultimate stamp of approval on the wedding?” He looked at her with a smile, saying everything he needed to.

Enterprise appeared in the room, having had some emitters placed throughout the house. She couldn’t do full fidelity, meaning holographic nerves, but she could at least have a solid form and walk through the house. “Good morning,” she said to them. “Thank you for accepting me, Bian.”

“Taylor loves you, Danny seems to as well. If the two best judges of character I know accept you as someone that important to them, how can I not?” She hugged Enterprise. “You’re easy to love.”

“Thank you. I have some news to impart to the group of you before your day starts, and it is better coming from me, who has a better picture of what is going on. There is a fight occurring in what used to be the Merchant territory, and it is drifting toward the docks. Apparently Lung had the idea to either take the territory - striking while the iron is hot, so to speak - or try to get in quickly and steal the money and weapons from the Merchants before any of them could return. The Empire had the same idea, I suppose, or realized that the ABB would do this and sent their own people in to prevent that. Neither side was happy to discover that someone else had already moved in and removed the cash and weaponry. The weapons have been collected for the police. But, there is a running battle between the ABB and the Empire happening near the docks area. I am keeping watch and if necessary will fire stun beams from orbit to keep them from destroying the docks.”

She turned to Taylor, who had been working on breakfast while Enterprise dealt with the report. “Also, I have been detecting chronoton emissions of an odd sort throughout Brockton Bay, and yesterday was finally able to localized them to an individual. I can’t tell what he is doing, but there is a man in an underground base in the financial district who has this happen to him regularly. He also has the same style subspace connection that all parahumans have, but it is muted. I have noted this muting in a handful of individuals, such as Battery, Triumph, and Gallant. I do not know what this muting means. But whomever this individual beneath the financial district is, he is likely up to no good, as they say, because the base is filled with explosives. Were these explosives to detonate, the financial district would be left in ruins.”

“If you haven’t already, infiltrate his computer systems and see what you can either shut down without his knowledge or disable important routines. I want him to not realize that if he presses his inevitable self-destruct, all he’s going to get is the Price Is Right failure sounds, or a trumpet wah-wah-wah failure noise.” She snorted at the end of that. “Are we going to have to intervene as far as the Merchants area is involved?”

“It would probably be a good idea, because they are approaching areas that belong to you and your companies now. Work has already begun on one building, in fact, and the battle is likely to damage the work already done.”

“Which means a likelihood of leaving school for a while to stop them.” She looked to Amy. “Does Arcadia have a ‘have to deal with moronic villains’ excuse for not being at school?”

“If they did, Vicky would never have attended, given the level of intelligence for most of our villains around town.” Amy laughed as she said it.

Taylor looked to her father. “Can you get contact the school and let them know that I’m going to at least be late, if not out completely? I’ll do what I can to get caught up, and I don’t think there are any tests today that I remember.” She snorted. “At least two teachers promised no tests because they knew that the romantic couples wouldn’t be studying.”

“Should I let them know what you’re doing?”

“Yeah. Might get me a pass in parahuman studies, or I might become the focus of the next few classes.” She sighed. “Well, it’s about time I start making more of a splash on the scene, rather than working behind them.” She wiped her left hand across her face. “I just know that I’m going to have to kill someone to make the point, dammit. I don’t want that on my conscience.”

“How are you going to deal with it?” Amy asked.

“I’ll go on board and take a look at the situation. If I can separate the PRT slash Protectorate from the others, then I’ll probably have Enterprise call and give a warning, then stun the fuck out of the area from space while beaming down. I suspect that if I have to kill anyone, it’s going to be either Lung or Hookwolf. Alabaster might require flat out disintegration to stop if he decides to be an utter nuisance, but his worst aspect seems to be just recovering quickly from things, so if we can cuff him while he’s still out, he’s under control at that point. I’d like to get out of this without killing anyone, but I suspect that Lung is going to require a giant ‘fuck you’ beam to the face.” She shook her head. “How has Hookwolf never realized that Lung is playing with him when they fight? I don’t see Hookwolf fighting an Endbringer in single combat.”

“No matter,” Bian said. “Just be safe out there, okay?” She hugged Taylor again.

“I remind you again, Bian, that I don’t have a problem with hot nude women hugging me.” She waggled her eyebrows. “Just ask Amy.” The girl in question attempted to ignite the house with her blush. “Now, I need to get to the ship, take a look at the scene, get armed, and make sure I’m wearing some body armor.”

Amy stood. “I need to make sure I’m ready for school, now that I’m not living at the Dallon place anymore. Carol’s not sure whether to scream and throw lawsuits or be glad that I’m out of the house now. I miss flying with Vicky, but I like being able to just beam to the school. Might want to see if we can get an area set up to beam in to.”

“I’ll deal with that a little later, I guess. Right now I’m going to have to go shoot Lung in the dick, most likely.” Everyone snorted at that, and Amy and Taylor beamed back up to the ship.

When they were in Taylor’s room, Amy grabbed her and kissed her forcefully. “Be safe, and come back to me.” With that, she left and headed to get her things and then beam down to the planet.

Taylor blinked at the unexpected forcefulness from Amy, but smiled at it as well. She chose full body coverage except for her head, and the outfit she was wearing was rated to withstand an RPG. There was technology in the suit to generate a force field to protect her face, but it tended to be a lot like Vicky’s force field - one hard enough shot and it drops until recharge. Luckily the recharge time was in the same range as Vicky’s.

“Enterprise, can you give me a holographic display of the scene as it is right now? I need to know what I’m beaming in to.” She said this as she headed toward the armory, where she planned to pick up the largest of the easily man portable weapons available. She was going after Lung and possibly Hookwolf, after all.

Enterprise displayed the scene as Taylor made her way to the armory, and she could see that it appeared that the PRT and BBPD were both on the outskirts, letting the two gangs fight it out in the middle. “Call the PRT for me, please. I want to get permission to beam down, but more importantly, to stun everyone from orbit.”

A moment later, the PRT was on the line. “Parahuman Response Team, how can I help you?”

“This is Grey Ghost. I am aware of the fight happening near the docks and wish to render assistance. May I please be connected to those in charge of the current incident, be it someone on site, or someone on console?”

A moment later, she was greeted with, “This is the PRT console. Grey Ghost, you said?”

“Yes, I believe that I have something that can stop this fight, but I need to be on site to do so, and get permission to … well, to do the thing that I think can stop the fight.”

“Please explain. Be aware that I am connecting Director Piggot into this conversation.” She heard a click, and Enterprise whispered that Piggot was now listening in.

“Perfectly understandable. What I wish to do is to fire on the fight in progress from orbit. The ship’s phaser banks can stun people from orbit - this has been possible for well over a hundred years from the point of view of my ship, since it was done in an original series episode called ‘A Piece of the Action’. The only onces I am uncertain that would be stunned unconscious are Hookwolf and Lung, which is why I would like to be on site with a phaser rifle that I can increase the power on until they are downed. I would prefer to avoid killing anyone, obviously.”

Director Piggot came on the line. “As loath as I am to allow firing from orbit, I can’t really stop you from doing so, and appreciate that you’re actually asking permission. How tight a beam would it be?”

“Given the view I have right now of the fight, I would not have to worry about any BBPD or PRT people - and I include Protectorate in that - unless they were in the scrum of the mass of fighting. It looks at the moment as if they’re more directing the fight, and running out to grab people and cuff them as it becomes possible to do so. As I say though, even if someone from our side is in the way, they’d just be stunned and maybe be a little groggy when they woke up. My biggest worry is Lung, and behind him, Hookwolf.”

“And you can guarantee stunning only?” she asked.

“Not to back-talk you, Director, but have you watched the original series of Star Trek? The original Enterprise was capable of doing that, and the technology has only improved. I can guarantee that this ship can fire a stun-only beam from space.” She laughed slightly. “Part of the request is that if I do it without warning, someone might decide that it’s a good time to set off the Endbringer sirens.”

“And that would be a bad thing,” Piggot replied. “Agreed. And yes, I have seen the episode in question, so yes, I give you permission.”

“If your bosses give you flak, Director, let them know that I was very likely to do it anyway, but by making you aware, I’m preventing even worse issues. This fight really needs to stop as soon as possible, because it looks like everyone but Kaiser is out there.” She snorted. “Can’t say that surprises me that he’s not there, the coward. He ‘bravely’ leads from where he’s not likely to get hurt.” She heard two distinct snorts being smothered and smiled. “Please let them know on the site that I’ll be beaming down in a couple minutes, at which point I’ll set off my patent pending Big Honkin’ Space Laser, set on stun.”

She got an actual laugh from Director Piggot. “We’ll do that, Grey Ghost. And thank you for the help.”

With that, the call ended, and Taylor picked up, as she had decided earlier, the largest man portable phaser weapon the ship had, then headed to the transporter room. “By now they should be expecting me,” she said, and chose a spot between the BBPD and PRT contingents.

“Holy shit that’s a big gun,” she heard Assault say, followed by the sound of a slap to the head. She frowned and shook her head. She never liked the blatant disrespect for a person that a move like that showed, which is why she’d never been able to like the character of Gibbs in the televisions show NCIS. She had liked how the show kept things to the human side of things, with the episodes only ever being cape adjacent, or maybe getting a Special Guest Star like Legend showing up for a cameo. (Usually meaning that his favorite charity got a donation from the production company.)

She nodded respectfully to the BBPD nearby before turning to the PRT people. She intentionally spoke to one of the troopers first, rather than ignoring them and going directly to a cape. “Hopefully the office told you that I was coming here. Let me know when, and I can stun just about everyone out there. Not sure if a single shot will take out Lung or Hookwolf, which is why I brought Bessie here,” she said, motioning with the phaser rifle by pulling it back to her shoulder and then relaxing her arm a little.

The trooper nodded. “They said you have a way of stunning them all at once?”

“Yeah, as I said to the Director, I’ve got access to my patent pending Big Honkin’ Space Laser, which I can set to stun. Wide area, but tight enough that it’s only going to hit them, and not bother you guys. Although you may want to shield your eyes. Not sure how bright it’s going to be.”

The trooper reacted the way the director had and snorted at her description. “If you can do it, I’d say go ahead. But be prepared for Lung to react badly.” She looked out at the fight, and Lung was obvious, standing about nine feet tall and apparently in close quarter combat with Hookwolf. She tapped her connection to the ship, focused the beam, and fired.

It was as bright as she expected, and she heard Assault say, “Shit, I saw that through closed eyelids! Damn!” To her surprise, it had downed Hookwolf, but it hadn’t taken out Lung. He looked toward the PRT and began to lope toward them, starting to grow again. She aimed the rifle and mentally set it to heavy stun, then fired. It slowed him down and he shrank some, but this just enraged him. She up it to the killing range and fired again, which staggered him backwards a bit, and he shrank to almost human size, but he responded by roaring and growing again. She upped the power just a touch more and fired again, this time dropping him.

“That might have killed him,” she said. “I had to up the power to human killing levels, and he’d shrunk some, so that final shot might have killed him. I hope not.”

One of the police spoke up. “Well, from my point of view, if it did kill him, it was justified, and he wasn’t taking the hint from the prior shots. And it says nothing but good about you that you hope he’s still alive.” She nodded, and asked for a pack of zip ties, and joined the police and PRT cuffing everyone who lay unconscious on the battle field.

Ships sensors told her that there was a helicopter in the area filming the battle, but she kept zipping people for the police or PRT to pick up. She looked around with the ship’s sensors to see if she could find someone like Victor hiding somewhere nearby, and located him just starting to climb down a building. “Be right back,” she called out and started to run in that direction. The musculature and nerve changes that Amy had done for her father and the others were working beautifully, because she reached the bottom of the ladder that Victor was climbing down before he reached the bottom. Before he could focus on her, she shot him with the rifle, having mentally reset it to stunning. “I need a heavy duty blindfold, in case his powers are visual, the way Oni Lee’s are.” A blindfold materialized in her outstretched right hand, and she quickly fastened it on him, followed by zip-tying him as well, then put him over her shoulder and ran back after she emptied his pockets of things like cell phones, walkie-talkies, or his wallet. “Can I legally claim the contents of his wallet?” she asked Enterprise after finding out that he was carrying not only a significant amount of cash, but also some incriminating information about the Empire and Gesselschaft. Enterprise took only a moment to answer in the affirmative, since everything he was carrying made it clear that he was part of the attack. She took the money, and just because she knew it would annoy him, she took his card from Honey’s Ice Cream Parlor, the best ice cream place in town. The card was punched for nine of the ten slots, so it was just funny to her to take that card as well. Besides, any excuse to go there, she had to admit.

When she returned to the PRT and BBPD, they looked at her in shock, because she was carrying Victor as if he was no worse than carrying a ten pound bag of rice. “Underwent some augmentation that my ship had in the databases, so I have improved strength and stamina,” she said as she lowered Victor to the ground. “He’s got nice equipment, like that scope of his. Gotta admit that if I were less honest, I’d have looted him to the bedrock,” she said with a laugh. She held out his wallet and the contents of his pockets and dropped them into the evidence bag that was held out for them. “Looked like he had information that showed that he was the Empire lookout for this attack, so that makes him part of this, which should help a lot.” She looked around. “And I think we’ve got everyone but the coward here, so it’ll be harder to break them out of transports unless Coil gets involved, and if he does it just makes it that much more obvious that he was involved.”

“The coward?” Assault asked.

“Kaiser. He sent everyone else out, but stayed behind?” So once we get these people packed up and sent wherever, lead me to the paperwork, because I’m sure that I’ve got some to fill out for you guys.” She turned to the BBPD. “Same for you guys. Let me know what you need and I’ll get it to you, as many copies as you need of it.”

“Finally, someone not terrified of paperwork!” one of the police said. “Usually people try to avoid it!”

“If we want convictions, the paperwork needs to be done.” She snorted. “And I run a starship up there. You think the paperwork is bad down here? It may not be paper up there, but it’s still a lot of stuff that needs to be dealt with. I wasn’t joking about the paperwork when I debuted.”

Chapter 40: Friday, February 18th, 2011 - Taylor

As soon as lunch hit at Arcadia, Taylor found an urgent message from Bian hitting her phone. She called immediately. “What’s wrong, Bian?”

“We’ve got a major problem. I guess someone managed to put the right bug in the right ear, because we are now forbidden to use any of the patents you registered. We have been given official notice that all patents in your name are now considered to be of national security importance, and you must be granted permission to build anything using those patents.”

“Okay. Did they say anything about our equipment? As in, did they claim it for themselves?” She was clearly agitated, and could see everyone else tensing up at the table.

“As of this moment, the patents are the only issue,” was Bian’s response.

“Okay, let Dad and as many guys are necessary know. The buildings are fine, we can figure out what to do with them. But any machinery we started to build to begin producing things? Tear it apart. When I get out of school, if they still haven’t thought to call for the machinery, then I’ll come and reclaim and then destroy anything absolutely necessary such as templates. They can have the disassembled machinery to figure out how to rebuild it, but they’re not getting my work in order to save themselves money. I want only stuff that they could find anywhere left behind. And if some of the machinery in question gets destroyed while being disassembled? Oops.” She took a deep breath to calm herself a little. “Also, begin the paperwork to rescind any of the patents that we can still legally rescind. And if they call you back, make sure that they are aware that there will be no more patents coming from me.” Her last word was a growl that made everyone at the table and nearby tables shiver. “Ever.”

“Understood. Let me get on that immediately, Taylor,” Bian said before hanging up.

“What was that about?” Vicky said.

“Apparently the United States government called the legal team for my companies and informed them that we are now forbidden to use any of the patents that were registered in my name, because they are a clear and obvious national security concern, or so has been claimed by the United States government. I am destroying all of the equipment that exists to build the devices I planned, since the next move for the government is to claim all that equipment as government property, since it will make it easier for whomever paid for this to build it and make the profit, other than letting the little teenaged dock whore make money.”

“They didn’t use those words, did they?” Carlos asked.

“No, but since I’m sure it was monetarily pushed - as in the right concerns threw enough money at the right politicians - that they were certainly thinking it. Well, now they have to make their own templates, and be happy with the patents that currently exist. I’m not releasing any more. At all. All they had to do if they wanted to use the patents was invoke Section 1498 of USC Title 28. But this actively takes over ownership of my patents.” She shrugged. “So I take a different route to uplifting the planet. I needed the money for some of my plans, in order to not crash economies. Now I just move everything off planet and build what I need with as much automation as I can create. The US wants to make sure that nothing improves without their permission? So be it. I improve it off-world.”

Carlos shook his head. “When I get to my intern job later, I’ll see if I can pass things up the chain. Maybe they can find out what’s going on.”

“Good luck. That reminds me - I need to figure out who to intern with, since I was originally going to do so through my own companies, but those are gone as of today. Well, the companies will exist on paper, but I’m not running a fucking thing because the government decided that I’m not allowed to.” She shrugged, but she was furious.

When school was done for her for the day, she beamed to the ship to begin the process of beginning off-planet mining of materials. Amy and Vicky went with her. “We’ll start by building our Academy on the Moon,” she said, “and a decent amount of manufacturing. I have the sneaking suspicion that someone thought that they could extort me for something they wanted by doing this with my patents. Basically ensure that they and-or whatever company or foreign government owns them gets a good slice of the pie and controls what I do next. Well, they’ll get to see things showing up and realizing that they have zero control over any of it.”

She shook her head. “It’s not so much that they’ve taken the patents as their own - they can’t legally do that yet. But what they have done is said that my patents are a threat to national security, and therefor cannot be used or disclosed, since that would violate national security. I’m sure that Bian will come back to me eventually with whichever agency did this. But in the meantime, I work on other things.” She shook her head violently, and she felt tears fly from her eyes as she did.

She felt both girls put their arms around her, and she fell to crying over the situation. Some from the release of her furious state, some from just general release of all the emotions that had been running through her since she’d heard, but so much of it was from the letdown. She so wanted to believe that things were going to look up, but she was slapped in the face with this, reminding her that there was a segment of the world that didn’t like change.”

When she’d finally managed to calm, she reluctantly pulled out of their embrace and stepped back. “We need to rework so many of our plans, so I need to get everyone up here. Deena as well. Did I misunderstand something earlier in the week, or is Charlie now dating Deena?”

“No, you saw it right. Charlie was reacting to you on Tuesday, and Deena finally said something that made Charlie realize that not only had she been wrong about Deena - she’d thought that Deena was heterosexual rather than bisexual - but that Deena was thinking that she was rather futilely in love with Charlie. Charlie decided to disabuse her of the ‘futile’ description with a kiss that damned near led to a detention, since the hands had started roaming. Four years of pent up feelings, basically. Charlie’s still more than a little interested in you, and so is Deena, but she’s not going to say anything.”

Taylor let loose with a laugh finally. “Jesus, I think I really am developing a harem.” She frowned suddenly. “Is this a side effect of my powers?” she asked.

Enterprise spoke up. “Not in the way that you are thinking,” she said. “No one is showing any signs of being Mastered, and take into account that I have a few more years of knowing what to look for, given some of the things that have happened to crew over the years. My belief is that with the mental healing that you’ve received from being connected to me, you have allowed yourself to … well, be yourself. Those that are attracted to you see you as being more open to being talked to about such things, and since you were raised to think that multiple relationships are fine as long as all parties are aware and fine with the situation, such a thing develops.”

“Which explains why I’ve got the sexiest thing on Earth as my girlfriend, with her sexy blonde sister as an occasional lover -”

“I’d say ‘Hey!’ in protest, but I can’t really argue with you about it, now that Amy’s found someone that lets her be her,” Vicky said with a grin.

Taylor grinned and continued. “I’ve got my uber hot starship, and I seem to have picked up a few others along the way.” She cocked her head. “Speaking of incredibly hot girls, where’s Sherrel?”

Enterprise chuckled and said, “Holodeck Six. I’m running her through some of the Engineering training, and when she’s done, she was thinking of doing some Tinkering. We’re finding that the tech level of the Federation is at a point that her power is happy, but I can follow all of the plans that she comes up with. There are no odd ‘black box’ sections that are clear uses of her power. I suspect that if we brought more Tinkers aboard and let them work with things like Federation power sources, there would be a lot less weird Tinkertech that breaks down.”

“We’ll have to look into that at some point. Maybe see if we can convince Kid Win up here to work.”

Vicky giggled. “Wear one of your more revealing outfits when you ask him. He’ll agree to anything.”

Taylor blushed a little. “I … have to admit that he seems very nicely put together. And surprisingly muscular, locally speaking, as Heinlein would say.” She looked at the amused girls and said, “I’ve seen him adjust once or twice because of Amy, you, Charlie, me … and I still find it a little weird that guys and girls react that way to me, after all the crap at Winslow. But it’s welcome. I can’t say that I wouldn’t mind getting to know him better. No idea if that would lead to me … ‘getting to know him better’, if you get my meaning.”

“Biblical knowledge?” Amy asked with a grin, getting a nod back.

Taylor shook her head again, obviously planning to change the subject. “Okay. Enterprise, we’re going to need another meeting about where to go from here, so get in touch with Bian and Dad, and the group of us can meet up here. I think Kurt and Lacey were part of that first convocation, so see if they can come as well. We can do some sort of dinner up here as well, possibly. But this is going to get a little contentious, I suspect, and you guys might be talking me down from things. For now? Enterprise, can you point me to a holodeck where I can break things? I just need to work out some of this anger I’m feeling.”

“Could always spar with me?” Vicky offered.

“Thanks, but no. Not in a mood to take a swing at a friend, even if she’s offering and can handle my blows. I just want to break shit right now.” She snorted. “I want to get my tantrum out before I meet with everyone.”

Chapter 41: Friday, February 18th, 2011 - Taylor

Amy was laughing as they left the holodeck. “You’ll need a shower from the sweating that you’ve done, but I find it funny that, since all the stuff you broke and dusted were holographic, that the dust you were coated in just vanished when the program ended.”

Taylor shrugged. “One of the things I like about it. I may go work on the Indian for a little bit before I get my shower, though. Enterprise? What’s the outlook on our conclave?”

“Everyone you asked for is coming, and none of them are happy. Bian has asked that I not tell you who signed the order to classify your patents, and I am allowing that, under the agreement that she tell you at the meeting.”

“I can understand that,” she said. “Telling me when she can stop an explosion is far better than dropping it on me and finding out I decided to disintegrate Lower Slobbovia in response.” She saw Vicky mouth ‘Lower Slobbovia?’ in confusion and added, “Unless the world has changed again and a new country has erupted, there’s no place by that name, so I can’t be said to have threatened a country or state.” Vicky nodded in response.

“Just thought it was an interesting name,” she said.

“Don’t know whether I made it up or came across it in something like Pogo or Li’l Abner or something. One of the older comic strips, back when they were mostly funny or didn’t have as big a problem talking about politics in an amusing way.” She led the way to the holodeck where she had the bike, and found Sherrel there, looking at it and nearly drooling. “Want to help me with it? That goes for you two girls as well,” Taylor said.

“I’d probably make it space capable,” Sherrel said. “Probably don’t want that.” She was startled about the laughter that erupted from all three of them. “What?”

Taylor stopped for long enough to say, “I’m actually thinking of doing exactly that. I talked to Enterprise and we can put a small impulse engine and life support - including some gravity - in place of where the current engine is. I want this to look like the Indian when done, but I fully intend on flying this thing out to Mars at some point.”

“Love to join you, but prison,” Sherrel responded.

“Well, if I’m your parole officer and you end up helping us all have our own motorcycles, we’re thinking of a road trip with them. For testing purposes, of course!” Taylor finished with a grin. “Enterprise, how long before the dinner meeting?”

“You have four hours before you should think about showering and dressing for the meeting.” A work table appeared in the room. “I have all the necessary tools here for you to do further work on the motorcycle,” she said. “Sherrel, I would like to speak with you at some point and see if your stealth technology is compatible with my own, because you can do far more portable versions that I am capable of building at the moment.”

“I’d love that! Be nice to be able to help you out the way you’ve been helping me.” She looked to Taylor. “We talk a lot, and I think she’s calling on some of the therapy stuff in the data banks.”

“Of course I am,” Enterprise laughed gently. “What’s the phrase - ‘if you’ve got it, flaunt it’? You seem like an interesting young woman, so why shouldn’t I help if I can?”

Taylor nodded and stripped to her skin to start working on the bike, and saw a huge smile on Sherrel’s face as she did the same. “I figure that with the tech available here, why get grease and oils on clothing, no matter how easy it is to clean off?”

“And I keep forgetting that you don’t have a problem with nudity.” The tinker snickered. “And to be honest, seem to enjoy other people’s nudity.”

“I’ve always enjoyed art of various forms. What’s the human body but another canvas?” She shrugged and turned to the motorcycle. “What I really need at the moment is to work on the body of the motorcycle, to make sure it’s up to snuff.” She snorted. “I’m learning how to ride on the holodeck, and I’m getting fairly good, according to Enterprise. But even if I plan on putting in a sound generator for putt-putt noises, I want the body as pristine as I can make it.” She paused. “It’s funny. Part of me wants to restore everything, including the engine, but I just like the idea of a flight-capable 1940 Indian too much.”

Enterprise cleared her throat. For obvious reasons she didn’t need to do that, but Taylor thought that it was a nice touch. “I have scans of the entirety of the bike and all its parts. Why not rebuild this one from the ground up and sell it. It would not be an imposition to create the new frame and such to have your flight capable Indian, built from materials up here. Either replicating it whole, or giving you the parts to build it with.”

Taylor cocked her head. “Hmm, a good possibility. Let’s get the frame worked on first while I decide on that, since we’re not going to have to worry about the engine for a little while. I’m still angry enough that I don’t want to be dealing with fiddly bits at the moment.” The others nodded, and helped where they could, such as Vicky working the handlebars with various levels of sandpaper grits, until she had a very shiny bit of steel in her hands. Taylor and Sherrel worked on welds where necessary, and Amy worked on checking out what of the leather and such could be salvaged.

They were all finished with what they wanted to be done by the time that Enterprise pointed out that they should get ready for the dinner meeting, so they headed to their staterooms to get ready. Taylor chose the single shoulder tunic and knee length skirt in Starfleet design, to show that she was acting as captain as well as Taylor. She met the others who had chosen decent clothing, but she was touched by Amy’s choice to wear a Starfleet uniform as well, in her Starfleet blue. They headed to the chosen room, where Enterprise had set up something of a buffet style, with hot and cold dishes available.

As they all sat, Taylor said, “I’m hoping that I worked out the worst of my tantrum in the holodeck breaking holographic representations of valuable things, then working on my Indian motorcycle a bit with Sherrell, Vicky, and Amy here.”

“I think it was more ‘righteous anger’ than ‘tantrum’,” her father said, “but that might be because I decided to go help the guys with dismantling. We’re trying to avoid to much wanton destruction in case the government goes back on their decision, so that we can rebuild faster, but yeah, I was … less than happy, shall we say?”

Taylor smiled her thanks at him before she looked to Bian. “Do we know which agency got a bug in the ear or ass about me patenting things?”

“Who do you think?” she snarked back. “Chief Director Costa-Brown was the only one who could sign such paperwork, and that group was also the one that I most suspected, since they like to try to claim - and constantly fail, mind you - that if a Tinker makes it, it qualifies as Tinkertech, even if a working version can be built by non-parahumans. You represent a … what’s the phrasing I want … a quantum shift, maybe? You represent a major change in things. You have a powerful ship, and have been patenting things across the board, not just tightly focused improvements. This is a very lucrative thing for whomever is in control of those patents. They legally can’t use the patents themselves without paying you for the usage, but there are too many court cases to list right now where the government is sued after the fact.”

“Then we need to get word to the PRT legal team in Washington that we are watching. We will go after anyone who begins to produce things that are based on our patents, which means that the PRT’s favorite Tinker company will end up sparking an international incident if they start producing our tech. Make sure that DragonTech is made aware of this. I am the owner, not the United States government, so the US can not give her permission to build things with my patents. I suspect that with the access to the money I have due to Enterprise’s machinations, I could likely bankrupt DragonTech if I needed to. I don’t want to, but I’ll be damned if I’m going to let them steal from me.”

“Good,” Bian said. “I’ve started writing such things already, since I suspected that you’d want to go that way, but won’t send them until you approve.”

Sherrel cleared her throat. “Might want to set up a press release thing about this. I wouldn’t put it past the PRT wonks to try to have their PR people spin it to make it sound like you yanked things, rather than them forbidding you from using them. Get ahead of the narrative, I think I’ve heard it called?”

“Good thinking, Sherrel. I can work on that tonight with Enterprise and the rest of you, and get something to be released on the internet in enough places that the PRT worms that they use to kill videos and such that they don’t like can’t stay ahead of it. I have long suspected that PHO is actually a PRT thing that they allow to look ‘lawless’ on the internet, so that people don’t think about the PRT’s stance. Because if you look carefully, the PRT takes a beating on there, but overall has a net positive view from the posters, who complain, but overall think that it’s Costa-Brown and the rest who cause most of the troubles.”

“It doesn’t hurt that the main admin for the site is Dragon,” Enterprise said. “I couldn’t help but figure that out after some simple - at least for me - detective work. So if the main administration for the site is run by someone known to be extremely friendly to the PRT and its goals? Taylor’s concept isn’t improbable.”

“I’m going to move ahead with building things on the Moon,” Taylor said. “The academy, for one thing, and I see no reason why manufacturing can’t be done up there as well. I want to wait for a bit to travel off world, because I’ve come across references that powers don’t work as well off planet. Hard to say, because mine seem fine here, and honestly? It’s a subspace connection to another world, so I can’t really see why that wouldn’t carry with you anywhere in the galaxy. Might be easier on Earth, but subspace is non-local. If it is true, then it says something interesting about the thing that grants powers, because it would mean that they were programmed to be that way, to keep people on planet. Which makes me curious about things if it’s true.”

She rubbed her face, and Amy rubbed her hand on Taylor’s back. Lacey spoke up. “I think that more than the announcement getting ahead of the PRT’s likely non-explanation, trying to blame the lack of work on you, you need something of a charm offensive. Start doing some interviews. Take advantage of the fact that you’re a damned good looking girl and dress as sexy as you dare for the interviews. I think between Bian, me, Amy, Sherrel, and Vicky - especially Vicky, since I know she designed those uniforms you’ve been wearing around town - we can get you dressed up in a manner that makes you look innocently hot as hell.”

“Well, she’s got a good starting point,” Sherrel said, “since she’s already hot as hell.” Taylor blushed slightly.

“Exactly. But dress her such that it looks like she doesn’t realize how sexy she is - she’s fifteen and just dressing properly for the interview, after all - and I guarantee you that the guys will watch the interviews, and the ladies will listen to what is being said. And they’ll all listen because I’ve heard you talk, and I remember your comments at your debut. You gave people hope. So when you talk about being forbidden to use your own stuff? I know you can spin it to put the PRT on the back foot. And that’s what you need to do. They want you acting like a child as they do this to you, so that they can offer to help you ‘if you’ll just sign up with the PRT’. If you come out swinging - especially if it doesn’t look like you’re swinging - then they have the burden of fixing their image.” She looked to Enterprise. “Would I be correct in assuming that you have a decent amount of information on demagoguery?”

“That I do.” Her face went a little dark. “And they’ve hurt my Captain, who is also my friend. I have no issue with teaching the PRT how to wage a battle of images.” She grinned an evil grin. “The problem is that they don’t realize that I’m a sapient being. The local group may, but I strongly suspect that this maneuver will be pissing off Director Piggot, who was looking forward to equipment improvements that she’s not going to be able to get now.”

“That’s something I’ll want to stress in the interviews,” Taylor added. “That it’s not the local PRT putting me in this position, because they’ve been more than helpful. I make sure that I stress that it’s the group in Washington that’s doing this. That could put even more stress on the Washington branch, because all the other directors might see that this would be hurting them as well.” She snorted. “Seeing Brockton Bay as the test bed for new technologies for the PRT to use, which have now been taken from them by their own leaders.” Her grin was as evil as Enterprise’s. “Getting her own people complaining, and pretty much demanding an explanation as to why the patents were declared national security risks? There’s got to be a mechanism for removing even the topmost in an agency, even if it means that it’s the President who does it. Get enough dissent in the ranks and I could see Costa-Brown being allowed to ‘retire after her long service with the PRT’.”

“The big thing,” Bian said, “is getting ahead of the story. Their biggest mistake so far was not having Glenn Chambers already have a story to go in the pipeline to release today. I’m betting we can get something on the Internet at the very least tonight. In fact, why don’t we work on that now? Willing to record our ideas, Enterprise?” Enterprise nodded.

Vicky pulled out her PADD and began working on designs. “I’ll kick in verbally as ideas strike me, as necessary, but I’m going to do my part in designing those ‘innocently sexy’ outfits for her to wear. She should start the process with her first release. And if I can come up with designs, we know that Enterprise can make them real at the drop of a virtual hat. I want her in something that looks innocent but stops traffic.” She chuckled. “And as we discovered, I can do sexy in an outfit design. It’s not just Taylor that makes you want to see that Starfleet microdress I designed on the floor.”

“Ooo! I want one for wearing around Danny then!” Bian said, making Danny blush slightly and shake his head in fond exasperation. They all chuckled and settled down to coming up with the message that Taylor would be reading to the Internet.

Chapter 42: Friday, February 18th, 2011 - Internet video

The video opened with Taylor sitting in what appeared for all the world to be Ten Forward aboard the Enterprise, with the stars in the background, and a hint of Earth in the view. She was wearing what looked to be a casual version of a Starfleet uniform in Command Red - loose slacks and a blouse with just a small hint of cleavage. She had a drink on the table in front of her and her face was serious, but open.

“Hello America. I’m Taylor Hebert, also known under my cape name of Grey Ghost, or the position I find myself most proud of, Captain Hebert of the USS Enterprise, hull number NCC-1701-G. I apologize if I am perhaps not the most engaging speaker you’ll hear on the Internet, but I have something I need to say.”

“During my debut to the world, I announced that I was planning on slowly releasing technology to improve the lives of people in the world. I wouldn’t be crashing economies by releasing Federation level technologies because of the inherent dangers with some of those technologies. Instead, I would be releasing things such as a literal room temperature superconductor. Most often that reference is actually referring to a superconductor that doesn’t require heroic measures to keep cold. The one I patented is literally a superconductor at temperatures up to ninety-eight degrees Celsius, or roughly two hundred and eight degrees Fahrenheit. Those who understand electronics will realize just how amazing a material like that can be.”

She sighed and leaned forward slightly, and the shadow between her breasts became ever so slightly more noticeable. A very slight scowl came across her face as she continued to speak. “Other patents include things such as lighter clothing that can withstand more than normal clothing. In a city like Brockton Bay, a shirt that can stop a bullet without being bulky can be a literal life saver. Other patents were things that would have very little use for the average consumer, but the police and fire departments would be able to use to make their lives easier, and by making their lives easier, making it much easier to save the average person.”

“There was a plan in place to put the first safe fusion plant in operation for Brockton Bay, as a test bed for rolling them out across the country, freeing up dwindling coal and oil reserves for other places that can’t yet switch from those technologies for various reasons, such as the many useful byproducts that can be extracted from coal and oil.”

She sat back in her chair and openly frowned, clearly unhappy. “But those plans are now permanently on hold, because the head of the PRT has declared that all of my patents are a national security risk, and I am forbidden to use them, as are all other companies and countries. There was no explanation of why these are security risks, at least none given to me or those who will run my companies until I am of age, Instead, just a statement that my patents are a risk to national security, so I am to cease and desist using those patents.”

“With this being the case, I find that I cannot in good conscience release any more of the patents that I was intending to file, since they are likely to immediately join the others under the national security umbrella. This means that none of the slight advancements that I was planning to slowly release to the world will come to pass, since the PRT has decided that the changes in technology that I offered are far too dangerous to be allowed into public use.” Her scoffing tone was not entirely hidden.

“Since I refuse to damage the economies of the world, this means that I will not be releasing anything. I will not develop them aboard my ship and slowly leak them to the world, because to do so would be taking jobs from those who need them here on Earth. I live in a city that is in an economic slump, so I understand about taking jobs away from those who need them, and I will not do that. My father works hard to ensure that the people who work for him have work, so that they are able to feed their families. I will not dishonor the lesson he and my mother taught me about how to be a good citizen; how to care for my fellow man.”

Her tone changed again as she spoke, becoming more openly scoffing. “I am certain that the PRT will release a statement regarding the patents soon. Listen carefully to what the Washington people tell you in that release. More importantly, listen to what they don’t tell you.”

She settled back to a friendlier mien as she took a momentary drink from the glass at her side. When she spoke again, it was far friendlier. “I have no beef with the local offices here in my city, or with any of the local offices. The East North East PRT offices have been as helpful as they possibly can be since I made them aware that I exist, and were looking forward to testing the equipment I planned to offer. Unfortunately, that now can’t happen, and for that I apologize, Director Piggot. You have been more than helpful since the very first day that we met. This came from above you in the chain of command. In fact, it was signed off on by the only person who was legally capable of signing such an order - the Chief Director of the PRT.”

The harsh tone returned. “A simple meeting explaining the issues would have been appreciated, rather than being blind-sided on the morning of Friday, February 18th. Perhaps something might even have been able to have been worked out. But now, we are stuck with an inability to hire people for jobs that can now no longer exist.”

She leaned forward once more and spoke in a firm tone, the type heard when delivering proclamations. “Since I still desire to improve the lot of my fellow man, I will be reaching out to Canada, the United Kingdom, the European Union, and Australia, to see if perhaps I am capable of registering my patents there without the likelihood of having them silenced for national security reasons. I believe that many of the items that can be built using those patents are vital to the improvement of our lot as a people. Not just Americans, but the entire world.”

Chapter 43: Saturday, February 19th, 2011 - Taylor

The group met again on the Enterprise, this time for lunch. Bian was giggling. “Well, you set the cat amongst the pigeons, Taylor. We’ve already gotten a number of requests from Good Morning America, Today, the BBC, and some I’d never heard of before.” She looked at Taylor. “This ship has a universal translator, right?” She got a nod back, since Taylor was right in the middle of taking a bite of her sandwich. “That means you should be able to do some of the Spanish and other language shows if you want.”

“We’ve gotten a couple opening salvos, if you will, from Canada and Australia, with requests to meet with you. Basically meetings to see if meetings can be set up. But that comment you finished with has international ramifications, and I’m surprised we haven’t seen the PRT on our doorsteps demanding to talk with you. Rebecca Costa-Brown does not like being challenged, and you didn’t throw down a glove at her feet, you slapped her in the face with a gauntlet.” Bian paused. “Why do the movies always get that wrong?”

“Because it’s more of an insult to the modern viewer to be slapped across the face,” Vicky said simply. “While the original was an insult back then - since you were, in a way, forcing them to be a servant and pick up the glove in question - today it just doesn’t have the same tone of offense. Who knows, in another hundred years, slapping someone across the face may not be the thing, but firing off a sternly worded memo will call down hell on you and yours.” She shrugged. When she saw Amy raising an eyebrow at her, she chuckled. “Remember, the bimbo act is to make people underestimate me. Like you, Deena, Charlie, and Taylor, I’m in the Honors track, and not just because I’m a parahuman.” She openly grinned. “I brain goodly.” The table laughed at that.

“Still, it’s a little surprising to hear something like that out of you,” Amy said.

“I pay attention to history because it really does have a connection to fashion, though most people only really skim the surface of it. I study for the understanding of why a given fashion may have developed a certain way. I’d love to know the logic behind the Minoan fashion of designing dresses that left the breasts bare, if the renditions we’ve seen are to be believed. But we know so little about them. And I’d love to bring back that fashion,” she said, thrusting her chest forward, “because these are spectacular!” She was grinning widely as she finished.

“Not gonna argue with you on that,” Sherrel said. She thrust her own chest forward. “These ain’t half bad either.”

Taylor snorted. “Saying that is like saying that Van Gogh was an okay painter, or that the Mona Lisa is maybe a little famous.”

“Magnificent breasts aside,” Lacey said, “where do we go from here? I don’t know how much of what we hear about Costa-Brown is the truth, but if she is used to getting her own way, then she’s probably going to storm into town and try to browbeat Taylor into submission. And she’s apparently really good at getting her way.”

“That’s why there will be no meetings with her that do not involve a lawyer present,” Bian said. “And since this is a single party record consent state, if she tries to meet with Taylor at the house, then I believe Enterprise can do a good recording from a believable angle?”

“Since my scans are completely three dimensional, it is literal child’s play - at least for the Federation - to choose an angle that looks like a camera might have been in that spot. Since I follow my captain everywhere, I can allow for at least an audio recording of all meetings.”

Taylor spoke up. “I was thinking - shocking, I know - that as much as it was said to make the US think twice about that ban, that it would be a good idea to expand to other countries. Canada at the very least, since it’s so easy to get there for me if need be. Need a passport to visit any factories we build, but by making it an international thing, it helps my cause so much better, I think.”

“Which cause?” Kurt asked. “Slapping the PRT in the head, or getting the tech out there to the masses?”

“Why can’t it be both?” she responded with a chuckle. “If I stay purely American in scope, then it makes the world think that I’m only doing this for America, despite what the series intended. I want to start in nations that I know are friendlier to us. I know that the CUI is going to do their damnedest to steal our tech, and will probably eventually succeed in getting some, but we know we can’t trust them. Hell, we’ve got that idiot Coil in Brockton Bay who is probably railing against RCB because it means that he can’t steal the tech.” She looked to the Enterprise hologram. “How’s things with him, by the way?”

Enterprise responded, “I’ve finally managed to find a point when he wasn’t displaying chronoton emissions of any sort, and worked my way into his systems. If he attempts to set off his failsafes, they will … well, fail. I own his system, and at a moment’s notice, I can take all of his money. I am examining things to find when the best possible chance to take him into custody might be. But he will be going into custody in one way or another. Given some of what I’m finding out in his personal files, I’m wondering if it might not be better that he leave in a body bag. The only thing the man needs to complete the image he’s cultivating is to have a mustache that he can twirl in an evil manner. His files show that he was in contact with Rebecca Costa-Brown, by the way, very recently.”

“How does he have access to her?” Lacey asked, confused.

“Given the files he has set for release in order to cause chaos in case his plans fail, I have no issue breaking the Unwritten Rules. They are, after all, not law. Coil used to work for the PRT, and is now a consultant for them. His name is Thomas Calvert. He appears to have quite a few connections, and it seems as if he is trying to engineer the escapes of several of the parahuman prisoners taken on Tuesday. The ones he seems to be working hardest on are Lung and Hookwolf.”

“Of course,” Vicky snarked. “The two most likely to go off half-cocked and start fights just because they were in jail.”

“Anything we can do to stop these plans?” Taylor asked.

“I suspect that our best bet would be to ‘strike while the iron is hot’, as they say. If I can work with Sherrel for a while, I believe that we can managed a man-portable cloaking device, as opposed to what is aboard the ship. Once we have that, it can be replicated enough for every member of the strike team. Phaser rifles and such, and all team members wearing clothing that the Federation sees as armored. I do not believe that any of his mercenaries could get through that with the laser rifles that they sometimes carry. Plus, emptying the armory just before the strike team enters, to avoid grenades.”

Taylor snorted. “Replace everything in the armory with bio-locked phasers and such. Only I can use them.” She giggled at that. “I can just see them running in, yelling ‘SWEET!’ and then discovering that the rifles don’t work for them.” Everyone at the table snickered at the image.

Her father spoke up. “I see it all the time in sci-fi movies, but don’t really recall it from anything in Star Trek, unless it was something Our Heroes were going up against. Armed drones? Is that a thing or a possibility?”

Enterprise smiled. “We don’t often use them, because the captains tend to like to send away teams for some reason, but I could easily create a large number of drones. If we can install some of Sherrel’s cloaking devices in them, I could flood the place with them and pretty much take out everyone we need to take down. If we can get this done soon, I could see us being ready to go after Coil by no later than the 25th of the month. Given how easily Sherrel can make certain things such as the cloaks, we could even be ready to go by tomorrow.”

“As soon as we know when we can deal with him, I’ll contact the PRT and the BBPD and let them know. I’ll need to be able to give them all the secret exits from the facility, so if you could have those prepared in a format the PRT can read easily, that would be great.”

Enterprise smiled. “It is nice having a captain who understands my capabilities.”

“I’m part of you, in a very real sense. I know what these sensors can do, and that they haven’t created a force field yet in this time and place that can completely keep you out. Plus, you said you’d mapped all the explosives, which means that you had to have checked out every nook and cranny.” She paused. “What the hell is a cranny, anyway?”

Enterprise laughed. “A small, enclosed space or opening. Current;y only used sparingly or to describe a certain company’s bread products.” Everyone else chuckled at the interplay.

“Okay, so Coil is kinda on the back burner until we’re ready to hit him all at once. As for the thing we came here to talk about, I’m realizing that I’m going to need someone to help me figure out what needs to be done and when. Personal assistant, maybe? I can’t keep relying on Bian for it, because she’s one of my lawyers. I need someone whose only job is scheduling meetings and media appearances and the like. Press releases. Social media posts. But it needs to be someone I can trust to do the job the way I want it done.
