I’m thinking of hiring Vicky on as my personal fashion designer, because this girl creates some of the most amazing stuff I’ve seen.” She blushed. “I don’t dare wear the mindress - well, more of a microdress, to be honest - that she designed, because it … well, it ends up looking more like something you wear for foreplay, to be honest. It makes even my body look amazingly hot.”

“It does have a good starting point,” Sherrel said simply. “I’m not sure it could make Roseanne Barr look that good, to be honest.” She shrugged. “Then again, that might just be because I don’t like Barr in the slightest.”

“Are you serious, Taylor?” Vicky asked, eyes wide. “Your personal designer?”

“As well as the designer for my version of Starfleet, if you want.”

“I can answer for Vicky on this one,” Amy said. “It’s basically one word - ‘IF?’” Vicky was nodded like a bobblehead doll.

“Then get with Bian and work out a contract for your services. You know what you’re worth, and I’m looking forward to seeing Amy in that uniform she asked you to design.” She smiled. “I may wear the skirt of that with the single shoulder tunic I wore at my introduction to one of my media appearances. I think I can manage ‘innocently sexy’ with something like that.”

“Well, you sure as hell have the ‘sexy’ down,” Amy said quietly. At the snickering from everyone else in the conference room, she asked, “Said that louder than I intended?” The others nodded at her with smiles on their faces.

Her father said, “I know a few people, and Bian can talk to some, and we’ll set up some interviews for you, to see if any of the people we throw your way are a fit for you? ‘Cause you’ve got to be able to get along with them, so us choosing for you just won’t work.”

“I trust you, but yeah, I need to be able to talk to them and not want to strangle them. Would they be heading my PR group as well, or should I be dealing with other people for that?”

“Probably want to find a good PR firm. To be honest, I’ll talk to some of our guys in the union,” her father answered her. “We toss things past them regularly to keep our name out there in the minds of the average joe. A smart union has at least some idea of public relations.” He rolled his eyes. “Which is why some of the big ones are a mess, because they forget that.”

Taylor got up and walked to the window, and heard her father chuckle, because he knew she was going to be thinking out loud. It was a habit she’d gotten from both of her parents; her mother especially, since the woman ended up doing it as if she was teaching a class via the Socratic method. “Okay, we’ve already got some inquiries from media and other governments. We need to respond but make them aware that we’re … how do we say that we’re still getting our PR group together without saying that we’re still getting our PR group together?”

“Leave that to me, love,” Bian said. “Part of being a good lawyer is knowing how to phrase things to say only what you want to say. I’ll tell both sides that since this is such a recent decision, that you’re exploring the various ins and outs of the ramifications. Only I’ll say it dressed up based on who I’m talking to; bureaucratic words for the governments and something a little more media based for the various media.” She grinned. “And I’d recommend definitely taking at least one interview with one of the Spanish speaking shows, since you’ve got a universal translator.”

“True,” Enterprise said. “And I’ve been paying attention to the world, so I have local idioms for just about everywhere, and since we’re so connected, I can ensure that your speeches use some of those idioms.”

“We’ll give it a day or two before we agree to CNN or Fox,” Bian said. “I think we can go with something like Good Morning America for Tuesday, if you’re agreeable. Today would like you for Monday.”

Taylor turned to look at the table and ran her hand down her face. “God damn it. How much school is this shit storm going to make me miss? Morning shows for Monday and Tuesday, okay. Any of the news networks only get me after school is done for the day, okay? I’ll likely have to miss Monday and Tuesday, although if we can let the school administration know in advance, they might even want to make some sort of assembly out of it, and turn it into a talking point for some of the current events and politics classes.”

Amy smiled. “This is one of the reasons I love you, Taylor. You have all this crap happening, and not only do you not want to miss school, you look at it as a teaching moment for the other students if you do miss school. You know what’s important. And yes, defending yourself against what Costa-Brown did is definitely important, but you don’t want to miss school.”

“I’ve got a school I like now. The fact that it’s got a bunch of sexy girls and guys there is just icing on the cake. I like my classes and don’t like missing them.” She shrugged. “As for everything else, well, I need that personal assistant soonest, as well as starting to get a handle on public relations. I’ve got a big backlog of patents to apply for, and one of the things to see is if someplace like Canada can let me patent things there that are US national security concerns.” She shook her head. “So much of what else I need to worry about are things that I can’t do anything about until we get this shit with the US government worked out.”

Chapter 44: Monday, February 21st, 2011 - Taylor

Taylor stood off in the wings, waiting for them to announce her. She’d chosen the skirt that Vicky had designed for Amy along with the single shoulder tunic that left her left arm bare. She had no idea what they might talk about, so she was prepared for a lot, but was very glad that she had Enterprise in her ear, so to speak. She also had the life support force field on to keep her warm, and because it would add extra protection if something managed to get past security. They knew that wasn’t likely, but there was no sense in being lax on your own security. She also had a cloaked drone about the size of a basketball near her, but placed such that no one should be able to tell it was there. Again, further protection. Enterprise was in complete control of that, with ‘orders’ from Amy to keep Taylor as safe as she could without ruining Taylor’s appearance on the show.

“Welcome back from the break. Our next guest is a young woman who has caused quite a stir since the end of January. Most recently she’s been involved in a situation with the United States government regarding patents. Please welcome Miss Taylor Hebert!” Taylor walked out and waved toward the audience outside the windows, all bundled up for the cold weather. She headed over and sat in the chair they had set aside for her, smiling at the hosts. “Welcome to the show, Miss Hebert. Do yo prefer a different name, by the way?”

“I’m good with Taylor, unless I’m dealing very specifically with the entity that is a part of my parahuman power. If I am dealing directly with issues regarding the USS Enterprise, then I prefer Captain Hebert, but this is just a meeting between friends, so Taylor is just fine.”

“It sounds amazing that the actual Enterprise is in orbit above our planet,” Matt Lauer said a little breathlessly. But we’ve seen it in the news, and there was that rather spectacular debut where Vista helped you bring the ship above Brockton Bay, and we all saw the registration numbers. The most recent version that is considered canonical to Paramount is the Enterprise E, which we saw in the movie First Contact. How did this one come about?”

“I’m still working my way through the archives,” Taylor admitted, but I suspect that my ship is from roughly forty years or so later than the movie, in that universe, that is. The movie came out the year after I was born,” she said with a slight laugh. “There’s a lot different in this ship, such as the addition of emergency holograms for all departments, not just Medical. There’s a hologram that can advise the captain, for example, as needed. I’m not sure how much her previous captain used her, but I’ve been relying on her a bit to help me figure things out.” She shrugged, “Hey, if you’ve got the resources, it’s foolish not to use them.”

“If you don’t mind me asking,” Meredith Vieira said, “but what exactly is your power? And is it how the Enterprise exists up there in orbit?”

“To answer your second question, the answer is sort of? When I Triggered, there was some odd confluence that no one understands, and I apparently connected to the Enterprise via a subspace connection and pulled her here. That’s a real Federation starship up there. If I were to walk out of this building and a bus fell out of the sky on me, that ship would still be there. As for my power? Insane multitasking, really. As I explained it to the East North East PRT branch when I went in for testing, I can basically simultaneously run every single function aboard that ship that doesn’t need someone to physically do something. Can’t do that to any other technology on the planet, but I can for that ship. If it requires something to be physically moved from point A to point B, and I can’t get a hologram to move it for some reason - such as no emitters where I need things moved - then I can’t do it. But as we’ve seen from the Next Generation episodes, there’s a lot that can be done by tapping a few things on those consoles, like rerouting power to a station, or setting up and firing a probe to explore the solar system. That I can do. But if the probe has to be picked up and moved and there isn’t automation to do it? That probe's not getting fired until I can get it loaded.”

“We’ve seen videos of some of what you can do, and heard some stories. That leads us into the most recent story,” Matt Lauer said. “Do you have any idea why your patents have been declared a national security concern?”

“I have suspicions, but nothing concrete. I honestly don’t see how a design on making a literal room temperature superconductor breaks national security. It’s useless as a weapon in and of itself. It’s only usefulness is in building electronics, and those electronics can be used for almost anything. I suspect - and I want to stress here that this is purely my opinion - that the Washington headquarters of the PRT did not like that my patents don’t fall under their jurisdiction. There is some serious money that can be made from these, by leasing rights to manufacture, or manufacturing things myself.”

“So you think that the PRT is making an effort to quash these patents?”

“Let me stress that I believe - and again, this is only my opinion; I have nothing concrete to back this thought up - that the Washington HQ is looking at the amount of money that can be made, and would like to force me to work through them to allow them to be used. This is something that has to come from the very top, especially since in the PRT, the only person who could sign such an order is Chief Director Rebecca Costa-Brown. The local PRT - local for me, I mean - is very helpful and I know that Armsmaster was looking forward to leasing some of my patents to build some of his own Tinkertech. I have nothing but good to say about the PRT East North East. Every interaction I’ve had with them has been excellent, and I really hope that rulings from Washington don’t end up severing that bond we’ve been building. I really don’t want to tar the entire PRT with this brush, because I suspect that it’s a very small group at the very top who have worked on this decision, with no explanations at all as to what make these patents a national security concern.”

“Your Internet response garnered some interesting reactions,” Vieira said.

Taylor winced a little and rubbed the back of her neck. “I … was still a little angry when I recorded that. I would likely have found a more politic way of stating my intentions had I waited a little longer, but I still stand by what was said. Unless I know what I did wrong in those patents, I can’t in good conscience release any more to the US, because I don’t know what’s forbidden and why.”

Matt Lauer spoke next. “To change the subject a little, what will you do if Paramount insists that you change the name of your ship, since it could be seen as trademark infringement.”

Taylor shook her head. “I’d really prefer not to. As I said at my debut, the name of Enterprise is more than just the name of a ship. It’s a label for a dream. A dream of space, and exploration, and unity, and constantly learning more. She never flew a mission, but the shuttle Enterprise was named for my ship’s original predecessor. And sadly, that word is accurate. The original is gone, disappearing in the skies over the Genesis planet. But the ship carried such a legacy that the next was given the same name, just with a change to the registry. And this has continued down the line. I suspect that her disappearance in her home universe has caused the building of a new Enterprise, the Enterprise H.” She unfocused for a moment as she said, “I have said it to others, and will doubtless say it again, but by becoming captain of this ship, I have an awesome and terrifying responsibility to the name and the legacy. I have to think about what my actions may do to the name and the legacy. I was uncertain about the route I have taken, basically throwing down a gauntlet in regard to the patents, but I want a world where the Enterprise could come into existence based purely on the people. We’ll never have a Utopia, because people just aren’t like that, not to mention the unsavory aspects of the literary Utopia that we get the name from. But we can work toward a world where we don’t give each other the hairy eyeball just because our skin is a different color or because we love someone of a different gender or religion. I want a world where it’s more important what you are inside than some stupid compartmentalizing because of a thing you’ve got no control over anyway, like skin or sexual orientation. And by slowly working toward the kind of world where replicators can exist without destroying the economy, I like to think that I honor the name.”

There was a little silence on the set after she finished saying that, and then she could see them cut to commercials. “From the way you talk,” Meredith said, “I don’t see you having any problems living up to the name.”

“Thank you. Sorry for taking so much, but when I get going on something, you kinda need to duct tape my mouth. And as for what I’d do regarding the name? Well, I’m a daughter of the docks and the sea. We’re a kinda superstitious lot, and changing the name of a ship is usually considered a really bad idea, unless that name is seen to have bad luck. And the Enterprise is anything but.”

They were given warning that they were coming back from commercial, and she was still on set. Guess I’ve been doing a good job. As the light came on, Matt said, “We’re back with Captain Taylor Hebert of the Enterprise. Perhaps we should have announced you that way when you came in.”

“I’m fine with the original introduction,” she replied. “I’m not so much here as the representative of the nascent Starfleet I hope to someday get going, I’m here as a citizen trying to do some good in the world. So really, in that situation, Miss was better.”

“We were impressed by your comments about the name and the legacy. Do you mind if we ask about the fashion?” Meredith asked. “We’ve seen you wearing things that give the feeling of the television series uniforms, but they’re nothing we’ve seen on the screen.”

“I’ve got a friend who is into fashion design, and I asked her to mock up some designs for me. This skirt I’m wearing is actually two separate pieces; one she designed for me, and the skirt for her sister.” She heard Enterprise tell her that Vicky had no problem with being name dropped. “I admit that it’s a little bit of a fan-girl moment to be able to say that I’m friends with both Panacea and Glory Girl. It was Glory Girl who did the designs, to be honest. She may be a superhero, but there’s so much more to her. She’s got a real eye for fashion and color, and I mean usable fashion, not some of those outfits you see on the runways that I can’t imagine anyone ever actually wearing out on the street. She has some long sleeved tunics, full body suits, a lot of interesting stuff. I’ve got the money and I’m going to be a name out there whether or not I originally intended to, so I decided to hire her on as my fashion consultant and designer. She’s already looked at a couple ideas I sketched out for outfits and pointed out that they might look good, but they’d better be something I don’t mind taking some time putting on.” She laughed. “That’s why I’ve decided to pay her, because she made me see exactly what was necessary to put together a dress like I’d designed.”

She smiled at them. “The other thing I’m looking forward to is being able to start training people so that I can eventually - in the future - think about starting to crew the Enterprise. I’ve seen Vicky fly in the holodeck in a shuttle. That girl took to flying as if she was born in the 25th century and had been flying Federation shuttles since she was old enough to touch the controls. That girl flies a shuttle so gently that I actually had to look to see that we’d touched down. And yeah, that means she’s actually flown a real shuttle out to the Moon and back.” Taylor laughed. “I’d complain about the volume of the squeal of joy from being able to look at the Moon from that close, but I was part of that volume.” Both Matt and Meredith laughed at that.

“To more serious things,” Matt said. “From what we know of the series, and apparently what happened about a week ago, the ship has some amazing weapons. What are your plans as far as those are concerned?”

“I can understand the worry, especially since I fired a beam from space on the 15th into the heart of Brockton Bay. The reasoning behind that incident was that there was a cape battle happening, and both Lung and Hookwolf were involved. I think you’ve heard the stories about how badly areas can be damaged when either of them gets going? Imagine them fighting each other. It was a full-on gang war happening, to the point where the police and the Protectorate were by necessity fighting more of a holding action to keep it from spreading. I got permission from the local Protectorate before firing a beam from the ship, set to stun. The only one that didn’t stop was Lung, who I had to hit with a phaser rifle several times before he was unconscious. For once, no one was killed in a gang war in Brockton Bay.” She sighed. “But as for the other half of the question, lest people think I’m avoiding it, I have no intention of doing something like that again if I can avoid it. If I do, it’s going to be with the permission of the locals. I’d prefer to use them aimed outward if they’re necessary.”

She laughed. “In a perfect world, I’d have to take the crew out hunting asteroids to get practice using the weapons, but this isn’t a perfect world. I suspect that at some point soon we’ll find out how the ship’s weapons do against Endbringers. I’d love to be able to say that they’ll have a major part in any upcoming battle, but that’s a surefire way for someone to post video with a trombone sound effect - you know the failure one? Wah-wah-waaaah.” This drew laughter from both hosts. “So the best I can say is that when it happens, we’ll see how well my ship does against an Endbringer.” She paused. “I think the next one is supposed to be Ziz, as much as they seem to schedule them?” That was followed by a frown. “And whichever one it is will probably be doing their thing soon. It’s been about three months, and that seems to be the way it runs. But that’s depressing to think about, so let’s find something amusing. I’d suggest talking about a couple of my outfitting fails, but I’d need to show pictures, and unfortunately, those are accidentally not safe for television.”

Meredith raised an eyebrow in amusement. “What happened?”

“Vicky decided to show me the problem with one of the dresses I designed. I wanted something spectacular in case I’m ever invited to the kind of fancy ball where I get to meet the president or something. I didn’t want to listen to her explanations, so we built one, and I put it on. Took three steps and was glad that they only people in the room were female classmates and had seen … that … before due to things like gym classes. Vicky proceeded to explain where I’d gone wrong, and redesigned it. The one she came up with? I’m just sorry that it’s considered gauche to wear a dress more than once to parties. That thing is gorgeous and deserves to be seen.” She grinned. “If I ever meet the president at a party, I’ll wear a Starfleet version of it.”

They went to commercial again and thanked Taylor for coming and talking to them, and she was led away from the set. She waved at the audience outside once again as she left, and could just about hear the cheering, even through the thick windows.

Chapter 45: Monday, February 21st, 2011 - Rebecca

“I need an explanation for your thought process, Chief Director Costa-Brown,” said the man on the video screen. “I have no idea exactly why you classified every single patent of Miss Hebert’s a threat to national security. I’ve had my advisers take a look at them, and had my national security people - you know, the ones hired to actually do that sort of thing for a living? - look at the patents, and not a one of them can figure out why they are classified as a threat to our security.” The president leaned back in his chair and glared at her image.

“Sir, this girl is a parahuman, and by definition, anything a parahuman produces is ineligible for things such as patents. A patent can’t be deleted once it’s in the system. But when she transfers the patents to the PRT as owner, they can be released again.”

He raised an eyebrow. “So you misused the system in order to get a larger budget. Either that or to bully a teenage girl that has a ship that can probably vaporize Washington DC if you piss her off too much. Remember something about what I did before I sat in this chair before you decide to tell me about the legality of what you’re doing, by the way. Unless you can give me a really compelling reason why this ban should stay, I am very likely to do an executive order rescinding your ban on those patents.” He leaned toward the camera again. “We are taking a beating in the press because of you, Rebecca. The law regarding patents and parahumans is specifically for Tinkertech, which by definition is technology that requires a parahuman Tinker to build. The patents you banned are all things that I have been assured are things that any competent shop could build, such as the superconductor.”

“I am doing it because this girl has access to a fuck-huge spaceship, Mr President, if you’ll pardon the language,” she fired back. “Equipment like that should not be in the hands of a child! It needs to be with an organization used to dealing with insanely powerful people and devices.”

“And the fact that the only way you can permit this is if she is forced into the Wards, at which point all of her patents and inventions done on PRT time become the property of the PRT, with a pittance going to the inventor plays no part at all,” he replied in a very skeptical tone of voice. When he spoke next, it was with the voice of someone who was done taking someone’s shit. “You need to remember something, Alexandria. Your dispensation to run the PRT despite the fact that it is forbidden for a parahuman to be in a position of power within the PRT membership is at the sufferance of the President of the United States. If I feel that you are abusing your power - which it certainly appears that you are - I have the right to ‘request’ you to step down from your leadership position. Do not make me regret leaving you in the position for the time being. I am ordering you to release the national security hold on those patents within the week. If March arrives and she’s still banned from using them, you had best have a good reason and a timetable for when they are getting released. Otherwise I do the release and relieve you of your leadership position. And trust me, Rebecca, I have a lot of information about you. If you do what I suspect you will want to do, it will end up being a mutual take-down. I have taken anti-Thinker measures to protect some of what I have. Which is information that has been passed down from the first president that you convinced to allow you to hold that position.”

“Yes, sir,” she said through gritted teeth.

“Watch the attitude. Hell, watch the Today show from this morning, and see what you’ve managed to do. Hell, I’m coming out looking better to the public than you. That girl is disarming and can talk, and Michelle commented that the kid is easy on the eyes, especially if you’re male. She didn’t make the threat that she did in her Internet video, but I’ve already had a smug call from that ass Harper in Canada about allowing her patents and companies in Canada, along with citizenship if they look lucrative enough. I haven’t heard from Cameron or Gillard yet, but it’s just a matter of time. Miss Hebert’s a master of playing to the audience, apparently, because she had an engaging ‘aw shucks’ attitude when necessary, but was a powerful speaker when she wanted to be. Her comments about the name of her ship? They had to go to commercial, the emotion was so strong. And she specifically laid the blame on PRT Washington - your group when you run around as Rebecca, in fact - while still stressing to everyone that it was purely her opinion. She lauded her local PRT office for basically being an example of how to deal with new parahumans.” He snorted. “If that’s how she talks on a regular basis, I’d look at her to run the PRT over you.”

She scowled at him at that comment. “Rebecca, whether you want to admit it or not, you don’t like not having control over something. I’d lay money on that being why you’re so hellbent on getting control of this girl’s ship and patents. Because you know that you could do a better job of using the tech because you’re you.”

He leaned back in his chair. “Fix this mess you’ve created, Rebecca. Don’t make me step in and fix it for you, because it will not make your organization look good if I have to.” With that, he ended the call before she could respond to him.

She took several deep breaths and quickly slipped into her costume before grinding out, “Door to Earth Me’ah.” She stepped through to a world where there were no intelligent species. She flew at high speed to a mountain, where she spent some time spending her fury on innocent rocks. When she was done, she spun to get rid of the worst of the rubble and dust, than called “Door to Cauldron.”

When she stepped through, Doctor Mother was in the room and just raised an eyebrow at her. “Not just yet. Let me shower and I’ll talk to you afterward.” She headed off to get a shower and a new costume, and returned to the meeting room a while later.

“Didn’t go well, I take it?” Doctor Mother asked blandly. It wasn’t accusatory at all, it was purely informational in tone.

“No.” Alexandria groused. “With that girl having a ship that powerful and no Thinker able to even know she’s there - and that apparently includes the fucking Simurgh - we can’t really use our usual methods to figure out how to get her under our control. Contessa can’t even begin to figure out how to Path her or even the people around her. We know who she is, but doing any Path involving her in some way comes back with gibberish. I mean seriously: Step Thirty-seven - spice the rock purple? That doesn’t even come up as oddball Thinker code for something. Hell, if it even came up with something like ‘purple vodka’ I’d be able to figure it out, based on prior codes they’ve thrown out.” She closed her eyes. “I really wish that one Thinker didn’t come out with everything in colors. Green is good, red is bad, blue is happy, orange is problems, and so on. We’ve learned that purple for them is the equivalent of ‘this is a situation that will bend your mind’. And the vodka one just means you’ll need a drink. Or at least I will. Just wish it wasn’t so hard to get drunk these days. Never got to enjoy it.”

“Trust me, the headaches and potential vomiting from overdoing it are not all they’re cracked up to be,” was the reply. Doctor Mother even seemed to have a small smile on her face.

Alexandria actually let loose with a tiny laugh. “I made the mistake with this girl of assuming that she was just a regular teenager. Instead, she’s got a backbone you just don’t tend to see in teens. I don’t know if that’s upbringing or just her, hell, it might be that the connection to her fuck-huge minion helps her with backbone. But now I have to figure out how to back away from my stance, or else Obama is removing me from my position. As it is, he’s pissed off enough that he’s taking a look at some of the things like NEPEA-5, and when he sees what it does properly, he’s likely to gut the hell out of it as it stands.”

“So we have to look at other ways of funneling people into our organizations. NEPEA-5 was basically designed to make people have some connection with the PRT if they wanted to make money, so that we could funnel them in various directions, or prevent the really dangerous ones from doing much damage. This man has shown decent intelligence, so if he decides to gut or remove NEPEA-5, then he’s going to replace it with something rather than just remove it.”

“True. We probably do need to gear in a new direction, because the Thinkers are pretty sure he’s taking 2012 as well. 2016 is too far out for any real plans to see who could win. One precog keeps muttering about ‘orange calamity’ whenever we try to figure it out, and we have no idea, because they aren’t a color-based response Thinker.”

Doctor Mother sat back and looked at Alexandria for a long moment before saying, “Run this idea around in your head and see if it might work. You back off on your national security ban because you misunderstood something that you heard in a conversation. The conversation, of course, was between Rebecca and Alexandria. Rebecca heard a line of thought from Alexandria and misunderstood what the hero was telling her. You, of course, can’t explain exactly what it was that was said, because the conversation ranged into things that actually are national security things that Alexandria is cleared for.” She smiled slightly at Alexandria. “Which is the truth. You have different clearances as Chief Director and as Alexandria. So you backtrack, stating that since the two of you talk enough that you thought you understood what she was saying, and therefore didn’t elucidate further. This allows something of a mea culpa from the PRT and is a good faith gesture, and should hopefully get President Obama to back down a bit from his anger.”

Alexandria snorted. “He stays angry. He might thank me for backing off, but the things he said he’s going to check on? He’s checking on. The only way I could stop that is a step way too far for me, and I suspect that Biden would just pick up the ball and run with it. I know that were I in that job, I’d make my potential successor aware of any problems.”

“Might be worth it to talk to the girl herself and come up with some sort of apology. Use that thinker power of yours to convince her that you jumped the gun for the best of reasons, as ‘faulty as they may have been’,” Doctor Mother said, actually doing the air quotes, “and you may end up with an ally. And if she’s got that powerful a minion, you can start feeling her out for whether or not she might be willing to help with our mission. Bringing her in as a full member? Not likely, unless she seems to actually lean that way, and some of her comments make me think that she would not condone some of the things we see as absolutely necessary.”

Alexandria snorted. “I can just see how that would work out, if I could convince her. The conspiracy theorists would say that I Mastered her, but then again, anytime someone changes their mind about something, someone is out there screaming ‘MASTER!’, so I’m not worried about that.” She sighed. “I just hate back-tracking.”

“You don’t like being out of the loop on things. The impolite phrase for it is ‘control freak’. I understand it, since you were so out of the loop before your vial, that you never want to lose that control over things you gained. But this is a case where I think it might help you to admit that loss of control.”

A frown was the response, but it was followed with a nod. “I’ll do that once we’ve figured out the best phrasing for it. I’d obviously like to take the least amount of flak from this that I can manage.”

Chapter 46: Tuesday, February 22nd, 2011 - Taylor

Tuesday worked much the same for Taylor, with a morning stint on Good Morning America. When she beamed back to Brockton Bay, she walked into the office Bian had set up to find the woman on the phone with someone. “Ah, she just walked in the door. Mind if I put you on speaker?” A moment later, she said, “Dragon? You’re on speaker now.”

“Excellent. Miss Hebert, As was said, I’m Dragon, and I’d like to see about setting up a meeting with you. Mostly in regard to my own company, but unofficially -” Taylor could almost hear the finger quotes “- I’d like to talk to you in regard to setting things up in Canada. I have contacts that lead me to believe that the issue with patents in the United States will be solved before we reach the weekend, but there’s no certainty regarding that.”

“I’d like that. Would this be a more detailed meeting over the telephone, such as this, or would we be meeting face to face? Well, face to armor.”

“Would you be available on Thursday to meet?” Dragon asked her. “I would, of course, schedule it for after you are finished with classes for the day.”

“I will make sure that my schedule is free. I have a question for you, and I hope it’s not offensive. Do I call you Dragon, or is there another name that you would prefer?”

“Well, since I am meeting you in my cape identity,” the amused response came, “Dragon is fine.”

“True. I’ll be meeting you as myself, unless doing it in my cape identity would be easier. No difference in who I am, just how the paperwork gets handled,” Taylor said with a small laugh, which was returned.

“You should be good meeting me as yourself, not your cape self. If cape things come up, I’ll let you know.” There were a few more pleasantries, and then the call ended.

“Well, that comes across as a good thing,” Bian said. “Dragon wanting to talk to you about manufacturing and such? She’s also known to deal with the Triumvirate and Armsmaster on a regular basis, so I’m suspecting that the patent issue is going to work out in your favor before the week is out.”

“I hope so. I want to talk to her and others anyway, because spreading out manufacturing around the world can only be good. My comment on Today wasn’t wrong - if I keep it purely in the US, then the global impact of trying to fix things worldwide is lessened. But if I show willingness to speak to other nations?” She snorted. “And maybe remember that I have a universal translator, so English speaking isn’t a requirement?”

Bian laughed. “I’ve already started on your passport stuff, and from a couple things I’ve heard from my friends in Washington, it just might be getting expedited even without us having to pay an exorbitant amount extra for that. FOAF-lore tells me that a certain individual on Pennsylvania Avenue might want you happy.”

“FOAF-lore?”

“‘Friend of a friend’,” Bian replied. “Nothing provable, but sort of a ‘he told this guy who told that guy.’ Pretty sure that the guy who told me is in the loop, but by phrasing it the way he did, we’re not officially told anything.”

“Gotcha. Anything I really need to do here, or can I run up to the ship? I’ve had an idea or two come to mind, and I want to run them past everyone, especially Enterprise. Because I’m looking at going after that snake tomorrow. Need to see if I can dampen the sparkle and noise form a beam in, or simply speed it up, because I want to fill his office with drones and stun the fuck out of him in however many timelines the fucker does something with.” At Bian’s puzzled look she added, “It’s the only reason we can come up with that he’s occasionally got chronoton radiation around him. Since he doesn’t seem to be actually doing anything here, we figure he’s got the ability to run out a scenario in a minimum of one other timeline. So what I want to do is pop the drones in while he’s in one single one, so that no matter how many he splits off, he gets stunned unconscious in all of them.” She paused. “Which I suspect will collapse things back down to one line without him actively running it.”

Bian nodded. “Makes sense, and you haven’t really been wrong yet about stuff like that. Got nothing here you need to work on, and if something comes up, I can call you about it.”

“Unless that ‘something’ is Dad. I don’t need to see that,” Taylor said with a laugh. “No matter how hot you look when it’s happening.” At Bian’s raised eyebrows, Taylor said, “Scanned at one point when I was about to beam down. The two of you were in the living room, and Dad was reminding you rather … vigorously … that he’s above the national average, locally speaking.” She blushed. “Never going to have any interest in him that way, but I gotta admit that I’m a little bit of a voyeur, because that was fu … fricking hot to watch.” She waggled her eyebrows. “Pregnant yet?”

“Thinking of waiting until the end of school, to be honest. We want to do a small ceremony, but we’re trying to work out who gets you. I want you as Maid of Honor, but he’s admitted that he’d kinda like you as Best Man, so to speak.” Taylor’s hand went to her chest, and Bian became very blurry suddenly. “I’m leaning toward letting him get you as Best Man.”

“Any way I could do both?” Taylor asked, sniffling.

“We’ll talk about that,” Bian said as she hugged Taylor. “Now dry your eyes and go do what you need to on board your ship.”

A smiling Taylor appeared in the transporter room of the Enterprise and headed toward her motorcycle holodeck, Enterprise walking beside her. It had been decided that she would rebuild the Indian as it was, with the closest possible parts available - if she could get good quality period parts for it, great, otherwise she would have some made. She was even practicing working with lathes and CNC machines. She’d developed a love of working with her hands, even though reading was still her major passion. But there was just something about building something that you could look at and say “I made that!” that appealed to her.

“I heard you say that you had an idea or two?” Enterprise asked. “Is it something you want to work on by yourself, or would brainstorming help? Sherrel’s come up with something useful, but she’s a little embarrassed by it as well, since it pointed out a side effect of her Tinker power, I guess.”

“Brainstorming would help, probably. First off, I need to know about … well, I’ve had this idea about body armor of a sort, and wondering if rapid micro- or nano-building is a thing. The sort of thing where I can carry a briefcase, or even smaller, and have the outfit grow onto my body from there.”

Enterprise stopped in the hallway, leading Taylor to stop as well. “No one has ever really considered that sort of thing within the Federation before. An idea from the movies or something?”

“Well, I imagined that there’s a lot of stuff in one of those doohickeys that Voyager’s EMH used to walk around the ship. And B’elanna was a damned sight better than most engineers if she could understand the technology from five hundred years later. Her pulling that emitter apart and being able to upgrade it? Sorry, that’s like giving DaVinci a black and white television and getting him to upgrade it to color. He’ll be grateful for the chance to examine it, but understand it? Rebuild it? Make it better? Not happening. So I think that was just some TV crap to make the viewer not ask why they hadn’t given him the ability before. But that thing was kinda small, but still powerful enough to give him a solid body.” She sighed. “I know that the life support device is down to pretty much implantable now from the original Enterprise’s belt requirement. I guess I’ll have to program it into the holodeck to show you what I’m thinking of, because as closely tied together as we are, I haven’t noticed actual telepathy happening between us.”

“Well, let’s head to the nearest deck, rather than where your Indian is stored.”

“Do you want me to move that to a cargo bay or something?”

“No, the logic for having it there is impeccable - the ship can generate whatever tools you need as you need them in there. Shall I have Sherrel and the others join us to help brainstorm this idea?”

“Yeah. How go the drones, by the way?”

“I’ll generate them as necessary, but we managed to get a drone to the size of a softball that has some level of armor and force field, a weapon that can fire up to a heavy stun - which will go past any of the armor I’ve detected amongst Coil’s people - and can have a stealth field up. Our hard part is getting them into the facility unnoticed.”

“Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that, since there’s light and sound from transportation. I think we’ll have to send as many as we can at a time into various areas in the place, including quite a few into the armory to drop anyone trying to re-arm, or simply get armed. I want a few in Coil’s office, to drop him the second they appear. He might get off as many new timelines as possible, but damn me if I don’t want to be able to drop him in all of them.”

“It is possible to make the use of the transporter silent and invisible, but it actually is more power intensive and would lessen the number of drones we could send at any one time.”

“What’s the maximum, and what’s the reset time from setting up the transporter that way?”

“With normal usage, I can probably send about one hundred as long as we don’t mind people seeing them coming in. If we’re running silent? Maybe ten. It’s that power hungry. Reset time would be about thirty seconds, if only to let some of the components … well, ‘cool down’ is the best way to phrase it.”

“So we could be silent with ten drones in Coil’s office, and then spam others all around the base? Take him out, so that even if they see them, there’s almost assuredly the need to call him to verify stuff, which slows down their reaction times. I want him and his people out cold before we call in the PRT.”

“Are you intending to be a part of the assault?” Enterprise asked, an eyebrow raised.

“My preferred part of the assault is showing up after the drones have taken everyone out. They’ll want to have a human type person to talk to, since people still think all Skynet and shit about non-biological intelligences. Eagleton certainly does not help that image.”

“My preference is that you are out of the line of fire as well,” Enterprise said.

“I’ll still go with phaser rifle and such, because I don’t want to risk anything. Plus, it will look a little better if I don’t look quite so ‘ho hum, I didn’t even need a weapon’. That sort of attitude, no matter how true, is guaranteed to make people a little twitchy.” They were at the door to the holodeck, and Sherrel came bounding up the hallway, dressed as she preferred. Taylor certainly wasn’t complaining about the bouncing involved in the woman’s approach.

“Did she tell you about my latest mistake?” Sherrel asked.

“More that you did something that embarrassed you, in her words. What happened?”

“Well, since we were talking about motorcycles and the like, I asked for the stuff to build one that was street capable, but my own take on spaceworthy. Thing’s a nice ride, I gotta admit.” She then blushed furiously. “Maybe a little nicer a ride than I intended?”

“I think your power bounces off your libido,” Enterprise said as the door opened to the holodeck. “Shall I leave it open for the others?” Taylor nodded.

“Well, the seat’s a material I invented, designed to be a bit more comfortable than most motorcycle seats. Well -” Sherrel drifted off into being unable to explain, and nodded when Enterprise asked if she could finish the explanation.

“Sherrel built a seat to mold to the rider’s body. It measures you as you sit on it and makes it the most comfortable possible seat. Well, it also takes into account what you are wearing, apparently, and that females have libidos.”

Taylor paused and felt her pulse climb as she contemplated what hadn’t been said yet. “Can I assume that since she was likely dressed the way she isn’t right now, that she … how shall I phrase it … had a ‘deeply inspiring understanding of her motorcycle seat’? Emphasis on ‘deep’?”

“Yeah,” Sherrel said. “Tested the bike and the seat fucked me silly. Ended up testing the ability for the bike to stay upright no matter what, though.”

Taylor thought for a moment. “Is that integral to that specific bike? And can that tendency be shut off?”

“No to the first and yes to the second,” Sherrel said. “Why?”

“Because if that’s a module that can be installed on any motorcycle and isn’t required to be running all the time, I think I want one on my personal bike when I build it. I was only half joking about flying my bike to Mars while completely nude. If a six to twenty minute ride can give me multiple orgasms on the way?”

“I’m kinda surprised you feel that way,” Sherrel said. “Most people have a bit more conservative a view on things like that.”

“You need to take into account a few things. You’ve seen me walk around this ship completely nude before. Then take into account that my mother had a second career other than college professor.”

“Strut is more like it,” Sherrel said. “Kinda wish you were at least legal, ‘cause I’ve had some interesting thoughts about … well …” She paused and added, “So that actress in a couple of those films my folks had was your mother? She looked a lot like you do.”

“Yes, it was her, especially if they had the one with the zaftig redhead. As for your thoughts? Sherrel, I can promise you that’s a two way street, and Amy feels the same way. She’s at least legal. I gotta wait until mid-June before I can legally do anything like that with you.”

“Talking about checking Sherrel’s tonsils from between her thighs again, beautiful?” Amy asked as she entered the holodeck with Vicky, Charlie, and Deena.

“Yeah, same as always.” She looked back to Sherrel. “How comfortable is the material of the seat?”

“Extremely. I think you could probably sell it as long as the secondary function was disabled.”

“Or sell that aspect as a bonus in more adult situations.” She shook her head. “We will definitely talk about this later, Sherrel, because if this stuff is good enough, we might be able to patent it in your name, and get you a decent amount of money coming in.”

“You’d patent it in my name?”

“I didn’t invent it, did I? So of course it’s yours. As long as it can be done without some weird little Tinkertech ‘black box’.”

“Nah, it’s just a new material that Enterprise tells me can be made by anyone with the equipment. The programming is the fun part.”

“In multiple meanings,” Taylor quipped. “Anyone want to help me see about designing an armored bodysuit? I’ve had an idea that I’d like to see if it’s even possible with Federation technology. If it is, it’s yet another way to remind people that this is not their father’s Star Trek.” She went to the wall and started typing, using her connection to the ship to increase her speed to a point where the others were shaking their heads in amazement.

When she was done, she turned and said, “Run program.” What appeared was a nude version of her that was quickly covered in a wave of metal, flowing as if water across her body. When it was done, even her head was covered. It was definitely a form fitting bodysuit she had designed, because no one would ever think that she was a boy if she was wearing it. “Damn, I’ve got some nice tits, don’t I?” she murmured.

“Like I haven’t been telling you that from the first time we ended up sharing a bed?” Amy asked with a laugh. “I’d say ‘spectacular’, rather than merely ‘nice’ though. Kinda like saying that people might have heard of the Mona Lisa.”

“Is something like that doable?” a blushing Taylor asked Enterprise. “And more importantly, is it doable in a manner that will actually provide protection? Being able to do that but not have anything more than a cool looking effect that doesn’t really give any protection isn’t worth it.”

“Right now? No, I can do that for you with any protection. But I suspect that if we take out Simurgh, I’ll learn the secrets of the dimensional folding she has to be doing to be that size but also be that dense. I’ve got her completely scanned, but to get to her core programming? I need that really dense part of her structure.” After a pause, she said, “Be prepared. From what I’ve been detecting, she’ll go for her target no later than Friday the 25th.”

“So it could be tomorrow, which is likely to be the case right when I’m in the midst of fucking Coil over. Well, if that’s the case, we take him down soonest and store the bastard in a brig cell, and put all of his mercs in a couple of areas completely nude, if need be. No, it’ll be right at the heart of the meeting with Dragon.”

“You’ve got a meeting with Dragon?” Deena squeed at her. Taylor grinned and nodded at her. The 14th had been the perfect day for a miscommunication from years prior to get cleared up between her and Charlie, and now the two were officially dating. They were also unofficially dating Taylor and Amy - and possibly Vicky, although Vicky wasn’t sure either - but that was on the down-low.

“Yeah. Word is that the ban on my patents is going to be overturned, but even if it isn’t, she’s unofficially talking to me for the Canadian government. Most likely though, we’ll be talking about setting up sites for my businesses.” She shook her head. “Damn. Canada, likely the UK and Australia, plus there’s the possibility that at least the French and likely the Germans will want to have me set things up. Little twitchy about Germany until they can get Gesselschaft under control. Nazis by any other name still stink to high heaven.”

Enterprise looked to Sherrel. “Would you have an issue with using your new material as padding for a bodysuit such as this? I can make one, but right now it would be pieces to be placed on the body. But the nanotechnology version? Especially if we have a good padding material, such as Sherrel’s? That would work, once I’ve got the dimensional folding worked out.”

Deena looked at her. “Can I see what you’ve got so far? I’m only 21st century math so far, but I’m a polymath and maybe just new eyes looking at it can help.”

“She’s better than me at math,” Taylor said. “And I’m pretty good.”

“You’re PhD level,” Deena said. “So am I.”

“And I am, in the end, constrained by being a computer,” Enterprise said. “Just because I’m from centuries later doesn’t mean that you won’t figure something out.” In Taylor’s ear she said, “Speaking of being a computer, are you aware that Dragon is what this century calls an artificial intelligence? She’s using the highest level technology of this era, so she could be called silicon intelligence.”

“Okay, why tell me this?” Taylor asked subvocally.

“Because when I learned that and traced her back, I found that there is a tap, or maybe a link, that goes somewhere else. And I don’t like what I see at the ‘somewhere else’. I was able to get into the computers there, and this looks like the Dragonslayers. There’s a computer there that I need to get my hands on to save Dragon, because it’s got a kill program on it. I think the only reason they haven’t activated it is that they’re stealing her tech left and right.”

Taylor rubbed her face, which drew some attention, but she waved them off. Continuing subvocally, she said, “So I’ve got Coil, the Simurgh, and likely a terrorist group to deal with in the next few days. Can we get in contact with the Guild and see if we can do something about the Dragonslayers? They’re enough of an issue that I’d really like to just beam them into space on wide dispersal, or hit them with a beam from space.”

“I’m on the telephone with the Guild right now, and they’ve connected me through to Narwhal, to my surprise. I guess our shared name carries some weight. Shall I put her through to you?”

“Yeah. Partition me off from the rest and I can carry on the conversation with her.” A moment later and she was in a small office, with the rest of the group outside. She heard the click in her ear piece.

“Hello, Grey Ghost? This is Narwhal of the Guild. I was told that you have some information for me regarding the Dragonslayers?”

“Yes, I do. Given the way that things are around me, my ship is constantly scanning for threats. Always at a low level, but the scan is there. In checking out some Dragontech hardware, the scans noticed a low-level connection and decided to trace it, just to ensure that it wasn’t something bad. Well, when she found the other end, it certainly doesn’t look good. It leads to somewhere out in the middle of nowhere in Nova Scotia, and there is a large amount of Dragontech materials there, to the point where it should be listed as a Dragontech warehouse, even if just a small one. But the area appears to be deserted. This strikes me as either being a secret facility of Dragon’s, or the lair of people who are known to steal her technology. I tend to think the latter rather than the former, especially with how complete our scans are. Let’s just say that there’s no actual doubt as to who is there.”

“Thank you for bringing this to our attention. And thank you for not just deciding to deal with it yourself, because that would probably cause an international incident, even if done for the right reasons.”

“I understand, especially with this foofarah about my patents. Given that it’s the Dragonslayers - at least that’s my assumption,” she said in what both knew was a ‘covering your ass’ tone, “there’s a part of me that would love to just fire a precision beam at their base and make sure that they’re never a problem again, but … well, international incident doesn’t begin to describe it. Just make sure that Dragon isn’t part of this, because I think that they have a way of tracking her, and if they do, they might leave before you could get there.”

“Understood, and agreed. If they see her coming, they’ll leave, and then they have to be found again.”

“If you wish help from me in any way, just let me know, but I’ll stay out of this as much as I can, okay?” Taylor asked.

“You’re definitely different from some of the other heroes I’ve dealt with. We may give a call if we need help, but thanks both for telling us, and for agreeing to not step in without our request.”

“I want these guys to go down. If I open any route for a mistrial, it’s a bad thing.”

Narwhal laughed. “True. I need to go now so that I can start setting up the mission. Send the coordinates to this address,” she said, tossing off an email. “I’ll be … well, I guess I won’t be waiting for it. That was fast.”

“All we needed was where to send it to,” Taylor replied. “Talk to you later.” The call ended, and a moment later, so did her little office. Amy and Vicky turned with questioning looks, while Enterprise, Deena, and Charlie all talked about the mathematics of dimensional folding. Taylor heard, “Theoretically we can do it, but it’s …”

“Problems?” Amy asked, kissing Taylor quickly.

“Not really. Enterprise told me about something that needed to be brought to the Guild’s attention, so I made sure that it was. That’s all.”

Vicky snorted. “That’s all. You just called up the Guild and let them know something they needed to know. You are running around in rarefied circles, girl!”

“True,” Taylor said. “I have the premiere healer in all the world as my girlfriend, an amazing ship as lover and friend, and the rather famous Glory Girl as a friend and lover once in a while. Anything else is gravy, as they say.”

“Wait,” they suddenly heard Charlie say, “We’re trying to figure out how to do this without using any power. This sort of thing relies on being powered, or else it can’t pack and unpack itself. Is what we’re working on doable by applying enough power to it? Because we’re pretty much at the point of meshing Starfleet tech with higher mathematics.”

Taylor looked to Vicky and said softly, “If they can solve this, then I definitely want to see if this applies to modern tech as well, because the three of them will have invented something that would make Han Solo have trouble imagining the amount of money made from it.”

[link] [link] [link]

I checked the rules, by the way. She's right. To declare a patent a National Security Threat (you should hear that as having been Read Importantly *grin*), you have to be in certain positions. A guard at Logan Airport can't do it. Only the head of an affected organization can. As is shown by:


35 U.S.C. 181 Secrecy of certain inventions and withholding of patent.

Whenever publication or disclosure by the publication of an application or by the grant of a patent on an invention in which the Government has a property interest might, in the opinion of the head of the interested Government agency, be detrimental to the national security, the Commissioner of Patents upon being so notified shall order that the invention be kept secret and shall withhold the publication of an application or the grant of a patent therefor under the conditions set forth hereinafter.


That's the legalese that allows patents to be declared under national security. But pay very close attention to the phrase 'head of the interested governmental agency'. Since that's PRT, that means that ONLY Rebecca Costa-Brown can be behind the declaration of all patents as threats to national security.
