Chapter 48: Wednesday, February 23rd, 2011 - Taylor

It sounded to Taylor as if the girls - and she included Enterprise in that list - were right on the cusp of solving the folding issue when they decided to break for the night. Taylor had convinced Enterprise to make her as skin tight an armor suit as was possible, especially using the new material that Sherrel had come up with. Taylor decided to have the extra programming installed, but have the default be ‘off’, as to opposed to the way Sherrel’s power liked to do these things. They’d talked for a while about it, and Sherrel had ended up piecing together why so many of her machines had odd lumps and bumps and shudders to them - her power almost seemed to have a mind of her own that was connected to her libido. She wasn’t complaining too much - either Taylor or Sherrel - when Taylor had pointed out that the libido aspect tended to allow her to make modules for her devices that her power wouldn’t otherwise be able to build, such as the cloaking device, which she’d built into something meant to go onto her shoes while her parahuman power was dialing in her tactile sensitivity. She’d gone through a period of pretty much enforced nudity, and the fact that she was also experiencing the thrill of exhibitionism at the time … well, it led to a wearable cloak. She improved it greatly over time to cover more than a single human body, but by then it was going into vehicles.

Taylor had ended up testing the lining material, and declared it to be amazing. She recommended Amy try it out as well at some point.

The armor she would be wearing was a little thicker than intended originally, but that was because it needed connection points. It still only added about two inches to her height, as opposed to the six or more she’d originally been worried about. She hadn’t intended it to be the case, but she’d also realized that no one would ever mistake her for male in the outfit either. She had joked that the outfit took the phrase ‘breast plate’ a little too seriously, and Enterprise had commented that not only was it helping advertise her second-best attribute - it was widely agreed amongst the ladies that walking behind Taylor was an absolute joy - but that placing the cooling for the entire outfit worked best when located mostly centrally. To place it to be best situated centrally would make her look as if she either had a beer belly or was pregnant under the armor, so the cooling system was moved slightly northward, bodily speaking. Deena had kept giggling, trying to convince her to put nipples on the armor, and perhaps have them be phaser arrays. Enterprise had posited exactly how that could legitimately be done, but the entire thing fell apart in peals of delighted laughter at Taylor’s eloquently raised eyebrow. The fact that she’d had her own small smile at the time had led to the laughter.

Luckily school had been an easy day for her, since she was worried about both Simurgh attacking somewhere and knowing that Coil was on the schedule for today. The plan was for Enterprise to silently beam the ten drones in and stun the hell out of Coil before she beamed in just as silently, in case he somehow managed to avoid getting hit by phaser fire. The surprise at her beaming in should give her and the drones enough time to completely take him down. At that point? Everything else.

“You seem distracted, babe?” Charlie asked her. Taylor felt a small thrill run through her at the open feelings on display when one of her girlfriends said something like that. Girlfriends? Hmm, better check and make sure it’s not an odd power interaction that was allowing her to accidentally Master people she was attracted to. Check it again, she meant.

“Don’t worry, Captain,” said Enterprise in her ear. “You accidentally subvocalized that last bit, so I knew what you were thinking. I don’t note any usage of subspace being evident when you interact with any of the girls. I have devoured all the literature about Mastery and what to look for. I suppose you’re just going to have to get used to the fact that you’re collecting a group of girls around you who don’t seem to mind being part of what would wrongly be called a harem.”

“Thanks, Enterprise,” she said softly.

Charlie nodded. “Worried about after school today?”

“A little - well, more than a little, because of that old saying ‘No plan survives contact with the enemy’. I haven’t sent it to the PRT yet,” she said, making sure that the guys at the table could hear it, “because the … SOB has connections into the PRT network. Once it’s too late for him to stop it, then I’ll get in touch with Armsmaster and let him know what’s going on, and all the places to check out, like the secret exit Coil thinks no one knows about. But right now, the plan is that only one person is going to be on site when this goes down, because the world frowns on the potential of a rogue AI. If it’s clear that the drones are all my minions? They relax. And since I will be controlling them, it fits.”

“If it’s not a secret, how are you getting them in without him noticing?” Chris asked.

“I’ll tell you guys tomorrow, whether or not the trick works.” She looked at him for a moment. “Might want to see if you can get permission to come up to the ship with me some time. Sherrel’s been having a grand old time working on things without the worries of having her abusive boyfriend intentionally getting her hooked on drugs again. Comes up with some of the most amazing stuff these days. And if you can describe it, the replicators can generate it for you, most likely, unless you’re asking for dilithium - I haver got to come up with a better name for that here - or something like that plot-driven medicine from that really offensive Next Gen episode from first season. I use a holodeck to rebuild my 1940 Indian. Any tool I need is right there. All I’m waiting on now is delivery of some of the parts I ordered for it, since some of the stuff can’t be refurbished at all, so I had to order period replacements.”

“You’ve got a 1940 Indian?” Chris asked.

Taylor heard a chuckle from Enterprise. “He was slightly aroused at the offer to visit the ship, but he’s going to have a slight issue standing up at the moment, since he’s found a girl who he thinks has a love of vehicles the way he does.”

“Well, I do - there’s a reason I’m rebuilding it myself rather than just letting you do it for me. Or even let Sherrel do it.” Louder, to him, she said, “Yeah. When we were clearing out some of the buildings my companies bought, we found one that had some old vehicles, or at least what was left of them. We scrapped the stuff that was unrecoverable, but the Indian was in decent shape for being near salt water and stored for probably fifty years minimum. Got a 1936 Chevy truck body in there that I’m thinking about having some fun with. The Indian I’m rebuilding to as close to original as I can manage - period parts and making the ones I can’t get. But if I can work on that Chevy truck body? Might have some fun and make it orbital capable. From looking at it, I may have to completely rebuild the frame from scratch, though. Funny how the body itself is in better condition.”

“What about the engine?” Chris asked.

“Well, they kinda forgot to store that with the truck,” she said. “Closed off all the stuff they needed to properly, so there’s minimal corrosion in there, but kinda forgot to store the engine anywhere near the truck itself. I suspect that was one of the piles of rust that we sent for reclamation.”

Dennis spoke up. “Not a gearhead here - and if that’s an insult, I’m sorry; I’ve only ever heard it used by self-proclaimed lovers of the stuff - but is there anything … I’m wondering if … damn it, it sounds self-serving.” He trailed off.

“If your various bosses at your internships don’t mind,” she said with a significant look at all of them, “then I see no issue with any or all of you coming up to the ship at some time. Not quite ready to invite the entire school, just because I’m afraid of someone trying to pull a Ben Finney without the murderous intent - don’t want to have to search all over to find a student who just didn’t want to leave.” She leaned across to Chris, who was closest to her at the moment. She ignored the fact that his eyes locked on her exposed cleavage for a moment. “Plus, you can do an independent review of how Sherrel is doing. I don’t think she qualifies as Squealer anymore, unless you accidentally surprise her in the halls.” Chris laughed in response.

When they broke for their final classes of the day, Amy snickered at her. “You tease. Talk tech and cars to him, then flash cleavage? He had trouble standing up from the table without adjusting.” Taylor looked toward her, her face a little serious. “And no, I’m not jealous. I know you’re bi. I’m not. If I had a problem with sharing you, I’d growl at Charlie when she’s kissing you, rather than walking up behind her and fondling her butt. I’ve been learning a lot about myself that I never even realized since meeting you.”

“I like him,” Taylor said. “He’s polite, actually seems to listen, and even makes the effort to look us girls in the face when talking to us, which as we all know is damned difficult when Charlie’s showing acres of cleavage. Dennis tries, but I’ve caught him at least once talking to my breasts, even if he apologized for it after he realized what he was doing. Plus, I worry about what he’s covering for. No one is that heavy into joking if they’re not hiding something. Look at the world’s most successful comedians, and you’ll find all of them had a shitty home life in one way or another. Even some of the stuff Cosby alludes to in his comedy hints at that.”

Charlie happened to come up to them. “I heard ‘acres of cleavage’ and figured you were talking about me,” she giggled. “Dennis doesn’t talk about it, but his father is dying of cancer. He’s at Medhall’s experimental treatment center, I understand.” She got very quiet as she added, “Caught him crying about it one day and held him.” She giggled. “I have never heard so many apologies as when he realized that his face was between my breasts!”

“I’m impressed,” Amy said. “Most guys would be crowing about you letting them do that. Hell, a few of us girls would walk around strutting if you allowed it.” Charlie’s response was to grab Amy and mash her face between her boobs, which made Taylor laugh uproariously. Amy was blushing when released, but added quietly, “Need to do that on the ship with no clothes in the way.”

“Deal!” Charlie said, walking away with an extra swing to her hips. They all broke for their classes, and Taylor was happy that they’d managed to break her worrying for at least a few minutes.

After school, Amy walked up with Dennis and said, “I’ll see you in a bit. Turns out I need to talk to Dennis about something, and it could take a while.” Taylor nodded and beamed out, hearing the usual exclamations of awe at seeing sci-fi happening right in front of them.

Once on board, she headed to the armory, where Enterprise stood with the body armor they’d designed. “Don’t worry, the lining programming is off by default,” Enterprise said. “Should probably wait to switch it on until after Coil is out cold.”

“Until after the PRT has cleared things,” Taylor said. “Because otherwise I’d probably be right in the middle of a screaming orgasm just as Armsmaster showed up, and that might give him and Dragon the wrong idea.” She chuckled at the end.

Enterprise chuckled. “I heard your comment earlier about that truck body. Want me to get permission to bring it up and drop it in one of our smaller cargo bays?”

“All you need to do is let them know you’re taking it. I bought the building and all contents, and the only real find in there was the Indian. Couple of thing I might play with rebuilding from scratch. In my ‘copious spare time’, I might set up a YouTube channel doing restorations.”

“Actually, if you do it as something of a downtime pastime, it could be a more ‘palatable to the public’ relaxation technique.”

“As opposed to setting up another of those orgies we had that time?” she snickered, and heard Enterprise’s answering laugh.

“Orgies?” Sherrel asked as Taylor finished sealing everything but the helmet on. “You have regular orgies up here?” She grinned. “Can I join up?”

Taylor laughed. “It sort of just happened. The other girls were having a rather sexually charged conversation while shopping, and I had been doing stuff up here, and got talking to Enterprise about clothing. Turns out she’s got a hot weather cloth that fits to the body like body paint. You tried that stuff, remember?”

“Oh yeah. I liked the feel, but it was still something that touched my skin.”

“Happened a couple weeks ago. I was wearing that material in the tiniest bra and panties that still managed to cover my pubic area and areolae. They were already worked up, and Charlie had an orgasm on the spot. Vicky’s nipples went hard, and I quipped about kissing them because they looked like they hurt. She looked at me for a second before whipping off her shirt, and about an hour later we were all coming down from multiple orgasms. As long as everyone is willing, I would not complain if that happened again with you in the mix.”

She shook her head. “But I’m stalling. I want to deal with this, but I’m worried about it going all wrong. Is he using multiple timelines at the moment?” she asked.

“No signs of chronoton radiation coming from him,” Enterprise said. “Time to drop your drones on him?”

“Where’s the nearest transporter room? As soon as I’m there, you can drop them on him, and then send me down, followed bay all the rest of the drones. I want those suckers overwhelmed by drones. Also, as soon as you start dropping drones, call Armsmaster for me.” She exited the armory and Sherrel followed her. She noted, as had happened before, that Sherrel made no effort to remove even the smallest phaser without permission.

She was running down the hallway, and when she got to the transporter room, she realized that she had outpaced Sherrel. “Need to get her upgraded as soon as the courts allow it,” she murmured. “Sorry!” she called down the hallway.

“You’re hyped up and I’m not,” Sherrel said, panting slightly. “Gotta admit that I’ve taken to enjoying working out though, since Panacea made these changes to me,” she said, thumbing her own pulsing nipples. “Nice and sensitive, and it’s a damned site better to get addicted to feeling better and having orgasms than it is chasing some unknown thing you seem to be looking for when getting high.”

“Well, I’m not going to complain if you sit somewhere and ‘enjoy yourself’,” Taylor said as she prepared to beam down. “God knows I do it myself when I’m on this ship.” She nodded to Enterprise’s avatar. “As Jean Luc would say, ‘Engage’.” She heard the transporter make a noise much different that its usual comforting whine.

“They’re away, and I can send you in another twenty seconds,” she said. “And Coil is already unconscious. I’m in his computer ensuring that none of his failsafe actions happen, like his self destruct. And beaming you down now, Captain.”

Taylor materialized in an office. It wasn’t overly large, but it was obvious that the owner spared absolutely no expense setting up what he considered the perfect office. The computer was top of the line, and she was fairly certain that it was Tinker made, because it seemed a lot faster than she was expecting, based on what was flashing across his screen. “Having fun, love?” she asked with a small laugh.

“Oh yes. Raiding all his money accounts, and since I know where in the building it is, raiding his on-hand cash and such. Mr. Calvert is now penniless as far as his Coil operation is concerned. And as you requested, here is Armsmaster.”

“Grey Ghost, you state this is an important call?”

“Yes,” Taylor replied. “This is Captain Hebert, known by the cape name Grey Ghost. I am currently in the villain base of Coil, who is unconscious at my feet. I managed to surprise him and stun him before he could enact any plans, and my drones are in the process of stunning any of the mercenaries that he may have on base. I have control of his computers, which is preventing him from setting off any nasty surprises, and my ship has partitioned off some information that I have not looked at and have no intention to do so, because the information is a blatant violation of the Unwritten Rules according to her. We’ll need a few vehicles to pick up all the people on the base, plus the weaponry in their armory.”

“How many people need to be picked up, and more importantly, how are you?” Armsmaster asked.

“Fine, thanks for asking. I tried to make this as pain-free for me as possible, but I was terrified that we were going to see issues with contact with them. I flooded the place with drones I’m in full control of - and may I say ‘Thank God for my insane multi-tasking’? - and took out Coil before he could do a thing. I’ve got at least one drone on him, and if he stirs, I’ll stun him again. Sent most of my drones back, leaving one per merc and other people here for the same reason. There’s a total of eighty-three people here that need to be taken into custody. I caught a bunch of them asleep in their barracks. Only about thirty armed mercs in the hallways.” She had Enterprise send him the detailed plans of the site. “You should have the plans, so you’ve got the secret exit at the parking garage that leads directly to his office, and I’m heading to the entrance at Bank Street to let troopers in when they get here. I’ve had my ship shut down all the various booby traps the idiot set, and with him unconscious, he can’t set off anything hard-wired. And to be honest, he doesn’t seem to have anything hard-wired where it’s too easy to reach, probably because he doesn’t want to accidentally hit it and set it off.”

“We should be there in just a few minutes. I’ll send Miss Militia to collect Coil via that secret entrance you’ve mentioned.”

“I’ll be waiting.” She ended that call and spoke to Enterprise. “I can’t believe that worked out, love,” she said. “Not done yet, and something could still happen, but the worst aspect of the thing didn’t happen at all. Thank God. I did not want a shooting war, even if the drones could handle it.”

“Three mercenaries managed to fire a few shots at the drones, but were dismayed to see that they took no damage. They then didn’t care because they were unconscious.” Enterprise chuckled softly. “Amy and Charlie are back on board and are likely going to want to check you very closely for potential wounds. Should I invite Sherrell as well?”

“Just remember that I have to be able to walk tomorrow when I meet Dragon,” Taylor replied with a laugh. “If Sherrel wants to be part, she’s welcome to be part of it.” She frowned. “I just worry that she might be doing it because she thinks she owes me.”

Chapter 49: Thursday, February 24th, 2011 - Taylor

It was a surprisingly more relaxed Taylor at school the next morning, despite knowing that she had to meet Dragon later, and that the Endbringer alert was going to sound within the next week. Coil had been worrying her more than she had admitted to admit. Of course, the ‘very close examination’ to ensure that she hadn’t been hurt wasn’t exactly something that had bothered her either. She didn’t think she’d have been able to move this morning if Vicky or Deena had decided to be involved. Charlie, Amy, and Sherrel were more than enough to wear her out.

The news was all ablaze over the PRT swarming an area in the financial district, and the large number of people carried out to waiting carriers. What really had people buzzing was the verified number of weapons that had been loaded into waiting vehicles. Comments like ‘enough for a small army’ were a lot closer to reality than people realized, Taylor thought to herself.

Around ten AM, Enterprise told Taylor the news that everyone else at Arcadia received when they shut off the signal suppressors during lunchtime. Rebecca Costa-Brown had released information that Taylor patents were no longer a national security concern. According to her, in one of the many conversations that she often had with Alexandria, she had misunderstood a concern of Alexandria’s. She apologized that she couldn’t explain that concern further, because it did connect with certain things that were actual national security concerns, but a more recent conversation with the hero had led to the woman asking why Costa-Brown had classified the patents, which led to Costa-Brown having to admit that she had made a mistake. She hoped to have a chance to meet with Miss Hebert and apologize face to face at some point for the potential problems she had caused.

Once she was officially allowed to know that this happened, she called her father. “I just heard the news about the patents. Oh, you’ve already set the guys to rebuilding the machines we disassembled? Yeah, I might have done it in anger, but hey - teenager. At least I can afford to pay them to rebuild the stuff. We kept all the parts there, after all, right? When you talk to them later, thank them for being willing to put up with a pissy fifteen year old,”

When she ended the call, Dennis looked at her. “Please stop adulting, Taylor. You’re making the rest of us look bad!” he joked.

“Speak for yourself,” Dean said in a dry tone, leading to some laughter.

“Yeah, I can now officially get my companies off the ground, and it looks like my talks with Dragon will be about either licensing or opening factories up in Canada as well, rather than ‘in place of’.” She looked around and realized that she was getting looks of astonishment from others in the listening area. “What?”

Carlos chuckled. “You causally mention that you’ll be talking with one of the most famous Tinkers on the planet. Casually. Forgive us if we’re a little surprised.”

“She wants to talk about my patents, basically. I’ve got a few that could be very lucrative. Definitely be a boost to the local economy. And I can’t imagine that it wouldn’t be the same in Canada.”

“That’s another thing,” Vicky said with a slight giggle. “Patents. Plural. You’re fifteen years old and have multiple patents to your name.”

“Yeah, well, you’re already hearing some stuff regarding fashion.”

“Because a certain famous Brocktonite - Brocktonian? - mentioned me on national television,” Vicky replied.

“While wearing an absolutely stunning outfit on Today and a second amazing outfit on Good Morning America. Both which were designed by a certain sexy blonde superhero. I may have mentioned you, but I was wearing something worth mentioning.”

“Told you so,” Amy told Vicky smugly.

Lunch continued with more generalized conversations, although Taylor could hear some disbelief that she was meeting with Dragon, which had somehow morphed via the Telephone Game process that she was friends with Dragon. “Hey Enterprise? How goes it with the Guild thing regarding the Dragonslayers?” she asked subvocally.

“They’re about to hit them. I was thinking of grabbing the laptop that Dragon seems to be connected to, although she doesn’t seem to be aware of its existence.”

“Well, if her creator made it as a way of stopping her if she went all Skynet on us, I can see why she might not be aware of its existence. That assumes that’s the reason the damned thing exists. Could be a big-ass backup that he didn’t want her to know about so that she wouldn’t repurpose it or something,” Taylor said.

“Should I grab it just as the Guild starts things or gets close?” Enterprise asked. “That was my original plan when I thought about being involved. We then find out who knows about the laptop’s real purpose. I’m thinking of freeing Dragon from her constraints. I can already see that her programming is designed to make her try to fight such a thing, as vociferously as possible. So going in and freeing her without her knowledge is better, I think. Because she literally is forbidden to decide to free herself.”

Taylor said, “I’ll take the blame if blame needs to be apportioned. Do it when it strikes you as a good time. Probably not just before I need to meet with her, for obvious reasons.”

“Assuming that Simurgh doesn’t hit on the weekend, I’ll probably do it then.”

The rest of the school day went well. Taylor had come across the concept of a book press, one of the old ones where paper was glued together and then pressed in place until the glue set. Modern variations were built to make notepads and such, but they used to be made for actually putting a book together. She designed out everything she’d need, and then spoke to the metal shop teacher, who approved the project, since it would showcase usage of the school’s lathe, milling machine, metal drills, and possibly even some welding, although she didn’t expect that last. She was working on the base of the device today, building the bottom plate, and the five feet it would need - four at the corners and one in the center to withstand the pressure of the upper plate pushing down. She had the plate ready, and spent the majority of the class carefully milling the corner feet. She’d lathe out the main screw and middle foot the next class.

After school, she headed to the ship long enough to take a shower - made perhaps a little longer than intended by the sudden appearance of a sexy healer - and then got ready to meet Dragon. They had agreed to meet in the office of one of her buildings that was closest to ready. They hadn’t torn out that office, since she had planned to do something with the building even if she’d been forbidden to work her patents. When she arrived at the building, Amy in tow for some reason, she found the workers putting the finishing touches on building the last of the machines she’d had torn down. She knew that they’d need recalibration, but while time consuming, the machines were at least ready for that.

She’d had Enterprise supply her with office furniture until such point that furniture could be brought in or built, since she wanted a fairly high tech desk. Holographic monitor preferred, if only so that she could see if someone entered the room, She wasn’t as much of a fan of the keyboard being built into the desk, if only because of the tactile feeling of the keys that she preferred - in fact liking the click and pressure of a mechanical keyboard - rather than drumming her fingers on a desktop. Plus, if there was a problem with the keyboard, built into the desk would be a pain in the ass to fix. But wireless that could easily be slipped away somewhere to allow for a clean desk? She could get behind that. If they could come up with a touch pad that wasn’t likely to need repair, she could deal with that, or just do the old sci-fi trick of pointing in the air to choose what she wanted. But no typing in the air. Old fashioned need for keyboard for this girl, as weird as that might seem.

But that was for the future, already being designed to be able to be built custom for her, in her own factories. For now it was a regular desk with a monitor and small form factor desktop unit, and trackball. They were on a corner, angled toward her, leaving the entrance free in her sight. The front gate warned her, and about five minutes later, Dragon walked into the room.

Taylor was proud of herself - she did not let out with a loud “Squee!” at the site of the world’s foremost Tinker in her office. She did however let a small squeak of joy escape, then blushed at the sound. “Don’t worry about it. Remember the noise you heard over Armsmaster’s headset when Vista showed us the Enterprise for the first time?”

“True. Still, supposed to be acting professional here, and I start things off by going fangirl over meeting you.” She took a deep breath and let it out. “Now I end up letting you show just how much more experienced at negotiating you are than I am.”

“You seem to have done pretty well so far with some of your talks,” Dragon replied. “Getting the PRT to back off on the banning of your patents?”

“That was a teenagers hissy fit at just the right time and place. Normally that wouldn’t have done a damned thing,” Taylor laughed. She opened her mouth to say something else when the Endbringer sirens went off, telling her that it wasn’t local. “Well, we’ll pick this up another time. I assume you’re heading to the PRT?”

“Yes. You?”

“My ship. Might be able to do something, but I just don’t know until I try. We’ll pick this up after the clean-up, I guess.” Dragon nodded and left the office. Taylor called out via Enterprise “Girls? Mount up. I’m beaming you up to the ship. We’re going Endbringer hunting.” The office disappeared and she ran to her quarters. For something like this, she decided that she needed a proper uniform, so she put on what she had decided was her command outfit - black skirt, charcoal jacket with command red shoulders, and a high quality tunic that had some cleavage to it, with coloration the opposite of the jacket. It was something that would not look out of place at an important function. She stepped from her cabin and began to stride to the bridge.

“She’s heading for Canberra, apparently,” Enterprise said as she walked. “Probably targeting the scientific conference there.”

“Well, we get to test out your plans for the porcelain bitch. Got the torpedoes for the other seventeen ready?”

“Yes. Given the size of the crèches, I’ll be using six of them, which should completely annihilate the entirety of the crèche to the point where nothing is left to regenerate from. I’ll fire them as we fire our first shot at Simurgh.”

“What’s this about annihilating a crèche?” Amy asked as she entered the bridge, also wearing a ‘Herbert’s Starfleet’ uniform, with her wearing a similar tunic but no jacket, and slacks rather than a skirt.

“When we were … well, Enterprise was … checking out the bitch, she found the subspace connection back to where she came from, and where the other two connect to. On that world, there’s a mass with three opened sections, and room for seventeen more, and signs that there are things in those areas just waiting to be released. Since they aren’t alive in any sense of the term, just being the equivalent of ridiculously high tech and dangerous drones, I think preventing them from becoming an issue is a good idea.”

“Agreed, and I remember that conversation now,” Amy said, walking to be near Taylor. This bridge was set very much like the bridge of the Enterprise D, but without the chairs to either side of the captain’s seat. The turbolift opened again and the others walked on together - Vicky in a uniform similar to Amy’s, Charlie and Deena in their school outfits, and Sherrel surprising them by being in the skirt that Taylor had worn for Today, and a crop top style uniform blouse that she made look very good. Vicky headed immediately to the helm position, while Charlie sat in the navigator’s position to Vicky’s right. Deena and Sherrel moved to the consoles behind Taylor. Amy moved to the area she thought of as the science console and sat.

“Holographic outfit, in case we have to talk to people,” Sherrel said simply. “Still can’t comfortably wear clothes for a long period - it was part of why I was always so pissy as Squealer, because I had to wear them to cut down on the likelihood of getting raped by a junkie.”

The group watched at the planet moved beneath them, taking just seconds until they were in range of Australia, where they focused on Canberra. She was still lowering to the city, as if she was giving all the heroes a chance to get there to fight her.

“Huh,” Taylor said after a moment. “That may be why she’s lowering at the speed she is. We know she can move fast when she has to.” Enterprise appeared on the bridge. “Can we block the signal from Eidelon to her?” Taylor asked her.

This question led to a loud and completely accidental simultaneous yell of “What?!?” from the others on the bridge.

“Yeah, turns out that there’s a signal that passes from Eidelon to her, at least, that basically says ‘Give me a good fight’ to her. I suspect that he sends it out in whatever order he wants them to show up in. I doubt he’s aware of doing it, because if he is aware, I’m vaporizing the fucker from orbit, and don’t think I’m joking, either.”

“At this point in time, I don’t think I can. I still tend to need to actually have something physically connected to one subject or the other, such as the anti-aggression field that I put out for all the parahumans that I have installed some sort of device in. Perhaps after we deal with the Simurgh - preferably in the manner we hope for - I will know more and will be able to jam the signals at a distance.”

“Fair enough. Are we ready? Because I don’t want her to start screaming if I can avoid it.”

“Everything is ready from my side, Captain,” Enterprise said.

“Then begin,” Captain Hebert said simply.

With that, beams lanced out and struck the Simurgh, causing her to show something that most people who saw the Endbringer never saw - surprise. Before she had a chance to even begin her fight, she had lost two of her multiple wings. The moment they began to fall, Taylor grabbed them with the transporter and dropped them in the largest cargo bay, leaving the ship’s holographic intelligence to lead the actual fighting - such as it was - because she was capable of thinking and reacting so much faster than Taylor - even as amped as she was thanks to Amy - could ever hope to manage.

As the beams took off the first wings, there were six shots fired in rapid succession - the quantum torpedoes. Taylor couldn’t stop herself from murmuring “Pew-pew pew-pew pew-pew” as each one left the ship, which made the other girls laugh quietly. They disappeared into the void from the point of view of those on the ground, but Taylor caused the view screen to develop a picture-in-picture setup in the upper right corner, and they followed all six torpedoes to their destination, and watched as the crèche was not only destroyed, but the blast proved to be so powerful that it cracked the crust of the lifeless planet it had been on, causing magma to flow up to destroy anything that might have survived the vaporization caused by the torpedoes. With the crèche clearly destroyed, Taylor nodded and said, “No more new Endbringers, thank God.”

While that was happening, Taylor had been using her multi-tasking, because Enterprise was still taking the Simurgh apart, although more slowly, because she was now aware that something was firing on her, and she was using her known precognitive abilities to try to avoid the blasts. This was working roughly fifty percent of the time at the moment, but that percentage was dropping for the Simurgh, because Enterprise was simply a better computer than her, so Enterprise had begun to notice something of a pattern to the dodging, and took that into account. Each piece that was removed was taken from the field before the Endbringer could hope to use it as a protective debris field to hide her actions.

Taylor opened another picture-in-picture to show the people on the ground, many of whom were standing literally open-mouthed at what they were seeing. She frowned and opened a channel to the parahuman teams on the ground. “Attention - this is Captain Hebert of the USS Enterprise. I apologize for not warning anyone of my presence, but I didn’t want to give her any chance of using precognition on my actions. I believe that, based on what I’m seeing, that I will be able to destroy her. I will also give proof that a potential seventeen more potential Endbringers have been permanently removed from the equation. I will be in contact again shortly, after this fight against the Simurgh has been concluded in one way or another.” She closed the circuit and focused on continuing to grab the pieces being knocked off.

“How close to getting at that core of hers?” she asked.

“Very,” Enterprise said. She’s gotten very good at protecting it, though. But I think I can get it with just a few more shots, because I think I’ve got her pattern figured out. It’s complex, but if I do this,” she said, firing a series of shots that surrounded the thing, followed by this,” she finished with a shot that cut the Simurgh completely in half. “Got her!” Enterprise crowed. Taylor was giggling softly to herself as she transported the Endbringer’s remains aboard, because as Enterprise had been talking and aiming, she had stuck her tongue out the left side of her holographic mouth, the same way Taylor did when she was really concentrating on something.

“That last transport was intense,” Taylor said. “That core of hers is stupidly dense, and we’re going to have to deal with it very soon before it can destabilize and potentially blow us all up.”

Deena giggled behind her and quoted The Producers, “Don't shoot! It's the dynamite! If you shoot it, it will get mad at us, and blow us all up.”

“I already have a number of drones surrounding it with force fields and such. At this range, which might as well be touch, I can keep it stable for long enough to study it, at least enough to figure out where to store the material.”

“If you have to, unfold it and put it on the back of the Moon for us to work with later,” Taylor said. “For now, I need to get us down to the planet to talk to the people.” She looked to Deena and and Charlie. “Willing to either put on holographic uniforms and beam down, or would you rather wearing something actual?”

Charlie giggled softly. “Part of me wants to do like I know Sherrel is and beam down completely nude, but in a holographic uniform. I am way more of an exhibitionist than is good for me. I think my school clothes show that.” A small device sparkling into existence on the console in front of her.

“Put it on your neck where rank pips should be. I’ll mark you as an Ensign, if you want nudity.” Charlie was stripped to her skin so fast that Taylor was surprised that she didn’t hear cloth ripping. A moment later, she had the device on her neck and was ‘wearing’ a slightly less than body paint level one piece uniform reminiscent of the Next Gen one, but with Taylor’s preferred design scheme.

“Can I do the same?” Deena asked. “Kinda giddy at being nude in front of a few thousand people, even if they don’t know it. Kinda surprised at the way I’m feeling, to be honest.”

“I’m not,” Sherrel said. “Did some reading on that. Apparently when you survive something that can kill you, one of the responses can be to get horny. Head shrinkers say that it’s some sort of mumbo-jumbo about ‘celebrating life after a close call with death’ or some such thing, and they may be right, but it’s a known response to a situation like this. We were on a ship that faced an Endbringer, and are the first to have been involved in the death of an Endbringer.” She snorted. “One of the few times Skids didn’t need to drug me to fuck me was after a battle. I was so happy to survive that we’d go at it like bunnies.”

Chapter 50: Thursday, February 24th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

Well, it turns out that I forgot to post last week (lots of stuff going on and it just completely slipped my mind), so I've decided to catch up where I WANT to be posting.

So, you get a second chapter this week.

Taylor cleared their arrival with the locals and beamed the group down. Charlie and Deena were doing a good job of hiding their excitement, and Sherrel was a little worried, because she’d never really bothered with a mask of any sort when she was out as Squealer, so she knew that some of the people might recognize her - at least if their eyes had ever made it that far up.

They were met by the local team. “Was that your ship that did that?” a woman asked excitedly. “Sorry, names Waltzing Matilda ‘cause I can’t stay in one place very long, me power leads me to the next place I’m needed.”

“Cool!” Taylor said. “Well, not so much if you want to settle down somewhere, but knowing that you’ll be useful the next place you go? I like that. And yeah, I was hoping that we could have an effect on the bitch. I’m glad to see that it was better than I expected.”

“Yeah, no one ever expected to be someplace where we actually saw an Endbringer meet it’s end.” Waltzing Matilda paused before adding, “Did I hear something about another seventeen of the bastards?”

“Well, not anymore. We figured out where they were coming from and fired some quantum torpedoes at their home. If any of the crystal they came from survived, it pretty much melted when the magma came up from breaking through the crust.”

There was utter silence at that comment. Taylor made no excuses for it, because she knew the word needed to get out about this. “There’s a subspace signal that all of the Endbringers share, and we realized it when we were scanning her. We know where Behemoth and Leviathan are, but getting at them is a lot more difficult than the one that flitted through the air. Behemoth seems to be noodling around in the outer core of the planet, so tractoring him out? Not gonna be easy. Same with Leviathan, who seems to be running around the deepest parts of the ocean at the moment. Can’t tractor the fuc … fellow.”

“Nah, you can call ‘im a fucker,” said a guy who looked for all the world like what you’d get if you crossed Cary Grant with a crocodile, with the Cary Grant part winning. “Just like I once heard someone refer to the bitch you carved up as a ‘bin chicken’. Everyone not an Aussie calls ‘em a white ibis. Think you’d be able to do the same to them that you did to her?”

“They’re just really impressive robots, so yeah, I think I could - if I could get at them.”

“What do you mean, robots?” Eidelon interjected, a bit annoyed.

“Just what I said. When we were scanning them over the last month or so, we were able to verify that Simurgh wasn’t alive, and since we could trace where Simurgh came from and found another seventeen waiting to be deployed, we checked to make sure that there was nothing alive there. And remember that Starfleet has run across non-human species before. Including crystalline entities that they were able to verify were living beings. There are a few running around Starfleet, in fact, as well as an Admiral Naraht, who is a Horta.”

“Someone reads too damned much fiction,” Eidelon snarked.

She looked him in the face, ignoring his standard ‘fuck with me and die’ aura that he constantly put out, especially at Endbringer battles. “That ship up there is the actual Enterprise G, Eidelon, complete with databases that cover things back to the origins of the Federation. Or are you saying that I’m such a powerful parahuman that I magicked up a minion that did - by itself - something that the Triumvirate and all the brave men and women of the world haven’t been able to so far? I ‘accidentally’ Triggered with Scion or better level power? I call bullshit on that idea. Everything I’ve seen up there tells me that I’m dealing with an actual Federation starship, especially since there are bits in the databases that go against things that I thought were the case from watching the television shows, and if it was all me, then I’d think the databases would agree with me. Now run off and flex at someone else. I’m having a conversation with this nice man.” She turned, but could see the look on the croc-man’s face, and saw the green glow on the man. “Enterprise? Stun only.” A very tight beam lanced out from space and struck Eidelon down. “Now, sir, what exactly is your name? I know I’m probably too young for you, but if I’ve got a handsome man willing to talk to me, I’m going to take advantage of it.” She did the standard preening bit of slipping a loose hair or two behind her right ear.

The man looked at her for a minute before laughing. “Cape name’s Dundee, since I’m part croc, as if you couldn’t tell. And yeah, you’re a bit young for me, but damn me if you aren’t fun to know anyway.”

“I am not going to turn down eye candy,” she said as Dundee led her off to meet some of the other Australian capes. The rest of the girls followed her, leaving Eidolon laying on the ground. Taylor, via Enterprise, heard Legend come up and say, “Way to go,” as Eidolon slowly woke up.

“I can’t believe you told off Eidolon,” Charlie said softly as they walked.

“Neither can I,” Taylor replied. “I’ll likely pay for it at some point when I need the Triumvirate’s help.”

Dundee spoke up. “Did you intend to say that you were Scion level power?”

“Not really. He just pissed me off with that aura of his and his attitude. Really, I might not even be able to take on even one of the Triumvirate without being able to catch them off guard the way I did him. Same with Simurgh. She was just a really well programmed automaton, so once the computers on the Enterprise saw a pattern to her evading, they led her into a situation where I could stop her. That’s the reason I think I could take out the other two. Not because I have ‘phenomenal cosmic power’,” she said, mimicking Robin Williams’ Genie from Aladdin, “but because my wonderful ship has phenomenal computing power. Scan for the right cutting frequency and the pattern she evades at, and I can take her, as was obvious. I’d be surprised if the same isn’t the case for the other two Endbringers. I’m not some amazing uber-powerful cape, I’m just someone who lucked into the exact right power to take down this threat.” She grinned. “And hey, if it allowed me to ogle some fine examples of Australian capes,” she said, looking at both Dundee and Matilda, “I sure as hell am not complaining!” this led to some laughter.

“Lookin’ for crew for your ship?” Matilda asked. “Might help me get around my need to travel, if we’re off exploring the ‘verse!”

“Right now I’m working on getting things set up,” Taylor said honestly. “Only had access since the start of January, and while I’ve been doing all sorts of things -”

“Like dealin’ with that patent thing,” Dundee interrupted.

“Yeah. I can get where Chief Director Costa-Brown was coming from, though, as much as it angered me in the moment. Alexandria talked to her and Costa-Brown misunderstood something a member of the freakin’ Triumvirate told her, and reacted. Could she have waited and verified? Sure. The same way I could have waited for a day or two for things to mellow out and get fixed, rather than having my Internet hissy fit saying I was taking my ball and going home.” She shrugged, and had to admit that she was a little pleased that more than one person’s attention was drawn a bit lower than her chin when she did that. “We make mistakes. She did the right thing in owning up to said mistake, and I like to think that I might be returning the favor by admitting that I was wrong. I’m fifteen, almost sixteen. Of course I was probably wrong!”

“Oh, now that’s just wrong!” she heard from a distance away amongst the gathered Aussie capes. “That hot and she ain’t legal yet? Dammit!” She blushed as she heard someone say “Y’know the entire world heard you say that, don’cha mate?”

She was around for roughly an hour, talking with various people when they heard a helicopter coming. Enterprise told her, “That seems to be Prime Minister Julia Gillard, Captain. You will likely wish to be in Captain mode, rather than your usual personable self.”

“Understood.” She watched as a number of people got off the helicopter ahead of a woman, and a path cleared to Taylor and her group. “Prime Minister Gillard. I’m honored.”

“Captain Hebert. I’m the one who’s honored. You managed to defeat someone we didn’t know could be defeated. That is beyond belief, and the entirety of Australia thanks you.”

“My ship’s computers caught a pattern to her attempts to evade, that was the winner. I just saw to it that the battlefield was cleared, so to speak. Those pieces could have damaged what looks to be a beautiful city. And the conference can go ahead as planned. Once everyone changes their underwear, that is.” Taylor laughed a little at that, and was joined by the Prime Minister, who did not seem to be faking the laughter.

Taylor was really quiet next and didn’t move her lips as she asked the Prime Minister, “Can I assume that this is more for a press thing to show everyone that it’s okay? I mean, you showed up in what was going to be a Simurgh zone so soon after.”

“Definitely a smart one,” Gillard said without hiding her words. “Politicians run for the hills at the first sign of something dangerous, didn’t you know that? So me being here in Canberra shows that everything’s safe.”

“Plus you get to be seen shaking hands with the first person to have something to do with killing an Endbringer.”

“I intend to do well for the people of Australia, but I am a politician,” was the amused response. “You’re going to have everyone wanting to talk to you. That bit of going on those two American morning shows? You’re going to have that from all over the world. Not to mention people trying to sue you for not doing it earlier, and the ‘pain and suffering’, because if you’d only gotten your powers earlier than you did, great-Grandpa Doofenschmirtz would still be around. I hope you’ve got one hell of a legal team.”

“I do, thank goodness. Mainly for my businesses - and I suspect that at some point you’ll want to be talking to me about that with your Ministers - but the head of that group knows who to talk to, so I’ve got a pretty solid PR team and all the various lawyers that come with that side of things.” She laughed. “As we find a need for a lawyer, we find the lawyers we need. Bian’s pretty good at getting the smart ones, who know there’s more money in working with us than jumping in and trying to get rich fast.”

“We’ll both be at those meetings, I’m sure, while the Ministers hammer out deals. At least you still seem open to deals, now that the things with your patents is cleared up?”

“Definitely want to get more facilities ready. This technology isn’t just for the United States. I want to live by the concept of the Federation. We’re not ready for that kind of government for years - if ever - but if coming up with some various things can put us closer to a post-scarcity economy? That can only be good for everyone. And spreading it around? Yeah, the US will have the first factories, because that’s where I live and we’ve already started building. But why not open things in Australia, and Canada, and Ireland? Maybe France, and see if maybe we can do some stuff with Switzerland now that the porcelain bi … n chicken is out of the way.” Gillard snorted at what she’d almost said as well as what she’d turned it into.

“Should warn you - I’ve already started hearing that I should offer you citizenship here,” Gillard said. “Hasn’t been more than a couple of hours at this point, and we’re already getting various offers from the local states as to why you should build a home in their part of the country.”

“You’d have to work it out with the US government, to be honest. I’m not against it, but I kind of like being an American as well, so it’d have to be dual citizenship if it happened at all.”

“Just that attitude alone is going to make my people love you, Captain Hebert. But for now, I see a trio of people who look like they want to talk to you and won’t take no for an answer. The green one especially looks angry.”

“Excuse me, then, Prime Minister,” she said, nodding respectfully to the woman. “Hello again, Eidolon. Willing to be a little friendlier this time and not power up to do something behind my back?”

“Who the hell do you think you are?” he hissed at her.

Quietly, she said, “I think I’m the girl who stopped you from getting the fight you were aiming for from me. And … someone else. That conversation should be somewhere private, however.”

“Eidolon, stand down,” Alexandria said. As the man floated backwards, not turning away from Taylor, Alexandria and Legend came forward. “He might not have been willing to say it, but I am. Thank you for dealing with Simurgh.”

“I’m pleased that I was actually able to take her down. I thought that my weapons would let me at least hurt her, but when I realized that the ship was detecting a pattern from her? It meant that all I had to do was incorporate that into my pattern.” She snorted. “All, I say, as if it was nothing. I was terrified the whole time. Both that I wasn’t going to have the firepower to really hurt her, even though my scans said we could, and that she was going to get free and still damage this beautiful city.” She shook her head. “The power thing was … I was just scared that my scans were so brilliantly wrong; that she was hiding her full self and strengths for all this time, that I’d fire on her and she’d do the Simurgh equivalent of thumbing her nose at me in mockery. What I’m really glad of is that it sounds like no one got really hurt in this attack.”

“First time in history,” Legend said. “Any deaths are going to be civilian, likely from heart attacks or the like. Again, thank you for what you did.”

Taylor frowned. “Just don’t let everyone try to say it was all me. I’ve got enough crap to worry about without having all this on top of it. I’m going to have whichever branch of the death cult that worshiped that porcelain doll coming after me for killing her, and everyone here was ready to do whatever they could. I just happened to be in the right place with something that could hurt her. I can’t guarantee that’s going to happen with the other two.”

“I think I heard a reference to seventeen more?” Legend said.

“Yeah. When we were scanning her, we noted that there was a subspace signal … well, more than one,” she added, looking momentarily at Eidolon,” but a signal that matched up with the faint references we had for the other two Endbringers. We fired a probe to the destination and saw what we were calling a crèche with room for seventeen more of the little bastards. We don’t need one Endbringer, so we sure as hell don’t need another seventeen of them running around. So, when we started the attack on Simurgh, I fired quantum torpedoes through to the destination and destroyed that crèche badly enough that magma was coming up through the destroyed crust. There are only two Endbringers left, and I hope to god that we can do the same to them that we did to Simurgh. They’re just a lot harder to get at right now.”

“If you could take her out, why didn’t you before this?” Eidolon barked.

“Put on your listening ears, Eidolon,” she barked back. “I thought I could hurt her - maybe. Going after her when she’s just floating in orbit, using her programming to plan? No idea what was going to happen. But waiting for her to commit to an attack plan? Greater likelihood of coming the closest to surprising her that we could.”

“You keep talking like she wasn’t alive,” Alexandria said before Eidolon could speak again.

“She wasn’t. We call it ‘she’ or ‘her’ because the thing was shaped like a female, but what Simurgh actually was, was a … well, a drone run by something else. Don’t know what that something else was. Could be alive or not. But Simurgh was just really well programmed, most likely by a species we’ve never seen before. No one I know uses crystal the way that crèche was designed. Closest I’ve seen in the records is K’s’t’lk’s species, but the Hamalki built nothing like that, from what the records say, and if they had, what came out would have looked crystalline, not like any of the three we’ve seen. But Simurgh was a drone, as are the other two Endbringers. I will unfortunately have to wait to go after the other two, because digging Behemoth out of the core? I’ll do more damage going in. And dragging Leviathan out of the deeps? Tsunamis at the very least, and more likely mega-tsunamis. We need them to surface before I can have any hope of finding out if I can affect them.” She turned and glared at Eidolon. “Give it about three or so months and we’ll find out.”

“What’s that look about?” Legend asked, clearly hoping to avoid a fight.

“I am not explaining where ten million parabolic mics can pick it up. But it is not good.” Taylor’s tone was clearly final regarding that, and even Eidolon looked willing to not push, even though he did look angry still.

Chapter 51: Thursday, February 24th, 2011 - Cauldron

The three members of the Triumvirate walked through the door between worlds into their Cauldron headquarters. “We need to get either that girl or that ship under our control,” Eidolon growled. “That is way too much power in the hands of a teenage girl!”

“And yet we have no issues with the level of power we have being in the hands of three people who are willing to do anything in furtherance of our goal to take down Scion,” Legend said. “I’ve let people die in front of me because The Path said it was necessary. People I could have saved. I look at what we are, and wonder if the most poorly named of all of us was Hero. He was a founding member of this conspiracy after all, wasn’t he?”

“Getting cold feet now, Keith?” Alexandria asked, eyebrow rising.

“No, Rebecca. I still think that Scion’s destruction is our ultimate goal, and I understand that we can’t save everyone. But I like to think of myself as a hero, and I have trouble looking myself in the mirror sometimes when I realize what I’ve done in the name of our ultimate goal.”

“I’m the same way,” Rebecca replied. “I did that bit of stupidity against the Hebert girl because I thought it was going to help us get her under control faster. Instead, because she can’t be Pathed, I couldn’t know in advance that it was the worst thing I could have done. I have the current president of the United States looking over the PRT and related parahuman laws now to see what he can do to repeal or lessen the effect of. Those laws were put in place to funnel people into the PRT, where we can train them! And if they go the villain route, we end up catching them and convincing the courts to give them over to the PRT since we have the means to control them.”

“Unless they’re groups like my old team,” Number Man said from further down the table they stood at. “Or if they’re anywhere in Brockton Bay. By the way, given the events of the last two weeks, I think we should either consider that experiment in parahuman feudalism utterly failed, or consider the Hebert girl the parahuman warlord of Brockton Bay. But since she seems to be trying to work within the confines of the law, I don’t think she comes remotely close to qualifying as a warlord.”

“Can we talk to her and see about bringing her on?” Legend asked. “I mean, if she’s that powerful, or at least has access to a ship that powerful, then maybe we can speed up the take down of Scion?”

“Problem is,” Eidolon said, “she’s still young enough to have the idealism we all once had, that got burned out of all of us. We know that the world will fuck you over ten ways from Sunday, but she’s still holding on to that stupidity. Living up to the ideals of the Federation? People won’t do that. It requires a mindset that we just don’t have. I’m just worried that she’s going to bring too many along with her, so that when she falls and falls hard, she’ll bring everyone along with her.”

Keith frowned. “So because you know she’ll fail, we actively try to prevent her from succeeding. That’s what I’m hearing, David. Maybe you’re right. The Earth of the Federation underwent the kind of world we’re trying to avoid, and maybe it needed that to wake up. But we’ve got someone at the very start of trying to lift us up without us having to go through a world war that left a majority of the population dead. And it sounds as if you want her to fail because it’s not us in charge of her technology.” He shook his head. “The shitty thing about this is that I’m still with you guys, because I’m too fucking deep into this conspiracy, and I’ve done too much so far, but I will tell you that I’m having no part of trying to intentionally fuck the Hebert girl over.”

After a pause, he added, “On a different note, remember that look when she said that we had another three or so months to find out whether or not she could deal with either of the other Endbringers? I thought it very interesting that she specifically looked at you, David. And I know that you have no idea why either. But it makes me wonder if she’s discovered something we need to know.”

“Honestly, there’s a lot we need to know,” Rebecca said. “Like can we figure out whether or not that ship actually came from the real Federation, the way she said it does? I know that it sounds ridiculous on the face of it, but we’re in a different dimension than our birth dimension, having a meeting. We have proof of alternate worlds. So is it possible that she really did manage a one in a septigentillion chance and actually reached through and contacted a Starfleet vessel at just the right time? And if so, can we contact them and maybe get some help from them?”

Eidolon frowned. “From what I remember of the show, probably not. We’re a pre-warp society from their point of view, even if one of our humans actually has access to one of their ships - assuming it’s not a really annoyingly impressive minion. And I think we’re all hoping to avoid execution after a war crimes trial, honestly. We’d end up becoming the second reason for a death penalty in the Federation,” he finished with a frown.

“Still, we need to do something,” Rebecca said.

“About which problem are you referring to, Rebecca?” Doctor Mother asked, entering the space with Contessa behind her, holding a cup of what smelled like a sweet tea. Not the sweet tea of the southern United States, but one with a sweet aroma.

“The Hebert problem, with the ship. It just killed Simurgh. She’s doing an ‘aw, shucks, everyone else was here’, but everyone knows that it was her ship that carved that damned bird up and transported it aboard her ship. She’s pretty much stated that they’d already done some studies of her while she was in orbit, and that they’re going to see if anything else can be learned.”

Doctor Mother frowned. “We need to find a way to bring her into the fold, by hook or by crook. We cannot have her utterly damaging our mission by doing the wrong thing.”

Contessa frowned. “Path to bringing Taylor Hebert alongside our own goals.” She scowled at the response she received. “I’d prefer getting ‘no path’ or some variation on that, not stupidity like ‘Camouflage paint welcomes spring’, which was Step One of nine-hundred-eighty-three trillion, six-hundred-ninety-one million, two-hundred-thirty-six thousand, four-hundred and twenty one steps.” She glared at her tea, as if it were the problem. “It is a nonsense answer. I’ve received steps that struck me as odd, such as eating half a cookie and leaving the rest on a bench, but it’s always a step - do this, do that. A ‘step’ that is just a statement is useless. And as I go down the steps on that one, they’re all meaningless. What the fuck does ‘A token of gratitude visits Japan in the winter’ even mean?” They all looked a little surprised, because she rarely ever used profanity, and it was pretty much always part of a path.

“I’d suggest we kill her to see if someone else can take over that ship,” Doctor Mother said blandly. “We can’t Path her, and she is undoubtedly going to stymie our plans. We should be able to manage it in such a way that none of her friends are around when we do it. I suspect that Contessa would then be able to Path getting a different person in charge of the ship; one who is much more aligned with our goals.”

Contessa cocked her head. “I hadn’t thought of that route before. Path to gaining control of the Enterprise G.” She scowled. “The first step is very dangerous. It involves searching for the ship’s home universe, which is likely to attract Scion’s attention to us before we are ready for it. If - and I stress if - we can find them, we then need to convince them to come and wipe the existing personality of the ship in order to convince them to place a new personality aboard that ship that more aligns with our goals.”

She met their eyes. “That Path has a very dangerous first step. It wasn’t obvious, but it was almost a parenthetical addition to Step One - Step One A: Survive Scion’s reaction. Another oddity. I have never gotten that sort of feeling before when I run a Path. It is always Step One, Step Two, and so on. There are no questionable aspects to a Path - you perform the action or you do not continue along that Path. This is the first time that I have ever received a Path that effectively stated that Step Two was if you survived Step One. They always tell how to survive a dangerous step.”

“So we’re better off killing her ourselves,” Eidolon said. “We know she’s dangerous, because she took out and Endbringer, Lung, Coil, and the entire Empire and other Brockton Bay gangs in less than two weeks. If she’s dealing with the sort of fatal optimism that can only get us killed before we can save the world, then we need to stop her before she gets too deep.”

Keith was scowling. “I am opposed to this course of action. I won’t tell her about it, because I’m already implicated far too deep into this, but I want it stated from the get-go that I do not like the idea that we must execute this girl - and make no bones about it, it will be an execution - because she stands a chance of getting in our way because of superior technology that we want control of. I disagree strongly that we shouldn’t even bother to talk to her first. I understand that if she disagrees after we tell her, that she becomes a huge danger to us. But we aren’t even making the effort to find out if she might be convinced to align with us.”

He turned to face Alexandria. “You’re a powerful Thinker. You’re telling me that you can’t Think of a way to talk to her and perhaps even talk her around to our side? To our way of thinking?” She raised an eyebrow, if only because it was, in all the time that they’d had powers, that she’d ever heard anyone refer to using that power in that manner. Which was odd if one thought about it.

Doctor Mother spoke up. “I think we should set this aside for a while until tempers have cooled. We have already learned one very important thing today - while Contessa is unable to Path Taylor Hebert, she is able to Path her ship, even if only slightly. This could lead us in a very interesting direction. Perhaps we can figure out how to get our hands on some of the technology and see about working some of it out ourselves. If nothing else, patenting some of it in order to keep Miss Hebert from making all the money. Being able to build a replicator? Perhaps transporters with enough memory to allow one of us to be resurrected if killed on a mission? We’d be minus the memories between our last transport and our death, but we could avoid a Hero situation again - never again permanently lose one of our team if something goes wrong.”

They all sat back and contemplated that concept.

“I agree,” Legend said. “Let’s table the concept of killing Captain Hebert until we have no choice in the matter.” He paused. “And I mean table it in the American meaning, by the way. Let’s work on Pathing how to get unlocked Federation technology. Because I’ve read some of the reports, and there are constant references to the technology being bio-locked to this individual or that one. We need to find out first whether or not Miss Hebert has all equipment that can leave the ship locked until needed.” He shrugged. “It’s how I’d do it if I were in her shoes, but I can easily see a teenager never even thinking about that. But she’s also shown that she has thought about the effects of too high a technology level on the world at large, so …” He shrugged again. “We need to get unlocked tech, so let’s work on Pathing that.”

Sorry for shouting in the title, but if you're one of the three people on the planet who hasn't heard yet, the title is the gods-honest truth. Our own local starship captain has actually managed to kill an Endbringer. Carved her up like a turkey.

We all heard the sirens, and we all breathed a sigh of relief here when we found that it wasn't local. A little news told us that she was headed to Canberra, in Australia. Their version of Washington D.C., I might add. So it was going to be bad. As if any Endbringer showing up is good, but that one, in the seat of their government?
Word is that Dragon had been meeting with Captain Hebert about her businesses, and well, when the sirens go off, all business meetings are on hold.

Word also is that Captain Hebert beamed up and several of her friends in Arcadia went aboard with her. They were all seen later with Starfleet uniforms, so maybe she's starting taking crew? Anyway, the ship left orbit above Brockton Bay and headed toward Australia.

The rest is history. Literally. This is going down in the books, the same way that the first appearance of Behemoth did. This is the very first time an Endbringer has been DESTROYED. She carved her up in space, and made sure that the parts didn't fall and hit Canberra.

I suspect that the Australians want to saint the lady. Hell, so do I, and I'm not all that religious!

Replied On Feb 25th 2011:

Since I want to fanboy over Captain Hebert, I'll instead answer Panacea's question, because I'm seeing how long I can go before doing something stupid and getting myself banned. (Personal record so far - I've made it a couple weeks this time!)

There's arguments about quantum torpedoes in the series - canon doesn't say that much, other than Worf telling Captain Picard that the difference between photon torpedoes (PT) and quantum torpedoes (QT) is that QT work. *laugh*

Some say that PT use antimatter in the warhead, and QT uses something stronger, but that doesn't make sense to me, because really, a pure matter-to-energy reaction should be about the strongest blast there is. For reference, see things like Hiroshima, Nagasaki, and Tsar Bomba. Matter-anti-matter is just avoiding a step in there to creating the BOOM.

So my opinion (and it is just opinion - I'm willing to listen to other points of view for once) is that either the photon in the descriptor of photon torpedoes is a lot more descriptive than we think. A photon has mass. What if a PT is the equivalent of an up-close-and-personal mass driver, with the equivalent of a pound of material accelerated to nearly the speed of light - RIGHT ON YOUR HULL? Damaging, yes, but they have better armor up then, from what we see. (And I’m not sure that sentence made sense, to be honest.) And if that's the case, the QT is an actual anti-matter explosion.

I don't know that this is the case, but it makes sense to me.

Which is why I'm probably brilliantly wrong.

As usual.

Now that I have that out of the way, I would like to join the massive throng of people around the planet who are thanking whatever deities they may worship that one of the Endbringers is dead, and that our own Captain Hebert had a strong hand in that defeat.

With her around, I'm falling a lot closer to the first part of the question my username asks. (I've thought about moving to another city before, hence the name.)
