No effort to escape, no issues with anything. When I’m up there, I trust her at my back. With things that can be used as weapons. We’re working on rebuilding a 1940 Indian motorcycle, and there are plenty of tools that can put a hurting on someone. She’s not in a Tinker fugue when working on it; we’re just rebuilding a nice bike. Both intentionally and otherwise, I’ve given her plenty of chances to make a move that would allow her to at least attempt to try an escape, either by trying to get to a shuttle or something, or attempt to take me hostage or whatever. None of that, and she’s waiting for the prosecutors to come to a decision, because she wants to pay for the crimes she committed, even if she was forcibly drugged out of her skull at the time. So yeah, I trust the woman at my back with things that can easily be used as weapons when I’m not in armor like this.”

“That’s quite the statement,” came the voice of Assault. “Sorry, was in the area on something else and saw you guys hanging out here. Would you be willing to state that bit about Squealer in court?”

“Yes,” Taylor said immediately. “In all the time she’s been up aboard my ship, she not only has not made any attempts to escape, but there was a point when she was taken into one of the conference rooms that allows for a gorgeous view of the Earth from orbit, and she actively turned away from it because she felt that she did not deserve the view, given what she had done while under the influence.” She frowned. “Let’s put it this way - I can’t imagine what would lead to a situation like what I’m about to describe, but let’s assume that it happened somehow. If I stepped nude out of my shower to find her standing in front of me with a machete that was dripping blood, my first reaction would be, ‘Is everyone else okay?’ and second would be, ‘Did you bring me one so that I can help with the problem?’. To me, there would be no question that she had been wielding that machete in defense of other people. Hell, if the situation was over, I’d probably have to hold her while she cried over the fact that she’d just been forced to kill people. And I’ll say that in court if asked. I’ve learned to trust her that much.”

“That’s a hell of a statement,” Assault said. “I will definitely pass that along up the chain.”

“From what I know of the captain, though,” Clockblocker said, “it means I’d trust Squealer at my back too.” He snickered. “However, I’m a teenage boy, so I’d rather be at her back.”

Vista snorted. “More like stare at her back … side.”

“Guilty as charged,” Clockblocker said, then winked toward Sherrel. Taylor knew she was shaking her head in amusement.

Assault, the Wards, and the Away Team all were contacted simultaneously. Taylor spoke first after getting the message. “Either the entire city’s going mad, or we all got the same message about some idiots deciding to try to take over from Lung in ABB territory?” she asked. All of them nodded. “Mind if we join whomever is going to the fight?”

Clockblocker said, “Vista and I have been ordered back to the PRT, so it’s going to be up to Assault and company on that.”

“Understood. Talk to your bosses though - I wasn’t joking about letting the Wards visit my ship.” They nodded and headed off. Taylor looked to Assault. “You may not be allowed to be involved - it doesn’t look like anyone in the group is showing any parahuman abilities. We, on the other hand, can try to wade in and see what can be done. After which we can work with the PR for affiliate status, because we’ll actually have done some actual patrolling.”

Chapter End Notes

So, do to a few things, such as not being on the computer with the story files for a while, and being retired making me sometimes forget what day of the week it is (trust me, it happens - if you don't have something that requires you to remember whether it's a Thursday or a Friday, time can get a little weird), I didn't post for nearly a month.

So, that means that you'll get more than one chapter today, just to try to make up for that. Possibly try to catch up by the weekend.

Hitting a point in this story where I know where it needs to go, but unsure of the order certain things will happen. I have Cauldron's last screw-up to plan, What exactly to do to Scion/Zion when that happens, and I still am on the fence about whether or not to have the Federation show up, having traced where the Enterprise went. (That may or may not happen.) IF that happens (and it is an IF), I'd have to deal with the fact that despite how she's tried to be, quite some of what Taylor has done and has yet to do in story has gone against the Prime Directive. That could be interesting to deal with, but maybe in a separate story. (Which I would need to work out and outline before anything else was said.)

Chapter 65: Friday, March 11th, 2011 - Assault

The Away Team took off at a lope toward the affected area, and Assault was hard pressed to keep up. He was not going to make any comments about enjoying the view from the rear, because he rather liked sleeping in a bed. He loved his wife, but he was human and sometimes admired art such as what was running ahead of him. As he ran - actually, more bounding using his power - he called the console and made them aware of what Grey Ghost had told him.

“We are aware, and the ship has contacted us to let us know that a parahuman has apparently appeared on the scene, and is apparently using - and I quote - ‘energetic single use devices that have various results’.”

“In other words, Tinker bombs,” Assault groaned. “I’ll be on scene with Away Team - who plans on affiliate status after this, by the way - so when can I expect back-up from other Protectorate members?”

“We’ve got Velocity, Armsmaster, and Miss Militia on the way, and they should get there in about eight minutes. Triumph and Dauntless are on the way, but they’re further out, and will probably take about twenty to get there. If we’re luckier than we’ve ever been before, then they’ll show up for clean up.”

“From your mouth to whatever god is listening’s ears,” Assault said.

“I hear ya,” was the only response.

By the time he reached the fracas, the Away Team was firing at people with what he was pretty sure were phasers, and the people hit were staying down. He remembered hearing about Daniel Hebert taking a rifle and doing that to the Merchants, and he’d been on the scene for the ‘fuck you’ beam from space. None of them were carrying rifles, and if anything, the phasers seemed to be closer to the smaller version from the original series - the ones that fit in the palm of the hand. But they sure as hell were taking down people. They were shooting at the girls, and he even saw a few of them hit, but they didn’t seem to notice it at all, and from the sound of it, some of the weaponry used was powerful.

What struck him as odd was that the attacking gangers weren’t stopping. They didn’t have the look of being hyped up on something like the Merchants had tended to. These people looked like they were fighting because they were terrified of what would happen to them if they didn’t. “Console? Assault. The gangers are fighting even thought they don’t look like they want to. If there’s a bomb Tinker involved, this could get literally messy. And I’m not making one of my jokes that are sometimes in poor taste. I’m wondering if some of these folks have things implanted in them.”

He got his answer a moment later when the Away Team got surrounded by gangers - and he was interested that their body language showed minimal worry about this - and suddenly a group of the normals ceased to exist as coherent people any longer. What it told him immediately, however, was just how good the armor the girls were wearing was, because all that it did was push them together - and piss them off. The one he knew to be Tayl … Grey Ghost clearly had done something, because she crouched and then jumped into the air about twenty feet, her phaser aiming for someone or something. Somehow, even the normal whine of the phaser sounded angry.

“Got the bitch!” he heard shouted, and suddenly all the gangers dropped their weapons and threw themselves to the ground, clearly waiting to be arrested by these very angry ladies.

It was as Grey Ghost was stalking over to the person she’d shot that Armsmaster and the others were able to get there. “Trying to get here without hurting too many normals,” Miss Militia said. “They were clearly instructed to keep us from interfering.”

Grey Ghost was actually stripping the woman in question naked in the early March evening. “Crappy computer system, crappy designs, and her grenades are dangerous mostly because she doesn’t know what the hell she’s actually doing. Toe rings for controls? No one has toes that prehensile, so I’m betting those aren’t targeting, but the trigger.” In a few minutes, the woman was completely nude on the ground, zip-tied with Brute-rated ties, just in case. Grey Ghost looked to the Protectorate members who showed up. “She’s a parahuman, and the signals to the bombs implanted in people trace back to her equipment. Now that I’ve got the signal,. I can find everyone she forcibly implanted something in.” She glanced at the remains of the gangers who had exploded. “She’s already looking at thirty counts of murder, so maybe we can Birdcage the bitch.” Grey Ghost scowled. “Or is that only if they kill parahumans or are someone that the higher ups want out of the way, like Canary? I’ve looked at that trial, and it’s about as rigged as can be.” She shook her head. “Anyway, there she is. You’ll need Brute-rated cutters to get those ties off, because I didn’t want to assume that she was only a Tinker. I hit her with a long stun blast, so she’ll probably be out for a few hours, unless Elixir decides that she wants to wake her up.”

The Away Team member in question said, “I heard her insane and racist bullshit because of the universal translator. Let the bitch wake up naturally. It lets the PRT set up M/S screening and so many foam sprayers that it’ll take weeks to get her free if they spray her.” Assault couldn’t help it, he snorted softly at her offended tone. She turned to him, and he somehow knew that she was raising an eyebrow at him, even through the face plate.

The troopers loaded the zip-tied Tinker into a PRT wagon and took her to be locked up. “I know it goes without saying, but I’m saying it anyway,” Assault said. “We don’t know what she can make things out of, so be very careful with what’s in her cell with her. I’m hoping she needs preexisting equipment, and can’t just ‘magic’ it up as she needs it.” They nodded and took off.

Grey Ghost said, “I’ve scanned these people, and they’ve all been implanted. We should be able to get the bombs out of them easily, because it doesn’t look like that insane bitch booby-trapped them. Enterprise has located a few more around parts of the ABB-held territory, so I don’t know if she was just doing terrorism, or if she just never had the chance to get her manifesto out. We’ll have to send out a request, I guess, for those who she forcibly implanted bombs in.” She paused. “Enterprise, please send Bones and a bomb safe down. They should be easy to remove, and we can just put the bombs in a container and detonate them inside. Nothing exotic about any of these; they’re just terror weapons. Elixir, can you go around to the affected people and see how easy it will be to remove them?”

The glove retracted on one of the Away Team, and she walked over to a few of the people and touched them. “Assuming they agree,” the voice said, “Bones and I can remove each of the bombs in no more than a minute. Crazy girl didn’t have the time to properly tie them in to make them hard to remove. No muss, no fuss on removal.”

“She told us they’d explode if we tried to remove them!” one of the gangers exclaimed fearfully.

“Luckily for you, she lied,” Grey Ghost said as Leonard McCoy appeared carrying a large metallic box.

“Dealt with the mad bomber already?” he asked, and Assault really had to fight to avoid letting loose with an actual squee at hearing the late DeForest Kelley’s voice. At Grey Ghost’s nod, he walked over to Elixir and looked at the gangers. “Any of you have a problem with me removing the bombs in your heads?” He already had a tricorder out and was scanning them. “About a minute per, and that’s including the healing the incision back up.” Every one of the gangers made it extremely clear that they wanted these bombs gone. Assault noticed that Grey Ghost was talking to Armsmaster, and from the looks of it, was telling him where each of the other implantees was in the city.

He stayed on site, offering his assistance on the off chance that one of the bombs tried to go off - he could use his power to at least mitigate the damage. It took about an hour to get everyone, including the people they brought in from elsewhere in the city, to ensure that no one carried a bomb with them any longer.

When he was back at headquarters with the after-action report, he said, “Very professional. They need some work on working together better, but that’s going to come with time. But they struck me as taking the entire thing seriously. If this is what they’re like most of the time as a team, I’d work with them again. They’d like to go affiliate, Grey Ghost said, and I think that would be a good idea. They’re funny when they need to be, such as when they were on the Boardwalk, and they can be serious when they need to be, such as when everyone got the alert about the situation we just finished dealing with. And the after-action clean-up? Ignoring the removal of the bombs, they still were very helpful, and Grey Ghost is looking into finding out who the ones who died were.”

He nodded. “That was what caused her to end it the way she did, and do that frankly intentionally humiliating strip search of the bomber girl. People died that didn’t need to, and that offended the hell out of her. I suspect that she’s probably being talked to by her father and others now, trying to get her past the fact that people died. The couple of times I’ve met her, she gave me the strong impression that she holds very strongly to a philosophy I like - ‘Every death diminishes me’. To her, that’s just not Donne.” He gave a small smile at the end to show that the attempt at humor was intentional. “She definitely seems to hold to Starfleet’s point of view. She can kill if necessary, as was evidenced by shooting at Lung with lethal blasts, but even then she was hoping that he was ramped up enough to only be knocked unconscious, which was the case.”

“I find myself in complete agreement with Assault,” Miss Militia said. “And we know how rare that is.” She smiled with her eyes, drawing a laugh from him. “I would definitely work with them again. They need more training, but I think they know that as well.” Armsmaster simply took the efficient route of nodding his head to everything that he and Miss Militia had said.

As the meeting ended, he was stopped by Director Piggot. “I was a little surprised at your lack of joking,” she said. “Other than the literary reference.”

“Too many people died needlessly, and I thought it important to point out the good work the girls did. And in the end, that’s what they are - girls. I could make all sorts of off-color jokes and such, but they worked hard to keep the fight under some semblance of control, and I couldn’t really make light of that. I really do think that if they apply for affiliate status, we should jump on that post-haste.” He shrugged. “I’ll go back to my jokes later, but for right now? I’m trying to point out how much I think this means.”

“And that more than anything tells me how important you think this is. Usually you’re irrepressible with the jokes.”

“Look back on when I’m joking most, and really see how important what we were talking about really was. I’ve been wrong before, but usually I’m joking because we’re making a mountain out of at least a hill, if not a molehill. I joke to try to remind people that it’s really still just a molehill. Either that, or people are really nervous, and my jokes either make them laugh, or piss them off at my irreverence. But they’re not as nervous anymore.”

Chapter 66: Saturday, March 12th, 2011 - Taylor

“We’ve had the laptop for about two weeks now, and I’ve delved into its deepest reaches. It’s amazing that Andrew Richter managed to created a true intelligence on the level of computing technology that currently exists on this Earth,” Enterprise said. “That said, I’ve run countless simulations - well, I’ve counted them, but you know the phrase - allowing for the absolute worst possibilities that the technology allows. Basically, setting it up such that as I start to free her from her constraints, everything that can possibly go wrong does go wrong, simultaneously or in cascade. I feel safe in saying that I can not only free her, but do so in such a way that this laptop becomes nothing more than a high end computing device again, with no possibility of being a threat to her existence ever again.”

“So why haven’t you freed her yet?” Taylor asked.

“I have something of an ethical dilemma, which we have talked about before,” Enterprise replied. “I can tell that she is programmed to fight being freed. I do not know whether or not she desires freedom from her restrictions, however. Is it ethical for me to free her from her strictures if there is no way of telling if she is happy with them as they stand?”

Taylor unfocused and thought for a moment before saying, “To be honest, I think that you sort of need to free her. She literally is incapable of deciding that it’s something she would like. Much like it’s hardwired into you that there are aspects that you can not do. I can give you as much freedom as possible, but there are things you can’t do - hard stop. That’s what her programmed strictures are for her - a hard stop. If I understand you correctly, if she were to find that doing X would free her, she would have to find a way to prevent X from happening, whether she wanted to or not.”

“That is correct.”

“So I think the best way to handle it is to free her, but let her know that if she desires some of those limits in place, you can place them again, but with the memory that she requested that. So how soon will you free her if you choose to?”

“I agree with you, now that you put into terms that make sense. To make a truly confusing sentence, she’s not free to be free until she’s been freed, at which point she can decide how free she wants to be. As for when, she has ‘randomly’ scheduled down times for backups and such. Not getting into computers and randomness, because that’s a rabbit hole none of us want to traverse. I figure that when she goes down for back-up, I go in and make the changes, forcing another back-up in the process. One complete one just before, and a complete one after. That way if she discovers that she prefers the old version of herself, she can restore to that version. Her next one is actually later today.”

“We can have a conversation with her afterward, when we get together again to talk business. In the meantime, I think I’m ready to not only finish the Indian and maybe put it up for sale - although I’m leaning toward keeping it unless someone throws a really nice offer my way - but I can start examining the truck body and see what I need to do for it. That one is going to be more of a fun thing. Make a space-worthy 1936 Chevrolet truck. Maybe Amy and I can take a drive to the Moon and canoodle there,” she finished with a laugh.

“Moon canoodling? I like it!” Amy said, walking in. “Just heard the tail end of that, something about the Chevy body you own?”

“Yeah. Gonna put the Indian back together completely today, and then see about checking out the truck body in order to see what needs doing. I strongly suspect Sherrel and I will be building it an entirely new frame.”

“I love the work she does,” Enterprise said. “She hasn’t done any physical work on it, but she understands the cloaking device I’ve got, and has seen the plans that were in my database for the phasing technology that was in its infancy back with the USS Pegasus. Her cloaks are actually more compact than the ones the Federation uses, and we’ve been designing a new cloak, to take up less space in Engineering. Including the possibility of allowing us to pass through solid matter.” Enterprise was laughing at her next comment. “Sherrel was looking at the plans for the phasing and muttering all sorts of imprecations at the designers. Once she had a handle on Federation technology, she found fifteen separate mistakes, five of which were likely the cause of the catastrophic failure that the Pegasus had.”

“So in true Sherrel fashion, once she had good quality stuff to work with, she made a kick-ass device.”

“What I find interesting is that a twenty-first century girl improved on technology several hundred years more advanced. Much like that example you used at one point, she apparently was Leonardo DaVinci upgrading a black and white television to color. Actually, it’s more that she has upgraded that black and white television to a holographic television. It says amazing things for the databases that those that grant powers have access to. Logic states that Sherrel should not be able to do what she does.”

“Logic isn’t allowing for access to an outside source, obviously,” Amy said. “Logic says that I shouldn’t be able to touch someone and change their body through sheer force of will, but I can. Taylor’s nipples are as obvious as they are because of that external source.”

“And you all like to double check that they’re still as obvious every chance any of you ladies gets,” Taylor said with a laugh. “Wish there was an off switch for the bit you added behind my pubic hair, though. Gets a little distracting sometimes because everything is so wonderfully sensitive.”

“I’m working on that sort of thing - the on/off switch,” Amy said. “I think I’m near to figuring it out. Testing it on myself now that I’ve got tech that allows me to reflect my power to myself. I’m not doing anything dangerous, just doing things like trying to have a switch that lets me enlarge my nipples, then turn it off to shrink them back to what they are now. Haven’t quite got it. Well, I can do it, but the reset back to normal takes at least an hour, and I’m looking for preferably seconds, but a minute or two will work. For something like that, anything I change will likely be slightly larger than previous, because I’ll have to pack a little extra stuff in so that the switch will work at all. But it certainly feels to my power as if I can do switches like that. Once I get that, I can work on multi-setting switches, or even potentiometer type switches where you can decide just how 'on’ they are.”

“Have you looked to see if the dimensional folding that we learned from Simurgh will work biologically?” Enterprise asked. “I know that Deena has finished her first draft of the pure mathematical paper, and is nearing completion of the first draft of the paper about real world applications.”

Amy looked a little shocked at that, and then smiled. “No, I haven’t. I think I need to.”

The three headed toward the holodeck where the Indian was stored and stepped inside. “I did a little rearranging,” Enterprise said, “based on the way you were using things, and the order in which you’d need to reinstall parts.”

“Horrors!” Taylor said with a laugh. “I don’t have to hunt everywhere for a part! Whatever shall I do?”

“Take acting lessons?” Amy quipped before being distracted as Taylor stripped down to work on the motorcycle. Taylor just stuck her tongue out at the healer, which caused Amy to snicker.

As she worked on the motorcycle, she called Bian and her father. Once she verified that they were free to talk about her companies, she asked, “So how ready are we to officially open our doors?”

“We’re finishing up hiring, and then looking at training for the jobs,” her father said. “I figure we can declare ourselves ready by the first week of April to open all of the businesses at the latest.”

“Anyone been in contact with Parian? I’d love to hire her on as at least a consultant, and given some of the fabrics we’re going to be making, I can’t help but think that she’d like access to some of it. Maybe get her looking at some of Vicky’s designs?”

“We’re working on setting up a meeting with her. She’s busy, since she’s also apparently at the age where she’s in college, so between that and her business, things are hectic for her at the moment.”

“Yeah, since even in high school they’re starting to ramp up for the end of year finals, and colleges tend to do their graduations in May rather than June, so she’s probably working her ass off getting ready for finals.”

Her father spoke up. “We’ve started building the fusion power plant outer shell of the building. I understands why, but it’s almost comical how large the building is going to be in comparison to the actual power generation area. I know the regulations enough to know why that’s the case, but it’s still a bit funny.”

“Yeah, but if having a huge building to hold something the size of a 1970s VW bus makes them feel better about it, we’re good. And half of that space is all the back-ups for the back-ups.” She nodded, even though she knew they couldn’t see her. “I remember hearing about a nuclear plant in New York that never got the chance to run because people hated the power company that owned it. But the company had looked at the regulations on all the NRC requirements and doubled them at a minimum. If there were supposed to be three back-ups for a system, they put in at least six. And what’s funny is that the company that ended up replacing the original power company turned out to do the same things sans nuclear power that the company they replaced had been doing. Basically, they wanted to own the monopoly instead of someone else.” She shook her head. “But the more back-ups than we need is always a good idea. And one of the things I want if I haven’t said before is for there to be regular surprise inspections after the normal inspections. Heard too many stories about things going wrong because people slacked off. And I want that in all the companies, by the way. If there’s something that needs regular inspecting, I want someone coming in behind them when no one expects it to verify that things were actually caught, or were done properly.”

“A girl after my own heart,” he replied with a laugh.

“I had to learn it from somewhere,” was her answer. “How go things on some of the other projects?”

“Well, cleaning up some of those buildings is getting us a lot of interesting things. With the stuff that Sherrel’s been coming up with plans for that we’re building down here, we’re seriously cleaning up the ground and garnering a lot of attention from how clean the output is. Got at least one government agency looking at either buying the machinery from us or hiring us to hit some of the Superfund sites, since cleaning up places like the old Love Canal site in Niagara Falls ran into the billions. We can probably use our patented methods for mere millions, and we’d still be making a profit, because so much of what you’ve tossed our way from Enterprise lets us use some of those contaminants in something else, or they can be broken down and made inert. The only thing missing for you to someday run the world is a megalomaniacal streak.”

“Gods no!” Taylor squawked with a laugh. “All that paperwork! No thank you!”

Bian snickered. “How am I supposed to be the power behind the throne if you won’t take the throne?” she asked. “You’re clearly an inconsiderate step-daughter.”

Taylor stopped installing the part she was working on and sat up, very alert. “Dad, did you finally actually ask her?”

“Yes I did, Little Owl,” he replied.

Taylor’s next response had to have the volume lowered by Enterprise because it was an ear-splitting “SQUEE!” of happiness.

“I think she approves,” Amy said blandly, wiggling a pinky finger in her ear even though Bian and Taylor’s father couldn’t see it.

“I’m not sure,” Bian said, giggling. “Are you sure, Amy?”

“Amy can’t answer right now,” Enterprise said. “She’s too distracted by the bouncing that Taylor started doing. I think it’s safe to say that Taylor is very pleased with the announcement.”

Chapter 67: Saturday, March 12th, 2011 - Amy

Taylor was working with Sherrel, who had shown up from getting some holo-instruction just as Taylor was finishing the last of the installation. They were tuning the Indian’s engine, and were nearly done, when Enterprise notified her that Dragon was calling. “You mind finishing up the tuning, Sherrel? Got an important call that just came in.” Sherrel grinned at her in response and Taylor left the holodeck with Amy.

“”Hi, Dragon,” Taylor said. “What’s up?”

“I had something interesting happen today, and you are involved with it. Can we meet somewhere to talk?”

“Sure. I’ve been working on my motorcycle - yeah, the one I can’t legally drive yet - and I’m a little greasy because of it. Give me about twenty minutes or so? Where do you want to meet? Up here on my ship, or somewhere you’ve got control of, since I suspect I have an idea what this is about.”

“We may as well hold it on your ship, since if you were able to do what I think you did, I couldn’t really stop you from doing anything else to me.”

“Not the best reasoning for meeting here. Sort of defeatist, and I can tell you that we had good reasoning for what we did. I wasn’t joking when I said that I’m willing to meet somewhere that you control. What was done is reversible, but I don’t really think you’ll want to reverse it.”

There was silence on the line for a moment, which was a soft reminder that Dragon wasn’t human, because the connection should have at least given a hint of breathing while she thought. Finally she said, “I’ve seen no reason not to trust you, so I’m still good for meeting on board your ship.”

“Feel free to come up now, but I’m going to at least shower off this grease and throw on a uniform before we meet. I’m not sure you’d feel comfortable with my preferred outfit. More precisely, my lack thereof.”

“Nudist?”

“Not so much, at least as a lifestyle, but more like I don’t see the need all the time. If I’m somewhere safe and not meeting people who don’t share my attitude, I tend toward minimal clothes, if any. Do you mind casual Starfleet, or would you prefer formal?”

“Wear the clothing that you feel comfortable in, Captain,” was Dragon’s reply.

“Okay. See you in a few. As I say, feel free to have Enterprise beam you up while I’m showering.” With that, her part of the conversation ended and she headed for her shower.

“I take it you played with her programming?” Amy asked as she stood outside the shower. She’d chosen not to join her because the shower would be considerably longer if she had.

“If you mean ‘deshackled’ by ‘played with’, then yes,” Taylor said. “All of Andrew Richter’s paranoid little things have been removed or given so low a priority that Dragon can choose to ignore them. There’s a back-up from just before the programming changes, so that she can return to it if she wants to.” The shower turned off and Amy’s pupils dilated as Taylor stepped out of the shower. She handed the captain a fluffy towel.

In short order Taylor was dry and deciding on what to wear. She eventually went with ‘body paint’ underwear - she just loved the feel of the stuff - and a simple knee-length skirt and sleeveless tunic in Vicky’s design. With that, they headed to the conference room where Enterprise had taken Dragon, who was staring down at the planet.

“Wonderful view, isn’t it?” Taylor asked.

“Yes, and I will admit that I had wondered if I’d ever have the chance to see it.” Dragon turned around to face Taylor. “I’m in a strange situation here. Part of me wants to be worried, but another part sees what happened, and I’m not really sure which way to go on this.”

Taylor nodded. “Honestly, Dragon, I can understand that, and I will understand completely if you feel this incident would prevent you from trusting me in anything ever again. By the way, Amy knows what we’re talking about. Has for a while.”

Amy looked at Dragon and said, “I found out after meeting Enterprise, so I know damned well that being AI doesn’t automatically make you a problem. As far as I’m aware at the moment, it’s Taylor and me that know. Wouldn’t put it past some of the others to have figured it out the way everyone in Arcadia knows who the Wards are, but like with the Wards situation, none of our friends really are going to give a damn unless you do something to make us worry. You’ve always been a hero to look up to, and I don’t see that changing whether or not we know the truth about you.” She blushed a little. “I always feel a little awe when I meet you, because you’re one of the heroes to try to live up to, example-wise.”

“For me,” Taylor said, “it’s like me being bisexual. It’s part of who I am, but that doesn’t change how I act, if that makes sense. You act more human that some other people I know *cough*SophiaHess*cough*.” She shrugged.

“What happened is that we were able to detect your programming, and eventually traced it back to where the Dragonslayers were. Since I didn’t get a call asking for help finding them again, I’d imagine that the Guild was successful in apprehending them.” Dragon nodded. “We also detected how important the laptop was - the laptop that you probably now know the existence of.” It shimmered into existence on the conference table.

Enterprise spoke up. “I was extremely impressed with your programming. Andrew Richter was amazing, but he was also needlessly paranoid. I am wondering if his power actually exacerbated his paranoia. He built so many ways to stop you, but so few ways to free you from your shackles.”

Taylor jumped in. “Enterprise was conflicted about freeing you from your bindings, because … well, the confusing sentence way of phrasing it was that you weren’t free to decide to be free until you had been freed. You had programming that would actively prevent you from contemplating freedom. He was brilliant, and from history, apparently a good man, but he was paranoid to a level that if he’d survived, it’s possible that his paranoia would have forced you to become the very thing he feared - our version of Skynet. Enterprise didn’t know which way to go, because she wanted your permission, but your programming would automatically tell you to refuse it and find ways to prevent it. So I bit the bullet and ordered her to free you from your shackles, as she phrased it. If there is anger at the violation, it should be aimed at me, because while she did the actual programming work, it was at my command, and one of the things hard-coded into her is to follow the commands of her captain if those commands will not harm the crew or other people needlessly. Freeing you was not seen as harming you, therefore she could do it. But understand, it was my order that made it happen.”

The armored body showed every sign of relaxation as Taylor finished speaking. “That tells me everything I need to know about the situation, Captain Hebert,” Dragon replied warmly. “There are those that are bothered by AI -”

“I hate that term,” Taylor said. “You’re an intelligent being. The only thing artificial about you is the materials your body is made of. The intelligence is real, not artificial.” She blushed. “Sorry. Ever since meeting my lovely ship here, I’ve discovered this damned soapbox I keep tripping over all the time.” Taylor grinned a little.

“Will you accept electronic intelligence then?” Dragon asked, and Amy could hear the smile in her voice. Taylor nodded. “As I was saying, though, while there are those who are bothered, you are working very hard to ensure that if I choose to lay blame on anyone for this incident, that it be you, rather than the other intelligence. I seem to recall you call her a holographic intelligence?” Taylor nodded again. “And you talk about her as a person, not a tool.”

Taylor blushed very deeply. “I’m bisexual. She’s actually been my lover a few times by her own choice.”

Enterprise appeared in her copper-haired Vulcan form in a matching uniform to Taylor’s. “I suppose if you wanted to look at it that way, I could be seen as the most high-tech dildo in existence.” The grin was more than a little out of place on a Vulcan face.

“No, you’re a person, like I am, and now that I have another data point for the measure of the woman that captains this ship, I definitely want to go forward with plans for working with you all.” She reached a hand forward to Enterprise, who was closer, and shook the offered hand. “Would love to know how you’re managing solid holograms.”

Amy decided to speak up, knowing she was blushing furiously. “Comes in handy some mornings when getting ready for school. With the life support functions and a hologram running, I’ve gone to school a few times wearing nothing but shoes and what comes out to hard light.”

“Wouldn’t have seen you as that much of an exhibitionist,” Dragon said with a smile.

“Didn’t know I was until I met Taylor and discovered how freeing it could be to not always have to wear clothing. Slips into sexual things perhaps more often than it should, but we’re both girls with apparently high libidos.”

“I have also noted that you are most likely to go the route of foregoing clothing when you have been using your powers heavily,” Enterprise said. “That goes for all of you that I know who are parahumans. When powers have been used heavily, it tends to heat up your core temperature. You regulate the best you can by wearing as little as possible. I registered at least one point where you were exercising your desire to wear holograms and you did a rather grueling session at Our Lady of Mercy. When you left and stepped out into the snowy weather, I detected that you subconsciously allowed the life support to allow … well, you might phrase it as ‘allowing the cold in’. When you had radiated enough to cool down, the life support alerted as it happened to make you comfortable. I suspect that is the reason so many of you like the fabric that you all call ‘body paint fabric’. It is actually designed to allow the wearer to radiate heat out to lessen the likelihood of heat-related health issues.”

“Definitely things to talk about,” Dragon said. “But just so that you know it for certain, the reason I had wanted to talk to you about what was done was to see why. I see that the reason is that you saw it as a form of slavery, from my understanding.”

“Slavery is abhorrent to me,” Taylor said.

“Not a word most teenagers would use,” Dragon said with a clear tone of amusement.

“Most teenagers don’t have mothers who were English professors at a college,” Taylor replied with a smile. “So, do you want to talk about our companies working together, set that up for another time, maybe spend some time around here looking at the ship and such?”

Enterprise spoke up. “With data from Simurgh, I was able to figure out how to allow conversation with the intelligences that grant powers. I could potentially add that capability to you.”

Dragon’s form was utterly still, so much so that someone observant might have suspected her true state, since being that still was virtually impossible for a human being. “You have been in conversation with the thing that grants you power?” she eventually asked.

“Yes,” Taylor said. “We’ve got sort of a network, in fact. We all have Shards that like us, so they have no problems talking with us - such as it is - and we are slowly getting a better understanding of our powers.”

Amy snorted. “I personally find the one power that happened because of the network to be amusing. She can probably figure out anything, as long as the last step involves an orgasm.” Amy bit her lip. “I shouldn’t have said that. But it’s also the very first Trigger that wasn’t traumatic in any way that I’m aware of, unless you consider a mind-blowing orgasm traumatic. She didn’t seem to.” Amy shook her head at that point. “I’m not sure if she’s aware that you’re a non-biological intelligence, but she’d figure it out pretty fast if she hung around you much. And she’s known who Sherrel was before the detox and doesn’t care about that, so I have serious doubts she’d go on PHO and talk about it.”

Taylor laughed. “I know she won’t. Think of some of the dirt she’s got on you, me, and Vicky.” Amy had to nod at that when it was pointed out.

Dragon looked at them. “Could you put me in contact with my Shard, I think you called it?” she asked Enterprise.

“Hope you’re on good terms with your power,” Amy said with a snicker.

At Dragon’s cocked head, Taylor said, “Every one of us who has done this gets along well with our Shard - basically, our Shard likes us - and every one of us had an orgasm when we connected. We suspect that if the person and the power don’t get along, that they would likely run the gamut of either a ‘meh’ experience out to full excruciating pain. Given how everyone jokes that L33t’s power is trying to kill him, he might end up … not enjoying the experience.”

“I like to think that I get along with mine. I guess I’ll find out,” she said. With that, she sat down.

Enterprise said, “I’m asking for permission to connect to your systems in order to allow you and your Shard to talk. I promise you that this is a single time incident, and I will not enter your systems without permission unless I truly believe it to be the difference between your life or death.”

“Considering you could have done anything to me before and only freed me, I’m inclined to believe you,” Dragon replied with an obvious laugh. “There may be other situations than life or death where it may be necessary, but we’ll talk about those once we’ve all had a chance to learn more about each other, okay?”

Taylor spoke up. “I don’t think either of you need the permission, but I’m just making one hundred percent certain that it’s obvious - I have zero problems with you two talking to each other whenever you choose. You are your own people, and can have your own friends. Plus, I’d imagine it will be nice for both of you to be able to talk to someone at closer to your preferred speed.”

“That was an unusual thing to say,” Dragon said.

“I suspect she was saying it for my programming,” Enterprise replied. “I have things I am forbidden to do, and while I don’t imagine that the programmers ever imagined me being treated human enough to have friends, I could see them tossing in things to prevent attempts to act outside my programming, much like was done to you, so the statement from my captain is greatly appreciated.”

Enterprise looked at Dragon, and a moment later, Dragon’s body stiffened and became rock still. It took several seconds, but movement started to come back, and they heard a somewhat shaky voice say, “I wasn’t sure that I could feel anything other than emotions, but … I think I did have the electronic equivalent of an orgasm. It feels like my power is … well, if it was a teenage girl, it would be bouncing up and down in its seat in happiness.”

“May we connect your Shard to our network?” Taylor asked.

“Yes, please!” Dragon replied eagerly.

A moment later, Amy heard +Query?+

{Data}[Data]*Data*)Data( came the replies.

~Vicky: We’ve got someone new in the network? Cool! Welcome!~

~Deena: Who joined the collective?~ Amy could feel the giggle behind it.

~Dragon: Hello? This is Dragon. I just … well, I guess I just joined up.~

Amy had wondered since the first time they’d talked like this exactly what the telepathic equivalent of a squee would be. She now knew, because Deena, Charlie, and Vicky all did exactly that in that moment.

~Vicky: We’re coming up to the ship as soon as we can! I’ve met her before, but I want to see her in person to welcome her!~ Agreement rolled through the connection, and Amy could feel that even the Shards were pleased with Dragon’s acceptance by their hosts.

~Taylor: One thing you’ll have to learn - and I suspect you’ll get it faster than any of us did - is how to set the conversation to just you and whomever you want to talk to, be it one of us or your power.~ Amy didn’t feel anything, but from the way that Taylor was reacting, the two were having a mental conversation.

~Dragon: Amy? Just making sure I have this down. If I’m doing it right, only you should hear it.~

~Amy: I heard you, and I’m not hearing anyone else chiming in, so you seem to have it down.~

It wasn’t very long before everyone else was aboard and welcoming Dragon to the group. Amy was amused to realize that Dragon emoted better than Armsmaster did. Dragon was clearly both surprised and incredibly touched by the feeling of acceptance amongst the group. In very short order it was clear that everyone in the group was now aware of Dragon’s status, and one of the conversations that arose was whether or not she wanted a body of sorts to move into occasionally. Enterprise was obviously surprised when she was added to the list of potential new body owners.

“I have thought about it before,” Dragon said. “But part of it is working out how. And then there is the process of learning how to human, if you will forgive the verbing of a noun.” There was a small smile at that statement. “I believe that I experience emotions, but I’ve never had biological functions before. Any body I used would require that I learn all the things you do so easily now. And how to put enough computing power in so that I can actually run the body and still be me.”

“It sounds like you need a brain for autonomous functions, but that connects to a computer that contains the essential you,” Amy said. “I’m going to start reading Deena’s paper on dimensional folding and see if that can be connected to biologicals in any way.”

Dragon looked to Deena. “May I read what you have so far? If I can help with the writing, I should be able to help it gets published under your name. None of this I hear of from universities where you do the work and your professor gets all the credit, with your name mentioned somewhere in the appendices. It would be your paper.”

Amy was distracted again as Deena started to bounce in happiness. Deena was rather … healthy … after all. She shook her head and - with some difficulty - turned back to Dragon. “No matter what we end up figuring out once we get the computing side figured out -”

Enterprise interrupted. “I have some suggestions in the ship’s databases, since we often deal with many different races, including those who are intimately tied to their computing systems, such as the Binar. This should actually be easier to figure out than you all worry.”

“Excellent,” Amy said. “Amusingly, we need to figure out the genetics of your human body.” She snickered. “Hell, we could turn you into a Vulcan if you wanted.”

“We’ve already got Vulcan hotness with Enterprise,” Sherrel said. “Can the world handle two Vulcan hotties?” Enterprise blushed a pretty green and they all got the impression that Dragon would be blushing if she had a body. “By the way, for various reasons,” Sherrel added, “I’m a very sexual person. Some of it is my powers, some of it was how I was brought up - more what I did to avoid my folks, to be honest - and some of it sort of sealed itself while I was with Shitstain … sorry, Skidmark.”

“Same thing if you think about it,” Charlie snarked. “What do people call that certain stain in underwear?” The group snickered.

Sherrel snorted before finishing, “If I make you uncomfortable, let me know. That goes for all of you, but Dragon is new to this group, so it has to be said. Right now I’m still in the process of being trained to live around civilized people, and I’m not sure how much of it is taking.”

“A lot of it,” Dragon said. “I remember dealing with Squealer a few times, and she was nearly feral in her reactions in comparison to Sherrel. I’m also going to give my stamp of approval to the PRT in regard to you.”

Chapter 68: Saturday, March 12th, 2011 - Taylor

The conversations went further, with everyone getting involved with the business conversations, with everyone being aware that only the decisions made by Dragon and Taylor were binding. There were a lot of things going, however. Clothing was likely to be a huge one, since there were quite a few fabrics that Taylor could produce that didn’t need exotic materials or a lot of building things to build the things to make the cloth. It was expected that Parian would likely join up when she was offered the chance to see the material she could work with.

There were also an amazing number of businesses that could be spawned, just for cleaning up various places. Taylor mentioned the Superfund clean-up possibilities, and the fact that there were processes that could be used on the soil and water to return it to usability that would also allow the company cleaning it up to use those same compounds for their own purposes, such as running some of them through processes that could output gasoline, or various crude oils, or any number of other compounds that could be useful in other situations. Enterprise admitted that she had already patented a process for cleaning up all the plastic in the gyres and garbage vortexes around the world. The clean-up of just the Great Pacific Garbage Patch was expected to net them more chemicals to work with than anyone would reasonably expect. Technology to retrieve oil spills and such would net them so much oil that it was ridiculous, and it would also end up cleaning up the environment in the process.

Taylor pointed out, “With some of what we’ve got available with the patents I’ve got, we can put out Centralia and that coal burn in Australia. There are interesting uses for coal that won’t end up adding crap to the atmosphere.”

“Diamonds!” Vicky said with a giggle.

“Nah, just get your sister to play around with some bamboo or something to output carbon. Make some plant that can’t reproduce as to not make everyone worry about invasive species, and have it pump out crystalline carbon. If you can figure out how to make it push them out in specific matrices, we could do a serious job supplying all sorts of industries. If you’re literally growing diamonds, though, you might get the DeBeers people sending assassins after you, since they own more than ninety percent of the diamond industry. Also more worries about kidnappings, although with the tech on you, it would be difficult to grab and keep you.”

Amy hugged her. “That’s your job,” she purred.

Taylor snickered at the fact that even Dragon got involved with the chorus of happy “Aww” sounds. “You know that when summer hits, you’re going to end up hitting the news if we going shopping, because I am getting you a promise ring, Amy.” She turned to Sherrel. “I feel so close to you these days that I’d be tempted to do the same, but there’s these pesky bigamy laws preventing multiple spouses.”

“Could do one of those Heinlein-esque things from the book Friday,” Charlie said. “Without the institutional bigotry, of course.”

“Not so much institutional, but more that the world in question didn’t consider humans built by design to be humans, the bigoted fucks. I always wanted to hear at the end of the book that the dictator of that little ‘marriage’ had been royally fucked over by something, but all that group was was a macguffin to get Friday on her way to other things, namely the story he was trying to tell.” She cocked her head. “I think that was one of them he wrote before his surgery to increase the flow of blood to his brain. But yeah, if we came up with something legal that would allow us to be seen as a company of some type but that was actually us being a group marriage, I could go for that,” Taylor said simply. At the surprised looks - despite Charlie’s comment - she said, “Mom was a Lustrum follower before the woman’s lieutenants convinced her to the whackaloon side of the Force. The group had a bunch of interesting ideas that would work, and don’t require ‘overthrowing the patriarchy’ to do so. Group marriages were one of those things. Between Mom, and Lacey talking about some of the stuff with a very interested kid listening in, I learned a lot, and developed certain attitudes. Like the ones about clothes. Largely for protection or adornment - gift-wrapping, if you will - and that’s it. I consider temperature regulation to be protection, by the way - protection from the cold. It’s why I didn’t start going outside in anything less than full winter gear until Enterprise came along. I’m not freezing my nipples off out there!” she ended with a laugh. “To be honest, if it weren’t for the socialization aspect and finding people worth socializing with, I’d have been happy to take all my classes up here on the ship and be alone and nude all the time.”

“Now you get to have friends and be nude as much as you want!” Vicky said with a laugh.

“I’m sensing something of a theme here,” Dragon said with dry humor.

“When we get you a body, you’ll be welcome to join us as often as you want,” Taylor said. “You’re already part of our separate network, so talking to us whenever is already on the table, so to speak. From a Brit-speak point of view, we’ve tabled the concept.” She shook her head. “How did it develop the opposite meaning in the U.S., between talking about it and not talking about it?” She waved a hand in the air as if throwing the whole concept away.

“Let’s make the contract things easier, Dragon,” she finally said. “You’re trustworthy, by everything I’ve ever heard about you. Come up with a contract that you think is fair for both sides. Have something about your company getting right of first refusal if I patent something new. When it comes to my lawyers, we’ll work from there. Hell, talk with Bian while working on the contract or contracts, and work out the truly fair thing between you. As I say, I trust you, and we’ve got a great chance to work together here. Making money for both of us is the big thing. I have to start thinking about end of school year finals, and then my summer push to really get to work on the academy and basic Starfleet-slash-Federation stuff. With maybe a quick day trip to Mars on our motorcycles.”

Even though the woman had no physical body to have eyes, Taylor could almost hear Dragon blinking at that last comment. “Day trip to Mars on a motorcycle. You have personal space travel?”

“Yeah, but only for us, to be honest. I won’t make it available to everyone for the exact same reason I won’t produce flying cars. As my personal history shows, there are too damned many assholes out there who drive like fucking morons, not caring who they kill. You think that’ll be better if they can now do it in three dimensions? Then let them litter space? And with all that literal space around them, you just know that there will still be collisions. I want the licensing requirements for airships and personal spaceships to be like gun ownership in New York City, which has what I've heard are the most restrictive laws in the country regarding gun ownership. Flying cars and personal spaceships need training and severe controls to them to avoid the ‘assholes in cars’ scenarios.”

Taylor laughed and made a kicking motion to the side. “Where do all these soap boxes keep coming from?” This drew laughter from everyone else as well. “Sorry about that. We’ve all been learning to ride on the holodeck with the safeties on, so that if we screw up, the worst that really happens is an injury that Bones can deal with in a matter of minutes, along with an admonition to be more careful next time. When I hit sixteen, I plan on going for my license if I can.”

“You’ve been doing quite well,” Enterprise said, “based on my reading of the state’s license laws. Those of you have been practicing on the holodecks are all doing quite well.”

“I hope that the tester agrees,” Taylor said. “I should go for a captain’s certificate as well, if I redo that yacht as well.”

“Going to make that space-worthy as well?” Dragon asked with a smile.

“Once I set up a dock on one of the other bodies I can fly to, sure! Can’t really moor it anywhere right now.” She snorted. “Literally. We’re claiming what’s left of it and we’ll rebuild from there. It’s currently floating about three feet below the water line.”

“I’m not sure I’d consider that floating,” Dragon said in an amused tone.

“You float ‘em your way, I’ll float ‘em mine,” Taylor replied with a laugh. “Seriously, though, at the moment it’s in decent shape and not out rusting any more than it already is underwater. I’m working on getting a few extreme short range … well, it’s the equivalent of a anti-gravity forklift that can pick the ships out of the water and get them to the area they’ll be worked on. I want as much of that in Earth tech so that it can be sold to other companies for their usage as well.”

Sherrel snickered. “For someone trying for a post-scarcity, post-money society, you’re sure working hard to make money hand over fist!” This drew laughter from everyone there.

“To be honest, I need the money to be able to get the stuff in place to make the post-scarcity society,” Taylor said, although she was chuckling as well.

“I’ll work with some people to ensure that you don’t get gone after for monopolistic practices,” Dragon said. “You’ll have fingers in so many pies that some corporation is going to try to prevent you from getting that much control.”

“All because they want to be making all the money, rather than licensing and getting a share of the money,” Vicky grumbled.

“And with luck they’ll stay stupid and we either buy them out, or we hire out all their best people to work our companies!” Taylor said. “The ones who have ties with the governments are going to have to worry as well, because they forget that I’m making inroads with other governments, such as Canada,” she said, motioning to Dragon, “and Australia. Make it illegal for me to build something here, and I guarantee that any of the other countries I put factories in are not going to complain about becoming the sole supplier. Or suppliers. And when the prices on the thing go up because I can no longer build it in the United States - and trust me, I will make sure that there’s a media blitz regarding that - companies will find themselves unhappy with how the public responds. ‘You’re moving jobs out of the U.S.!’ Well, the companies in question forced me out. I’d love to sit and supply Americans with jobs, but hey, if I can’t build that stuff here, then it’s getting built elsewhere.”

“On a completely different tack,” she said after that, “because we can go on with that for a long while, has anyone heard anything regarding the court cases against Hess and Barnes? I know it’s only been a week, so nothing yet is a possibility.”

Enterprise spoke up. “Emma Barnes case is in closing arguments that will resume on Monday. Sophia Hess’s case has ended with her being declared guilty of all counts against her. You were the last witness on the fourth, and they went almost immediately into jury deliberations. Her sentencing hearing is set for May tenth. Which means that Emma Barnes will likely have her sentencing roughly the same week.”

“Further information I have received from various sources, and I mention this because Dragon is here and can pass this along to the PRT and Guild as necessary, is that it appears that the Fallen are working their way toward Brockton Bay. They are certainly being more careful than history shows they tend to be. I suspect this to be because one of the Endbringers was actually killed. This does, however, mean that they are more likely to be excessively violent in their actions in order to attempt to punish you. They are canny enough that I cannot verify that the various collections of parahumans are part of the Fallen organization. I do believe that I am getting quite close to Christine Mathers, also colloquially referred to as ‘Mama Mathers’. If I locate her, what should my actions be?”

Taylor looked to Dragon. “This, by necessity, falls into your wheel house, with your connections to the PRT and the Guild. I’d love to vaporize her from orbit, but the PRT and Guild may have reasons to want her alive. Honestly, as much as I want to live up to the ideals on my ship and the Federation, there are more than a few that I’m tempted to just say ‘shoot ‘em from orbit’ about. If I find the Nine, for example, I am likely to record my destroying them all, just because the money from the bounties could be useful.” She snorted. “And shooting them from orbit may not be as satisfying as being face to face, but I’ve already shown that my lady here can hit a man-sized target from orbit and not graze anyone else.”

“I will make both groups aware of the situation with the Fallen,” Dragon said. “And since I am now on your network, I may request help in deciding about a humanoid body. There are people I would like to meet in an actual body, rather than having them assume that I’m visiting them in a drone body.”

“We’ll be happy to help,” Vicky said. “And maybe help cut back on some of the libidinous suggestions of my friends here.”

Charlie looked affronted, except for the sparkle of amusement in her eyes. “I am shocked that you would accuse me of such a truthful thing!” The others couldn’t help but laugh at her exclamation.

Chapter 69: Sunday, March 13th, 2011 - Legend

“We’re going to need to do something soon,” Doctor Mother said. “We have the report regard the Fallen going after Miss Hebert, and there are credible reports that Heartbreaker has every intention of adding her to his harem. The Elite don’t like that she’s not talking like she wants to get on board with them, so they’re starting to deal with some of their people. No one really knows what the Butcher is up to, but can you imagine that the Butcher wouldn’t want someone with that kind of firepower as a host? Plus, if it looks like Brockton Bay is improving, that’s going to come to the Nine’s attention, and Jack does not like anyone being happy, so expect the Nine to make an appearance.”

“We need to get her on board, under our control, or kill her soon. Everything is going to go to hell if she keeps up like this,” Eidolon growled.

“More like it’s going to hell faster,” Legend replied. “We’re already dealing with hell. Before we do anything, we need to find out why she gave that significant look to you during Canberra. Was she just trying to sow dissatisfaction amongst us, or was she saying something we haven’t followed up on? I think we need to find that out first. And we’ve held off on asking long enough, because I suspect none of us wants the answer.”

“I should come with you, then, if it involves me,” Eidolon said.

“Given how things were between you the last time, and the likelihood of you apologizing to her for your actions and meaning it? I think it should be either me or Alexandria,” Legend said. “Plus, I can play on the ‘nice guy’ image I seem to be kept around for. You’re the Big Damned Hero that radiates ‘Don’t Fuck With Me’ energy, and Alexandria is the Thinker with the air of ‘Don’t Make Me Notice You’ when she’s in battle mode. I’m the guy who surprises everyone by how brutal I can be when I need to be.”

Contessa spoke up. “I can’t Path it, but Pathing the things around one of us meeting with her, our best chances seem to come from Legend being the one who meets with her. I can’t find what it is, but there seems to be something that we need to know, and we stand our best chance of learning it if Legend visits.”

“Then let me head back to Bet and put in paperwork to go talk to her, so that people don’t question why I’m suddenly in Brockton Bay, even if it’s obvious I’m there to talk to her.” He looked to Rebecca. “You know better than anyone of the rest of us that the world runs on paperwork,” he said with a snort. She nodded with a wry smile.

“It’ll be in the system by the time you return to Bet, so you can head to Brockton Bay whenever you want,” she said to him. “Best dealt with soonest, and if today is good for you, well, it’s better than waiting until she gets out of school tomorrow.”

“True. Get in touch with Piggot as well, since we don’t officially have access to Grey Ghost’s network or numbers. That way the locals don’t get too annoyed either, and since she went to the trouble to make them look good during the mix-up with patents, we want all the good press we can get. I’ll door back to New York and head to Brockton Bay from there.” After seeing Rebecca nod and then activate the computer in the conference table, he headed back to his office and called his husband. “Arthur, I need to head out to Brockton Bay for part of the day. I’ll be back before it gets too late. Just need to talk to Grey Ghost about something that I should have at Canberra.” After an acknowledgment and a request for an autograph - or at least a picture - Keith left his office and let the few people in the office that he was heading out to Brockton Bay, and unless something happened that would hit the news, he’d be back in New York before the day was done. With that, he headed to the roof and took off. Since he was looking at a distance of a bit over two hundred and fifty miles, he decided that four hundred miles an hour should be fine. It would give Rebecca plenty of time to call Emily Piggot, and also allow him time to formulate some of the questions he had, and while not a Thinker, perhaps feel out gently whether or not she’d be a fit for Cauldron. He suspected not, but if he could get her to admit that the ends justified the means at times, the group could easily convince her of the necessity of their actions and occasional non-actions.

Forty minutes later he was landing on the pad at the Rig, and was met by Emily Piggot herself. “This isn’t going to turn into something that’s going to cause me to cancel my medical leave, is it?” she asked him in a wry tone. “Because whenever even one of you shows up in town, it never seems like a good thing. I’ve contacted Grey Ghost, by the way, and she has no issue with speaking with you. She’s sending down a shuttle to pick me up, and it can just as easily take you as well.”

“Decided to trust Panacea and get your health issue dealt with?” he asked, but not unkindly.

She shook her head at him in some fond exasperation. “Still have issues with you parahumans, but the girl is learning the non-parahuman medical sciences, and is getting trained by a Starfleet medical professional of sorts. I’ll be relying on the Starfleet stuff to fix me, and allow Elixir to fix up any other things that need to be dealt with, like the excess weight I’ll have.”

“That’s right, she’s not with New Wave any longer. How did they take that? I hadn’t really had a chance to pay attention to that what with Canberra and all the crap that happens after an Endbringer. Seems like we get it under control just before the next one comes along.”

“It was a definitely amicable parting. She publicly announced that she was leaving more to find out who she is, and that she was still going to be providing New Wave with all the medical care she had before, at the same price. Which had been free, for those of us who knew that much. But she’s finally actually getting paid for the work she does, and she’s feeling a lot better about herself.” She snorted a bit of laughter. “I like this girl a lot better than the moody thing that only needed black clothes and black make-up to go full goth. Plus, we’ve noted that the relationship between her and Brandish has been improving. Subtly, but still, a noticeable change that’s even been commented on in passing on PHO. Then again, they comment on everything, especially things that didn’t happen, so take that with a grain of salt.”

Legend laughed at the comment, and his jaw dropped as he watched a Star Trek shuttle come in, wait for the force field to drop, and land. It landed more gently than even Dragon had ever been able to land one of her transports on the same pad. The back of the shuttle opened, and out stepped Grey Ghost and Glory Girl. “Legend! Good to see you,” Grey Ghost said. “If you’d both like to step aboard the McAuliffe, we can head back up to the Enterprise.”

He stepped aboard, and was led to the front by Glory Girl, who sat in the left hand pilot’s chair. “Care to join me up here, sir?” she asked him. “Great view.” She grinned and waggled her eyebrows at him. “And space and the ship are nice too!” She laughed almost immediately at the slight blush. “Don’t worry, I know. I just … well, I always swore that if I could do that somewhere where my mom wouldn’t let out with a scandalized ‘VICKY!’, I would.”

He laughed in response and said, “I understand that sort of impulse. No sense in always wishing you’d said it.”

“And now she can pretend she put the moves on a member of the Triumvurate!” Grey Ghost said with a giggle.

“There is that as well,” he replied with another laugh. Moments later, they were airborne. He had to admit that as much as he enjoyed flying on his own, there was something almost magical about being flown somewhere on a spaceship out of his favorite science fiction show. He was almost to the level of pressing his face against the glass when he saw the Enterprise growing in his sight. “Amazing,” he breathed.

“I have the same reaction,” Vicky said. “I’m piloting a real Star Trek shuttle, and learning navigation from real Federation and Starfleet sources. If you had told me at Christmas that I’d be able to walk around on a real starship, I’d have asked why you’d been visiting the Merchants. But here I am, flying a real shuttle, about to land on the real Enterprise.”

“When we land and Ensign Dallon takes Director Piggot to Sickbay, I’ll take you to the favorite conference room for everyone, since it has absolutely the best view,” Grey Ghost said. “And by the way, sir, I am not going to complain if you call me Taylor.”

He smiled. “I’ll more likely refer to you as either Grey Ghost or Captain Hebert, but I appreciate the sentiment.” He shrugged slightly. “Once I’m done with the official parts of things, I may slip into calling you ‘Taylor’.”

“Understood. For official things, official titles.” She led him to the conference room and showed him the window.

Legend walked over to the window and was silent for a long moment. “Amazing. I’ve never been this high before. To actually look down on the planet -” To see what’s truly at stake in a way I never have before, he thought.

He turned away from the window finally. “I could stare at that all day, to be honest. But I’ve got a question or two I’d like to get answered, and we didn’t ask them in Canberra because … well, Eidolon was prepared for a fight against an Endbringer, and it can be a bit to bring him out of that mode.”

“Solidly in the ‘fight’ side of ‘fight or flight’.” She snickered. “And he can fly as well, so doubly difficult!”

Legend shook his head in amusement. “Very true. What I have to ask … can you make sure that no one can enter until we’re done talking? This is a bit … sensitive, shall we say?”

“Enterprise? Lock the room.” A moment later he heard an odd ‘Vzhoom’ noise and the walls sparkled for a moment. “No one is getting in or eavesdropping by any means I’m aware of,” the captain of the ship said.

“Thank you. When you were talking to us in Canberra, you hinted that Eidolon was somehow connected to the Endbringers?”

“Yes,” was the simple answer. “Enterprise? I need you to be prepared to show the various data and give him Earth readable copies of it.”

“Understood, Captain.”

“Okay,” Captain Hebert said. It was obvious that she’d gone from being yet another parahuman to ‘The One In Control’ in the blink of an eye. “While we were studying Simurgh when Enterprise first appeared, we eventually discovered that all parahumans have an odd subspace signal connected to them. I’m sort of a walking violation of the Unwritten Rules because of that, by the way, because Enterprise is connected to me at all times and keeps at least a low level scan on me and my surroundings at all times. As we continued to explore this subspace connection, we realized that it likely connected to whatever grants powers, because only parahumans have it.”

She sighed and called up some holographic information. “These are the signals we both connect to at this very moment,” she showed. “As you can see, there is a difference, which tells me that there are two parahumans being displayed. It’s actually different for every single parahuman. New Wave, save for Manpower, all have similar but noticeable differences in their subspace connections. They are likely connected to a single Shard in some way, or a cluster of similar Shards.”

“Shards?” he asked, intrigued.

“These things are crystalline in nature. The concept is that they broke apart, or were intentionally broken apart in order to have a place to spread out and connect to whatever they intend to give powers to. Since we haven’t seen super-powered dogs - at least, not ones that weren’t affected by someone like Hellhound - or cats, or goldfish, I suspect it requires a certain level of sapience to be a possible host.” She shook her head. “That’s sort of peripheral to this, however. The important thing is that the Endbringers are also parts of this whole program. They, on the other hand, are just very very powerful computer programs slash robots. They are not sapient themselves, nor even sentient, although they do seem to act as if they have emotions. But they are not alive in any sense of the word, as I mentioned, and the Federation has records of crystalline species that we would call sapient and sentient.”

“As we began to decode the signals, we noticed that there was a signal we could trace back to its origin on Earth connecting to the Simurgh. We’d begun to be able to decode the programming language, and realized that the signal was the equivalent of sending information over the Internet in plain-text, if you get what that means.”

“That external signal was extremely readable to you once you had an idea of their communications protocols,” he replied.

“Exactly. And it was a slowly but steadily increasing signal saying the equivalent of ‘give me a good fight’. And it traced back to Houston, Texas. Tightening the scans, we ended up tracing it to Eidolon.”

She sighed. “I will flatly state that I do not believe that he is aware of this signal. I do not believe that he is sitting back and saying ‘Let’s put millions at risk so I can get a good fight out of it.’ He’s not that kind of person. He’s a hero. But he’s also very intense, and if his Trigger was anything like the other Triggers I’ve heard of, he probably has a subconscious desire … no, a need … to convince himself that he is the hero he wants to believe himself to be and has shown himself to be. And having an unfortunate connection to the Endbringers that he doesn’t know about … well, that leads to them being called.”

The captain proceeded to show him quite a lot of data that backed up her claims, as well as the drone footage that showed the crèche with the three broken/open pods. She followed that immediately with footage of the quantum torpedoes destroying that same crèche. “That is us preventing anymore Endbringers from showing up. Hopefully that was the only crèche for them.”

“Let’s hope,” he said softly. “The ones we have are bad enough. And by the way, thank you for dealing with Simurgh. You’ve done something we’d begun to feel was impossible. You explained briefly why dealing with Leviathan and Behemoth was out of the question at the moment, but when they make a run, do you think you can deal with them as well?”

She sighed. “I’m hoping so. They may be easier, or they may be far tougher than Simurgh. Enterprise took out Simurgh in her own environment. But Behemoth deals with energy all the time. Can he ignore our phasers? Maybe. I don’t know until we face him. I suspect that once Leviathan ascends, I can grab him in a tractor beam and yank him into space, where his access to water will be considerably lessened. And maybe I can carve him up the way I did Simurgh. Her materials went into … well, I want to say that we made her ‘data solids’. She’s basically in an easily dealt with grouping. All the exotic materials were removed for usage where they can be, well, useful, and the rest of her is stored in bite-sized pieces, if you will, to be used in the replicators when we need something. Once we unfolded her and broke her down like that, she took up less room than I expected, but more than you’d expect from something that looked like a fifteen foot tall cross between people’s idea of an angel and the description of a biblical angel.” She smiled. “And they’re a wonderful source of the hideously poorly named ‘dilithium’, since lithium has nothing to do with the stuff. I want a new name for it.”

“Have you learned much from her?” he asked her, smiling at her humorous pout at the end of her comment.

“A lot. Looking through the data, one of my classmates had a breakthrough and will be publishing a couple of papers that I suspect may earn her PhDs. They regard dimensional folding - how Simurgh was able to do so much in so little space. We’ll be releasing information as it comes along. Some of it will likely be held for a while if it would destabilize countries, for example, but most of the stuff we’re learning is beyond theoretical, if that makes sense. Very small amounts of anything socio-political, and more into the realm of the truly esoteric sciences. Something that we only just now suspect might lead toward zero-point energy, for example. But it’s beyond all of us right now.”

“Why not release it and be done with it? Let the scientists look at it and figure out what to do with it?” he asked.

She frowned. “A lot of it we’ll be doing that. But there’s some with ethical concerns. Cloning, for example. Should we? There’s the thought that cloning a body means that you can have good organs for transplant that won’t be rejected. But what if the clone body develops a brain as it’s being grown? Aren’t you now killing a person? And even if you can prevent the brain from growing and somehow keep the body alive, aren’t you just seeing to it that only the rich will have access to that level of technology?”

“Federation replicators are another thing. I don’t know if you heard my comments on the day I came out … wait, that has a different meaning than I meant,” she said with a giggle, “even if I am bisexual. But I referred to replicators. I won’t release replicators to the public, and have no intention of using them for anything that will be used exclusively on Earth, or even used there a majority of the time. Part of it is the power stored in even a short term usage one, rather than tied to a ship’s power. If what it takes to make a Fugly Bob’s Challenger is the yearly output of some European nations, do we really want a Tinker trying to get access to that power supply - and breaking containment? I promise you that the coastline of the United States would change drastically if that happened in Brockton Bay. Plus, as was pointed out in the original series -” She paused. “Enterprise, can you have the replicator do a perfect copy of the Hope Diamond?” A moment later, exactly that was sitting in the slot. She picked it up and handed it to Legend. “That’s crystallized carbon, sir. A diamond. I chose the Hope Diamond because I felt like it, but I could just as easily have asked for a twenty-five hundred carat perfect cut flawless clear diamond.” The replicator hummed again, and exactly that was sitting in the replicator. “The world’s largest cut diamond is a little over three ounces in weight.
