That is over five times the weight of that diamond, and is perfect in every way. I can do the same with gold and any other precious material. So the ethics of the situation won’t allow me to allow that technology to be available to the world until such point as we are ready for it.”

Legend nodded and handed the Hope replica back to Captain Hebert. “I understand, and support where you’re coming from. Just the two examples you gave would irrevocably change the world, and not for the better, and I am certain that there are a number of other ideas that are just as dangerous.”

“Yeah,” she said. “Time travel is canonical for Star Trek, remember. And this ship is literally a generation or more away from So Long And … sorry, from The Voyage Home. I’ve got private names for all the Star Trek original series films.”

He laughed. “‘So Long And Thanks For All The Fish’?” he asked, and she nodded with a blush.

“But they were able to figure the calculations to end up exactly when they needed to back then. More than a hundred years passed between then and when this ship was commissioned. Look at the difference from 1911 to 2011. In 1911, they ridiculed you if you talked about going to the Moon. A 1930s New York Times opinion piece ridiculed Robert Goddard for suggesting that it could be done, because everyone knew you had to have something to push against, and it was vacuum out there. July of 1969 saw that same paper print a retraction of that opinion piece because we’d just landed three men to go to that same Moon. Let’s not even bring Tinkertech into things. A computer was a thing of ridicule, then something only universities could have, and by the time that Scion showed up, we were dealing with being able to own our very own one in our own house! Now we have the Internet and cell phones and all sorts of other things. And that’s without Tinkertech added in. In a hundred years! So yeah, I could easily go back in time to this point or that point and change things. Maybe figuring out a way to save Hero? Save my own mother? But where does it stop, and what changes because of it? There is no one who knows how everything would change. So the only way to deal with time travel is to not use it, unless there’s something that should have happened that didn’t and we somehow know it. I suspect that would be because there was still a chance to fix the issue, so those who could fix it would be at least partially immune to the changes, but I’ll be damned if I’m going to experiment with that.”

She rubbed the back of her neck. “Yeah, sorry. I get mouthy about things when they mean a lot to me. Kinda hard to shut me up about them.”

“It’s all right. To be honest, it gives me a good feeling that you’re the one with access to all this technology. There are so many others who would be a nightmare with it. L33t? Squealer? I know she’s better now, but I’m referring to the girl who was drugged out of her gourd, not the Sherrel of today. And those are the ones that would be vaguely trustworthy with it. I can think of many other Tinkers who would be horrid choices. Mannequin?” He shuddered, and so did she.

“I think I’ve learned what I needed to. Could I get that data from you so that we can talk about this? And maybe we can find a way to block that signal you mentioned.”

“I suspect we could, but he’d have to trust me about it. It turns out that there’s something of an aggression signal in the subspace signal that goes to each parahuman, and Enterprise has blocked it in me, Vicky, Amy, and Sherrel, as well as one other. You’ll notice that there haven’t been any Collateral Damage Barbie moments in the last month or so?”

His eyebrows rose. “Do you have that data as well?” A small USB drive appeared in the replicator as they walked near it.

“That contains all the data regarding the signals we have talked about here,” Enterprise said. He thanked her and slipped into one of the pockets that wasn’t a pocket in his costume.

Chapter 70: Monday, March 14th, 2011 - Legend

“So she’s definitely not a candidate for Cauldron,” Rebecca said. “Too principled to do some of the things we’d want to do, like get our hands on some of that tech that she won’t release to the public. As much as I’d love to figure out a way to save Hero, I can’t argue with the time travel thing. We’d pretty much have to use Contessa to Path out anything we wanted to do with time travel, and I’m not sure that her power would allow for that. It’s just too fraught with world or universe ending possibilities.” She snorted. “And it’s a bad thing if we do what we’re trying to keep Scion from doing.”

Eidolon frowned. “The data she gave you. How certain are we that this wasn’t a careful set-up to get me out of the way for some reason?”

“Honestly? If she wanted that and she’s that good at seeming so utterly sincere, then we’ve already lost. If this data is true, she thinks that it is at absolute worst, a subconscious thing on your part, and maybe it’s just wishful thinking on my part, but I think she’s kind of hoping that it’s something that comes from your Shard. She sees you as a hero, Eidolon, and figures that the reason you two got off on the wrong foot is that you were both ramped up for a fight against someone that we luckily didn’t have to fight. She thinks that you were prepared for the fight of your life, and that she was the unfortunate first person you came across to vent. She’s not entirely happy with you, but she seems to be the type that, if you went to her with an honest apology for your attitude, she’d forgive you in a heartbeat. Look at the bit with Rebecca. When she came out with that masterful bit of bullshit, but sounded amazingly honest about it, Grey Ghost forgave her and understood immediately how these things happen. I suspect she’d greet Rebecca fairly warmly and probably apologize for the video she posted. After all, listen to some of how she’s referred to that incident. ‘Having a fifteen year old’s hissy fit’? She’s either an amazing level of Thinker that we’ll have to search hard to counter, or she’s being a genuine fifteen year old who wants to fix things. I’m honestly betting on that being the case rather than her being an ultra-devious Thinker.”

Eidolon frowned. “I just … I don’t want to believe that I’m the one who has been calling those damned … if it’s true, then I’m the reason hundreds of thousands, if not millions of people have died!”

“What if it’s your power?” Legend asked. “We still don’t know everything about the vials and why they do what they do, or even all of the various things that happen. Why do some people become Case 53s? We just don’t know. Why are your powers decreasing; getting harder to use? We don’t know. Is it energy levels? Is it something built in to the power? For all we know, there’s a time limit to how long you can use them, and you’re supposed to find a way to gain more power. For that matter, we don’t know if you drank the entirety of a Shard - you may have only gotten part of what it was supposed to do. So I’m willing to agree with her that you were sending out a ‘come at me, bro’ call, but that you were definitely not in control of that call. I suspect it’s your power doing it, in which case you have zero cause to feel guilty.”

“Are you absolutely certain about all of this?” Rebecca asked. “The data, I mean?”

“Again, it would require a more powerful Thinker than any we really have access to, in my opinion, to be pulling the wool over my eyes. She felt to me as if she didn’t want to point the finger at David, but the data led her there. She showed me the data that they found, and how they traced and tracked it, and even narrowed it at one point to his secure office space. She showed me multiple points along the line where she could pinpoint to where he was at the time. There were a few times he disappeared, and I didn’t tell her that they coincided with when we were holding meetings here. There was no trace to here, just him disappearing from her sensors, and from listening to her, I think she suspected that it was him activating a power that hid him for a time, since he’s known to come up with all sorts of interesting powers.”

“Good,” she replied. “If she’s not Cauldron material, then I really don’t want her to have any idea where we are. Do you think she can be convinced to take on certain jobs for us, as long as we can give her good ethical reasons for why it needs to be done?”

“Yes, but I am certain that any killing is going to have to be led up to. She was willing to use killing force on Lung when she took him down, but only after she’d exhausted stunning force, and even then, as low a killing blow as possible, hoping that it wouldn’t actually kill him. She’s definitely got that attitude that the original series and Next Gen had about dealing with people - kill as a last resort. She’s more of a Kirk or Picard than a Sisko.”

He took a breath. “Also, if you want to try to convince her to allow use of her technology, she’s either going to have to be the one in charge of it, or assured absolutely that it will be used sparingly. She is extremely serious about not allowing Trek technology of certain types into anything that could be considered public usage. No flying vehicles until people stop being idiots in cars - so that means no flying vehicles,” he added with a laugh, “but also nothing that could have any chance of damage society in any way. She handed me a perfect replica of the Hope Diamond. She also created a literally perfect clear diamond that was over two thousand carats. The damned thing weighed a pound, Rebecca! A one pound perfect diamond. Something so priceless that it swings back around to worthless, because there isn’t enough money to purchase it. So she’ll absolutely not allow access to replicators or the power sources for them, and I can support her on that. If she did use them, it would have to be on very specific things that we couldn’t get any other way but would be absolutely needed. That struck me as one of those concepts she would not be able to be moved from, so it’s best to not even try. Like her, the concept of that replicator power source is too much of draw for Tinkers to try to steal for it to be allowed, because you know someone like L33t would manage to crack containment, and with the energy in one of those things? He wouldn’t even have time to say ‘Oops’ before the Eastern seaboard underwent an explosive change.”

Eidolon gave a wry look to him. “Yeah, that could be bad,” he said in a voice that made it obvious that he knew he was doing the understatement of the century.

“Y’think?” Rebecca snorted. “Did some of the calculations myself and she’s right. Making a one kilo mass uses the energy output for a year of someplace like Ireland. Having that released all at once would be bad enough, but enough energy to make thousands of one kilo masses? It’s possible that New York City would be destroyed if that went off in Brockton Bay. The wave alone would do damage to the African coast at the very least.”

She frowned deeply. “We’re going to have to work on this. The technology is far too important to lose. It took out something we thought was unkillable. But the person in charge of it is too principled to join up with us. And she can’t be properly Pathed. Killing her to take over the technology is on the table, but really needs to be a last resort, because we need to see how the ship would respond to that. Would it return home? Would it go on a rampage that would potentially make … his eventual attack look like a temper tantrum?”

Contessa spoke up. “This can be approached carefully, since I am probing Paths to Path her, if that makes sense to you all. But it should be soon, because if she has not done so already, the is likely to set a first officer for her ship, who would by necessity be her second in command, whom command would fall to should something happen to the captain of the ship. Said person might not have the deep connection to the technology that Hebert does, but could certainly cause issues.”

Rebecca thought for a while before saying, “Unfortunately, not before the next scheduled Endbringer attack, I fear. Right now she’s in the midst of setting everything up, and security of all sorts will be on high alert. Assuming the schedule hasn’t changed radically regarding the Endbringers, our best bet for doing what we end up deciding will be roughly the point of the next battle, which is likely sometime in May, if not early June.”

“She’ll probably still be on some level of alert, since we know that Heartbreaker is not going to allow a girl that age to not be part of his harem, especially when she’s that attractive,” Keith said. “We may have to bite the bullet and take him out for her, and damn the potential issues with all of his thralls. Because getting her under the thrall of either Heartbreaker or Mama Mathers? We’re all doomed at that point. Heartbreaker is easier for us to go after, and if Canada complains about it, we simply remind Harper that Nikos Vasil in charge of a starship is not something that anyone in the world needs.”

“Nor the Fallen, for that matter, but it’s that damned anti-Thinker field Mama puts out that keeps us from doing anything,” Eidolon said, scowling furiously, as if thinking hard enough about her might make her burst into flames from a universe away.

“What about her other potential foes?”

“The Elite will either make their way into controlling her businesses the way they want to, or they’ll end up discovering that perhaps starting a mob war isn’t the best route to take,” Keith said. At the looks he got from the others at the table he explained. “Do you really think that Antonio Francisci Castaleogne is really going to take some other group of organized crime trying to muscle in on his niece terribly well? He’s got some serious hitters in the bunch, so I think that they Elite might find themselves a little stretched if they try. If I know Tony, he’ll wait to see Taylor Hebert’s response. If he likes it, he’ll keep watching, and if he thinks that the Elite might be going a bit too far, he’ll step in, likely with his niece never even knowing it.” He snorted. “Either that or she’ll send him a nice thank you letter afterward. I get the strong impression that the girl can be very scary if she needs to be. Given her family, I can’t say as that surprises me.”

“Well, there’s not much more we can do at this point, so let’s call it a day, and if any of us come up with something that we think needs to be dealt with, call a meeting. Let’s look hard at dealing with Heartbreaker and the Fallen as best we can,” Rebecca, now in Alexandria mode said before they broke up and headed their own ways.

Chapter 71: Monday, March 14th, 2011 - Taylor

“I’m not going to ask the question I want to, because that’s just me hoping that you’re pulling a prank on me, but you’re not that cruel a prankster,” Taylor said to Enterprise as they talked on the bridge. “How did you find them?”

“It came about from noticing that, since I had signatures for all of the Triumvirate, I started looking for them just to verify that I can find individuals. It’s harder from orbit unless I put more resources toward it, but I can at least identify large masses of parahumans together, which has given me locations for pretty much all of the PRT bases that house parahumans. It’s also helped me find some other groups. But in this case, I was curious about something after Canberra, when all three signatures of the Triumvirate disappeared at once. So I went back through my records and noticed that whenever one of them disappeared from my sensors, so did the other two. When he was here, I decided to put a tracker I was fairly certain that they couldn’t detect into the USB drive. Nice thing is, if they’d asked you, you could honestly have said that you hadn’t ordered one to be put in. But I was playing on his likelihood to still think of you as a fifteen year old who might not be that devious. Once I’d gotten a bug on them, it was simple to scan for the signal through the subspace frequencies that seem to be in use by the Shards. It was easier because I was scanning when Legend stepped through a portal of some sort to the other universe. Wasn’t long enough to get a solid lock, but it was enough to tell me the range I needed to search. Once I found it, I punched a few drones through to that world and searched for the three of them. The recording is the result. I picked them up as they were poring through the data we gave them.”

“What kind of drones did you send?” Taylor asked.

“They are roughly the size of a baseball,” Enterprise replied. “Dimensionally folded engines, so they can stay there for a few years as necessary. As much sensory equipment as possible was put in, as well as enough memory to record for a month non-stop. I sent three drones through, with plans for them to rotate their operating periods, since only one drone at a time is needed. There is no weaponry installed in those drones. If necessary, I will send others that have weapons systems installed, but they will likely be larger, roughly the size of a basketball.”

“So all those rumors of a worldwide conspiracy that grants powers aren’t just the ravings of some Internet cult. Wonderful. And it appears to be run by the three most powerful heroes on the planet. And from the sound of it, they just want to use me. Or more precisely, use you.” She sat up straight. “Enterprise, if I am in a situation where I no longer am capable of protecting you from these people, I am ordering you to protect yourself from them. You are to do whatever is necessary to prevent the technology you represent falling into the hands of those people. They sound as if they think they are on the side of the angels, but are willing to treat with the devil himself for their aims. I will not have them gaining access to you.” She paused. “And I do mean anything, up to and including killing them. I am assuming, of course, that I never got the chance to use my ‘go’ word.”

“Understood, Captain Hebert,” was Enterprise’s solemn reply. “Question, Captain.” She asked a moment later. “I keep constant scans on you, and to some extent have a consistently running copy being made of your engrams. Do I, if you are killed, have permission to use the most recent logs I have of you to bring you back using the most recent engrams that I have at that time?”

“Resurrect me via transporter?” Taylor paused for a long moment, then stood and walked to the view screen. “For the time being, Enterprise, my answer is yes, because I suspect that something will happen. I would like to think that I’m immortal, but I’m not that kind of stupid teenager. My stupidity runs in other directions.” She laughed at her self-deprecating comment. “I officially grant you the right to recreate me from the most recent information that you have. We will probably revisit this at another time, because I have no intention of attempting to use that tech to be literally immortal, but while we’re in a situation like this, with enemies on all sides? Yes. I also give you permission to ask the others the same question if you choose to. That one, by the way, is not an order. Only ask them if you want to; you aren’t required to.”

“Understood, Captain,” she replied. “I suspect that our future Chief Medical Officer will agree to it, as well as being able to keep us alive for hundreds of years.”

“Us?” Taylor asked with amusement.

“Yes, Captain. When you finally pass on, I intend to ensure that the ship properly passes command to the next captain, and I will ensure that my personality matrix is shut down. That mental entity that I classify as ‘me’ does not wish to survive your passing for longer than it takes to give control of my body to another worthy captain. Another way of looking at it is that you are my captain and I will have no other. Were you to leave this Starfleet, I would transfer my matrix to a device that could properly contain it and go with you if you chose to allow it.”

“If I chose to allow it?” Taylor asked. “What do you mean ‘if’? Of course I want you in my life for as long as it lasts. In a very real sense, you and I are married in a way that even Amy and I will never manage. Or anyone else, if we figure out a legal way to do that Heinlein ‘Friday-esque’ thing.”

She heard the turbolift doors open, and knew that Vicky had shown up. “Amy’s coming along in a few minutes. She’s just working with Bones about a few things.”

“Okay. I’m working through some stuff here, a little bit of it things I need to worry about with my businesses and school and Starfleet, but more of it is information that I have gotten through channels that aren’t necessarily entirely trustworthy, but the information makes sense. If that makes sense.”

“Not from the PRT, but what you got told fits with what you know,” Vicky said, getting a nod. “What’s the what, then?” Taylor couldn’t help but hear the Kim Possible theme run through her head for a moment.

Taylor snickered at that phrasing, and then opened her mouth to speak just as Amy showed up to the bridge. “Okay, we know the Fallen are likely headed our way, because I dealt with one of their gods, so they either need to kill me, control me, or figure out if they’re going to worship me because I was more powerful that one of their deities. I’m the perfect age for Heartbreaker to add me to his harem, especially since not only do I have a smokin’ hot bod, I am in control of the most powerful weapon on the planet so far. Anyone with Masters under their control is going to be gunning for me.”

“Nice to hear you say that you’re sexy without making jokes about it,” Amy said. “I’d say I do good work, but most of what I did was tune-ups and such, and doing those sexy abs of yours.”

“I’d say you’ve done more than her abs, Ames,” Vicky said with a good-natured leer.

“You know what I meant, Vicky,” she shot back with a laugh. “But hearing you say it without any arrogance or self-deprecation is nice, you know, Taylor?”

Taylor nodded. “When I look in the mirror and see someone who could nearly be my mother, who I have always thought was probably the sexiest woman on the planet, I have to admit to myself that I’m attractive. I’ve got Dad’s height and some of his better features - those abs, for example, come more from his side than Mom’s - but so much of it is Mom. And even without sensors I can tell that Bian sees it as well at times.”

“Well, I’ve seen those movies of hers,” Vicky said without shame. “I will not deny that if it was VHS that I would have worn out the tape re-watching her scenes. Didn’t want to admit that I was bisexual, but kept watching her scenes.” She laughed. “Expect that company to reach out to you when you hit eighteen.”

Taylor snorted. “Bian knows the women who runs the studio. Completely above board stuff, and their work is predominantly lesbian in nature. Apparently the woman who runs the company is complaining that I’m going to be far too famous and need the good press too much to end up working for her, because Bian says that the woman could make bank on me as an actress.” She blushed furiously. “I have the only existing copy of something I did when I was eleven. Literally. Mom was on set and being with her was the only place I could be at the time - Dad was out of town for something and the Barnes family was elsewhere as well. I understood that I needed to be anywhere but near the set, so I sat in an office that no one ever used except to store cameras and such. I had been hanging around all these scantily clad women and was more than a little horny, so I jokingly aimed a camera at the chair I was going to sit in and … pleasured myself. I didn’t realize that I’d accidentally activated the camera, and my little session got stored in camera memory.” Her blush went on afterburner. “When Mom handed me the DVD and assured me that it was the only copy, because they’d erased the camera memory, she said that not only had the director - who had been the one to find it - said that I was a natural for those kinds of films - apparently I accidentally played for the camera such that it caught everything perfectly - but that if I was interested when I hit eighteen, I should look them up if they were still in business.”

Vicky was blinking. “You were told at eleven that you’d make a good porn star?” she asked incredulously.

“Had something to do with knowing how to move for the camera, I understand. I don’t admit it anywhere on Earth, because it qualifies as child pornography, even if it’s me on the camera and me who recorded it. There’s a recording, therefore …” She shook her head. “I’m really tempted to move all my … questionable … things up here to protect them.”

“That will be easy, just let me know what needs to be sent here and I will bring it up.” Enterprise interjected.

Amy snorted. “Imagine contacting that owner/producer and allowing her to use the holodeck for some of her sets.” Taylor, rather than laughing as well, paused and thought about it. “You know, the Star Trek universe had/has a more reasonable view of sex than modern day, even if they’ve never really been allowed to show it. I liked those people, and from Bian’s statements, they’re still the same people I knew then, just a couple years older. I just might do that, in memory of Mom, who enjoyed working for them.”

“Wouldn’t that put a bee in someone’s bonnet?” Vicky asked with a laugh.

“More like shove a murder hornet up their ass,” Amy said. “Oh my God would the fur fly over that!”

“And you know something? I’m willing to let it. Because I’ll be the only one supplying some of the stuff that people want at prices that they’ll be happy with. I’m pretty sure we can set up a holodeck without the hard light aspect easily enough with technology we can patent.” She looked to Enterprise. “Can we legitimately add the solidity with current tech, or do we need to have something figured out first?”

“Stationary solidity is possible. It will take making the tools to upgrade that will allow movement.”

“So we could offer a holodeck that set up a room with immovable furniture, but they’d have to supply food, drinks, cups, movable tables and chairs and such, correct?” At Enterprise’s agreement, she said, “So, we have Bian talk to them and see if I can offer them good terms on a holographic set.” She snorted. “The Annette Hebert Memorial Holofuck Suite.” The girls laughed about that for a while before Taylor got serious again.

“Okay, we know about Heartbreaker and the Fallen,” Vicky said. “Who else?”

“Butcher is going to want to come after me to commit suicide against, because like the others, someone like Butcher in charge of this ship? Of course Butcher wants it! The Elite are going to come after me, but they’re organized crime, and they’ll try to gain controlling shares in order to allow me to build my stuff.” She gave an evil grin. “I’m guessing that they’re assuming that being parahuman trumps family history. We may not roll with them, but we understand them. So I think they’ll maybe be less of an issue than they think they will be, but I’m not getting arrogant about it.”

“I just worry about the Nine,” Vicky said. “You’re a powerful cape who is doing well and doing good. Jack Slash doesn’t like that. He likes to tear people like that down.”

Taylor shrugged. “We’re looking for them, and then I’ll claim the bounties for them, because every one of them is vulnerable to antimatter. We’ll see if Bonesaw is savable, but -” Taylor sighed. “I suspect that we’d pretty much have to do a complete mind erasure on her and train her up from childhood. And give her a completely new identity. If that looks too difficult to do - and we’d be bringing in the PRT on this one, I guarantee - then we’ll just have to kill her, as much as that idea appalls and sickens me.” She straightened. “The others though? They’re adults and have made their decisions. We do scans and recordings of killing them. If at all possible, we grab Bonesaw first, just because she’s known to rebuild them if a fight goes on long enough. Sorry to say this, Amy, but everyone knows that in the fight, you take out the healer first if possible.”

“First off - Hey!” she said with a chuckle, but added, “I understand. It’s a little twitchy around me because aiming for me is a good way to not only get New Wave pissed off at you, but the PRT and just about any other parahuman I’ve ever helped at Endbringer events.”

“The only taking out of the healer I want to see,” Vicky said, “involves movies, dinner, and long romantic walks. If we’re talking about Amy, that is.”

“I’m good with that,” Amy said with a giggle.

“I’ll keep that in mind,” Taylor replied with a mock serious mien.

Chapter 72: Monday, March 14th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the delay in posting. I'm trying for the weekend, but when little things decide that they need to be taken care of NOW - well, you take care of them NOW. (Small stuff, but necessary.)

“I know that we haven’t done it for reasons of privacy, but we’ve hit that slippery slope that could mean my doom if I ignore it. Enterprise, can you show me concentrations of parahumans that don’t match with a PRT site? United States and Canada, please. Otherwise I know you’ll show me the CUI.”

A satellite map of North America showed up, and a handful of sites lit up. “This one appears to be Heartbreaker’s compound,” Enterprise said as one started blinking. The large number of children and nude and semi-nude women tend to back that point of view up. The fact that they are all of an attractiveness near to yours also backs that assumption up. He is currently not showing signs of sending anyone in this direction, but if he has, then they are not parahuman.”

Several spots in the Ozark and Appalachian mountains lit up. “These are the main compounds of the three basic Fallen sects. There has been movement recently, and I have been following them as best I can. They do appear to have been smart enough to have sent their people out in ones and twos, however, making it harder for me to properly track them.”

Boston lit up next. “I have reason to believe that this is Accord’s territory. I have had the chance to look through his plans and every one of them has fatal flaws that he chooses not to see. All of them make the assumption that most things such as Communism, Capitalism, and Libertarianism make - the pure forms look good on paper, but fail to take into account that human beings actually react in unexpected ways. His are different in that it assumes that humans will react, but in manners that do not quite match with historical fact. His plans assume that people will realize that the plans are for the best and simply allow them. They do not take into account the companies that will wish to monetize every part of it, since making money is more important to them than saving people’s lives, for example. He has interesting ideas, but they need to be run through actual human beings first. Also, given the tendency for the Shards to push for greater conflict, some of his plans require mitigating things that his plan caused a few steps earlier.”

“Have you contacted him regarding these plans?” Amy asked. “I know he’s a villain, but I’ve heard that as long as you allow for his OCD, he is one of the more … tractable? … villains to speak with.”

“I have contemplated doing so through secure channels, to see how he reacts. I suspect that if his powers are behind the creation of these plans, then the drive toward conflict is behind most of the problems with the plans.”

The next few areas that lit up were in major cities in the United States, such as Houston, Los Angeles, New York City, and so on. “These are sites with known Elite groups,” she said. “I am in their networks and am aware of many of their plans for you and taking control of your companies. My thought is to prepare for these contingencies and allow them to commit their resources to them before ‘pulling the rug out from beneath them’, I think the phrase is?”

“I suspect that we’ll have to either massively injure or kill some of their members, like Bastard Son,” Vicky said. “He’s a piece of work. Honestly, given what he does to people, if we get a line on him? Kill him. No questions, just kill him. Evidence shows that he ‘knows’ that he’s the best, and when he empowers someone, they permanently lose their mind. They become zombies, basically. ‘Go there and harass. Go there and kill.’ And he just keeps doing it, and walking in to a situation with him and assuming he’ll act fairly? Will get you killed. There’s too much information about him that says that.”

Amy was looking at Vicky in shock. “You’re usually the ultimate superheroine - save them when possible. You’re advocating death for someone?”

“Read the files on him, Ames. The Elite would really like to get their hands on you as well, and honestly, the group is parahuman organized crime, even if the most out members of the group all try to look like ‘legitimate businessmen’.”

Taylor couldn’t help but snort at that. “Sorry, but one of my … well, I call him ‘uncle’ but he’s really more of a great-uncle or something like that … Uncle Tony is a ‘legitimate businessman’. His name is Antonio Francisci Castaleogne. They’ve looked for years for stuff on him and found nothing. If it makes sense, he’s what most of the Mafia people think of when they refer to it politely. He’s a gentleman, and if he makes an agreement with you he will honor it. There are things he is not involved in and will … ‘have words with’ … people if they try to go into those lines of ‘business’, such as hard drugs. Money laundering? Illegal gambling? Loan sharking? No proof, but probably. Prostitution? Nope. Hard stop.”

“Jesus fuckin’ Christ,” Deena breathed as she stepped onto the bridge. “You’re related to the real Teflon Don? They can’t get anything on that dude!”

“He probably has connections in the police and such, but yeah, he’s a relative a bit along the line. Great-uncle probably.”

“Well, at least if something happens and organized crime steps in, you’ll have someone to contact if it gets out of your hands.”

“If I know Uncle Tony, he’ll want me to prove myself first. He might step in anyway, but the degree of how much depends on my response to their attempts.” She shook her head. “Doesn’t help that he has to fight that whole ‘she’s a girl so protect her’ thing that his generation has. But he’s also got Aunt Serafina, who will smack him with a solid wooden cooking spoon if he goes too far in that direction. Sort of a reminder that some girls can take care of themselves.”

“And you can shoot ‘em in the dick from orbit,” Charlie said with a laugh.

“More satisfying to do it face to face when possible, though,” Vicky said.

Enterprise smiled and said, “It looks as if the Slaughterhouse Nine are in Virginia, on what is commonly called the Delmarva Peninsula. They appear to be working their way north, but are apparently avoiding most people right now. Given prior inferences regarding them, I would assume that it is because they do not feel that they have enough escape routes at the moment. They may be heading for Brockton Bay, but I don’t know that for certain.”

“Can you drop a cloaked drone near them, maybe?” Deena asked. “Sorry, Captain. That should come from you.”

“For something like this, the only difference between this and a regular meeting is that we aren’t around a conference table. If you have suggestions or even just jokes, I’m not going to complain.”

“In answer to your question, yes, I can place a drone near them, which will also allow far better scans to be taken of them to know who is there. One thing I would suggest, Captain,” she said, looking directly at Taylor, “is that if any of you go to face them directly, that you let either Deena or myself - via a drone - deal with Jack Slash. He seems to have some capability to talk to other parahumans Shards, which makes him very hard for a parahuman to fight.”

“Which means that if we face directly, Deena should be in a sniper set-up, with us not knowing where she actually is. Probably even better if you send her separately without us knowing.”

Deena shrugged. “Honestly, I’m probably better off not being there at all. Situation like that I’d be terrified. I was okay during the ABB fight, but against the Nine? I’d probably end up in orbit from crapping myself so hard.”

“Agreed. Even if he knows that there are drones around because he’s talking with your powers, he won’t know where they are because I won’t let you know where they are until he’s down.”

“Okay, so let’s work on that being the first one we deal with. Oddly enough, I suspect that - and I can’t believe that I’m about to say this - the Nine will be the easiest of our targets to deal with. Bonesaw in Level Ten confinement so that none of her signals or biologicals can get out - or just leave her in the pattern buffer for long enough for us to prepare everything. A drone for Jack Slash, and whatever else is necessary to deal with the others. Hitting Crawler with a full power phaser rifle blast should deal with him easily enough. I’ll have to be on hand if we’re making it known that drones are being used, because the PRT is a lot more accepting of them being under my control than it is with them being under the control of a non-biological intelligence. Just the way they act makes that clear.”

“What about Siberian?” Vicky asked, worried. “She’s pretty much unkillable. Immovable if she wants, can’t be stopped if she wants, and she’s damaged people like Alexandria before.”

“She is the zebra-striped one, correct?” Enterprise asked. “I am uncertain what the readings I get from her are, but I suspect that she may be a projection of one of the others. I have noticed since I began scanning that there is always a man near or with the group that does not fight alongside them, but is apparently accepted as a member, since he continues to travel with them in some way. He has a subspace connection that Siberian does not. She does, but it seems to be an echo that seems to trace to the man.”

“Do we know what the man looks like?” Taylor asked. Enterprise answered by placing a picture of a slightly disheveled man on the screen.

“He is not always dressed like this - this was taken after the group stopped from a long trip.”

Amy scowled before gasping. “Holy shit, I’ve seen that man’s picture before! That’s William fucking Manton!”

“The same -” Taylor started to ask.

“The man who came up with the explanation. The Manton Effect is named for that man!” Amy said, pointing at the screen.

“Okay,” Taylor finally said. “First we deal with Bonesaw, then Manton, then the others. Probably Jack should be third, because if he can cause problems by talking to other people’s powers, he can probably make them act as much like a well-oiled machine as they are ever going to be. Pattern buffer Bonesaw, then kill Manton and Jack at the same time if possible, and go after the rest.” She snorted. “We know Hatchet-face is a nullifier, so if he thinks that stopping my power will stop the drones, he’ll be a bit surprised. I don’t like it, but we have to go after them with killing intent. And contact Dragon just before the fight starts, so that she can verify to the PRT that what our recordings show is what happened.”

She turned to face them all. “I have to be there physically. I leave it to the rest of you if you want to be Away Team on site or not. Don’t think about whether or not you want me to be there alone, think about whether or not you can honestly see yourself facing the Slaughterhouse Nine. I’m terrified, but know that I’ve got Enterprise to help me out, so that things will be a lot safer for me.”

“That honestly goes for all of us,” Deena said a little shakily. “With Enterprise backing us up, I’ll feel safer. I like the idea of facing him as a team, and it sort of helps you out too, because if the public gets footage of it being just you, that puts you even higher on a pedestal and makes people want to knock you off it. But if it’s a group effort? You don’t come across as quite as dangerous to the public - it took a team effort to bring them down sort of thing.”

“Can Shatterbird’s cry damage the face shields?” Vicky asked. “That’s the most dangerous thing in this entire scenario, as far as I can tell.” She snorted. “And isn’t that a weird thing to say - that I’m more worried about Shatterbird than I am anyone else?”

“Not really that odd,” Charlie said. “That face plate is, after all, covering your face, and if it’s broken the way ‘bird can?”

“I have not had a chance to test it versus her abilities, for obvious reasons, but I do not believe that Shatterbird will be capable of destroying any part of the armor, or even the watches that the armor exudes from.”

“Well, we’ll find out the hard way,” Taylor said. “I intend to go after them as soon as feasible.”

Chapter 73: Tuesday, March 15th, 2011 - Taylor

“You look a little concerned, Taylor,” Chris said at lunch.

“Yeah, got something after school I don’t want to do, but need to. Clearing up a problem or two.”

Chris raised an eyebrow at Amy’s snort. “I take it you know what she needs to do?”

“Yeah, we all had a conversation about it yesterday, figuring out what needed to be done. And she’s right - it’s something that needs to be done, but no one ever looks forward to doing it.”

“If you need a hand with it and it’s something I can lend a hand with, then let me know,” he said.

“I appreciate that, but I think I got it,” Taylor responded. “Too many people involved with it and there’s more trouble keeping everything under control than actually doing it, y’know?”

“Too many cooks sorta thing, right?” She nodded in answer to his question. “Say no more; you’ve clearly got a reason for not being more precise in explaining what it is you need to do.”

“Given how I’ve been getting in the news so much for doing things like going on the Boardwalk to pick up doughnuts? I’d have everyone trying to watch me do it, and then I’m wrangling press instead of getting things done,” she said with a laugh. “You’ve seen how it gets. The Wards are on the Boardwalk and everyone is out, including the press.”

“And so often they’re just trying to get somewhere,” Dennis said. “Still, it looks good for the PRT that the Wards are out talking to the public and not breaking things.”

“No, usually they’re trying to stop other people from breaking things,” Chris said in agreement. “Still, if it looks you need help, let me know and I’ll send Dennis out,” he finished with a grin. Dennis just gave him a sidelong glance with a small amused smile, which made the others at the table chuckle.

When the school day was done, the members of the Away Team all headed up to the ship and got ready. Amusingly, this meant they all stripped to their skin to allow the armor to cover them far better. “Standard Away Team outfits, or knock ‘em dead with the sexy?” Vicky asked with a laugh as she activated the Away Team uniform she used.

“Vicky, you’re sexy enough as it is,” Deena said simply as she activated her own. “You trying to make Jack Slash fall over dead because all the blood in his body decided to visit the head guys aren’t supposed to think with?”

Amy snorted. “Trying to imagine explaining to the police or PRT that Jack died because his dick exploded. The proof would be there, but still, just trying to explain it without giggling madly, if nothing else.”

“We need enough of him still existing to be able to get the bounty on him,” Taylor said with her own snicker. “Preferably the recognizable head.” This drew snickers from the rest. “Enterprise, do we have the Nine in a position currently where we can take them with minimal civilian impact?”

“They are on the road at the moment, William Manton in a white van a mile or so behind the stolen RV they are using. I am gathering from my drones near them that will be stopping soon, and do not currently have any plans for mayhem. Siberian is currently not extant, so if we wished to do something to Mr. Manton, now might be the time to do it.”

“What do you suggest? Grabbing him with a cargo transporter and slipping him in the pattern buffer until we can figure things out?”

“They are currently driving on Route 13, and I find myself slightly amazed that they went through Norfolk, Virginia and across that bridge and tunnel complex. Also somewhat amusing is that the last town they passed through is called Capeville,” Enterprise said, which drew snickers out of the girls. “If we contact Dragon now and simply grab Bonesaw and Manton at the same time, that should throw them off their game for long enough to ‘get the drop on them’, as they say. With Siberian and Bonesaw out of the loop, and Jack being dealt with via other means, the others should be easier to deal with, especially since I suspect that Shatterbird will be unhappy that she can’t shatter the face plates.”

“Remember we’re going for killing shots against them. Crawler may need maximum power, but these people need to be put down. That’s why we’re having Dragon watch our feed as well.”

“Agreed,” came Dragon’s voice over the speakers. “I’m patched in now, and Enterprise zip-squealed what seems to have been decided so far. Bonesaw and Manton, which will apparently remove Siberian from the board somehow? Jack taken down by a cloaked drone, so that no parahuman on site can warn him where the shot is coming from. The others are accepted members of the Nine, that makes them valid targets for execution. And make no mistake, that’s what this is.”

“I’m not happy about it,” Amy said, “but I agree with doctors on this - sometimes you have to injure someone to heal them. Surgery to remove a cancer is an injury to the body, but it helps the patient improve. In this case, society is the patient, and the cancer is the Nine.”

There was agreement around the room. Taylor said, “Hon, find a good place and time and yank the two into the pattern buffers as you put us on the ground.” They armed themselves with phaser rifles and headed to the transporter room. A moment later, the world sparkled around them and they were on the planet, facing a slightly beaten RV. It was useless a moment later as several people almost literally exploded out of the vehicle. Jack started to speak. “Well, if it isn’t the captain of -” He never finished what he was going to say, because a beam hit him square in the chest, and he simply fell over. Shatterbird saw that and headed straight for Taylor, screaming her lungs out. She pulled up short when she realized that none of the Away Team’s helmets had broken in the slightest. A moment later, Deena shot her in the side and she fell like a rag doll to the ground.

“I am detecting an external source trying to affect each of you, and am currently blocking it as best I can. It would be best if you can speed up the resolution, Captain.” She nodded and aimed at Crawler, who was charging toward the group. Ramping the beam up to near disintegration levels, she fired, and he slowed to more accurately live up to his cape name.

“Is that all you got?” he yelled. She upped the power and answered him, firing multiple times amongst his taunting, having to take it amazingly high before he fell and moved no more.

“Is he dead?” she asked Enterprise.

“As best I can tell, yes. His body does not seem to be altering any longer, the way it had been before.”

She growled and said, “Enough of this shit. Wide beam and open fire on the RV and whatever human is in the vicinity. Since Enterprise put us down where it was just us and the Nine, we’re not looking at collateral human damage, and no animal is going to have stuck around with this kind of noise.” With that, they aimed toward the remains of the RV and took out the rest of the team, even the one still inside the vehicle.

Taylor took out a tri-corder after they were done and scanned the area closely. “By my reading, we are the only living beings in the area. We have multiple cooling bodies. Dragon, if you would please contact the PRT and let them know that it is safe to come to the site now?”

“The Washington D.C. team has been waiting for my call, and they are currently lifting off, and if they take half an hour it will be a long time.” They heard her snort her laughter. “Now is the time to go through their pockets and look for loose change.”

Taylor snickered again and said, “As you wish.”

“Love you too, Captain,” Dragon said with a giggle.

The girls actually did set to emptying the pockets of the Nine, finding some wallets and cash on them, but left whatever weapons they might have had alone. They learned that the person who had apparently been trying to Master them was named Cherie Vasil, according to an ID they found on her. “Wonder if she’s any relation to Heartbreaker?” Taylor asked. “Vasil’s not a common surname, and with a Mastery power?” Her body language asked the rest of the question.

“She is one of his powered children. Well, was one of his children,” Dragon said. “What do I tell them about the other two?”

“Well, I’ll need to get up to the Enterprise and deal with them. Manton I’ll …” Taylor stopped and then sighed deeply. “Siberian is a projection of his. We’ve seen how psychotic Siberian is. She fucking sliced Hero in half. Manton dies so that she can’t go on a rampage. I don’t like the idea of summary execution, but if he’s got a projection that bad, then we can’t trust him at all. So I think dropping him back here and shooting him the second he’s solid works.”

Enterprise spoke. “I can make the solidification process take long enough that you can line up to shoot him before he is properly released from it. Or, what might be easier is to simply beam him into space on wide area dispersion, since I doubt that there will ever be a proper way to prove that Manton controlled Siberian, or even that she was a projection of his.”

“Dragon?” Taylor asked. “What’s your take on the matter? The first might give an option for Siberian to come out and destroy before Manton is killed, thereby proving that Siberian is gone, but the second option prevents any damage to anyone or anything.”

Taylor could hear the frown as Dragon responded. “I suspect that the only way that the PRT will admit that Siberian is gone is if we see her disperse. As much as I hate it, we need to bring Manton back to kill him, because you know the moment he’s capable, Siberian will come out.”

“Enterprise? Be prepared to do what we talked about, since I suspect that Siberian will go straight for me, and she was able to cut others in armor in half.” She took a deep breath and then said, “Beam him back down, slowly.”

As the vehicle began to materialize, everyone aimed at it, but Taylor ensured that she was the one in Manton’s sight. The moment that he was released from the beam, a nude black and white woman appeared in front of Taylor, swinging a hand wielded like a claw. She pulled the trigger on the rifle as the blow intersected her.

She awoke on the Enterprise as the transporter beam finished. “She got me with an insta-kill?” she asked the ship. Her answer was for the hologram to appear and engulf her in a tight hug. “There is knowing that what I have planned will work, and actually having to test it. I was terrified that I was going to be ‘brilliantly wrong’ as they say.”

“Well, I’ll need my watch, or I can just transport down nude and take it from my own corpse, since I do not want the PRT getting their hands on that thing.” She tapped behind her ear, activating the communicator. “Away Team? Can one of you retrieve my watch? I don’t want the PRT getting it. I may trust ours mostly, but I don’t know anyone from the other sites.”

There was a babble on the line of the team being extremely glad that she was alive, and Amy finally said, “You scared the ever-living fuck out of me, Taylor! I’m looking at your dead body right now!”

“Hmm, yeah, we should grab that and add it to the data solids, since I’m not in it anymore. I’ll freak out and go through fucktons of therapy over this after I have a chance to sit back and calm down, but we’re still on a mission. Enterprise? Grab my body and do whatever with it. I don’t need it anymore, since I’ve got this one, and this one shouldn’t be from a pattern more than a few minutes old, so we’re good. Pretty good on the memory grab, too. I remember everything up to seeing Siberian swing at me, but don’t remember the actual impact.”

“I didn’t think you’d want that memory to stay. You’ve only lost a handful of seconds.” A new watch appeared in the nearby replicator. “Put that on and I’ll beam you back down to the planet.”

The moment she appeared, the team swarmed her and hugged her furiously. Amy touched helmets with her and sent privately ~Amy: I’m going to kiss you so hard that the others will feel it without me broadcasting it through the network, once we can get out of these outfits.~

~Taylor: Not sure I believe you. Going to need scientific proof on that, love.~ She sent a wave of love and humor to Amy as she ‘said’ it.

About then, three PRT transports landed a short distance away and disgorged an amazing amount of people, who immediately headed to the various bodies. Taylor immediately broke from the group hug to head over to the obvious commander of the team. “Away Team reporting. Dragon was watching this as well, so I assume that she will send her own copy of the data to the PRT so that it can be matched against our version, which is being sent to your agency as soon as you let me know whom should receive it.”

“Captain Jorgenson,” the trooper replied. “Send it to the Director of the Washington, D.C. branch, as well as your own local branch. Dragon will also know who to send hers to as well. So, what happened here?”

“We were scanning for large concentrations of parahumans.” At a raised eyebrow, she said, “In exploring since I first gained access to this technology, I discovered that all parahumans share an odd … connection? Energy? Something that is detectable by my ship’s sensors, although it takes a deep scan to locate a single person as more than ‘somewhere near Virginia’, for example, let alone someplace like Capeville, since that’s the nearest town I’m aware of. It’s sort of like using an infrared camera to locate candles. A single one can be found with some work. The more candles, the easier it is to focus on where that grouping is. Since I’ve got this tech, every group that wants power wants it under their own control, so I scanned for groups, ignoring places that were clearly PRT sources.” She laughed slightly. “Like I’m not going to find parahumans on a Protectorate or Wards site?” Jorgenson snickered as well.

“Anyway, we noticed this grouping here on the peninsula, and weren’t sure what it was. In finding out that it was the Nine - deeper scan of the area to see what was going on, and if it had been something that didn’t need to be worried about, like a Wards camping trip or something, we’d have simply ignored it. But we rather quickly realized that it was the Nine, so we set up plans to deal with them. The only one you won’t find here right now is Bonesaw. She’s on the ship, currently sitting in the pattern buffer, but she’ll be materialized into a room with Level 10 containment. Nothing gets out of that sort of containment that we don’t want released. Even the air is recirculated as necessary. The others were executed as criminals with kill orders, but Bonesaw is a child, or at least appears to be one. I don’t expect it to be possible, but we want to see if she can be rehabilitated at all. I can allow for execution of adults who know full well what they were doing, but it sits wrong with me to just kill a child without making some effort to try and fix what’s wrong. We might still have to kill her, but I think you can understand where I’m coming from on not immediately killing her.”

“Commendable, and completely understood. You’re sure that you can contain her? She’s supposedly got some pretty ugly pathogens she can release.”

“And if she’s an acolyte of Jack Slash, probably got a ton of crap in her own body to release if she thinks she’s going to lose. So we’re probably going to rematerialize her and knock her out in the process, then remove everything foreign from her. I’ve no problem with having at least Dragon nearby when it happens, to verify that what we’re saying that we’re doing is actually what’s being done. Just for safety reasons, I’d prefer that the number of watchers be fairly low, in the almost impossibly unlikely event that something does manage to be released. What can be removed without Elixir’s help - Panacea was her New Wave name, in case that name change hasn’t made it everywhere yet - will be done within Level 10 containment by a holographic doctor patterned after Leonard McCoy, so the worst we’ll get out of that is good old Georgia doctor curses about what the girl did to herself. Since you can’t infect a hologram with a literal virus or bacteria, that’ll be safe. And those spider-bots of hers are not known for their extreme programming, so I doubt a computer virus is likely either. Once Bones is done with what he can do, then and only then will Elixir enter the picture and only one hand will be exposed while she clears up what Bones couldn’t. After she’s clean, we then see what can be done about the girl mentally. We haven’t looked into whether or not it’s possible to erase a person’s memories completely, because if it is, that’s likely the route we’ll go, and have her raised as a normal child. Well, a normal parahuman child.”

“I’ll run that past my superiors, but I can’t see any problems with that,” Jorgenson said. “I assume that you can be reached through channels via the Brockton Bay PRT?”

“Dragon can also reach us, so you can have her reach out as well.”

With that, they led through the entire encounter, which surprised the PRT troops regarding its brevity. “Remember that we’re using technology at a level more powerful than most parahumans are prepared for,” Taylor said. “And we didn’t know what would happen with Crawler, given his tendency to shrug things off. I was afraid we were going to have to try to beam him into space, throwing him toward the sun or something. As it was, it took a power level that disintegrates most other things to finally kill him.” She looked at his body. “At least I hope he’s dead and not just slowly recovering from that.”

“He’s not an irresistible force nor capable of creating one, so entombing him in concrete or something harder should keep him even if he’s still alive,” Jorgenson said. “Sounds like you did something I’m honestly supposed to admonish you for, but it was the Slaughterhouse Nine.”

“And that’s the only reason we walked into this with killing intent,” Taylor said. “The Nine was not known for kindness of any sort. Any other group we shoot to stun unless they state that they aren’t stopping without a death happening. In that case - well, if it’s them or me, I hope you can understand if I choose me?” She got a nod from the nearby troops who were, as the phrase goes, ‘bagging and tagging’ the Nine.

Chapter 74: Tuesday, March 15th, 2011 - Taylor

“Before we go anywhere,” Taylor said once they were back aboard the ship, “Enterprise, do we have any information on erasing people memories, as in completely erasing them rather than suppressing them?”

“There have been instances in the past. Nomad seemed to be the first the Federation encountered, but that device simply scrambled the connections to the pathways, which was why it was so easy to return Nyota Uhura to herself so quickly. As for actual erasure, it is likely that the only way to do that will be something that Amy is going to be extremely uncomfortable with.”

Amy looked at Enterprise for a moment before understanding, and blanched at the thought. A few moments of thought had her cock her head, however. “Huh,” she finally said. “The problem I have with doing brains is exactly the reason that we want this done in this instance. I am terrified of making someone not who they once were. But we don’t want Bonesaw around in any way, shape, or form. Working on her brain specifically to cause the removal of her current personality would work for me in an instance like this. But only with something like this. I only brushed past the brain, so to speak, when doing the work on you guys to enhance you in the manner that was listed in the Federation databanks. I changed the material and not the substance, if that phrasing makes sense to any of you.”

Sherrel spoke up. “You did the equivalent of switching out old aluminum wiring for copper wiring, but followed the old paths through the house, right?”

“Exactly!” Amy said, smiling.

“So it sounds like we need to get Dragon on board in some way or another and have her record while we work on Bonesaw.”

“If you can wait roughly an hour, I can have one of my bodies ready for transport to the ship,” Dragon said over the speakers. “Enterprise has kept me in the loop regarding this. If we are completely erasing Bonesaw’s mind, then it might be a worthwhile thing for us to go the full route and alter her appearance and create a new identity, and tell the PRT that we were forced to kill the last member of the Nine. I would prefer that there be some in the know as to what truly happened, if only because having a girl show up with the same powers as Bonesaw, but clearly not Bonesaw? People will figure that out. But with the PRT on board, we can come up with a somewhat more solid explanation.”

“I’ve no problems with that,” Taylor said. “Most likely bring the Chief Director and at least some of the Brockton Bay people, such as Director Piggot and whomever she feels most needs to know.” She paused before saying, “So roughly an hour before we pull her from the buffer and ensure she’s unconscious as Bones removes everything he can under Level 10 confinement.”

“Holodeck,” Sherrel said. “Do the surgery on a holodeck, in case she’s got something that allows her to wake up. If she’s in Sickbay, she might be able to Tinker something with the equipment around, but if everything is generated on the deck, if she gets her hands on something, it can simply be derezzed.”

“That sounds like an excellent idea,” Dragon said. “I shall contact you in roughly fifty minutes. Enterprise will keep me apprised, but I need concentration on some of what I’m doing right now.”

“Understood. See you in about an hour,” Taylor said. When the call ended, she asked, “Is there a method of sending her directly to sleep as soon as she comes out of materialization?”

“Given the modifications that I detected when transporting her, nothing that I can say will work with one hundred percent efficiency, unfortunately. What I can attempt to do is to stimulate the brain into a sleep state the moment she solidifies. Taylor, at that point you should probably see if you can manage to talk to her Shard, so see how much of a fight it will put up, if any.”

“Can I do that without your help?” she asked.

“I don’t see why you can’t. Your Shard particularly is designed for contact and administration of other Shards. It would make sense that you wouldn’t need my help to talk to it.”

“Huh, I never thought of it that way. Might have to do some experiments to see if I can talk to Shards that we haven’t networked ourselves to. Sort of do what Jack Slash did, just from the side of the angels. And for me, it would definitely be a conscious thing. From what I’ve read, I think it was unconscious for Jack.”

“How long do we have until we have to bring Bonesaw out of the pattern buffer?” Amy asked.

“I can safely keep her in there at this point for long enough that you and those you care about would begin serious consideration of having children. I have both the power and resources to keep her pattern stable for years.”

“Considering it even now,” Vicky said. “I just can’t wait until we’re at a point that I can see what a cross between Amy and Taylor looks like. Whether male or female, they’d probably be so cute they’d get an automatic Master rating of YES.” Taylor blushed furiously at that, but looked at Amy with a soft smile at the concept. Vicky continued. “Honestly, I think that children from any of us are going to be dangerously cute, what with Amy likely being our preferred doctor.”

“Yes! I shall rule the world through the power of uber-cute!” Amy said, thrusting a hand into the air with a pointing finger. She was also giggling madly at the idea.

The remainder of the time waiting for Dragon to arrive was spent in various conversations, and then Dragon walked into the room they were talking in. “I’m a little surprised that you’re all not a little more nervous,” she said.

“Not much we can do,” Vicky said. “Nothing for me to punch unless I want to have Enterprise make me a range to practice hitting things on, and ever since she started numbing that signal - numbing isn’t the word I want but I think you know what I mean - I’ve been less likely to cause collateral damage these days. Maybe by the time I’m twenty-five I’ll have lost that nickname.”

“Enterprise, lead us to the holodeck you think would be best to use, and then set it up, please?” She appeared and led them deeper into the ship to an open door. Once inside, a force field shimmered into place, followed by the side that would contain Bonesaw starting to glow slightly before the familiar transporter effect came into being as a Sickbay also formed. A girl in what Taylor thought of as a blood-covered ‘Alice dress’, for Alice in Wonderland, shimmered into view and was immediately wobbly on her feet, although she seemed to be fighting going to sleep. The glow intensified and as the girl started to fall, a small tractor beam caught her and placed her on the bed. It was at that point that Bones appeared. Her clothes were rapidly removed by the ships other holograms, which disappeared with the clothing as soon as they were done.

“I’m going to see if I can talk to her Shard, okay?” Taylor said. “I’ve got what seems to be called ‘Queen Administrator’, so I should be able to.” She shrugged and tried.

~Taylor: [Query]~

^Data. Query^

~Taylor: I am the host who has the Queen Administrator Shard, and we need to do something to your host. We need to find out your view of what we wish to do, so we need to know what you do for your host, and whether the methods by which she uses you are required.~

^…Data^

~Taylor: Okay, you’re called Chirurgeon in our language. You allow your host to make changes to people through the application of force, if you will. Something we would call surgery. You can’t simply change the body, it needs to be manipulated in some manner. In our species, your manipulations cause pain. Is this a requirement for your usage?~

^Data. Explanation. Data^

~Taylor: Ah. So the reason the host that we call Bonesaw causes pain is due to the manner in which she Triggered, and you thought that she had an understanding of our species nature, and that was how best to learn. Were we to erase her current memory and give her a new chance to grow up, as we refer to the process of mental aging, would you insist on the usage of pain as your indicator of whether or not something she is doing is successful? Given that I and others will be able to talk to you, we can help you find other indicators if you are willing.~

^Query^

~Taylor: The process will not disconnect you from your current host. If we are incapable of making her safe to be around our species, then we will be forced to sever your connection from our side. While this would bother you, what information I have states that it should not harm you, although your host would no longer be alive. We wish greatly to prevent this outcome. We wish your host to survive and have a long life free of past trauma.~

^Affirmative^

~Taylor: Perhaps we can work together to find new ways for you to learn what you desire that do not cause our species pain, because causing pain tends to make our species not wish to do the thing that causes it, and those who enjoy causing it are generally not accepted by society. If we can find non-painful methods for you to learn, society is far more likely to allow your host to experiment.~

^Query^

~Taylor: I can’t promise that the acceptance will be immediate, but I strongly suspect that it will allow access to far greater sources of information than you previously had.~

^Acceptance^

Taylor came out of her communion with Chirugeon and said, “Her Shard shouldn’t give us any issues, now that I’ve explained things. Like all of them, it wants data, and I mentioned that if we couldn’t fix things so that she can function in society, the amount and quality of the data was going to be minimal. And perhaps we can find other things to judge success off rather than pain.

Bones, in the meanwhile, was doing a running monologue of all the things he was finding in Bonesaw’s system. She looked no older than eight, but was actually only slightly younger than Missy, by no more than a few months. In Bonesaw’s case, all of the quick and dirty surgery she had done to herself to make herself tougher had also stunted her growth and effectively stopped puberty for her. He was grumbling about the pockets of disease he kept finding, but admitted that the methods she seemed to have set up to release them was ingenious. “By the way,” he said in that southern drawl of his, “due to the pathogens I’m findin’, the temperature on this side of the force field is a little dangerous for you guys. I’m not quite cookin’ the poor girl, but her pathogens are findin’ it a mite hard to survive for long. Hot enough down here, but they’re getting pulled to the ceilin’, which is hot enough to kill anything biological.”

It took him close to three hours to clear her of all her sneaky little traps, and even though he was tied in to the ship’s systems, still took the time to scan the area and Bonesaw to ensure that she was free of any and all diseases. “I’ll be lowering the temps in here now,” he said once he had verified, “and then our future Chief Medical Officer can come in and do the things that she can do faster’n me. Gonna need a bit of biological material to properly fix her up, because she’s got some interesting things in her body. Armor and weapons that aren’t biological, and those need to come out.”

Enterprise spoke up. “I’m going to weaken the field directly in front of you when we’re ready, and tell only you. Make sure your armor is fully on. Level 10 is remaining in effect until we have verified that she is safe to be around other people.”

Amy’s suit shot back onto her body in a much more solid form that she was wearing a short time ago, opaque face mask and all. A couple minutes later she stepped forward and the force field shimmered around her. Her armor unfolded only around her hand, and she reached out to touch the girl. “Nicely done, Bones,” she said. “I’ll get rid of some of the scars that surgery leaves behind, but only after I’ve pulled out all the non-organic stuff. I’ll be resetting her back to baseline human, and only after we’ve had a chance to re-educate her will I think about doing all the upgrades I’ve been doing to you guys. I’ll warn you that I’m likely to be fairly quiet during this, so don’t expect me to go all chatterbox. I’ll describe to Enterprise what I’m doing so that she can make sure that Dragon has a recording for the PRT and Guild, but I can’t promise that it’ll be loud enough for you guys to hear.” With that, she began to do her own work on the girl once known as Bonesaw. She spoke more as if talking to herself from that point on. “Okay, the first thing is to simply - Enterprise, can we tell where some of the learned things are stored? Like eating and bathroom training? Because not having to teach a twelve year old those things will make things easier.”

“Unfortunately no, but I suspect that you will find it something hard to erase, since it has had years of training to be pushed to an almost autonomic situation. We shall see, however.”

“Yes, we shall. Erase Riley-slash-Bonesaw back to being a blank slate, and then work on converting what biological stuff she has to make up for what she’s lost. Get rid of the non-biological stuff she inserted to perform some task or other, and then turn her puberty back on and rebuild her to what she should look like at twelve and a half.” With that, she began to work, and things were quiet for about an hour or so. Enterprise turned the side with Dragon and the rest of the Away Team into something of a waiting room that they could do card games and such in while Amy worked.

It took her ninety minutes before she was willing to consider herself done. She had taken it upon herself to alter the girl’s appearance, to make it harder for anyone to connect her to Bonesaw ever again, and given that she now had copper hair and freckles - and since she was now of an age to show so, the hair color was natural - no one was likely to ever mistake her for having been Bonesaw. The work completed, she was covered with a sheet and allowed to slip into normal sleep, especially after Amy ensured that she would sleep. A scan ran through the room and the watched the force field drop. “We now get to have Enterprise teach her as best she can, and we try to socialize the new girl.”

“This is being sent ‘Eyes Only’ to the Chief Director and to Director Piggot. Those two can decide who else needs to know this information.”

Chapter 75: Tuesday, March 15th, 2011 - Amy

When she rejoined them after finishing with Bonesaw, Amy put her hand on Taylor’s skin, but she also put a hand on Vicky, who was sitting next to Taylor. She smiled after a few seconds, because she’d been reading their vitals. “Well, one good thing,” she said. “I suspect that she’s still got some of the stuff we didn’t really want to have to reteach her - like bathroom training - because I was detecting that she was processing language while you guys spoke, but I couldn’t tell if she was understanding it. That’s why I touched Taylor and Vicky here. I know these two understand what you others are saying, so I suspect that while she’ll have no real other knowledge, I’m fairly certain that she’ll at least have enough English to be able to be taught more easily. If not, the Kirk Enterprise was capable of teaching Uhura her languages again, so I suspect that it’ll be even easier for this Enterprise to do so.”

“If it looks as if she’s fine,” Enterprise said, “I may teach her other languages as well if she so desires. In fact, I can begin that for all of you if you so choose. Let me know the languages you desire and I can teach them to you.”

“If Vulcan doesn’t have any telepathic components to it,” Charlie said, “I think that all of us learning it could be an interesting choice to be able to have a conversation that no one around us will be able to decipher until they also learn Vulcan.”

“I like the way you think,’ Taylor said. “So Vulcan for me, and I think the languages I’m most likely to want to use when dealing with other companies and countries - French and Russian for certain. I know we can use the universal translator functions, which I guarantee will come in handy when someone decides to talk about us in their native language, but to actually have the language itself? I want that.”

“I can begin teaching the languages you desire tonight. I will start with one and continue until you are fluent in it before I pause for a short time and start the next language. If I don’t do it that way, you could end up speaking a rather intriguing amalgam of Vulcan and Russian, for example.”

“Let’s start with Vulcan, then,” Taylor said. “The sooner our group has a language that’s just for us, we’re good.”

Amy walked over to Taylor and said, “I promised you something a little while ago, and I think it’s time I made good on that promise.” With that she pulled Taylor to her feet and proceeded to Kiss her. She poured everything she was into the kiss, telling her how much seeing her body had hurt; how much she felt love for the girl; and more than a little arousal as well, along with so many other emotions that she could even begin to put a name to.

When she released her, they noticed that all of the girls were fanning themselves, and even Dragon quipped, “I needed to turn my fans on to full power from watching that kiss.”

Amy just hugged Taylor and said, “I told her I was going to kiss her like that when I saw her next.”

“How did you survive that attack?” Dragon said.

“Via a method that we’ve talked about before but I intend to use sparingly. Enterprise has such a connection to me that she has my engrams at all times. We’d also beamed down just minutes before. So when Siberian took that swing at me, the moment my vitals flat-lined, she … well, in one sense of the term, I’m a clone now, and the original Taylor is dead. But since that body no longer exists and I’m here with all the expected memories - Enterprise didn’t let me keep the actual strike, so I only lost a second or two’s worth of memory. And despite what some might think, this doesn’t disprove the existence of a soul, since this had been planned for just such an occasion. So if the soul exists, it knew that I’d be back seconds later and never bothered to leave the area, so to speak. At no point was I at a point where metaphysically I might be considered dead. To be honest, the brain was probably still working in the body I left behind for a minute or two after she struck me.” She shrugged. “I’ll probably wake up screaming some morning, or go through some existential crisis at some point, but as far as I’m concerned right now, I’m me. I’m still that sexy thing that woke up this morning.”

“Well, with the drone footage, I think that I’ll say that your medical technology is beyond anything we’ve seen before, because telling them the truth will open gates I don’t want to see opened,” Dragon said. “You know that there would be nations that would try to mandate you doing exactly that to allow ‘important people’ to be healed to peak health and youth.”

“Exactly. It’s part of why I’m hoping I never need to use it again. I intend to live as long a life as I can manage, be it another twenty years or two hundred and fifty, what with Amy’s capabilities. But I have no intention of being this woman who’s young and sexy and can legitimately say, ‘I remember back before the sun ate my birth planet when it went red giant.’ Unless nature somehow allows me to get that old. I’m no Ronald Tracy, working toward immortality. God knows that I love the idea of sticking around to see what’s next, but I’m not going to go crazy trying to make sure that it happens.” Amy snickered when Taylor added, “And there’s that damned soapbox again,” giggling.

Dragon turned to Amy. “Enterprise and I have been working on what would be necessary to build me a more human body, and we think that we have a great deal of what is needed done, at least in theory. ‘On paper’, one might say. None of the physical work has been done yet. When we are ready, would you be willing to help create my human body? I have no idea why it was preserved, but I have Andrew Richter’s DNA profile stored. I would simply need to figure out who I would prefer my ‘mother’ to be, as it were.”

“Need help figuring out who you want it to be?” Taylor asked.

Dragon’s entire body language screamed ‘embarrassment’ to Amy, and she suddenly had an idea of whom Dragon was contemplating asking, and failed to suppress a giggle.

“I suspect that Amy has figured out the identity of the person I was considering asking.” Amy was amused by the very human movement of embarrassment from Dragon of rubbing the back of her neck as she said, “Captain Hebert, it was your ship that permitted me the freedom that I have wanted for so long.
