I would ask her, but she has based her appearance on your genetics. Would you permit me to base the female genetics of my human body off you?”

Taylor jerked slightly in surprise, and Amy wondered how she had not seen that coming. It was clearly not an unwelcome surprise, because she smiled brightly. “You’ll want to change the hair color to a more coppery look, but I would be honored, Dragon. If you go the copper-haired look, we can say that Enterprise is your mother, at least amongst those of us in the know about this. Maybe even go with very slightly pointed ears?”

Amy added, “And go with part of the reason you chose Dragon being that you have very mildly draconic features? Maybe little horns? Sharper teeth than normal? Not into Case 53 levels, but a minor physical change from your ‘human baseline’ when you Triggered.”

“Might even be used as part of the explanation for your anthropophobia,” Vicky said. “The physical changes made you worry how you’d be treated, and being able to make suits like you have … well, I think you can see where I’m going with this.”

Dragon was nodding. “It would work. Since I was hoping to get Amy to build my body, she should be part of the design process, I think. If for no other reason than being able to say how difficult it might be to do a given idea.” She smiled. “Plus, I think she needs someone to sort of guide her. I was running Riley Davis’s new appearance through some scans and realized that Amy made her look very much as if she is the daughter of both her and Taylor.”

Amy couldn’t help but blush furiously at that. “I need to change that,” she said. “I think some wishful thinking crept in while I was working.”

Taylor said, “Have to admit that if her genetics are a mix of yours and mine, we’re gonna have some damned good looking kids.”

“Not all of it. I left a lot of her genes alone, but changed the ones that tend to regulate appearance. People might assume she’s related, but genetically she’s not. Well, she’d probably register as a distant relative to us.”

“Still, we’re gonna have to keep an eye on any kids we have, Amy.” She looked around the room. “Honestly, if I have children by any of you, we’ll have the same problem. At this point, we’re all very good looking. A cross between me and Amy? Adorable? Me and Sherrel? Depending whose genes control the figure, we’ll figure out then how heavy a bat she’ll have to carry. Can honestly say that about any of you.”

Dragon spoke up. “If it turns out that Jack Slash was the one to have created Bonesaw, and it’s not a side effect of her power -”

“It didn’t seem to be when I talked to it,” Taylor told her. “It seemed interested in what I had to say about things, and seemed at least intrigued about using things other than pain as a measure of how to understand the things she was doing.”

“Excellent. What I’m thinking is that if she turns out to be a stable person after she’s re-educated, it might be a good idea to have her be a distant relative to one or both of you. Not necessarily so close that one of you has to take her in as family, but certainly as an explanation of what she’s doing in Brockton Bay, if that’s where she ends up settling.”

“We’ll also have to see about changing her name completely. We’ll have the issue no matter what of her eventually wanting to know who she was before we ended up dealing with her. With that appearance, perhaps giving her an Irish or Scottish name? Maybe training her up with an accent? The more we can disassociate this new girl with Riley Davis, the better in my mind at least.”

“What sort of name are you thinking?” Amy asked, curious the direction Taylor’s mind was going.

Taylor paused for a moment before saying, “Maybe something like Aisling.” She pronounced it ASH-lyeen, with a decent Irish intonation to it. “Means something like ‘dream’ or ‘vision’ from the sources I’m able to find. I just think it’s a kind of pretty name, and something a little different from the standard Colleens and Bridgets you’re likely to hear, and to be honest, I suspect that people who might even try to suspect that she was a ‘redesign’, if that somehow happened, would tend toward the more obvious names.” She shrugged. “Just my thought on it.”

“And the more you can make it a name to be happy with and about, the easier it will be to help keep her from slipping back when she eventually discovers the truth of her history,” Amy said. “Because you know that will happen, one way or another. It’s the way the universe seems to work.”

“True, and since I’m certain I’m going to end up at least mentoring her, if not someone finding a way for me to somehow adopt her - I’m fifteen and she’s twelve, so she sure as hell can’t be my kid - it’s best if I start thinking in that direction in the first place, right?”

“Considering you’re already trying to work out what’s best for her even before the re-education has begun?” Dragon asked. “Of course you’re going to likely be involved in some way, unless you specifically request otherwise.”

“No, it was my insistence that we keep her alive because I didn’t want the death of a child on my conscience. If I altered her fate that much, then I can’t abrogate my responsibility to do whatever I can to ensure that she has as good a new upbringing as I can.”

There was silence for a short time before Amy simply said, “And that’s why we all trust you. Because you say things like that and mean them.”

Chapter 76: Thursday, March 17th, 2011 - Taylor

It was a little before lunch and Taylor suddenly had a thought about something from Tuesday, and contacted Enterprise sub-vocally. “Love? I think I was rude to Dragon on Tuesday. Would you please contact her through channels and let her know that I wish to speak with her? If she’s angry or hurt, I can appreciate that and will not push, but I want to apologize for what I think I did.”

“May I know what your ‘crime’ was, so that I can let her know what the issue is?”

Taylor sighed softly. “The conversation regarding her eventual genetics. I think I blew past that faster than it deserved. We sort of mentioned it and then were talking about something else, as if I was bothered by it or something. It’s exactly the opposite, in fact.”

“I believe I understand. I shall contact her and let her know that you’re about to go to lunch at your school, if she wishes to talk to you soonest, otherwise she should wait until after school.”

“Thank you, love. All of you mean far more to me than I can say - even Dragon, even if I haven’t known her too long - and offending one of you is the last thing I want.”

The bell went off and they all headed to lunch. Taylor knew the moment that the communications field dropped, because there was a quick susurration, and then utter silence. As people read the news - which Enterprise had already warned her about - people started to look in her direction. “I’m guessing that the news about the Nine has finally made it to the news people,” she said blandly. What she found amusing was that you could accidentally tell who in school might be on the Away Team, because Amy. Vicky, Deena, and Charlie were all simply eating their lunches, rather than sitting looking at them the way the rest of the lunch room was.

“I’m … guessing that was the ‘problem’ you needed to clear up?” Chris asked, his voice a little faint.

“Yes, and it wasn’t phrased that way because it was a walk in the park. I was injured very severely by Siberian - one could say ‘unto death’, even - and it was only Federation technology that saved my life. But if I’d blandly said, ‘Yeah, I’m distracted because we’re going to surprise attack the Nine later today,’ I guarantee that you would not have reacted blandly to the news.”

Dean spoke up. “That’s … a fair statement. But damn, you were so blasé about it.”

“That’s because I was trying like mad to not explode from fear,” she said. “It was the fucking Nine! The only reason we stood a chance against them was a cloaked drone that Jack couldn’t get any info from, and a blazing fast attack before they could get ready. As it was, it turns out that even Federation armor can’t withstand Siberian’s claws. Luckily, with her projector dead, she won’t be back ever again.”

“I’d be a gibbering mess if I’d somehow survived a slash from Siberian. She fucking cut Hero in half when I was five or so,” Dennis said with a shudder. “And here you are two days later, eating lunch like it ain’t no thang.” He stood and saluted her, and she was surprised there was no mocking in the salute.

She returned it from the seated position before saying, “Sit down, you nut,” with a smile. “And thank you for that. I do understand what you’re saying.” She could hear and see that the rest of the school wanted to come over and talk to her, and she knew that she’d probably be swamped by thank yous and such as soon as she left school for the day.

Carlos said, “I’m suspecting that the news explains why our various internships have decided that we need to come to the office to have an emergency conference. This sort of thing changes a lot for a lot of businesses, if you think about it.”

“What will the insurance companies use as an excuse to raise their premiums again?” Vicky asked snidely. “The Nine was their usual fall-back reasoning.”

“They’ll find one,” Amy said with an equal tone. “Trust me, they’ll work hard to find one. From their point of view, they at least still have two Endbringers to blame.”

Enterprise spoke in her ear. “Feel free to contact Dragon when school is done. She looks forward to your call.” Taylor bit her lip very slightly and nodded..

“Enterprise tell you something?” Vicky asked.

“Yeah. I need to talk to Dragon later, because I think I brushed off a query she made when she was verifying that Bonesaw was no longer a problem. I need to apologize for that, because I didn’t intend to basically ignore her.”

“Horrors,” Deena said, “the captain of the ship, overseeing a procedure being done on her watch on her ship, might have glossed past a question. Was the question part of the procedure you were watching?”

“No,” Taylor said.

“Then I suspect that not only should you not worry, but I also suspect that Dragon will chuckle when she hears you’re worried about offending her.”

“I find it somewhat amusing that you talk about contacting Dragon so simply,” Dean said with a laugh. “As if any of the rest of us can simply call her up and talk to her.”

“Well, I have the in, if you will, that we are doing business together, with her leasing several of my patents in order to make so much money for both of us that it would make Han Solo look at it and go ‘DAYUM!’” Taylor couldn’t say that with a straight face, though, and started laughing as she finished. “Seriously, though, I’ve dealt with her mainly in business, and when I had to do stuff that the PRT needed to know about.”

“It does say a lot of good about you, though,” Chris said, “that you’re worried that you might have offended her.”

“But to be honest, I’ll probably get her answering service, who will have her call me back. It’s not like I have a direct line to her.” Her phone chirped at her, so she pulled it out and looked at it, then face-palmed. “And my ship apparently just put her direct line on my phone, since we’ll be doing business together.” She just shook her head and started to chuckle softly, then set to finishing her lunch.

When school was finished for the day, she headed to the ship and called Dragon, who answered immediately. “Taylor, I apologize if I gave you any impression -”

“Dragon, it was me,” Taylor interrupted. “I thought about the conversation, where you asked if it was alright to use my DNA as mother, so to speak, and it seemed like we moved away from the conversation very quickly, and I was afraid that you might take it wrong. When you decide it’s time to build a human body, I would actually be honored if you used my DNA.” She thought for a moment. “I may look and see if there’s any of Mom’s stuff around that might still have something viable, like a hairbrush or something. It’s been about three years, so who knows. Then you could use hers if you want, and we could secretly be sisters, if something like that would appeal to you.”

There was silence on the line for a long moment, and Taylor was afraid that she had offended Dragon. She opened her mouth to speak, but Dragon spoke first. “You … you wouldn’t complain about having me as a sister?”

“No. I need to ask Dad about it, because he might have an issue, but I suspect he’ll have no problems with it either. It would be our secret, because we couldn’t really explain how Mom had you, but I would be proud to privately call you my sister. Or my daughter, if Dad says no to Mom being your mother as well.”

“I appreciate your decision. We’re not ready yet, because I’ll need to test the hell out of the transfer into the body, and still being able to interface with my current technology. Plus slipping whatever we can into folded space with my technology. But I appreciate whichever route you decide to go with this.”

Taylor responded with, “One thing, Dragon. If you absolutely want me as your mother, then I will make sure that Amy has scans right now. I just offered the possibility of my mother’s DNA in case you wanted another option, but still wanted the connection to me. Even if I couldn’t tell anyone but a very small set of people, I would be ridiculously proud to know that you were my daughter, even if nothing I’ve done gives me any right to be proud of it.”

Dragon laughed. “We’ll see. We might end up with you as the default simply because there’s nothing around your house with usable DNA from her. As you said, it’s been about three years. But I appreciate the extra option as well.” She snickered over the line. “One of the things that makes me think that even if I decide on your mother’s DNA if it’s an option, I might still privately call you ‘Mom’.”

Taylor sniffled at that. “And I would definitely be honored to be considered as such, as I’ve said.” After a moment she added, “A silly thought came to mind that we’ve got some time to think about, as you’ve said, for various reasons. We’re making the girl formerly known as Riley into a distant relative of mine. Maybe the two of you could be vaguely related, and how I discovered her existence? Spit-balling here, so no need to actually contemplate any of this if you don’t want to, but you could say that you were doing some research and discovered our connection, but that led you to other avenues and found her as well, as the only survivor of something or other.” She shrugged, even though she knew Dragon couldn’t see her. “As I say, it’s just a quick off the cuff thought that may go nowhere or may be a very bad idea. Just thought I’d toss it out there to let someone far better at this sort of thing work out connections.”

“I’ll work through the ramifications and logistics of something like that. It might work especially well if both of us end up coming into your life physically at roughly the same time, although I could see the concept of one showing up, which allows for the explanation of looking for other missing family members and finding the other one of us. As I say, I’ll set some processes up to work on the concept to see what works best.” After a pause, Dragon added with an audible grin, “Mom.”

Taylor laughed. “Just be careful, daughter,” she replied. “Your mental well-being is important as well as your physical, and I don’t want you rushing into this, okay?”

She couldn’t help but laugh when Dragon replied in a laughing petulant voice, “Mo-o-om!”

Chapter 77: Saturday, March 19th, 2011 - Taylor

“Captain?” Enterprise said as she sat in her ready room, working through carious things, not the least of which was paperwork for some of the various degrees that she was capable of going for. She needed some required classes for each of them, but she was likely to end up with multiple PhDs when she was done. Homework, of course, was always important.

“Yes? What’s up?” Taylor asked, putting the pen down and stretching her fingers a little.

“Two things, amusingly enough both having a connection to Dragon, although amazingly dissimilar in content. The first is that I’ve scanned the house, and it appears that there may be some of your mother’s DNA in a form that would allow a proper scan for her genetics. This means that you’ll need to talk to your father about the situation with Dragon.”

“Okay, I’ll deal with that sometime soon, maybe even today. What’s the second thing?”

“This comes from Dragon, who reports that Nikos Vasil’s compound has been raided, and that the man has been taken into custody. What Dragon told me privately is that he will be ‘accidentally’ placed aboard a transport that has missed some scheduled maintenance and that will undergo catastrophic failure en route to international court. She has gotten me some of his genetic material, so I have cloned various … viscera, shall we say … to be found as necessary on the off chance that someone actually finds the remains of the transport. But the attempt is being made to hide his death, because it is known that he has plans in place to bring down as many governments as he had people under his control, which he did and made known in order to prevent kill squads from coming after him. In discovering the wording of his command, we have this opening, because it requires the verified death of Heartbreaker by mischance, and not due to something such as natural causes. This was to allow that he might need to go on the run and be out of contact with people for a time. So he is simply going to ‘vanish’, and we will hope for the best.”

She sat back in her chair and thought for a moment. “I can’t complain. He’s another one who needs - needed? - to die, and I likely would have killed him from a distance if given the chance. I’m just sad that the necessity is there in the first place for so many different idiots out there. I know we’re going to have to kill Bastard Son, but maybe we can make the point to the rest of the Elite that they really don’t want to mess with us.”

“Well, they’re going to be gunning for regaining power, because a not-insignificant portion of their funding was tied up in illegal activities, and … well, you own that money now through various means that even Dragon would have trouble tracing. So they’ve lost some power in the markets, and they need something big. They’re already making a few mistakes that are just barely avoiding the courts due to … gifts … given to various individuals. So expect a big push when they make their move. I’m surprised that they haven’t already.”

“In other news, I think that I've located the main Mathers compound, and it appears that Christine Mathers, AKA Mama Mathers, is on site. Shall I send a few drones in and deal with the ones that are there, and only after their parahumans are dealt with contact the authorities?”

“This will still leave the ones on their way here coming, correct?”

“Yes, but it will be much harder for them to coordinate with Mama out of the picture.”

“Then do it. And don’t worry too much about keeping them alive. Dealing with Masters like Mama Mathers is so much of a pain, and those hints about how much of a Master she is? Perhaps it’s cruel and heartless of me, but I’m damned if I’m going to make everybody’s life harder by trying to keep her alive so that she can continually try to Master people to let her out to continue ‘her holy crusade’. We’ll still have the ones who show up here to try to get me, via directly or through control of someone else to get me to come forward, but for those that require skin contact? That’s what force fields are for.”

She sat back in her chair. “So, the Nine aren’t an issue anymore, and the same goes for Heartbreaker. The local assholes are dealt with, and they’ve managed to keep them contained, which is a bit of a surprise. You haven’t given me warnings about groups like Gesselschaft or the Herren clan, but in both cases there, they really connect via the Empire as far as Brockton Bay is concerned, and right now, I can’t be gallivanting off trying to fix the entire world’s problems. Let me stick with local and business stuff. This is going to bring the ones who want to control me or you out of the woodwork coming here, like Butcher and The Elite. One is dealing with them more on a business level, and the other is figuring out how to deal with the damned insane person without becoming the next host for the personality. The Fallen are going to be far less of a problem shortly, from what you’re telling me. Let me know what you’re doing, and then patch me through to the authorities when you contact them, because we need that protection for you. Yeah, I seem like a big ol’ badass by being there supposedly having taken them out, but they’re just too damned dangerous otherwise. What about the McVeays and the Crowleys? Are we dealing with them as well?”

“I figure that would be best.”

“And it reminds the world just how much I can control, because I could do the entire attack with a fuckton of drones at all three sites at the same time. When they end up asking me about it, I simply remind them of that. That I can do everything aboard you that doesn’t require a physical presence to Do A Thing.”

“Agreed. In other news, I had word from yesterday that Emma Barnes has also been convicted, and will be sentenced at the beginning of May, much like Sophia Hess will be. There was an attempt at a diminished capacity plea, but there was just too much in the history of the case that showed planning on her part. If either of them were to get diminished capacity, it would have been Sophia Hess.”

“So now we see how the world turns. The PRT will find a way to keep control of Sophia and place her somewhere else, because she’s not Birdcage material, but putting her in the general population? They need a prison of some sort to hold parahumans, and to be honest, they’re more likely to place her at Gary or Ellisburg.”

She shrugged. “I find that as far as Emma is concerned, I just … I used to care, and wonder where the girl I knew went, but I’ve got too much too worry about now. Let her go wherever they send her and deal with whatever punishment they give her. I suspect that mandated therapy is going to be a part of it, even if she’s not getting a psych verdict. And it’s better for her this way, without the psych verdict. With the one she got she gets X amount of time, and gets released at the end, or earlier for good behavior if she manages that. With a psych verdict, they keep the prisoner until they feel safe releasing her to the public. So they might want a five year sentence, for example, and normally the person gets out after five years. With a psych verdict, though, if they think she’s still dangerous after that five years has passed, she might still be in there twenty years later. And all it takes is her pissing of the wrong person in charge, and she’s in there for a long time.” After a little pause, she finished with, “Actions have consequences. Or, as I’ve been hearing people say, fuck around and find out. Well, she’s finding out right now.”

“Still, I am sorry that you lost your friend,” Enterprise said.

“It’s sad, but I can honestly say that if she hadn’t decided to ‘see you next Thursday’ out on me, I’d never have met you or be where I am today.” She giggled softly. “That’s got to really be annoying both girls. They have to know that what they did caused me to Trigger into what I am now, and I’m always in the news in a positive light. They may try the ‘She’s where she is because of me!’ bit, but I think enough people will remind them that they’re just taking credit for an attempted murder.”

“We have something else coming up on the radar, so to speak,” Enterprise said, “and I am completely uncertain as to how to deal with it, or even if we should. In grabbing the money the way I did, I have managed to severely damage, shall we say, several small countries that were already destabilized. The nearest ones to us are the Dominican Republic and Haiti. Several of the smaller African nations are in the same boat, as it were. I mention no names because with the warlords running around, the places get renamed every other week, it seems.”

Taylor wiped her hand across her face. “This is going to require a conversation with the crew I’m building, and a few others. The Prime Directive would say not to get involved, but we already did, causing the inevitable collapse faster than it would have happened. Also, we’re not in the Federation, so they can’t exactly bring us up on charges if we do interfere.” She sighed. “Get in touch with everyone - Dragon included and see if she’s got the time to hang out with us while we talk about this issue. Since this will take some time, I’m going to go down to the planet and talk to Dad about the DNA thing.”

“Set it up for about six or seven, so it can be a dinner meeting?” Enterprise asked as Taylor got to her feet and started toward the Captain’s yacht.

“Sounds good to me. I’m taking the yacht down, since I want flight time. When I’m close enough, please do as detailed a scan of Mom’s DNA as you can manage.” In a few minutes she was entering the atmosphere of the planet. The concept still made her smile at the thought of being able to be in space, and that someday she would set foot on the Moon itself, and even on other worlds!

Her father met her in the back yard and hugged her. “This is unusual. What led you to landing a spaceship in the back yard?” He paused. “And the fact that I live in a world where that sentence actually makes sense is still amazing.”

“Got something I need to talk to you about. It’s not bad, so don’t get worried, but it needs a decision. Sort of an important check box on a form, if you will.”

“Okay, let’s head inside. Just got a call from Enterprise, by the way, wondering if I wanted to be involved in a dinner meeting aboard the Enterprise?”

“She’s thinking ahead of me, that’s good. Bring Bian too, if she wants. Not going to say more about that until the meeting.” Once they were inside the house, they headed to the living room and sat down. “Just going to drop this out there for your consideration.” He took a deep breath before saying “Dragon is an intelligent computer. She wants to build a human body. She asked if she could use my DNA as the ‘mother’ contribution - and no, it’s just growing a clone body, not me carrying a child, and I mentioned Mom. It turns out that there’s stuff we couldn’t bear to get rid of that still have readable DNA on them of hers.”

He sat back in the chair. “Huh. So there’s the possibility of me ended up with the equivalent of either another daughter or a grand-daughter. If she uses either yours or Annette’s DNA is going to end up drop-dead gorgeous, mind you.” Taylor couldn’t help but blush at her father’s compliment.

“Exactly on the daughter/grand-daughter thing. But it has to be your decision if the option to use Mom’s is even on the plate. Dragon may still decide that she wants me as ‘Mom’, since she’s already joked that she may call me that after the procedure is done. It won’t be done for a while, because she and Enterprise are still working out all of the little issues. We’re all going for as close to perfection as is possible for this operation, but the genetics are huge part of this. If you allow Mom’s to be used, it would be the equivalent of Andrew Richter and Mom having a child. That might bother you to think of.”

“It’s not like she actually ever even met the guy, but I appreciate the fact that you thought about that sort of thing. Let me think about it for a bit before I give an answer, okay?”

Taylor winced. “I’m sorry if I gave you the impression that it was a ‘right now!’ situation. We’ve got time for you to think about it, and for Dragon to contemplate as well. I just didn’t want you blind-sided when we are ready with more of a ‘right now’ deal.”

“I appreciate that, and I didn’t assume that it was right now.” He stood up, pulled her to her feet and hugged her. “Annette would be so fucking proud of the woman you’re turning in to. Even if you’re always going to be my little girl, you’re a woman to be proud of.”

“I love you too, Dad,” she said softly, and just melted into the hug.

Chapter 78: Saturday, March 19th, 2011 - Deena

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Deena walked into the conference room on Charlie’s arm, wearing a simple blouse and skirt, albeit out of her preferred Federation technologies. Charlie was dressed similarly. They walked over to the window as they always did and looked down at Earth for a minute or so. “I can’t see myself ever getting tired of that view,” she said.

Sherrel walked up beside them and said, “I’ve been enjoying it as much as I can, ever since Tay … no, in this case it was the Captain who told me that she appreciated what I was trying to say by avoiding the view, but that I was just as worthy of looking at the view as anyone else.”

“It was the fact that you were able to deny yourself the things you wanted that really sold me on how truthful you were about getting clean and paying for your crimes,” Taylor said. “Most people who end up in the drug scene as deep as you were aren’t looking at the long term; they’re looking at the next hit. You were showing that you were thinking ahead, and that you were showing no signs of falling back into that previous life. Hell, there’s footage for the PRT and others that you were involved in the assault on the Nine. And I certainly trust you at my back.”

“That’s ‘cause she’s staring at your butt,” Vicky said with a snicker.

Sherrel was blushing, but shot back, “Isn’t it rude not to admire a work of art?”

This drew some laughter from everyone, and they sat down at the table after grabbing something buffet style. Dragon was there, but for reasons obvious to Deena at least, didn’t eat. After people had done their main bit of eating with some basic conversation, Taylor called the sort of meeting to order.

“Okay, this is mainly to talk about something that Enterprise brought to my attention. In doing what we have done with the illegally obtained money around the world, we have managed to destabilize several governments to the point of collapse. The closest are the island nations of Dominican Republic and Haiti. One island, mind you, with a fairly clear demarcation of where one ends and the other begins. If we were in the Federation, we’d sort of sit back and let things happen, but we aren’t in the Federation, and there are things we can do. However, we need to be careful if we do these things. I’m not allowing any Federation technology down on Earth that isn’t under our strict control.”

Bian spoke up. “To be honest, and this sounds worse than I actually mean it, Captain, but under your strict control. What are you thinking of to help them out, assuming that’s the reason for this get-together?”

“First is whether or not we should. I admit that I’m of a mind to do so, since it was actions done for me that put some of these places in this situation. Test case can be Hispaniola, which is the entire island. If we interfere there - and I do mean if - I was thinking of starting small and speed-building a couple factories there to help give some jobs. We’d need to see about fixing up the farming situation as well. The big problem is who would be running the country.”

Deena spoke up. “To be honest, Taylor, I think that if you’re going to do something like this, to make it work, you sort of have to swoop in and take over politically as well, otherwise the same corrupt people in charge are just going to take things over and funnel all that money into their own pockets. You need to be in control of the process. In this case, that means you need to control the country itself.”

“Which opens you to other issues,” Dragon said. “Public relations will be much harder on you at that point.”

“Of course,” Taylor said. “I come swooping in, take out ‘the big bad guys’, and then start taking over countries. I know where minds are going to go at that point. I go from being the helpful starship captain to being the Great White Colonizer, out to take over the world one country at a time.” She sighed. “And this is where my problem comes in, and why I need your help. I can’t just sit back and watch something so close to the United States go the way Somalia has been going, but I also need to be in charge of the aid being given, or else the people in power come in and control who gets the aid, to which the answer is always ‘their friends, and the people who can pay enough’. None of it ever makes it to the people who actually need it.”

Danny Hebert said, “I’d say that you’re too young to be this cynical, but you grew up in Brockton Bay.” This drew a bit of a chuckle from everyone there. “Seriously though, no matter what you do, you’re going to get people who will go after you for the decision. ‘Why aren’t you helping when you have the means?’ will be the basic question if you choose not to interfere. Go the other way and you’ll be accused of trying to take over the world. You’ll never please everyone. The question you need to ask yourself, when it comes down to it - actually there are two questions: Why are you making the decision you’re making, and then can you be happy with the complaints that people will make?”

Charlie spoke up. “He’s got a point - whatever decision that you make, you need to be able to explain the why of it. You don’t get involved. Why? Is it because you’re worried about the public? Is it that you’re afraid of the slippery slope, where you did this thing that goes against the Prime Directive, so why not do that thing that maybe stretches things further? There are other reasons you might not want to get involved, those were just the first two that came to mind. Then with the second one, part of it comes down to how involved you want to be? It might be that to do what you properly want to, you have to be in charge of the nation. Which leads to a whole bunch of other, interesting issues. Is fixing the nation worth making yourself a political entity? A world leader, basically?”

“And now you see the problem. I need to work on unifying things if we’re ever going to have something that even closely resembles a world like the one from Star Trek, but right now, the only way to do that is to take over. Because I guarantee that if I end up in control of the island of Hispaniola, I’ll end up dealing with other crap. Cuba’s right next door, for example. Raul’s in charge there, but do you really think that he’s not listening to Fidel? And having their next door neighbor suddenly prospering with help that they’re going to assume is coming from the United States?” She put her head back. “There are a host of good reasons not to, but also good reasons to do so.” She stopped and took a deep breath. “Chesterton’s Fence. There’s an idea on the table to do something - help Hispaniola. The obvious thing is that the people get helped. Yay. What are the secondaries out of this? What are the knock-off consequences of doing it?”

“Usually Chesterton’s Fence is used to figure out why you should wait before getting rid of a rule at a job,” Danny said. “Haven’t heard of anyone using it in a political sense, and to be honest, that’s what this is. Political, no matter the reason you’re doing it. It becomes political anyway.”

“Do you have the wherewithal to do this?” Vicky asked. “As in, do you have the bodies to work with? If so, then you work the problem past that. If not, then the problem is put on hold until you have the necessary people to do what you need, and then we come back to the question again. Unless I miss my guess, you’d need to hire a bunch of people right now that you could trust to do the job, because as far as I’m aware, the only people you have for this are right here in this room, and we all have other things that we’re involved in, like school for most of us. The rest of the group have jobs that they can’t just abandon, so the question right now is a non-starter.”

She paused. “However,” she stressed, “this doesn’t mean that it has to be abandoned. Part of the process can be figuring out what needs to be done and how to automate most of it. A lot of the farming can be done mechanically, although I’ve seen references that you can get more crops per acre if you’re not having to worry about paths for the machines to run down. The Amish do more per acre than most other farmers for that reason, for example.”

Enterprise spoke up. “We can also begin to set up some of the colony modules that the Federation uses. Quite honestly, over ninety percent of what a module involves can be done with technology either currently available right now, or with a small tweak to what exists. The remaining parts are honestly things that these days most would consider luxuries, but were standard in our time and considered essential, such as built in connectivity to subspace communications. Since the Simurgh is gone, I have actually gotten into creating a cheap satellite-based Internet service provider, with the money going into your coffers. I’ve built it with slightly better than modern technology, and have spun up a handful of intelligence-mimicking programs to run the help line. They aren’t actually intelligent, but for these purposes, they can handle pretty much anything. I mention this because we could put Internet connectivity into the colony modules. Set a few of the modules up and you have a small city with a higher standard of living immediately.”

“We’ll need to run something like that past a few agencies, I suspect,” Taylor said. “But that comes down to how we’re handling this. If we start doing this, we need people involved who are going to be able to spend all their time on this project. I won’t be able to until the school year ends. At that point I’ll be at the point where I won’t legally be required to return to Arcadia to finish out my last two years, since I could apply for at least on PhD right now, it looks like.” She leaned forward and put her elbows on the table with her hands in sort of a praying position, placing her nose and mouth between her hands, completely covering them. She spoke without changing her position, leading to an odd echo-y sound to her voice. “This is where it’s hitting me just what I’ve signed up for. The worries I have here are like the worries I’ll have for setting up my academy, and so many other things. My businesses. The amount of stuff is teetering between whelming and overwhelming.” A couple of the others snickered at her use of ‘whelming’.

She sat back up suddenly, clearly having mentally put on her Captain’s Hat. “But it has to be done and I’m in a position to do it. Can I get each of you to come up with a list of reasons for and against doing what we were talking about for the Dominican Republic and Haiti? Feel free to talk to Enterprise if you need to know if an idea you had is actually possible at the tech level we’re thinking about. I am personally in favor of helping them out, but not if it’s going to end up causing more easily preventable problems cropping up. Things we should have been able to see coming, basically. We can try to get together again about this on April 3rd? Gives us two weeks to think about it and write stuff down. And for my fellow students, don’t think of it as homework where you have to do your very best. Get stuff written down as it comes to you. We may end up with everyone coming up with the exact same things on all of the lists. I don’t care. If you think of it, write it down, because if you thought of it, it might be important, and make everyone else go ‘Why didn’t I think of that?’.”

It was clear that the meeting was done, so they fell to idle conversation at that point, and Deena walked over to Taylor. “Feeling okay?”

“Like I said, it’s … a lot. But I think that Rabbi Hillel’s famous comment is important here. ‘If I am not for myself, who will be for me? If I am only for myself, who am I? And if not now, when?’ I need to think of me, of course, but the second sentence is the important part, to me. ‘If I am only for myself, who am I?’ My whole mission here is for the planet as a whole. It’s why I fight Endbringers and why I’m dealing with the Nine, and the Fallen and whomever else is a problem. But I have to think of myself as well, which is why I have that gorgeous 1940 Indian that Sherrel helped me rebuild. Why I get the girls together and we have a beach day on the holodeck.” She laughed. “‘All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.’ I take time for myself to recharge. But in the end, I do this because it needs to be done and I’m in a position to do it. ‘If not now, when?’ Why wait longer than I have to? Don’t jump in early, but if I have a working plan? Put it into effect as soon as feasible. That’s what part of this is about - is there a feasible plan? Can we make one?” She paused. “Who keeps leaving these soapboxes around the decks?” she finished with a laugh.
