Chapter 80: Sunday, March 20th, 2011 - Amy

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

She was utterly astonished at the reactions they got around town when the group of them decided to just head out and enjoy the beginning of Spring. What had truly amused her was that Charlie had decided to take advantage of a Maine law and was wearing body paint in a camouflage pattern - sky blue and pale grey - but it was obvious if you looked - admittedly you had to look fairly closely, inviting a slap if it was unwelcome - that it was paint. Taylor had, instead of a camo pattern herself, gone with a very nice shade of green that went with her eyes, with a pale blue under-outfit as her hologram. Amy herself had chosen similarly, only hers were a bright blue that managed to accentuate the freckles on her face, and a matching pale blue under-suit. It was only light for them, true, but everyone else was staring at the very attractive teenagers walking the Boardwalk. Or, as Vicky phrased it, “They’re checking out the girls checking out the stores.”

After one incident at a store, Amy had decided that today was going to be a day for her to be ‘clumsy’. She had dropped something and had bent at the waist to pick it up, and had heard a strangled, “Jesus Christ, what a perfect ass!” It was clear that the guy hadn’t intended her to hear it, so she didn’t draw attention to her having heard. But she got similar reactions throughout the day as she managed to find excuses to draw attention to the fact that she was not wearing a shapeless skirt. The other girls had been giggling over the fact that she had unconsciously started to strut as she walked. Taylor was strutting as well, but that seemed to be because they were making it somewhat obvious that they were a couple, and Taylor was strutting because she felt she had the hottest girl in town on her arm. This also helped Amy feel good about herself.

“I may have to do like Charlie is someday,” Amy said when they stopped for lunch. “I’m really enjoying the looks I’m getting. I’ve never felt sexy before, what with having a blonde goddess as my adoptive sister, so hearing that guy nearly hurt himself because he liked the way my butt looked?”

“Demi-goddess, maybe,” Vicky said with her nose in the air. “But not a goddess. That’s for when I hit eighteen.” She couldn’t hold the arrogant look for long, though, and burst out laughing, along with the others at the table.

They already knew that there were comments about their outing on PHO, and Charlie had definitely been figured out, albeit via a number of people figuring out to point out her clothing and lack thereof without earning a ban-hammer. The person who was surprising everyone in all of this was Void Cowboy, who not only had not earned a ban for any period of time, but had also been carefully pointing out the statutes that allowed Charlie to do exactly what she was doing, and that by wearing body paint, she was effectively wearing a shirt, because her toplessness was not immediately obvious. And since Maine law allowed her to walk around without a shirt as long as it was not for obviously lewd purposes, she was well within her rights. He also stated that he was glad he was not out on the Boardwalk, because the ladies were beautiful enough as it was, and he had no desire to step on his own tongue while following them around, which he admitted that he undoubtedly would be doing. This had led to a derail about the laws regarding public nudity and such, and Amy had wondered if Void had done that on purpose, since he appeared to have been improving since January, having avoided the ban-hammer altogether.

After they left and headed back down the Boardwalk, they were surprised to run into Carol Dallon. “Hello, ladies,” she said. “Those outfits must be warmer than they appear, to be honest.”

“Yeah. To be honest, a little of this is advertising,” Vicky said.

“Given how form fitting that is, I’m not sure that you’re advertising what you think you are.” She looked to Amy. “Either of my daughters.”

“Well, we have these amazing billboards,” Amy replied, motioning down her own body, “so why not show off some of the materials that the clothing can be made out of. And yeah, first of Spring and a nicer day than we normally get for the first day of Spring, so … well, we decided to show off.” She shrugged. “And we’re teenagers, so … we decided to show off,” motioning at her figure again the second time.

Carol actually laughed, and Amy felt good that the woman really was trying to mend things. “I’m sort of torn between the ‘Go home and put on more clothing!’ thing or the proud ‘Those are my daughters!’ thing in looking at you two. You’re clearly working out, and while I wish you were still Panacea - the name is still there for you if you ever end your sabbatical, by the way - Elixir’s costume being a bit more form hugging is a good look for you.” She looked to Vicky. “And having torn a hole in one of my wool skirts this morning, I’m definitely coming around to the concept of Glory Girl losing that skirt from her costume.” She laughed. “I just don’t want to go through all the paperwork required for a change like that - trademarks and such can be such a pain to work with.”

“Sorry,” Vicky said, “but you really understand now some of why I want to get rid of the skirt now. I loved it a couple years ago, going with the princess look, but there’s a reason a lot of princess stories have the girl in something a little closer to the body now, or have her tearing the skirt down to at least make it shorter.” She grinned and put on an air that only the truly stupidest people would assume was real, “And when you look like this, you should show it off!” She posed comically and added, “I need that little ‘DING’ sparkle from the teeth that Gilderoy Lockheart had in that Potter movie.” That drew laughter form everyone nearby.

Carol just shook her head fondly and looked at Amy. Much softer in volume and tone, she said, “Something tells me that despite the ‘evidence’, you’re not cold at the moment.” Her eyes flicked quickly to Amy’s chest.

“Well, I’ve never really done something like this before,” Amy responded. “A little scary and a little freeing, in a way, you know? I might never do this sort of thing again -” She blushed furiously at the chorus of unhappy “Aww” from people who were not her immediate friends. “But after a reaction like that, I just might do it again.” This was immediately followed by a louder chorus of “Yay!” from the same group. “It’s just, I don’t want to look back in years to come and think, ‘what if I’d?’ about things, even stuff like this. So I decided to … well, I guess you could say I’m being a tiny bit exhibitionist?” Another chorus of “Yay!” from the crowd - a larger group this time, who were now clearly doing it for the humor, and she couldn’t help but laugh at the reaction. She also wasn’t about to admit just how exhibitionist she really was at the moment.

She was smart enough to ask Enterprise to turn on the feeling of cloth when Carol started to move to hug her, and she reveled in the fact that it felt like a real one, and not something perfunctory. Like the woman really was fighting her attitudes. That made Amy feel even better about being out and about today, if it meant that she got a loving hug from this woman at least once in her life.

Carol turned to Vicky after releasing Amy - and Amy was surprised to realize that there might have been some reluctance in the release! - and hugged her as well. “I know I’m not often demonstrative in public, and I’m trying to change that,” she said conversationally. “Too often I come out as ‘Carol Dallon, attorney’ or as ‘Brandish’ even when I’m in civilian clothes. I’m trying to be out and about as ‘Carol Dallon, mother’ a bit more often.”

“You’re doing a good job so far,” Amy said. “And Panacea’s not off the table, to be honest. I’m out in more ways than one, given that everyone knows I’m a parahuman healer and that I’m dating Captain Hebert of the Enterprise, but it might almost have to be as something of a split personality thing. Elixir for my stuff that isn’t New Wave related, like if I’m working toward my M.D. license.” She shrugged. “Looking carefully into things. I’m far enough ahead of the schedule on schooling that I might try to look into colleges for what would be my senior year. Too late in the school year to even think about trying to apply to various schools now. Because I’m serious about that. I want to be able to properly explain to the doctors and researchers, using language that they’ll understand, what I’m doing, so that maybe someday I don’t have to be around for anything other than immediate trauma. I like the idea of putting myself out of business, as I keep saying.”

“Part of me wants to tell you to stay in high school, but you’d just be starting college a bit early. And I certainly support anything that can help the people. If only we could get a way to not need superhero groups anymore without going the totalitarian route, governmentally speaking,” Carol said.

“It’ll take a while,” Taylor said, “but that’s part of what I’m aiming for somewhere in the future. I want us to get to the point where we can potentially be a post-scarcity society, where everyone can be as free as they want. Providing, of course, that you are aware that your freedom to so something ends at the point where it infringes on someone else. Or as I heard it somewhere else - ‘Your right to punch me ends at my nose’. You can throw the punch, but if it actually hits me without getting my permission first? Then I can respond. It’s more nuanced than that, but it gets the general idea across.” She frowned. “I think Bian and I will need to set up and appointment with you sometime soon. Got a thing or two we need to talk about. But that’s going to be lawyer-speak and therefore billable, and therefore not to be talked about here. I’ll ask that you contact Bian tomorrow or something, if she doesn’t get to you first. Just thought I’d mention that while we were actually face to face.”

Carol nodded and said, “I’ll talk to her tomorrow then, most likely. Ah, there’s Sarah and Crystal. See you girls later.” She gave Amy and Vicky a second, quicker hug, then walked toward her sister and niece.

“Huh,” Vicky said very quietly. “I’ve never seen her like that with you before, and didn’t smell anything vaguely alcohol related on her breath either.”

“I think that her comment about turning into your grandfather was serious,” Amy replied. “Even you never really liked him, and you make an effort with everyone.” She smiled. “That hug was real, too, not one that was for the cameras. I’ll admit that I could have stayed like that for a while.”

They walked around for a while more before heading back up to the Enterprise, where Charlie almost immediately leaned up against a console and shuddered happily. “Oh my God was I turned on walking around like that!” she panted. “Sorry, but I’ve been holding back on that orgasm for a little while now, and not actually sure how I did manage to keep it from happening.”

“Probably your power,” Amy said. “I’m betting it was a powerful one when it happened? Since your power can let you do damned near anything as long as it leads to an orgasm, I suspect it helped you hold back until you could do it in peace. The fact that it would be a stronger one just made it easier for your power to do that.”

Charlie thought for a moment before saying, “Yeah, that makes sense, and my power is doing its equivalent of nodding its head. It’s weird to think that I might be able to do a lot of interesting things, as long as it leads to an orgasm.”

Taylor chuckled. “Especially Tinkering, since Sherrel was one of the people here when you had your unique … well, let’s call it a Trigger, since it led to you having powers.”

Charlie smiled and said, “Hmm, Amy was here as well, so I’m curious about something.” She looked as if she were thinking for a moment and then got a sly smile on her face. She reached out and touched Deena, who ended up having a When Harry Met Sally moment in the transporter room. “Yup, I can bio-manipulate only so far as to cause an orgasm. Doesn’t have to be mine, even.”

Deena grabbed her and said, “It’s more fun the regular way, though,” and started toward the door. “Come with us?” she asked the others.

Amy giggled and said, “The way I’m feeling, and how I suspect everyone else is? In every sense of the word, yes.”

Chapter End Notes

So due to a few things that have nothing to do with writing, I'm about a month behnd on posting. So here's the first of four that will show up in the next few days. The next three chapters will all be set on the 25th of March, and actually remember that certain villain groups exist. *laugh*

Chapter 81: Friday, March 25th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

She started to get the first hints of trouble from the Elite on the day that she received good news regarding the Fallen. Enterprise called her with a small chirp in her ear, so she went to the main office to talk to them. “Yes, Miss Hebert?” the secretary asked.

“I’ve just received a small contact from my ship. The systems are aware enough to only forward issues above a certain level to me at school, so this means that it must be important. May I have permission to exit the school to get just outside the deadening zone?”

The principal walked out of her office and invited Taylor in. Once the door was closed, she said, “We know that your ship can easily get through out field here, because it works outside the cell network. We also appreciate that you actually don’t abuse your ability to get through the system.”

“I’m not learning anything if all I do is cheat,” she replied honestly with a shrug. “Besides, from a purely selfish point of view, if everyone knew that I was the only one who wasn’t stopped by the system, it would irritate them and make my life harder, because they’d be very unhappy with me. So I’m officially affected by the system, and intend to keep acting that way, and my ship reacts the same way as well. So if she’s calling me right now? Something is up.”

Principal Halliwell reached over and turned on a device. “That will stop just about everything but your equipment from snooping. Feel free to call from this office, if it’s not a security thing.”

“Thank you,” Taylor said quite honestly. She pulled out her hand-held communicator. “Enterprise? You rang?”

“Yes, Captain,” was the reply. “Conditions are most favorable for an assault on the three Fallen sites. Shall I begin the run and contact the PRT as well?”

“Yes. Also, contact Haven as well, since they’re one of the big ones fighting the Fallen. I’m sorry that they’ll be a bit unhappy with me, because there are members of the Fallen that won’t survive, because they’re too dangerous. But contact everyone, and I’ll tie into the systems from here in the principal’s office.”

“Understood, Captain. Enterprise out.”

“I thought you didn’t have much crew?” Principal Halliwell asked.

“That’s the ship’s computer. Ever see Voyager?” When the principal nodded, Taylor said, “Think the Emergency Medical Hologram, but for the ship itself, since it’s at least a generation later than Voyager. It can do a lot of things, but requires someone like me, or some other sentient, to be the physical captain. So I can tell her to do things and she can. What I need to do now is connect so that I can guide the drones during the assault on the Fallen.”

“Take the couch,” she said. “It’ll be a bit more comfortable, and if you need to lie down at all - well, it’s more comfortable than the floor.” Taylor snickered and moved to the couch and more openly connected to the ship’s systems. She could carry on a conversation with the principal if she wanted to, but the more that the public thought that something like this required greater concentration from her, the better in her eyes.

The first few times she had connected to all the available drones, it had been disorienting, but she knew that there would be times when she’d need to pay attention to multiple points, so she had practiced with it, and now she thought that it might be how a compound eyed insect might see things. If their eyes happened to be meters apart, that is.

She could see three different places, one of them she could tell by geolocation data was the Kentucky compound of the Mathers family. She was also looking at the Crowleys and the McVeays compounds as well, and sensors reported a lot of activity at them all. Hearing information from the Mathers compound told her that they had wind of people perhaps having figured out where they were, but that the information had only come in that morning, so there was no real time for them to have prepared. With them running around like chickens with their heads missing, Taylor started things. She did so by beheading the top chicken at the roost. Mama Mathers found it very hard to control things with a hole the size of a softball through her chest, neatly destroying her heart. The immediate loss of their connection to the person who had contact to the entire group set off worse problems - for the Fallen. They no longer had that communication back to Mama Mathers, so it staggered most of them. This was the point that Taylor fired on everyone in the various compounds. In short order, everyone was unconscious or dead.

At the same time, she was talking to the PRT in the various areas. “Come loaded for all the bear,” she told them. “I’m controlling drones at the compounds, and have everyone I’ve found down and unconscious, but the sensor suites aren’t perfect on these, what with all the other tech I needed in them. So I’ll keep them around just in case, but you’ll need to get there to arrest the unconscious ones, and … well, to be crude, bag and tag the ones that I was forced to kill, like Mama. There may be some in hiding, which is why I suggest coming prepared.” She gave them the coordinates of the various sites and pulled her main consciousness back to the principal’s office.

“Sorry about that. Would have preferred another time for that, but the universe doesn’t check my calendar before doing things.”

The principal snorted her laughter and said, “It’s inconsiderate like that sometimes.”

Taylor added, “I’m still connected to the drones, but the main job is done. A sh … boatload of drones with phasers in them tends to make quick work of a situation like this. I’ve got the PRT and Haven in one of the cases on their way to the sites, so my attention is going to be slightly on that for as much of the day as necessary. I think that I could concentrate on classes, though.”

“Truly?” the principal asked.

Taylor thought for a moment. “I might need to step out of a given class at some point or another, but it would be a short term thing. My attention is always on my ship at least a little bit,” she said, “so I’m used to slightly divided attention. I mean, I’m literally mentally connected to it, so there’s always some bleed-through.”

Principal Halliwell pulled out a sheet from a folder and filled it out, then handed it to Taylor. “Hand this to the teachers you have today, and tell them it’s fine to call and verify that it’s real. I don’t think you will, but I wouldn’t be doing my job if I didn’t tell you not to abuse the privilege today.”

Taylor laughed softly at that. “I won’t, but you don’t know that, so it’s a good admonition. Thank you very much for allowing this. And this looks like it ate my first class of the day, so I’ll stop by there first and apologize to her, and then head to my next class.”

“You are an educator’s dream student,” the principal said with a smile. “Then again, so are the friends you’re hanging out with.” Taylor opened the door and exited with a smile. She could hear the secretary asking what was going on, and heard the principal say, “I guarantee it will be on the news within a day or two, Doris, but I can’t tell you about it right now.” Taylor didn’t worry about that sort of question, because she’d come across it so many times hanging out at the DWU compound, and Doris’ reaction was the same as most Union members who asked something similar and received a similar answer - acceptance.

She headed to the first teacher and showed the note, and recommended that they call the principal, since she needed this for later classes just in case. She was waved off on that, since she’d already developed a good reputation as a student since starting at Arcadia. She slipped into the second class and nodded to the teacher, showing her that she had a note, and the teacher simply nodded. She shared this class with Deena and Charlie, who gave her a curious glance each.

~Taylor: Later, at lunch. It’ll hit the news, but I’m not sure when. Probably not until either late today or tomorrow at the earliest.~ They gave quick nods to that and went about the business of the class.

At lunch, Taylor tapped her forehead quickly when she looked at the other girls, and they nodded.

~Taylor: Since you’re curious, I missed first class and am ready for other issues throughout the day, because this morning was the perfect time to take down the Fallen. They’ve likely only got a handful who weren’t on any of the three compounds, so while they’re still a problem, they’re nowhere near as bad of one anymore.~

~Charlie: So what happened?~

~Taylor: Enterprise called me and let me know that now was the right time, since they’d somehow gotten word, and were mobilizing to move. We hit them while they were distracted. Several of them … did not survive the assault.~

~Amy: PLEASE tell me that Mama Mathers was one of the ones who didn’t survive! She’s been a thorn in so many sides for so very long, since she’s got such a broken Master power.~

~Taylor: She was the first one hit. Phaser punched a hole through her chest. There might have been some heart muscle left, but with the cauterizing of the softball sized hole, blood wasn’t going to be moving very well anyway. Some of their other Masters were off-site, and probably headed here, but they might be captured simply because apparently Mama had a connection to all of them, and killing her affected everyone on the Mathers compound. I told the PRT that there might be others on the compound, but there weren’t. I got them all. I just don’t want them realizing how good my tech truly is at the moment.~

~Enterprise: I’m sorry, Captain, but I need to inform you that it seems that the Elite have begun their moves to gain control of your companies. One of the small convoys carrying raw materials here was stopped and the cargo stolen. It was one of the nearly vital shipments to get the smelting process going in the metal workshop. We have enough for a few weeks worth of production, but we will eventually need that shipment.~

~Deena: Any possibilities on tracing where it went to?~

~Enterprise: I know where it is at the moment, but I am uncertain as to whether or not I wish to show just how much I know at the moment. I could easily place all ten of the containers in Cargo Bay 10, but that then lets the Elite know that we can trace maneuvers such as this, and given the psychology of those that are known to be members of that group, they will likely take maneuvers to gain control of the company somewhat more violent. This set of companies stands to be the major supplier for a good many businesses over the next few years. Just the metal that Armsmaster figured out from the data given to him in January will make quite a change to the automotive industry. And the oil industry, for that matter, although a negative one for them. He patented that metal in your name, by the way, Taylor, since he stated that he was simply working from plans given him by you.~

Taylor pulled out her phone for a moment, looked at it, and pinched her nose in mild frustration. ~Taylor: Sorry, I needed a reason for people not to ask why I’m looking frustrated right now. They don’t know we can talk telepathically.~ She sighed. ~He figured out the process. He should have the patent. I’m not complaining about the money going to him.~ She snorted. ~Honorable … git.~

~Vicky: Going British on us now?~

~Dragon: ‘Git’ is a prefectly useful term for a situation like this, especially since there was some fondness to the way she used it. He owes me now, because I told him you’d react that way.~

~Taylor: Any ideas on how to get him to at least accept some money for it, since I gave the concept for it, but he did the actual mental work necessary to make it happen here in the real world?~

~Dragon: I’ll work on him.~ They could all feel the amusement.

~Charlie: I’m still mildly happy-freaking that I can talk to one of the world’s greatest Tinkers whenever she’s of a mind to talk to me.~

~Dragon: I’d say that I’m just like you, but we all know that I’m not. But as far as I can feel, I’m as human as I can be, given the limitations of my current situation. And Taylor? Once again, thank you for pointing the Guild at the Dragonslayers.~

~Taylor: I was just doing the right thing. For all intents and purposes, they had kidnapped you. In a real sense, they had, at least, because they could kill you with that laptop. That functionality is gone now, by the way. None of your father’s paranoia can kill you now.~

~Dragon: Now I can go crazy and show my power by … hmm, building a human body and showing off my bikini bod? Is that evil enough?~

~Amy: If you end up with either Taylor or her mother as your genetic mother, and that figure breeds true, so to speak? Don’t know how evil it is, but I suspect that you’ll be ban-hammering a lot of people on PHO.~

~Vicky: Start with small evils, like not repairing cracks in sidewalks, before escalating to rickrolling people.~

There was a general snickering through the mental link at that.

Chapter End Notes

The second one on my way to catching up to where I should be. Probably will not get another one out tonight. (12-22-2025)

Chapter 82: Friday, March 25th, 2011 - Deena

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Up on the Enterprise, the group talked more openly about what was going on, that they couldn’t talk about at the school. “I’m glad the Fallen are basically dealt with,” Vicky said, “but that means that the remaining free ones are likely to be a little more fanatical, now that they’ll see it as having to rebuild their ‘faith’.”

“In other words, their breeding farms,” Taylor said. “Everyone was taken in, but a lot of them are getting medical attention because they had been kidnapped and Mastered because the groups found them useful. Females especially.”

There was a general growl through the group as she finished. “I hope that the main jailers of those people went down for good,” Deena said.

“That was why I said that multiple people were killed,” Taylor said. “I don’t go with the ‘I vas chust following orderz’ thing I know they’d have tried. It was obvious from watching the previous data that they enjoyed their positions. And sometimes … ‘enjoyed’ … their positions.” The growl was a little louder this time.

“Our next worry is the Elite,” Enterprise said, appearing in the publicly acceptable rework of the microdress that Vicky had designed. Still sexy, but far less likely to derail conversations than the previous version. “If I grab the containers, I should do it sometime early in the morning, when they are less likely to have heavy coverage.”

Vicky cocked her head in thought for a moment and said, “Is there any other group out there with access to Tinkertech that we might want the Elite fighting with?” As the rest of the group looked at her, she explained. “I was thinking that we start things with a set of cloaked drones designed to display a hologram or series of holograms. If there’s another group out there that uses teleportation as a method of doing things, we make it look like that group’s specific aura, visual, whatever you call it is taking the containers, all while Enterprise is using the stealth method of grabbing them. If we really want the Elite and whatever group we choose at odds, Enterprise reverses that and makes it look like the group in question delivered it after it was stolen. Of course, that means that it either needs to be a group that would be friendly with you slash us, or a group that would see something like this as a beautiful way to spit in the eyes of the Elite, even if it means giving up the material for you to use.”

“I’m a cape groupie,” Deena said.

Before she was immediately interrupted by Charlie, who reached over and gently squeezed one of Deena’s breasts. “More like a cape grope-e,” she said with a giggle. “Sorry.”

Deena rolled her eyes, but she was clearly not bothered by it. “I pay attention to the cape scene pretty well. “I’m actually one of the people that Bagrat gets some of his info from that allows him to be ‘The Guy In The Know’ on PHO. He admits that occasionally. So I know a lot of the various groups that pop up and disappear, usually because of some silly arguments that get blown all out of proportion because people have powers to make their point with.” She paused. “Where I’m leading to with this is that there’s a group out there calling themselves Sherwood, who pattern themselves on the whole Robin Hood mythos.” She giggled. “Kinda annoyed some Brits, because Americans thought of the group before they did.”

“Part of what they do is a lot of what Robin Hood is famous for. They try to steal from the people who are stealing from others, and give it via untraceable means to others who can use it, or return it to those it was stolen from. Part of why they’re so successful is that they have a Tinker who makes teleportation technology. I … might know that Tinker.”

“Well enough to ask if we can blame them for the theft of our goods?” Taylor asked. “Because while they sound good, we don’t want to walk in and make them an enemy by blaming them without good cause.”

“Let me find out.” She stood up and walked to the other end of the room and a force field went up around her. “John? It’s Deena. Got a question for you. You know that I’m friends with Grey Ghost, also known as Captain Taylor Hebert, right?”

“Yeah. What’s up?”

“The Elite are trying their tactics to gain control of her companies. She wants to use the money to improve the world, and they … well, they’re the Elite. We know that they want to enrich themselves by hook or by crook. They stole a shipment from her. We want to take it back late night slash early morning, but one of our team suggested pointing the ‘theft’ at another team. We are not going to use anything to hint that Sherwood might be involved unless you guys think it’s a good idea.”

“So you’d be stealing your own stuff back, but if they know that you guys did it, they’d ramp up quickly against you - probably sending someone like Bastard Son, whom they can ‘disavow his actions’ - whereas we’re in a running battle with them because we openly call them on their bullshit. Give me about half an hour and I’ll get back to you. We can maybe - and I repeat maybe - even do this for you, since I assume you want to make it look like we made off with the stuff?”

“Yeah. We’d be mimicking your teleportation technology’s look to move quite a few containers of stuff. They hit a convoy on it’s way to Brockton Bay. And no, I didn’t intend the rhyming.”

She heard him laugh. “Okay. Give me a bit and I’ll get back to you.” The call ended, and the field dropped. “Spoke to their Tinker, Little John, and he’ll get back to me in about thirty minutes or so.”

“Nice bit of misdirection there as well. I wonder if he’s as tall as the legend, or if he went the other route and really is short?” Vicky asked. “None of my business, really. Just a passing thought.”

“No matter what, I want to open our doors officially on the first Monday in April,” Taylor said. “After getting Parian on board - she damn near offered to pay us for the ability to work with some of our cloth - we’ll have quite a bit of available stock for the clothing store when it opens. Basically planning on turning one of the areas of the docks near one of the ferries into a shopping area. We’re getting the ships out of the way, I’ll be working with Sherrel and whomever else on repairing that yacht, and I’m looking forward to tomorrow especially, even though it has nothing to do with any of what we’ve been talking about so far.”

“What’s going on tomorrow?” Deena asked.

“Three visitors are coming into town, and I’m taking them on a tour of a few places. James Lovell, Fred Haise, and Neil DeGrasse Tyson all managed to schedule for tomorrow. I intend that Misters Lovell and Haise get the chance to set foot on the Moon, and I sure as hell can’t imagine that the man who raved about how innovative a design that the Enterprise had for the time would turn down a chance at either the Moon or the Enterprise. And since Mars is a little over 2 AU away at the moment - other side of the sun sorta but visible if you could somehow blot out the blue of the sky - we can take them there. I want footage of them being the first humans to set foot on Mars.”

Charlie leaned over to Vicky and said, “Any bets one of them insists that since she made it possible, that she gets the bragging rights?”

“Nope, from everything I’ve heard about Lovell and Tyson, that’d be a sucker bet, and I’m pretty sure Haise is the same way.”

“What about our naked Mars time?” Sherrel asked with a grin.

“I figure we’ll use our Spring Break for that. Somewhere in mid-April. We can either yacht it by that point, since I’m pretty sure that we can get that working by then, or do motorcycles with your … special seats … for the drive to Mars.”

“Or we could get the yacht going, and use the bikes to go to the surface from the yacht,” Sherrel said. “I’m sorry, but I really like the idea of riding a motorcycle around on the surface of another planet. And the exhibitionist in me especially likes the idea of doing it totally nude.”

Taylor was about to respond when Deena’s communicator chirped, and she stood and walked back over to the other side of the room. “Hello?”

“Deena, John. Talked to the rest of Sherwood, and they love the idea. In fact, how soon can you put us in touch with Captain Hebert? Or Grey Ghost, whichever is more accurate or proper for this situation?”

She grinned and the force field dropped. “Enterprise, please transfer my call to the speaker, so that Captain Hebert can talk to Little John of the rogue group Sherwood.”

“Absolutely,” came the soft voice of Majel Barrett Roddenberry. “Sorry, couldn’t resist that,” she said in her normal voice.

“Little John, this is Captain Taylor Hebert of the USS Enterprise. You wished to speak to me?”

“Holy crap, I believed her, but there’s believing someone and then getting proof of it. Sorry. Deena explained the situation to me, I think. You had materials stolen from you by the Elite?”

“Not officially the Elite, since they like to use cutouts, but the Enterprise is a little better than they are at computer stuff, you understand?” The captain laughed at that. “They basically hijacked seven trucks that were carrying cargo containers for my factories. Not having that will set us back a bit in manufacturing, and given their modus operandi, I think they’d swoop in and offer to get me replacement material, and then try to sell me my own stuff. They’re basically parahuman organized crime.”

“That’s how we see them as well. Could you use the information to get them in the court system?”

“Sort of a ‘fruit of the poisoned tree’ issue, since the means by which we know they’re involved wasn’t entirely legal to do, you know?”

“Gotcha. One last thing - this is going to make you a ton of money, right?”

“Hope so. Got plans for fixing things with that money, but I can’t spend it if I don’t make it. Yeah, oodles of money sounds good on paper, but I hate paperwork, and that kind of money needs it, especially with what I plan to do with it. I’m not going to do one of my standard soapbox speeches at you, but I want this world to be a lot more like the Earth of the Federation, where we don’t have to worry about where our next meal is coming from, or where we’re going to live. But to get to that point, I need money to do the things that needs the other things, if that makes sense.”

“It does, and helps me with the final decision. Let’s talk about where you want them delivered to, and where they are right now. And when you think the best time to hit them is going to be.”

“Okay. Right now, they’re too on edge and it’s early enough in the day that so much would be obvious. I was thinking that we all get a little sleep and prepare for some time after midnight for this? It’s rare for any group to be even more active when it’s dark out, and for something like this, it’s too soon for them to try unloading the containers to move them into their own, just for selling back to me.”

“After midnight sounds good. If you can let me know where they should be dropped, I can start preparing my teleporter for the transit. Mine’s not as good or fast as the stuff the Federation makes,” he said with a laugh.

“But it works, right? That’s the important part.” Taylor worked out the coordinate system with him and gave him the location where the containers were to be stored. “We’ll give as much credit as you want to your group. This will definitely put you on their radar if you weren’t before.”

“Well, they’re going to know it was us based on the teleportation we use. But we won’t complain if you thank us for returning your stuff to you,” he said with a laugh.

“Let’s aim for roughly 2 AM then, okay? Glad I don’t have school tomorrow, but I can get some decent sleep between helping you guys and something I need to do tomorrow.”

“What kind of help are you thinking?” he asked the captain.

“I figure some drones with some built in phasers hovering cloaked around the area when you start working, in case they’re a bit more on the ball for that hour of the morning. That’ll make our part in it more obvious, but I’ll be damned if you guys are going to get badly hurt doing something for us.”

“You do remember that part of this is to hide your connection? That we’re trying to make it look like we were offended and decided to return your stuff to you?”

“Yeah, but if you guys get badly injured …”

“It’s what we signed up for, Captain,” he said. “I won’t complain about maybe having them there to keep an eye out and maybe warn us, but to keep you out of this, let’s try to save phasering people until the very last second, okay?”

Deena smiled as she watched Taylor fight with herself for a few seconds. “You have an excellent point, as much as it irks me,” she finally said with a small laugh.

“Just wait until you have a chance to interact with Locksley. He has being smugly irksome down to an art form.” In the background they could hear a faint voice yelling “I resemble that remark!” which led to laughter all around. “So you’ll be back in contact with us at around two, or were you thinking the assault is at two?”

“Which works better for your team?”

“Assault at some point between two and three in the morning,” he replied. “In my experience, that’s some of the most boring time of the night. By four in the morning, they’re starting to think about shift change, so people are starting to pay more attention leading up to four. We’ll just find out tonight how competent the specific group is that grabbed them. It’ll be a lot more exciting if they were one of the more competent branches.”

“Can’t say as I like the concept of exciting in this meaning,” they heard the previous voice add. “But we’ve dealt with it before, and hopefully will live to deal with it again. Locksley, dear Captain, in case you didn’t know who’s talking.”

“Pleased to speak with you, sirrah,” she replied. “May tonight’s work be exciting enough to talk about, but not so exciting that someone needs to see a doctor about it.”

“I like the way you think, Captain,” was the reply. “Now, I think we need to get some down time ourselves if we’re staging a raid against the Elite tonight! Good evening, Captain, and may we speak again.”

“From your mouth to God’s ears, as the saying goes,” she replied. “Until later.”

Chapter End Notes

Meant to do this earlier in the week, but the holiday got to me. There's this one, and one a little later, and then hopefully I will remember tomorrow to return to posting on my usual weekend schedule. So this is number THREE of the four I promised to catch up with.

Chapter 83: Friday, March 25th, 2011 - Taylor

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Enterprise stimulated their brains to let the group sleep for a while, and then began waking them starting at about thirty minutes past midnight, depending on how long each person tended to take in properly waking up. Taylor was awakened at one, which gave her a chance to do a short bit of exercise before showering and heading to the bridge, where they had all agreed to meet, since this was, for all intents and purposes, a mission. By one-fifty, they were all on the bridge, and Taylor had Deena call Little John again, but it was broadcast to the bridge from the start.

“Even without some semblance of caller ID I’d know it was you, Deena, based on earlier. I assume that your people are ready as well?”

“We are indeed,” Taylor said. “You’re on the equivalent of speaker phone at the moment. We’re on the bridge, and I’ve got the feed from the drones up.” The scene was a quiet one, and the scans showed that they didn’t have a huge group guarding the containers. The drones had already verified that those were the containers that they were looking for, and that they still contained their cargo.

“Right now it looks fairly quiet. The guards are few and far between, and look like what I’m used to seeing from security that doesn’t tend to see much by way of action during their shift. Depending on how fast your technology is and how much it can transfer at a time, we might get out of this without a lot of problems.”

“Probably be a bit of an issue, so we’re going to have most of the team set up a distraction elsewhere on the site. It’ll probably take me roughly fifteen minutes to get each container moved. The teleport is quick, but there’s shifting both ends after a send is done. First I need to get the new lock on the cargo, and then the lock on the destination. Maybe ten minutes, but I’m figuring two minutes per container just for annoyance sake. I’d love to get it down to a minute a move, but I’ve never been that lucky before.” Taylor heard a snort. “At least the team’s teleport is a different, dedicated circuit. When I tell them, they can be gone instantly.”

“I’ll be keeping an eye on the receiving end just to verify that they successfully made it here. The containers, not your team,” she finished with a laugh.

“Yeah, having the landing zones switched would be a bit of a problem. The containers probably are a little heavy for the current spot the team lands in. Also, a little large for it.”

“The team wouldn’t be cramped at our landing zone, though, so that would be a plus,” Taylor said back. “Okay, joking aside, the two guards closest to the area with the containers actually just stepped inside a small shack to light up some cigarettes. They’re about as off their game guard-wise as I think they’re going to be and still be awake. Next couple minutes would be a good time to start your distraction.”

“I watched the show, so I’m not going to ask just how good those sensors are,” Little John replied. “Sending the team in now.” The group on the bridge knew that something had happened when about two minutes later, the guards in the shack, as well as a few others started running in the opposite direction of the containers that were the actual objective. Sherwood clearly had some sort of scanning available as well, because the moment that the guards were out of sight of the containers, the first one of them disappeared. Split screen showed it appearing on Taylor’s property, where they were originally supposed to be delivered.

The scene at the site where the Elite had stored them was showing that there was now apparently a pitched battle going on. There was evidence of gunfire, and the occasionally airborne person. Focusing on the fight showed that Locksley was apparently a crack shot with a bow, even if he did have some of the more ridiculous Green Arrow trick arrows from the Silver Age comics. She had no idea whether he was an archery Tinker or the things were built by Little John, but they were certainly effective. The Elite guards had no problems going lethal from the start, but Sherwood seemed to working very hard to keep the lethality down. To some extent, they seemed to be working from the more swashbuckling and almost comedic versions of Robin Hood and his Merry Men, especially when one of the team leapt off a building hanging onto a rope that led … somewhere … to strike one of the guards who was aiming at a teammate. “Yoiks, and away!” giggled Vicky from the helm position. The Sherwood member in question was quickly back atop a roof after knocking over not only their target but the five people near them.

Amy snickered. “They’re effective, but I think one of them has Cinematic Combat powers, given how oddly this is going.” She looked at the screen and groaned. The team was somewhat obvious - Locksley made no bones about doing the Robin Hood get-up, even going the forest green colors. There was a clear Brute dressed all in red, and Taylor heard Amy mutter, “Must be Will Scarlett. But who are the people in the maid’s outfit and the short order cook costumes?”

Charlie groaned even as Deena giggled. “Obviously the girl in the maid costume is Maid Marian, and I’m betting that the guy who looks like he’s wearing armored short order cook clothes is Fryer Tuck,” Charlie finally said.

“You got it,” said Little John over the connection. “Got three of them so far, looks like I’ve got it down, so we can get the other four out and to you just a touch faster. And we’ll relieve them of a couple other of their ill-gotten things while we’re at it, to make it less obvious that we were only after the cargo.”

As he spoke, there was a rather violent light show off toward what was probably the Elite’s headquarters for this specific operation. It didn’t appear to do any damage that was obvious, but it certainly got the attention of the ones fighting Sherwood, and quite a few more of the guards lost consciousness when they changed the focus of their concentration at the sudden alteration of circumstances. It looked to Taylor and crew as if the Sherwood group was trying very hard not to kill, which she appreciated about them. The remaining group that hadn’t been distracted began working their way away from Sherwood, to head toward the light show.

It was interesting enough of a show that Taylor didn’t realize that the last of her containers were hers again until she heard Little John say, “Done! And now to extract the team, and the safe with all that lovely evidence in it!” She looked to the screen, and sure enough, her containers were placed exactly where she’d wanted them.

“Thank you very much, Little John, and let Sherwood know that they have our thanks as well. And if you need help on extraction, let us know. Or medical help, for that matter.”

“We’re pretty good on that right now. We caught them off guard enough that we didn’t take more than bruises and a few small cuts. The only one who actually got shot is a Brute, so the bullets just bounced. But we appreciate the offer.”

“After we get some other things dealt with, I’ll have Deena contact you again if you’d like a tour of the ship.”

There was a pause before he said, “I’ll say this for Maid Marian, so that she doesn’t blow out your speakers or eardrums - squee.” He chuckled, as did the group on the bridge. “Seriously though, I can’t think of a one of us who would complain about that. Even if Will likes Star Wars more.”

“No shame in that. Star Wars was fun, and I enjoyed it. Even with running a Federation starship now.”

“Too true. I need to see to my team, so we’ll be back in touch. Toodles!” he said as the line disconnected.

“Seems like a decent group,” Taylor said. “I especially like their tendency toward non-lethal options, and the fact that they have a sense of humor. Given that they do have a sense of humor, does that one guy call that ‘rope from nowhere’ his punch line?” The rest of the group groaned. “C’mon,” Taylor said, “that one was obvious, even for me!”

Enterprise chuckled. “I liked it. I’ve also done a scan of the cargo, and it doesn’t seem as if the Elite did anything to it. They haven’t done anything to the locks, and the cargo is fine. I imagine our people will be happy when they get to work and find out that they have work to do,” she finished.

“I suspect that they were going to hold off until today to do anything. They grabbed it less than twenty-four hours ago, after all. They were either going to hold it and try to make us pay for our own containers, or they’d try something else. But I’m pretty sure that they’re going to escalate now. They need to try to get into some control of my businesses, either through the businesses themselves, or control access to needed things. We know it’s coming, so we can prepare for it.” She looked at the screen and smiled. “For now, I think we should go back to sleep, because tomorrow we get to meet two honest-to-God astronauts, and Neil DeGrasse Tyson!”

Amy smiled. “You captain a starship, and I love how you’re excited to meet the astronauts.”

“I’ve got it easy. They rode a bomb into space while siting in the equivalent of a can of SPAM, with them being the SPAM. That’s damned impressive, and I’m just sorry that Mr. Lovell never got to set foot on the Moon. I intend to change that tomorrow.”

“Yet another reason we love you, Taylor,” Vicky said with her own smile.

Chapter End Notes

...and now we're caught up!

Chapter 84: Saturday, March 26th, 2011 - Amy

Chapter Notes

The next few chapters are dedicated to the late Commander James Lovell. When these were written many months ago, he was still with us.

Amy was amused on Saturday morning, watching Taylor trying to get ready for the day. She was having a huge amount of difficulty trying to decide the uniform to wear for the day. “I never thought I’d see a day when you would manage to ‘girl’ so well,” Amy finally said. “You’ve spent the last fifteen minutes completely nude, trying to figure out the best of everything that you want to wear.”

“I need to make a good impression,” Taylor dithered back at her. “I need to look professional. So obviously no minidress or the like. But I had some really positive feedback with that skirt that you had Vicky design - the upside-down V that shows off tap pants? That can look rather good. But the astronauts are somewhat old school, so slacks would be a good possibility. Or a long business skirt. The jacket is a given, but what to wear under it. And today is a definite bra and panties day, on the probably far too likely chance that I’ll end up doing something that gives me a Ron Stoppable moment where I de-pants myself.”

“And thereby make everyone in the area very happy,” Amy said. “You have an amazing ass.”

Taylor chuckled. “But I would embarrass myself so badly in front of these people. Everyone thinks of people like me who run out and fight crime as heroes, but two of these men risked their lives for science. And circumstances kept them from ever setting foot on their intended destination. I wish Captain Swigert was still alive, because I’d have invited him as well. They deserve this. And I need to make a good impression on them.” Taylor snorted. “Which is why Vicky will be piloting the shuttle. I’m good at it now, but she’s an utter natural at it. If this was a Star Wars universe, she’d be a pilot that Han Solo would bitch about because he wouldn’t want to admit that she was better than him.”

As if that had been a summoning spell, Vicky chirped the door and entered the cabin. “Interesting outfit choice, Captain, for meeting the men!” she said with a small laugh.

“She’s having a ‘girl’ moment,” Amy replied with a laugh. “Wants to give the absolute best impression to her guests, so she wants to be as professional as she can manage. Think of it as wanting to be seen as a peer.”

Taylor snorted. “Peer? Not going to happen. Ever. Yeah, I can scoot around the universe with amazing technology and such, but I’ll never measure up to those men. Or even Dr. Tyson. I’ve set myself an impossible goal, to be worthy of this ship and her legacy. I’m never going to measure up to Kirk, Picard, April, or even Archer. Hell Archer was more like the men I’m meeting today, because this was all new to them, and a true danger, since they had no idea what was out there. They just knew aliens existed at that point.”

“What do we know about our universe?” Amy asked. “Are there Vulcans? Andorians? Are there Wookies out there? All we know is that some form of aliens exist, because our Shards tell us so because of their history, and they seem to stick within their birth universe when they do whatever it is that they do. So we know that they’re aliens, and that they’ve come across other species. Beyond that? We know nothing about this universe. So you’ll be doing the same kind of exploring, love.”

“In a ship that can sit for a time within the coronasphere of a star, Amy,” Taylor replied. “As opposed to a vehicle that wasn’t perfectly capable of stopping the radiation that permeates space. It’s sort of like saying that I drove from here to Los Angeles in a modern vehicle, but claiming I did something just like the pioneers did. I’m in danger of running out of gas on my drive, or maybe having a breakdown in the car, where I can use a cell phone to call for help. The pioneers had none of that and the trip took months, and a lot died. Not at all the same.”

Amy shook her head, trying to figure out how to get Taylor out of her thoughts that she wasn’t worthy of the respect of these men. Men she was about to grant the ability to do what they should have done almost forty years earlier.

Vicky stepped in. “Taylor, you want professional, so let me figure out your wardrobe for the day. Work for you, since you’ll end up naked otherwise from not being able to decide.” After a quick pause she added, “Mind you, any crowd would be happy with that wardrobe choice, but it kinda gives the wrong impression.” She asked for a hologram of Taylor, which she then dressed from the skin out. French cut panties, black slacks, her left shoulder bare top she’d worn the day she’d announced herself to the world, and a dress jacket. Basically, the outfit she’d worn when she let the world know that the Enterprise was real.

When Taylor gave her an odd look, she said, “Think about it. While you change up your look, you tend to come back to that top that leaves a shoulder bare. Whether you realize it or not, you’ve decided that that specific top is your go-to command shirt. So wearing it makes the most sense for you. You’ll use the bra Amy built for you the way we all do, and maybe a built-in for the blouse to hide how pointy you’re going to be during this.”

“Yeah. Probably need you to put an off switch on the pulsing, Amy,” Taylor said. “Not the time to be enjoying a rapid heartbeat.” Amy nodded and touched her hand, and the pulsing stopped. “Weird. I was so used to it that now it feels weird to not be doing it. On-off switch?” Amy nodded at her, shaking her head in mild amusement.

In short order, Captain Hebert stood in front of them. “Okay,” the nervous girl said, “time to head down to the planet and make sure everything is ready. I’ve tried to keep this under wraps, which means that probably everyone from Portland to Key West has heard about this. And I mean Portland, Oregon.”

The three of them, dressed in variations of the Dallon designed uniforms, beamed down to Taylor’s house. Danny greeted them and said, “It’s going to work out fine, Taylor. You’re better at this than you think you are.”

“I hope so. I just worry. I’ve been told that they’ll be coming in via helicopter to the PRT, where I’ll meet them and take them to the Enterprise, where we’ll get on a shuttle piloted by Vicky, since she’s absolutely amazing at the job. First the Moon, where they’ll be allowed to set foot at the site they should have landed at. I’m contemplating seeing if they want to visit Mars as well.”

“I want to see Mars,” Danny said, “so I can’t imagine that an astrophysicist and two astronauts wouldn’t want to.” He sighed. “We just have to put up with the fact that there are probably going to be a bunch of extras along for the ride, just for the political points it will give them.”

“So long as I’m permitted to remain in control of things, I’m not going to worry too much. And once we’re aboard my ship, I’d like to see one of the congress-things try to order my ship around.” She snorted. “Any bets that someone like James Tagg will be there to actually try to claim the Enterprise in the name of the US military or something?”

“Not taking that bet. It wouldn’t be smart of them, but not all of the available generals are known to be intelligent,” Danny said.

“Well, the nice thing is that I wasn’t given a list of names other than the three that I offered to. As it is my property, from their point of view, I have full permission to deny them access. And I believe that Director Piggot would find it a chance to speak to someone in Washington, who might lead to speaking to their ultimate boss in Washington if it goes that far.”

“Do you really think it might go that far?” Amy had to ask. “That would … I don’t have the words. Problem is, I can see politicians thinking that they have the power to force you to take them aboard your ship.”

“Well, I make a couple enemies then, if that happens, because there has been no hint of anyone other than those three coming along. Anyone else gets a polite no, followed by a firmer no if they choose to push the issue.” Taylor looked at the clock and said, “Shall we head to the PRT building, in order to get things started?”

Amy looked a little worried about the day, now that the options of people trying to insert themselves into the situation reared its ugly head, but Taylor seemed to be prepared for it. Or was faking it like the rest of Manhattan, as the phrase went. Upon the nods from both her and Danny, Taylor called and asked permission to beam to a secure spot on PRT property, and it was granted. A moment later, they were standing in a secure conference room, with Emily Piggot waiting for them. The woman did not look happy.

“I hope it’s nothing I’ve done,” Taylor said, looking a little bothered.

“No, it’s that they dropped people on the list for today at the last minute. Two senators and an admiral from the Navy.”

“I suspected that they’d try something like that. Bad part for them is that I’m only really prepared for the three gentlemen that I originally requested. I suspect that it’s the first salvo in attempting to convince me to join up or sign over my ship. Not happening. I am not giving any one nation the ability to crack the planet easily. And make no mistake, applying the full power of a Federation starship to the surface of the Earth would be an extinction level event. I don’t want the power, but I trust me with it a lot more than I do any government. The ones that are more trustworthy rotate people into positions where a megalomaniac can get control, and the untrustworthy ones have the megalomaniacs already in control.”

“Well, I suppose that we’ll find out soon,” Director Piggot said, “because I’ve been informed that the helicopter is about twenty minutes out.”

Chapter 85: Saturday, March 26th, 2011 - Taylor

Taylor’s father and Starfleet people stood under cover as the helicopter carrying the visitors came in. The first three off the helicopter were the ones she’d invited, and as soon as it was clear to do so, she went out to meet them. “Captains. Doctor,” she greeted them. “I would salute but I’m not actually military, so I believe that it would likely be seen as an insult to someone who did serve,” she said to the retired astronauts. She did shake their hands, however.

“You are a captain yourself,” Captain Lovell said.

“Only by dint of having my parahuman power decide to latch onto my beautiful starship. I haven’t been through any sort of academy - and I want to set one up to teach how to deal with a ship like mine - and should probably be seen as more the type of person who is considered a captain because they have a boat of some sort. I haven’t earned any sort of military rank.” She then turned to the other three who had exited the helicopter. There had been a total of eight who had debarked. “I wasn’t made aware that anyone else was arriving with these gentlemen until this morning when I came to await the helicopter. So I apologize if I’m not prepared for your appearance here, sirs.”

As she approached one of them, she saw that one of the other was a photographer. “I don’t necessarily agree to photographs being taken of this, especially where there may be secrets that could be disclosed. She looked to the one man who had stepped forward first, whom she recognized - with Enterprise’s help - as the representative for the Maine district that held Brockton Bay. “Nor do I agree to a photograph that might be used in a later campaign, Representative Boone. I don’t mind shaking your hand, but I don’t want pictures of it that could be used in a later campaign to hint that I agree with your policies. If I am given advance warning of such pictures, I may well agree to them. But I have enough savvy to know how things like that can be used.” She looked over at the cameraman, who looked unapologetically back at her. After a moment or so, she shrugged and turned to the man in uniform. “And what brings an admiral to this gathering, sir?”

“Actually, let’s get right into it, then. I have zero issues with allowing these men to go to the Moon, but when we return, you will be signing over ownership of the Enterprise to the United States government.”

She heard the sound of skin hitting skin, and just knew that it was Director Piggot who had just done a face-palm. “Might want to get on the phone, Director,” Taylor said. “Chief Director Costa-Brown is going to want to know, and she’s definitely going to want to bring in this guy's ultimate boss.”

Sub-vocally, she asked, “Can you target just my people, Doctor Tyson, and the two astronauts?” She noted that the men in question were looking distinctly uncomfortable, especially since one of them was a Navy man himself.

“Easily, Captain. I’ll prepare that, and you give the word. They will be the only ones beamed up.”

“Excellent.” Then, so that she could be heard by the others, she said, “I’m not getting into that right now. These men were invited to visit the Moon, so we’re going to do that and worry about the rest later.” She pulled out her communicator and flipped it open to the familiar chirping. “Enterprise? Commence transport. Sorry, Director Piggot.”

When they materialized on the transporter pad, everyone looked around. “Where are the others?” Captain Lovell asked.

“I didn’t beam them up with us. This trip was for you, and they invited themselves along. Sorry for using the cargo bay, but since there are more than six of us, the standard transporter room wasn’t feasible.” She found herself amused at Doctor Tyson nearly vibrating at the fact that he had just undergone an actual transporter beaming. “So would you gentlemen like the tour of the ship before or after your visit to the Moon?”

Captain Haise spoke up. “I’m a Marine rather than Navy, but I can tell you that Admiral Blaukamp is not going to be a happy man when you go back down. As for me? I’d love to see the ship, since we’re already here.” The other two agreed with him quite vociferously, so she began the tour, first by heading next door to the shuttle bay, where she showed them the shuttle they would be taking to the Moon, the McAuliffe.

"This ship came through from one of the variants of the Star Trek universe,” she told them. “I did not just ‘magic’ this out of nothing to hover over the planet. As near as we can tell, since we’ve found that there is communication among the Shards using subspace - and while I never quite understood the meaning before, being directly connected to the ship’s systems has gotten me a better grasp on a lot of things - the moment I Triggered, the subspace connection that connected me to my power also apparently opened a connection to the universe she’s from,” she said, motioning to her ship, “and sort of pulled her through, I guess? Or traveled along her length and ‘kidnapped’ her?”

“It was nearly instantaneous, Captain,” Enterprise said. “If anything, it was more of a teleport or instant transport without the effects. I was in one universe one attosecond and here the next. And I was connecting to my new captain.”

“Do you know if there is going to be a mission to find you?” Dr Tyson asked.

“It largely depends on what traces were left behind. If there was enough of a residue of my travel, there will likely be an attempt to at least send an unmanned probe through to check things out.”

The tour continued, with Taylor explaining that many of the ship’s processes could be dealt with by holographic entities. “I consider Enterprise herself to be a holographic intelligence, much like Voyager’s Emergency Medical Hologram turned into, but not all of the others are at her level. She can think and make decisions, but is hard-wired to defer certain very important things to me.” She snorted. “You’ll recognize the doctor when you meet him, by the way. They managed to convince Leonard McCoy to let his engrams be copied, and they used them for this ship’s doctor. Not sure if he’s also a holographic intelligence, or if he just fakes it really well. I tend to think of him as just like Enterprise here.”

“I have an incoming message from Director Piggot,” Enterprise said to Taylor’s surprise.

“Send it to my implant, rather than a regular communicator, unless it’s something she needs everyone to hear.” A moment later she heard her internal communicator tell her the call was transferred there, and she subvocalized, “Yes, Director Piggot?”

There was a wry laugh at the other end. “You’ve got three annoyed people who think they’re important down here, and a couple press people who are sort of shrugging at the whole thing. The admiral is threatening all sorts of various things, and the two representatives are fairly clearly distancing themselves from him, politically speaking. I’ve been in contact with Chief Director Costa-Brown, so we’ll see where things go from there. I know that there are some segments that are looking at the laws to force you to turn your ship over, although how exactly they would enforce it is beyond me, but you never heard that from me.”

“Understood,” Taylor said with a small laugh. “So given a few things, do you think it likely that I can be expected to be clapped in irons when I come back down to the planet?”

“If the admiral has his way? Yes. But right now, we’re waiting from on high. I suspect that you’re going to end up pulling the president in on this debacle.”

“Can’t be helped. Too many don’t realize that I can’t be separated from the ship other than death, and if someone else causes it, Enterprise is likely to show her disapproval before … heading off to elsewhere.”

There was a laugh at the other end. “Watching your language around the gentlemen?”

“Exactly. The admiral keeps going the way he is, he’s going to learn the other part of the phrasing isn’t usually fun - ‘finding out’.”

“And as usual with that, it will be the least fun he’s ever had.”

“Well, I’m giving our guests a tour, so I’ll need to go now, but if there’s an update you can legally tell me, I would greatly appreciate it, Director.” She snorted.

“Sorry, gentlemen,” she said in a normal tone. “The admiral was displeased with my response, and is likely complaining to others. That, however, is not your problem, and I will do my best to ensure that it stays that way.” The tour continued, with the men marveling at the technology. The view from her favorite conference room, of course, was also a hit.

“I never thought I would ever get a chance to see this,” Doctor Tyson said. “And aboard a Federation starship? I knew that could never happen.” He had a smile on his face at that last.

Taylor smiled. “I know exactly what you mean, Doctor. And yet, here we are. Would you gentlemen like to come back to the shuttle bay and make the trip I invited you along for?” She paused. “My late mother would probably have cringed at that sentence.” Everyone in the room chuckled softly.

When they got to the shuttle bay, the astronauts were intrigued by Vicky walking over to the shuttle with a PADD and beginning a check of the McAuliffe. A few panels were opened and then closed again, and after she had made a complete circuit of the vehicle, she opened the shuttle door at the back. When they stepped into the shuttle, Vicky automatically took the pilot’s seat, and Taylor took the seat next to her, but turned it around to speak to the others in the shuttle. “The rest of the people here are potential crew - we’re getting them trained up properly on ship’s duties and such - but none of us have ever set foot anywhere else but either Earth or this ship. So, I figured we could all do with a trip to the Moon.” By this point, Vicky had made it through the checklist and said, “Shuttle ready for take-off, Captain.”

“Then by all means, Ensign Dallon, let us away.” The shuttle rose gently from the floor and flew toward the force field holding the atmosphere inside the ship, gliding through the field as if it weren’t there. Taylor stood and walked back to the others. “Captain Lovell? Would you like to sit up next to our pilot?” He stood and walked up to the front and sat in the seat, and clearly enjoyed the view.

“Bit different moving around this than in our tin can, huh, Fred?” he asked with a laugh.

“Got that right,” Captain Haise replied. “Can actually stand and not do that interesting ballet we had to.”

Taylor chuckled and said, “I could shut off the gravity in here and make it a little more what you were used to, if you want.” Her grin made it clear she wasn’t serious.

“Nah,” Lovell said. “I kinda like having a verifiable up and down reference at this point in my life.” He looked at the rapidly growing Moon and added, “Amazing how fast this is. Three day trip for us to get there, and a couple minutes for you now.”

Vicky blushed as she said, “I could have gotten us there faster, but the view … well, I wanted to take it our version of slow.”

Amy chuckled. “This from the speed demon back on Earth. You race every flier you see, whether they know it’s a race or not.”

“Yeah, but …” Vicky trailed off and motioned to the windows. “It’s worth the slow approach.” She looked at Captain Lovell. “But not as slow as yours,” she added with a chuckle.

“Hey, if we’d been able to get there this fast safely, you can bet we’d have done it,” he replied with a smile.

Vicky continued the approach, and aimed for a specific area on the Moon. She did not land there, because there was equipment there. “This was where they intended to have you land,” she said. “They had Apollo 14 land there instead. We can land here if you want, or we can set down in territory no one has landed on before, such as the lunar south or north poles, or something like Mare Humorum.” She smiled. “Everyone thinks of landing at the Sea of Tranquility.”

“Well, you have to admit,” Captain Haise said, “there’s something to be said for visiting a famous first site. Some of the most famous words in mankind’s history, and we still tease Neil for that slip up.”

“We let him say it was a radio glitch, because we knew how important it was, and everyone knew what he meant,” Lovell added with a laugh. At Vicky’s look, he explained. “That ‘One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind’ thing was supposed to be ‘for a man’, because otherwise it can be taken to mean that it was a small step for humans, but also a giant leap for humans. Sort of opposites, you know.”

“I always understood it to mean the singular for the first one, to be honest,” Vicky said.

“Yeah, but we still love to tease him about it,” Captain Haise said.

Lovell thought for a moment. “Can we set down here? This is where we were supposed to land, and there’s something about a feeling of completion. We don’t need to be the first to set down somewhere on the Moon.” He looked back to his fellow astronaut, who simply nodded.

“It’s your call, Commander.” With that, Lovell nodded, and they watched as Vicky gently set the shuttle down.

Taylor stood and walked to a cubby and opened it, pulling out three belts, then handed them to Captains Haise and Lovell, and also to Dr Tyson. “Luckily for you, I’m not stuck to the rule of cool, or the rule that it has to look good to the viewing audience,” Taylor said. With a grin she added, “Another way to put it is that the animated Star Trek series was canon where this ship came from, so there are life support belts. You can’t live on the Moon with them, but you can certainly visit for a few hours if you choose to.” She motioned to the others in the shuttle who had her variation on the Starfleet uniform. “They are built in to the uniforms, so we don’t need the belts.” With that, she opened the back of the shuttle. They saw the force field flare to life before the door opened, and they were suddenly looking out at the surface of the Moon.

“If you would care to lead us, Captain Hebert?” Captain Lovell said.

She smiled. “Thank you, but I think it would be more fitting if you finally got to set foot where you were supposed to nearly forty years ago. Please, Captain Lovell, lead us out?” With that, the man nodded with a smile and started slowly down the ramp that used to be acting at the back wall of the shuttle. He paused for a moment before stepping off the ramp onto the lunar surface. Captain Haise followed, then Dr Tyson.

“I’m supposed to say something profound, I’m sure,” he said, “but I can’t think of anything more than ‘This is amazing to actually stand here’. Thank you, Captain, Hebert.”

“I’m not a real captain, sir,” she said. “I’m one by dint of having the ship. You’re one because you earned it.”

“Well, from what we’ve been hearing, you’ve been doing a pretty good job of living up to the ideals of a Starfleet captain,” Captain Haise said. “From what I can tell, the technology increases are only things that we could have come up with ourselves in a few years. You basically pointed people in the right direction, but aren’t releasing things like the replicators or transporters.”

“Part of that is the dangers of a Tinker getting their hands on the wrong things, and also, I don’t want to lock anyone into a technology tree. If someone comes up with a portal technology that allows for actual instantaneous travel from point A to point B, I’m certainly not going to have a problem with that. I might try to see if I can replicate it without Tinker technology, since the older exuberant blonde over there is really good at doing Tinker stuff, but can also build things with Federation technology that are repeatable. And if we can repeat it, it can often be taken back in tech level as far back as necessary. Yeah, the Federation thing might be the size of a loaf of bread and the modern technology version takes up a small building, but if it can be patented by the one who made it? Keeps him or her from having to go criminal in order to use their powers.”

Captain Lovell was laughing as she finished. “And you prove with that why you’re a good choice. I have no problem considering you a captain, Captain.” He paused for a moment and then straightened up and saluted her. Captain Haise was mere seconds behind him.

She jumped slightly, which was amusing because she lifted off the surface of the Moon for a moment because of it, but managed to land properly before straightening as well and solemnly returning the salutes. “Thank you, gentlemen. I don’t feel it myself, but it means a lot to me.”

When they were done with the salutes, she chuckled. “I know it’s supposed to be illegal, but there were those in government that knew where I was bringing you. If you each decide to take a souvenir from here, I’m certainly not going to yell it from the mountaintops.”

Dr Tyson chuckled. “I looked this up when I realized that the offer was legitimate. Turns out the only lunar rocks illegal to own are those from the Apollo missions. Some of the ones from Soviet missions ended up at auction and have legally been purchased. So even if video comes out of the group of us each grabbing our own rock, it’s not illegal for us to own them, because this isn’t an Apollo mission.” He punctuated this by gently picking up a palm-sized stone from the surface. “Need to be careful, because they’re sharp, what with no weather around to 'weather’ them smooth.”

The rest of the group followed suit, and they were soon re-entering the shuttle.
